Summary

“Hey! I’m sorry about the other day, is there some way we can try again?”

“Oh? Uhh I wasn’t expecting this.”

“What do you mean?”

“You got out of there in a hurry. I assumed it didn’t go well and you really didn’t like me!”

“No! My son actually crashed my car!”

Or Agatha and Rio get set up on a blind date. Neither one of them know that Rio was the one who got Agatha pregnant 12 years ago. And they slowly fall in love with one another. Will they find out? What happens if they do?

Also, intersex Rio. In which it affects her confidence and love life!

    Chapter 1: Date night out!

    “You know, Agatha I have a friend, of a friend, who is looking to meet someone…”

    Agatha slowly turned her head at the young punk woman. “What?” Alice gave her a small chuckle. “My friend Hela… she has this friend who’s super cute by the way! Who’s looking to get into the dating scene. What do ya say!?”

    Agatha squinted at her. She wasn’t sure what part of her screamed ‘I need a partner in my life.’

    “Why?”

    Alice sighed. “Look girl! You’re a very single and ready to mingle mom! You need to get out there! No offense but every day you come into work I swear the cloud above your head gets bigger and bigger! You’re killing the vibe I’ve been working so hard on maintaining! Go! Find love! Or get laid! Or both! Something! But I can’t watch you stumble around like a loner anymore!“ Agatha’s face fell. She glared at the security guard. “What are you saying? I look like a loser or something!?” She pointed at the woman. “I’ll have you know I work very hard as a single mother! I don’t need you telling me how to live my life!”

    Alice rolled her eyes. “Come on! It’ll be good for you! At least go meet the girl! You don’t even have to commit to anything. Maybe… you two could even be friends or whatever. You don’t have many of those either!” Agatha scoffed and looked away in disbelief. “Unbelievable…” “I know! Someone as hot as you, single!?”

    Agatha’s head shot back at her. “Well if you think I’m so hot then why don’t you ask me out yourself!?” She pushed. She didn’t like Alice in that way. She just wanted to make the girl uncomfortable so she’d leave her alone.

    Alice had to suppress a chuckle.

    Only offending Agatha more.

    “Okay! Not what I was getting at with that one! You’re…. Not my type first of all. You’re a bit too…” She was trying to figure out how to lay it on lightly. “Dominant for me. You need someone who can handle all that.” She gestured to Agatha. “And I also don’t make it a habit of dating the people I work with. Especially my boss!” She chuckled.

    Agatha scoffed again. “Well sorry! I’m not good enough for you! Gulliver!” Alice grinned. “Look I know! I’m a heart breaker! But I’m afraid this heart-“ she tapped at her own chest. “Is looking for that special someone that gets me! Someone I can share my passions with and has the same hobbies and interests I do.”

    Agatha rolled her eyes. “Like…” she paused for a moment. “Wanda’s son Billy?”

    Alice grimaced. “Okay! First of all! He’s too young for me and underaged! And second he’s gay! And I’M! Gay!”

    Agatha busted out into laughter. “No shit you don’t say?” Her voice oozed with sarcasm.

    A blush spread across Alice’s face. “You know what sure! You and me! Right now! Come here boss woman!” Alice opened her arms and approached her.

    Agatha’s ceased her laughter and threw her arms out. “Okay I get it! I was just teasing! I’m not into you either! You’re too…” she looked her up and down. “How do I put this nicely.”

    Alice’s arms fell to her sides as she glared at the woman. “There isn’t a spark. We aren’t even friends… more like acquaintances.” Agatha noticed the hurt on the woman’s face and she immediately felt terrible. “But that doesn’t mean we can’t be! You me, Lilia and Jen should… hang out sometime. Have a girls night out. If that interests you?” She offered a comforting smile. “It’s just… we only see each other at work. And I really don’t know a whole about you. I’m sure you’re a great girl I just…”

    A smiled came back to Alice’s face. She held up a hand. “You don’t have to explain it to me. Olive branch accepted. But seriously! I’m usually right about these things!” She tapped on her desk. “And Lilia is backing me up on this! Rio is perfect for you! She’s tough and can handle you! And I think you’ll find her pretty cute! Think about it?”

    Agatha sighed then nodded.

    Alice fist pumped in the air. “It’ll be great for you and maybe eventually Nicky! You may be a supermom but having another one would do him good.”

    “Alright! Text me the details. You’re dismissed!” She shooed her off.

    Agatha went to the spot that was agreed upon for them to meet at. Alice had told her this Rio woman didn’t mind where they met. As long as it was a public space.

    Smart.

    Agatha appreciated that.

    She ended up choosing a park.

    Simple.

    Because honestly she wasn’t even sure what she’d get out of this meeting and she wanted as many possible exits as possible.

    She took her seat on a bench that overlooked a small pond of geese and ducks and sighed.

    “Is this seat taken?”

    Agatha looked up at the voice. Her eyes widened slightly and she let out the faintest gasp.

    Alice lied.

    This woman wasn’t ‘cute.’

    She was down right beautiful!

    “That depends… is your name Rio?”

    The woman nodded. “Agatha?”

    Agatha nodded in return.

    She took in the woman’s appearance as she sat down. She was wearing a sparkling, cropped, green jacket over a matching green dress shirt; that complimented her skin tone, and a pair of black pleather pants. Her eyes were as dark as obsidian. They were round and somehow… familiar. She had wavy, mid length black hair and beautiful plump lips. She gave off a cool and mysterious vibe. She had such a unique beauty about her and oh how unfair it was, but even still it drew her in, wanting to know more.

    “I hope this isn’t too forward of me. But you have such kind and beautiful eyes.”

    Agatha came out of her stupor. She felt her face flush at the sudden compliment. “Oh! Uhh… Thank you!” She stammered, glancing away for a moment to find her bearings.

    It had really been a long time since she’s been on a…date? The woman spoke up again. “This is odd, huh? My friend insisted I come meet you. Honestly, I wasn’t even expecting anyone to show up. I thought she was just messing with me.” She paused for a moment. “But then I saw you sitting here alone and I… was really hoping it was you.” She said before looking out at the pond, smiling.

    “Well I’m real. And by the looks of it your friend didn’t prank you. Besides, it can’t possibly be hard for you to meet people.”

    Rio shrugged. She leaned back and nonchalantly slid her arms out to the sides.

    Agatha glanced at the arm close to her shoulder and blushed at her boldness. She cleared her throat. “I am Agatha Harkness. I’m a…business owner.” She held out her hand.

    Rio turned and beamed at the gesture and took her hand. “Rio Vidal. Mortician and florist.”

    Agatha nodded. “So you run a funeral home I take it?”

    Rio nodded. “Yeah, my very own actually. With a good friend of mine. What’s your business?”

    Agatha looked away for a moment, she decided to change the subject. “So what kind of things do you like to do for fun Rio?” She looked back at the woman. Hoping she’d take the hint.

    Rio tilted her head in confusion before deciding to just leave it. “Oh, I play in a band. Sometimes I play basket ball, and… I enjoy knife throwing. Just to list a few.”

    Agatha’s eyes widened slightly. “A band? Is it Alice’s?”

    Rio nodded.

    Agatha rolled her eyes with a scoffed. “Friend of a friend my ass!” She grumbled.

    Rio quirked a brow in confusion.

    Agatha noticed and quickly got back on track. She didn’t want to scare the girl away. “What instrument do you play?”

    “Drums!” Rio said excitedly.

    Agatha nodded. “Pretty cool. My son loves music! He enjoys to sing! I know he wants to play every instrument under the sun. I just hadn’t got him anything yet.” She gushed as she spoke about her darling boy. For a moment though she worried that the mention of children would put the other woman off. But it couldn’t have been further from the truth. Because Rio was currently beaming from ear to ear. “You have kids!? Oh! I love kids! I don’t have any of my own but I wish I did.”

    Agatha smiled.

    “Do you have any hobbies?”

    Agatha shook her head. “I haven’t had time for myself since having my son.”

    The woman in green frowned.

    Agatha felt bad for souring the mood. “Well… I guess I enjoy singing as well and dancing.” She looked away shyly.

    “That sounds like fun. You and Alice are friends right? Do you two ever get together and sing?”

    Agatha shook her head.

    “Oh you should totally come to one of our shows sometime! It’d be fun!” The prospect made Agatha nervous. She went to open her mouth but stopped when her phone buzzed. She quickly pulled it out of her pocket and read the message. “Sorry one second.”

    Agatha’s eyes widened, she grabbed her purse and quickly stood up. “I’m sorry! I have to go! My son crashed my car!”

    She seemed agitated.

    Rio looked up at her with worry as she stood up too. “Oh? Is everything okay? I could give you a ride if you need or—“ “No it’s okay my friend is coming to get me. I’m really sorry about this!” She gave Rio an apologetic smile, before rushing off.

    Rio watched her leave. Her face fell as she looked down at her feet and sighed.

    Agatha couldn’t even begin to describe how angry she was. She paced back and forth in front of the two boys, who looked down in shame. “I leave you alone for an hour!” She stopped and stared at them. “And you crash my car into the neighbors fence!?” She growled out. Her son tried giving her his puppy eyes. But it didn’t work. “I’m sorry momma I-“ She held up her hand cutting him off. Before stepping in front of the older boy and glared at him. “I entrusted my son’s wellbeing into your hands! Billy!”

    He coward at the harsh tone of her voice, staring down at his shoes. “I’m sorry.”

    “I don’t want to hear sorry! It shouldn’t have happened in the first place! You’re only 15! Why were encouraging Nicky to drive!?”

    “It’s not his fault Momma! It was my idea! Billy was trying to stop me! Honest!”

    Agatha’s head shot in his direction. “And why would you do that!?” “I wanted to see you! I haven’t seen you since this morning! We always hang out after I get off school!”

    Agatha shook her head. “That is no excuse! Do you know how much this is going to cost me to fix!?” She gesture toward the dented suv and broken fence. “And I told you I had plans today! That’s why Billy’s here!” The young boy looked down, unable to meet his mother’s eyes any longer. Ashamed at what he had done. He started tearing up.

    “And where is Tommy!?” Agatha held out her arms incredulously. “He’s not feeling well… he’s um in the bathroom.” Billy said awkwardly. Agatha covered her face with her hands. She didn’t want to deal with this right now. On top of the crash she may have a sick five year old blowing up her bathroom.

    “Ugh! I’m calling your mother!”

    If you asked anyone what their first Impression of Rio was they’d probably tell you they thought she was grumpy or goth or whatever. And also that she had a confidence about her. A weird confidence, but confidence. And while a lot of those things were true, people still didn’t know a thing about her.

    She had a lot of confidence in herself. Sometimes her ego would get the best of her. There was a lot she liked about herself. Her quirky sense of humor, her unique personality, her style, her taste in music, that she was kind; for the most part. She was smart. She knew she was pretty. But she still had her tough days where she couldn’t go out without makeup. She liked her body…. Mostly. She liked her strong arms, her toned thighs and abs. But her breasts… they weren’t all that big. But she could deal with it. It wasn’t the end of the world and she didn’t have to prove anything to anyone.

    But her biggest insecurity. The one thing that held her back. That made it hard for her to even attempt relationships. Was the very thing between her legs. Rio didn’t have the typical parts a female would. She was intersex. She had male genitalia and it made her uncomfortable. But the thing was, that it was part of her. It had always been part of her. But, she still felt like an outlier.

    She was aware she came off as suave and aloof. Cool and interesting. But when it came to dating… she didn’t have a lot of experience. Her longest relationship was six months back in her college days. And that went up in flames all for the sake of physical intimacy.

    But according to her ex girlfriend it was because she lied… She grimaced at the thought. Rio knew the relationship crumbled because she wasn’t ready to go all the way. So she broke it off and rightfully so, with how the other girl acted.

    She thought everything was going great. But In the end they went their separate ways.

    So yes, Rio Vidal wasn’t the best when it came to dating. So she honestly wasn’t surprised when Agatha left in a hurry. Even still it hurt. It had been a long time since she’s even tried. She didn’t expect much.

    But now…

    Her phone rang.

    She finished up some paperwork before answering it.

    “Hello?”

    “Hi, is this Rio?”

    “It is…” She trailed off. Not recognizing the voice.

    “It’s Agatha!”

    Her eyes widened. She quickly shoved the paperwork away near the flower shops register and hurried to her office.

    “Oh, how are you?” She shut the door. She didn’t need Hela overhearing anything.

    “I’m alright. You?”

    “Good.” It was a half lie. She was lonely.

    There was a pause before the other woman continued to speak. “Hey! I’m sorry about the other day, is there some way we can try again?”

    Rios eyes widened. She moved the phone away as she silently cheered then brought it back to her face and spoke calmly. “Oh? Uhh I wasn’t expecting this.”

    There was a pause.

    “What do you mean?”

    “You got out of there in a hurry. I assumed it didn’t go well and you really didn’t like me!”

    “No! My son actually crashed my car! Here, look.” She sent a picture. Rio held her phone back to look at the photo. Her mouth fell open in disbelief. She brought the device back to her ear. “I… honestly thought that was a made up excuse to… you know what never mind!”

    Agatha sighed on the other end. “Look we really didn’t get much of a chance to talk the other day. And I— I’d like to get to know you better and make it up to you! Let me take you out? On an actual date this time?” Rios heart pounded in her chest. She couldn’t believe it. No one had ever asked her out before. “Yeah, that sounds cool!”

    She could hear the relieved sigh on the other end. “Alright, how about that little Italian place on 5th street? This Friday at seven, work for you?” Rio had to think about it for a moment.

    “If that doesn’t work then—“ “Yes that works!” She lied, partially. But she’s her own boss. She could move some things around.

    “Good! I’ll see you then. Send me your address and I’ll pick you up!” Rio had to suppress the squeal she had been holding back. “Okay! See you then!”

    Friday could not have come slower for Agatha. She had meeting after meeting. Bombarded with client complaints and all.

    She needed this night out.

    And with the amount of apologizing Wanda had done last week she was more than happy to watch her son for her while she went on this date. She looked herself over in the mirror. This was a nightmare! She wasn’t sure how nice she should dress! She didn’t wanna come off like she was trying to hard. But she didn’t want to look like a slob either. Something about this woman made her want to impress her. To keep her interested.

    She sighed as she decided on a little purple cocktail dress. It would do. The neck line plunged just enough to show a bit of cleavage. She wore her mother’s old necklace around her neck. She decided to go with an updo for the occasion. She allowed a few strands to dangle purposely framing her face.

    She groaned as her phone vibrated again. Billy would not stop sending her good luck messages and advice.

    Like she’d take advice from fifteen year old! And gay male one at that! She snickered. The boy did give her good advice on fashion though. And even what nail polish complimented her best. Thankfully purple was her color. Which was her favorite.

    She smiled at his text.

    Billy: You got this! I believe in you! She’s gonna love you I just know it! Agatha: Thanks kid.

    He was like a second son to her. They had a close bond. One that she really didn’t have with that many people. And as prickly as her and Wanda’s friendship could be at times she knew the Maximoff family had her back. Even if they did drive her nuts from time to time.

    She sent Rio a quick text letting her know she was on her way and headed out.

    She needed to calm herself down. Her heart was pounding in her chest. Full of nervousness and excitement.

    She pulled up to the apartment complex. Her mouth dropped when she saw the woman on the curb, who had yet to look her way. She rolled her window down and smiled. “Well aren’t you just a vision. Who’s the lucky guy, hot stuff?” She joked.

    Rios head turned. A look of confusion strewned across her face before it was overtaken by a smile. She went up to the window and leaned against it. “I can promise you there’s no man. And… no other woman who’s lucky.” She glanced Agatha up and down. “Because the only lucky one I see tonight is you beautiful.”

    Agatha blushed. She stammered trying to find a response.

    Rio giggled before opening the door and hopping in. She got an even better look up close. She reached out to touch the material of Agatha’s dress, directly over her thigh. “Such soft material. This looks… expensive.” She moved her hand back as if she herself would taint the lovely material. And now that she thought about it Agatha was driving a pretty pricy car. A fucking Mercedes! She whistled. “What a car.”

    Jeez was she out of her element. And here she was wearing an outfit she bought at the mall!

    “Dang I should have got something nicer.” She let out a nervous huff, as she looked down at what she was wearing.

    Agatha cursed under her breath. Rio was feeling bad about herself now. She reached out and placed a comforting hand on her leg. “I like what you’re wearing. You know… name brands aren’t everything! They’re honestly overrated. This is the only name brand dress I own and this car is from my job. My actual SUV is being worked on.” She glanced up at the complex she had just picked Rio up from. This part of town wasn’t exactly cheap to live in either. “And by the looks of it you’re doing pretty good yourself. I’d argue better than me.”

    Rio looked up at her. “Oh don’t be fooled. Me and my friend split the rent and I don’t have a kid. I also uber everywhere. So not the best comparison. But I guess…” she rubbed the back of her neck and looked up at her home. “It’s… I wanted to live in a nice neighborhood.” She looked back at Agatha and smiled at her.

    The two women made their way into the restaurant. Agatha smiled at the host. “Reservation under Harkness.”

    Rios eyes widened. It was rare she frequent somewhere that required reservations. She looked around and took the place in. The place was gorgeous!

    “Right this way ladies!” The man said with an accent.

    Rio grinned as she ran around Agatha to pull her chair out for her. “Mi lady!”

    Agatha snickered. “Aren’t you a gentlewoman!” She took her seat. “Thank you Rio.”

    She pushed her in before going around and taking her own seat. “So what do they have that’s good?” Rio picked up her menu scanning it over.

    Agatha shrugged. “It’s honestly been a while since I’ve been here. I’ve come here once for a company meeting. Aside from that no clue.” The woman stared at her. “Seriously what do you do for work!? I must know!”

    Agatha glanced up from her menu before signing. She sat it down and gave Rio her full attention. “I’m…” she cleared her throat. “The owner of Harkness Inc.” she pursed her lips as she held her head high. She would never be ashamed or embarrassed by her inherited job. It’s what kept food on the table and roof over their heads. But the company didn’t have the best reputation. Many rumors of it being a predatory business that destroyed smaller ones were common place. Even if they were further from the truth. Just fake bull shit spread by bitter people who weren’t able to get their projects funded.

    But Rio only tilted her head in question. She was glancing up as if she was lost in thought. “Never heard of it. Sounds fancy. What do you guys do? Or make?”

    Agatha was honestly surprised. She had become pretty well known in the area. Since moving to westview and along with herself, her mother’s company. They were the most influential business in the county, if not, that side of New Jersey.

    “Originally it was a publishing company for aspiring authors. My mother’s business actually. But it eventually shifted into an investment firm. Boring stuff really.”

    “Your mother? So… you always wanted to take after her or?” Agatha shook her head. “Absolutely not. But…” she looked away for a moment. “I had planned to become a psychologist, but I got pregnant near the end of my college career. I was unable to finish. I didn’t have any other options other than to work under my mother’s wing. But it worked in her favor, in the end.”

    Rio reached for her hand, “I’m sorry to hear that!” Trying to distract her for a moment.

    “You know what the worse part is? I don’t even remember how. Or who! And let me tell you I have never wanted to sleep with a man in my life! I had felt like I betrayed myself. But my mother didn’t care. As long as her daughter got out of that stupid and useless field it didn’t matter what it took. My job keeps my boy fed and roof over his head. It’s a job.” Rio ran her thumb up and down the other woman’s hand.

    “Shit sorry. I didn’t mean to ruin the mood.”

    Rio shook her head. “Not ruined. I’m happy you’re venting. You can talk to me whenever you need to.” She smiled.

    Agatha smiled back. “So what makes someone want to start their own funeral business?”

    “Ahh yes. Well, most people are weird with death. Not me. I wanted to be able to help grieving families. So I do a job many people don’t want to do. Plus! I love flowers! I’m kind of a nerd for flowers and plants! I have a thing for nature. And life and I guess… death.” She chuckled. “But my friend Hela seemed to share a similar sentiment. I’m not the religious type by any means. But she is. So we started this business together. Even…” Rio looked down. “I’m gonna be honest it’s not exactly a hot job. People tend to get put off by it. I thought maybe that was the reason you left.” Agatha shook her head. “No my son just decided he wanted to come see me. But he doesn’t know how an automatic transition shift works and reversed my car into the neighbors fence.” She let out a giggle. Rio chuckled at that. It made Agatha’s heart flutter.

    “Well that sounds expensive!”

    “Tell me about it! But lucky for me it was the neighbors kid watching him so her husband offered to pay for the damages. A good thing too. I may have a well paying job but… my boy gets sick easily. I have a lot of medical bills to pay off on top of his medication. And kids just aren’t cheap in general. So in the end it wasn’t terrible. I was honestly worried my son hurt himself. But then his babysitter decided to clarify a little better over text.”

    “What a handful!”

    The two women giggled as they walked hand in hand down the street. “Sorry we have to walk, my building is weird and won’t let anyone park on the street past nine unless they’re big shots or something.” The woman swayed a bit.

    Agatha pulled her in. Keeping her from tumbling over in her almost drunken state. “Wow! You sure got tipsy!”

    “Aw you worried about me Harkness?” She stopped in front of her and pulled her close. “Is it cause I’m so charming?” She grinned before letting out a hiccup.

    Agatha rolled her eyes but chuckled. “You’re something alright.” “I hope that something is a good thing!” She booped her nose then turned and continued walking.

    Agatha looked at her fondly. “I…think it is.” She said under her breath. They made it inside. Agatha walked her over to the elevator. “Well I had a really nice night. Would you like to do this again?” Agatha chanced the question.

    Rios face lit up as she nodded vigorously.

    Agatha couldn’t help but think how adorable she was right now. “I absolutely wa—Ugh!” She keeled forward. Agatha shot her arm out and grabbed her.

    “Maybe I should help you inside.” They went into the elevator and Rio clicked the button to her floor. “Someone’s smooth. Wanting to come see my apartment already? You have motives Aggie?” Rio winked. Agatha blushed. “Well… if by motives you mean make sure you don’t throw up in the elevator and help you get home, then yes.” “Now who’s the gentlewoman now!”

    They fumbled out of the elevator.

    “Boy you really can’t hold your booze!”

    “I take anxiety meds! Intensifies the effects.”

    Agatha’s eyes widened. “Why didn’t you tell me I wouldn’t have order that wine for you!”

    “Oh! We only live once! And… honestly I was distracted.”

    “By what!?”

    “A pretty lady.” She grinned.

    Agatha rolled her eyes. “Now aren’t you smooth!”

    Rio giggled as she fumbled for her keys. She cursed under breath before dropping them.

    Agatha sighed and leaned forward to pick them up for her. “Alright you!” She unlocked the door and pushed it open. “There you are. Can you make it or do I need to walk you inside too?”

    Rio smirked. “Aw while I’d love for you to, my roomie is here. And I don’t think she’d appreciate me having a lady friend over. I can get pretty loud.” She smirked.

    Agatha blushed. “Someone’s confident! But that’s not what I meant sweetheart.”

    “Oh I know what you meant.” She winked then backed away into the doorway. Keeping her eyes on the other woman.

    Agatha smiled as she watched the drunken woman slowly make her way inside.

    “You know…” Rio started. “I don’t usually kiss on the first date but…” she moved forward, back toward Agatha and kissed her cheek. “I think a very special lady deserves a little treat for being such a gentlewoman.” She leaned up and kissed her cheek again, pulling a blush from the other woman. “I’ll text you about that second date Aggie.” She backed away, smiling from ear to ear.

    Agatha grinned and nodded. “Yeah! Alright! I can’t wait!”

    “Soooo! You and Rio going on a second date! Is she smokin or what!?” Agatha glared as her security guard snuck into her office. “If she’s so… ‘smokin’ then why didn’t you ask her out? Hm? Gulliver? You two seem… like you’re into the same scene.” Agatha wasn’t trying to give her any ideas. She just wanted to make sure there’d be no competition. “Rio!? She’s been my friend for a while! We met through Hela. She’s cool and hot and all! But… I don’t know. I guess I’ve just never got that spark? Besides, Rio needs someone who will be attentive to her feelings. I’m terrible at that kind of thing. She’s… she hasn’t had the best life growing up. And I know you like to… come off as cold. But I know you can take care of her. My intuition is strong. Honestly, if I dated anyone it’d be Hela. But I’m not sure I see that happening. Not to mention I’m not as… rough as those two. I want someone mellow and chill, and not the way Rio is! Rio is a feisty babe! And so are you! You two are perfect! I expect to be the best woman at the wedding!”

    Agatha rolled her eyes and groaned. “God you are dramatic! But… by some miracle you were right. I… Rio is an amazing girl.”

    “I know right! She’s a total manic pixie dream girl! And god! You’re the sexy older… younger? CEO. How old are you?”

    Agatha glared. “That is not an appropriate question to ask your boss! And I’m 39! I’m not that old!”

    “Holy shit! You’re younger than Rio! Wasn’t expecting that! But I guess she has a young aura about her. Even if she has a very old soul.” Now this caught Agatha’s attention. “How old?”

    “She’s 42! Isn’t that like super hot! And she looks good for her age! Damn I’m surrounded by MILFS and MILF potential babes! How lucky am I!?” “Your lucks about to run out Gulliver!” She growled.

I m-meant to tell you! But m-my phone slid under the seat of my friend’s truck that I b-borrowed, and a car cut me o- off! I almost s-slid into a telephone pole...” She chuckled nervously.

    The worry that overtook Agatha was overwhelming. “Oh my god! Get in here! Let me look at you!” She pulled Rio into the house. “I’m s-sorry!”

    Agatha softly gasped at the sight of tears streaming down the woman’s face. She shook her head then pulled her in for a hug. “What are you apologizing for? The weather!? I’m just happy you’re okay! Oh you’re shaking!” She pressed a comforting hand to her head and rocked them side to side. She heard a little sob come from the woman and she shushed it away. “It’s okay sweetie I got you.” She kissed her head. “I’m not mad. You’re okay.”

    Rio nodded against her chest. She squeezed her closer and listened to the beat of her heart.

    “Here,” she led Rio over to the couch. “Come sit. Relax. Let me get some towels and some dry clothes.”

    “W-wait! I d-don’t w-wanna g-get your couch w-“ But before she could even finish Agatha was pushing her down onto the furniture. “Oh whoops it’s wet now. Guess it’ll have to dry, like you!” She smiled. She grabbed a blanket and draped it over Rio before disappearing. Rio hugged the blanket to herself then looked around. Her body was still shaking. The mixture of cold and adrenaline was not a great combo. Not only did she just experience one of the scariest moments in her life, she was also upset for making Agatha doubt her.

    Upset that she made Agatha think she stood her up. When it couldn’t have been further from the truth. She picked up on a sweet scent. She sniffed the blanket and sighed.

    It smelled like Agatha.

    “Alright! Come here you!” Agatha sat down and pulled the blanket off to wrap a towel around her.

    The older woman blushed at how close she was.

    Rio sighed as Agatha started drying her hair.

    “Are you hurt?”

    “Huh?”

    “I asked if you’re hurt. You said you almost hit a phone pole?” “Oh. I’m… I’m okay.” She snuggled closer to Agatha. “It was close though.”

    Agatha wrapped her arms around her a tightly. Trying to ground her. “I don’t know what I would have done if you got hurt!”

    “I’m okay. Just shaken up over it!” She was starting to warm up. Agatha sighed. She turned and glanced out the blinds behind the couch. “Well it’s pouring down out there. I think we should just save the escape room for another time.”

    Rio sat up. “Oh! I was really looking forward to our date!” She pouted. Agatha caressed her face and smiled. “You can stay here. I’ll cook for you! We can hang out! Play a board game!? Watch a movie!? Whatever you want!”

    Rios face lit up before she smirked. “Whatever I want huh?” Agatha tilted her head as she watched Rio turn in the direction of the tv. She followed her gaze and realized she was staring at her son’s switch. “Oh. My son has Mario kart. Wanna play?” Agatha offered.

    Rios face brightened up as she nodded. “Yeah! You sure your son won’t mind?”

    Agatha waved a hand at that. “No. He hasn’t played with it in a while. He’s been so busy playing at the neighbors house on their PlayStation. I think I play it more than he does. Is that childish?”

    Rio shook her head. “No! I love video games! If it’s childish then I’m the biggest child around and I’m 42!”

    “I can’t believe that. You look so young. Alice thought I was older than you.” Agatha chuckled.

    “How old are you if you don’t mind me asking?”

    “39. I’ll be 40 next month though.”

    “Oh! Come on! You look your age! Sexy and mature!” Rio smiled. Agatha looked away with a blush. “Thanks.” She snickered then looked back at her. “You’re funny!”

    Rio quirked a brow at her. She slid her arm across the couch and leaned against her. “I’m serious.” She said flatly. “You’re beautiful.” “Oh! You’re gonna make my heart burst!” Agatha fanned herself off. Rio grinned. “I know! I know! I’m a heart throb! Guilty!” She winked. “Now! I call dibs on Yoshi!”

    Agatha’s eyes widened. “Oh no! Because I totally wasn’t going to pick a random character! But first!” She finished drying off her hair. “Change into these! I don’t want you catching your death! Not on my watch!” She held out some of her own clothes.

    Rio smiled. “Such a gentlewoman!”

    Agatha waited for her to come out of the bathroom. She had the game ready for them.

    “Hey I got the game up and some snacks if you wa—“ she blushed at the sight of the woman in her own clothes.

    “Your clothes fit nicely. They’re pretty comfy. May have to steal them.” She grinned and took her seat next to the younger woman.

    “I’m glad you’re feeling a bit better. Ready for me to destroy you!?” Rio snickered. “Oh! You are so on Harkness!”

    After an hour they decided to take a break from the game. They were having so much fun.

    Rio was relaxing in the living room while Agatha cooked. But she decided she wanted the company so she got up.

    The younger woman sung and danced while cooking something on the stove. Unaware of that she had an audience of one.

    Rio leaned up against the kitchen door frame with her arms crossed, gazing lovingly at the woman.

    “Smells good!”

    Agatha jumped, cursing under her breath. She turned then flashed the other woman a smile. “How long have you been standing there?”

    Rio took in her appearance. Her ‘kiss the cook’ apron was adorable and her messy updo; with fallen strands of hair framing her flushed face, was perfect. She was a vision. One that made her heart skip a beat. “Long enough.” She pushed off the wall and made her way over to Agatha to see what she was making. She looked back up at the woman and gazed into her eyes. “Looks good too.”

    Agatha stared at her for a moment before snickering. She was unsure if Rio was referring to the food or her. “Thanks! I hope you like it! It’s a family recipe.”

    “Oh? I should feel honored then.”

    Agatha beamed as she stirred the soup. She continued to hum. Now very aware of the woman’s gaze.

    They stood in a comfortable silence. Rios gaze drifted over towards the fridge and her smile widened. She walked over and grabbed a photo. “Is this him?”

    Agatha hummed without turning around. “My boy? Yes.”

    “He’s so cute! I see where he gets it from though!”

    Agatha giggled. She turned and looked at Rio from over her shoulder. “What? From his unknown father?”

    Rio shook her head. “Nope! From his gorgeous Momma!” She looked back down at the photo. “His eyes are so pretty! I thought they were brown at first but the closer I look the more I realize they’re a mixture of brown and blue. Almost a green tint to them! How unique! His father must have had brown eyes!”

    Agatha sighed. “Possibly. But we’ll never know.“ she watched the other woman look at her photos. And with a quirk of her brow she asked. “You said you wanted kids of your own?”

    Rio looked up and nodded. “Yeah. I always wanted to have a family of my own.”

    “Why didn’t you?”

    Rios face fell.

    “You don’t have to answer! I hope I didn’t make you uncomfortable. It wasn’t my intention!”

    Rio sighed. “No it’s not you. I… I don’t think I can have a child of my own. I’ve never tried but… there’s reasons and I considered adopting but… I didn’t want to raise a child on my own. I don’t think I’d be able to. I haven’t been with someone in a long time. It was just never a realistic option for me.” She shrugged. “Some people aren’t meant to have families. Maybe it just wasn’t in the cards for me.”

    “Oh! I’m sure your parents don’t think that!”

    Rio turned and out the photo back up on the fridge. “Um… I wouldn’t know…”

    Agatha softly sighed and then approached her. “Rio I’m sorry I didn’t realize! I shouldn’t have assumed.”

    Rio shook her head and turned around. She was smiling now. But it didn’t reach her eyes. “It’s okay. You didn’t know. It’s fine. It’s how I met Hela. We grew up in foster care.”

    Agatha placed a comforting hand on her arm.

    “It’s just another reason why I was so apprehensive about starting a family. I wouldn’t know what that’s like. How could I even be a mother, when mine didn’t even want me? My last name is all I have. Surprising. Honestly. My parents gave me up when I was only one. What a way to screw me over, they should have just given me up the moment I was born. Most people want babies. The older I got the less likely I was to be adopted. And… there was another reason. I just… I can’t talk about it right now.” She looked down at her feet.

    The pain on her face struck right into Agatha’s heart. How could anyone not want this wonderful person? She pulled her in for a hug. “I’m sorry. Rio. No child should have to go through that!”

    “Yeah, I know right. It sucked!” She chucked sadly. “But I had Hela through it all. She’s basically my sister. We aged out together. We managed to save up enough money from part time jobs to go to college together. We survived together. I honestly don’t know if I’d still be here today without her.”

    Agatha held her tighter. She couldn’t imagine a world without Rio Vidal in it. “I should send her a million flowers as thank you. You’re so wonderful Rio.” She ran her hand up and down her back. She knew it wasn’t nearly the same but Agatha understood to some degree. All she had was her mother growing up and the woman was horrible to her. Honestly she wished she had been given up for adoption. But she wouldn’t mention that right now.

    Her mother would berate her. Tell her she wasn’t good enough and that she was a bad person who’d grow up to do bad things. The mental scars she left on her may have dwindle after years of separation. But her physical scars from years of caning stayed with her. Eventually her mother stopped with the beatings. Agatha wasn’t sure why. But she was thankful. But the evidence stayed with her. Her mother mostly targeted her calf’s and rear. The scars were her most self conscious parts of her. She had a couple on her hands. She use to cover up with makeup. But eventually got them tattooed over in a skin tone pigment. It was faint. You could still see them if you looked close enough. But Agatha never met anyone get that close. The only one who knew about her scars were Nicky. Who on occasion had kissed her hand and calf scars. She never told him how she got them though. She didn’t want him to know how she used to be treated by her own mother.

    “I’m almost done with our food! Come sit down relax!” She pulled the older woman towards the table.

    She sat her down. The other woman felt bad for not having helped set the table. “I can wash the dishes afterward if you’d like?”

    Agatha shook her head. “Nonsense! You’re my guest!”

    Agatha hurried back toward the stove. She was excited for Rio to try this. She wanted to impress her.

    She say the bowl down in front of the woman, along with some bread and butter. “Would you like something to drink? Tea? Water? Juice? Maybe Gatorade?”

    Rio chuckled. “Wow you have it all huh?”

    “Well Nicky loves everything. But I don’t bring pop into this house so I’m sorry if you wanted a coke or something.”

    Rio shook her head. “Ew I don’t drink it anyways. I’ll take a water.” “Coming right up!”

    After grabbing their drinks Agatha sat down across from her. She waited for Rio to pick up her spoon and taste the soup before she even bothered to move herself.

    Rio slurped the soup and let out a satisfied moan.

    The sound shot tingles up Agatha’s spine, making her face blush. “Do you like it?” She tapped at her mug nervously. “Is it good?

    Rio sighed with her eyes shut as she enjoyed the meal. “Good!?” She opened her eyes. “It’s amazing!” She took a few more spoonfuls and groaned. “Fuck!” Her eyes widened and she covered her mouth. “Oh shit sorry!”

    Agatha made a face at her, like she was serious, before moving on. “It’s that good!?” She tried some for herself. She enjoyed this soup but it wasn’t necessarily something that brought her immense joy like it seemed to be for Rio. Then again she has had this her whole life. Even if this is her own version of her mom’s recipe.

    “Yes! And I’m not just saying it!” She took her bread and dipped into her bowl. “Aggie did you make this yourself!?”

    Hearing the nickname again did something to hear. She can’t believe she just let it slip so casually the last time Rio said it. But now here she was enjoying her cooking and being adorable as ever and… ugh!!! “I… yes. Is it okay?”

    Rio nodded. Closing her eyes again.

    Agatha sighed. She laid her chin in her hand and watched the woman chow down. It brought her comfort to know that Rio was enjoying something she provided for her. Especially after her almost getting into a car wreck, just to get to their date on time.

    After dinner the two decided to retire to the couch and watch a movie. They sat side by side. A blanket strewn across them.

    Agatha let Rio pick.

    It was an action adventure film, she could get into it. But the romantic subplot was stirring things up inside her. She always found these types of things to be cliche. But now that she had Rio sitting next to her she wondered if she felt the same. Or if she ever fantasized about being the hero or the maiden in distress.

    Agatha slowly turned her head in Rios direction. Her heart jumped when she met her eyes directly. She was looking directly at her. Rio gave her a small smile before turning back toward the screen. Agatha smiled back. She slid a bit closer to her. Moving slowly into her space. Rio had her arm laid across the back of the couch. It was a clear opening for Agatha to lean in and snuggle.

    So that’s what she did.

    She could hear the slight gasp in Rio’s chest before she relaxed. The arm on the couch came down and around her.

    She closed her eyes and relaxed her breathing. Just enjoying the moment.

    By the time her eyes fluttered back open the room was dark, only faintly lit by the moon. The light outside now done. The sky was now shrouded in stars. The storm had subsided, the sky was now clear. She found herself lying on her front.

    The last thing she remembered was hanging out with…

    She felt around. She wasn’t lying completely flat. And there was movement. A slight but steady movement. She sat up.

    Her face went flushed as she realized that she had fallen asleep on Rio. Who was currently cradling her in her arms against her chest. She must have felt to awkward to wake her up!

    And… shit! What time was it!?

    She reached down into her pocket to pull out her phone.

    2:00 a.m.

    She sighed.

    She had work in the morning and Nicky would be back home by 7:00 to say bye before going to school.

    But Rio was so warm and soft. And… she sighed again.

    Screw it!

    She shook Rio awake. “Hey. Rio wake up. You fell asleep.” Her gentle breathing shuttered for a moment before her eyes fluttered open. “Huh? Oh, crap! Sorry!” She sat up. “Oh I should go!”

    She went to get up but Agatha stopped her. “Hey wait! No! Not why I was waking you up.”

    Rio squinted at her.

    “Come to bed with me?”

    Rios eye widened. “Oh?”

    “To sleep.” Agatha clarified.

    Rio nodded. “Oh. Okay.”

    “I have a guest room you could stay in. I just don’t want you to sleep on this uncomfortable couch!”

    Rio shrugged. “I didn’t mind it. You were warm. It was nice. Missed a good movie though.”

    Agatha rolled her eyes with a smile before getting up. “Follow me I’ll lead you to the guest room.”

    Rio nodded and followed her upstairs. She wanted to keep cuddling her. But she was worried maybe they were rushing into things too fast. “I can hear you thinking back there.” Agatha pulled her from her thoughts. “It’s nothing… just happy I got to spend the day with you.” Agatha stopped and turned to smile. She leaned in and hugged her. “Me too!” She sighed.

    Rio pulled her close. “I… could get used to this. It’s so nice. To have someone to hold. Is it weird for me to say I feel like I’ve known you for a long time?”

    Agatha pulled back. She smiled and shook her head. “No. I feel the same way.” She glanced away for a moment. “You know… you could… stay with me tonight.” She glanced back.

    “Just to sleep?”

    Agatha nodded.

    “I’d like that.”

    Agatha practically bounced excitedly on the spot. She took Rio’s hand and continued pulling her down the hall to her room.

    She opened the door and walked in first. Allowing Rio the chance to opt out if she wanted to.

    The woman looked around for a moment before stopping at the end of the bed. She watched the other woman with curiosity as she laid down. “Rio, get over her!” She held out her arms.

    Rio chuckled. “Coming!” She climbed into bed.

    Agatha’s eyes watched her every move. She let out another contempt sigh when Rio finally laid into her arms. She ran her fingers through her hair and left a kiss on her head. “Goodnight Rio.”

    “Goodnight Agatha.”

    Chapter 3: Just the three of us!

    Chapter Summary Rio and Nicky hang out and Agatha falls deeper.

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Nicky stirred awake to the muffled sound of cartoons blaring from the living room. The smell of toast and scrambled eggs wafted in from the kitchen, and for a moment, he forgot he wasn’t at home.

    He glanced up and saw the flash themed curtains, and teal colored walls. That’s right he spent the night at his neighbors house again. He sat up, yawning and wiping the sleep from his eyes. He looked around then peered down at the bottom bunk, but to his surprise Tommy wasn’t there.

    He fully registered the sound of cartoons and processed that the boy must have awoken before him.

    Which was actually odd.

    He climbed down off the bunk and made his way into the living room. And there was the young boy with bright blonde hair.

    “Morning Tommy! Where’s Billy?”

    The little boy looked up at his friend and smiled. “Sleeping. Mommy’s making breakfast if you’re hungry!”

    Nicky nodded and headed toward the kitchen. “Morning Wanda! Smells good!”

    The red haired woman smiled at him. “Good morning sweetie! I hope you’re hungry! Why don’t you sit down and eat before you head back?” Nicky nodded with a smile.

    “Last one to my house is doing the others homework!” Nicky giggled as he ran out of Wandas house towards his own.

    Billy cackled as he ran after him.

    “Boys! No running! Ugh!” Wanda threw her hands up in the air before going back inside to tend to Tommy.

    “Hey Nicky wait up you little shit!”

    Nicky squealed as Billy gained on him, he stopped at the front door for a moment to see how close he was. He was still a bit aways back. He giggled then pushed his way inside. “I win!” He threw his arms up in the air. “Mommy! I’m home!” He shouted.

    He looked around for his mother but didn’t see her. Usually she was up by now.

    “Jeez I swear sometimes you’re faster than Tommy!” Billy caught his breath as he entered the house, shutting the door behind him. “I think momma is upstairs. I’m gonna go give her kisses then grab the homework I left!” He ran up stairs.

    Billy followed. “Maybe you should knock before—“ “Momma! I’m home!” Without thinking Nicky pushed the bedroom door open and ran inside. He stopped though when he realized his mom wasn’t alone.

    Agatha sat up quickly. Looking like a deer in the head lights. Nicky’s face fell. “Hey!”

    “Shit Nicky!” Billy came up behind him.

    Now Rio was awake and she too sat up. She looked at the two boys confused.

    Billy took in the scene before smirking. “Woah. Did you two do it last night?”

    Both women blushed. Agatha looked over at Rio. Feeling mortified when she saw the woman’s embarrassed expression.

    “Do what?” Nicky turned to look at Billy.

    The teen was delighted to answer. “Oh doing it means—“ “Nothing! It means nothing! Billy!” Agatha snapped at the teen and gave him a warning look.

    Nicky turned back toward his mom and stomped his foot, pouting. “This is ridiculous! You never let me have sleepovers here! Why do you get too!?” He gestured at Rio!

    Agatha’s face softened at her son’s innocence and she chuckled. “Well when you pay the bills you get to make the rules.”

    Billy coughed awkwardly. “Okay I’m gonna go! I still need to get ready for school!” He turned and walked out.

    Nicky shut the door behind him then looked back at the two women. He took Rio in and smiled at her. “You’re really pretty! Momma never lets me have any friends sleep over. You must be really special.” Agatha chuckled. “I think she is! Nicky honey this is Rio!” She gestured to the other woman.

    Rio smiled and waved. “Nice to meet you Nicky! Your mom’s told me so much about you! She said you like music. I play the drums!” Nicky’s face lit up. He crawled onto the bed, excited to know more. “That’s so cool! I always wanted to play the drums!”

    Agatha chuckled. “And guitar! And piano! And the ukulele!”

    Nicky nodded. “I wanna go to college for art and music!” “Wow thinking that far ahead already? That’s good! You focus on your goals and dreams and anything is possible!”

    Nicky smiled and turned to his mom. “Momma can I show Rio my drawings?”

    Agatha smiled. “Not right now baby. Maybe some other time. I need to get ready for work and you need to get ready for school! And I’m sure Rio is busy.”

    “Aw!” He turned toward Rio. “Wanna come over later after I get off school? We can play games and I can show you my art?”

    Agatha answered before Rio could. “Nicky Rio probably has a lot to do today.”

    “Nah I don’t have much going on. I’m off today. I don’t mind coming over later! Sounds fun! Is that okay with you Agatha?” She looked over at the woman.

    Agatha was shocked. She wasn’t expecting Rio to want to hang out with her son so soon. Especially since meeting like this. “Oh! Uh…” she glanced at Rio then over at her son who was giving her that look! Those damn puppy dog eyes! She sighed. “Yes it’s alright. But I expect your homework to be done before!” She shook her finger at him.

    Nicky cheered. “Yay! A new friend!” He crawled over to his mother and hugged her. “Thank you Momma! I’m so excited!” He pulled away. “Okay! I’m gonna go get ready for school! Bye Momma bye Ms Rio!” He skipped out of the room happily, shutting the door behind him.

    Agatha sighed. “You don’t have to come over later if you don’t want to. I understand.”

    Rio quirked her brow. “Oh but why? He seems like fun! I meant it! I really don’t have any plans today! Plus! I’d get to see you again!” She beamed. “If that’s alright with you of course!” She looked at Agatha a bit nervously. “I’m not… coming on too strong or anything am I?”

    Agatha chuckled. “No, sweetie. You’re fine.” She moved over and hugged Rio. “It actually sounds really nice.”

    Lilia sighed.

    She recognized the number that was currently calling.

    Nicky’s school….

    After speaking with them she called Agatha.

    “Yes Lilia?”

    “Your son needs picked up early from school. There was a power outage on that block. And the other buses are busy with other districts.” “What!?” She groaned. “I have a very important meeting in twenty five minutes! How am I going to pick him up? Have you called Wanda?”

    “Yes. She already picked up Tommy. She mentioned she’s very busy today and Nicky’s class hadn’t gotten out yet and she just didn’t have time to wait for him. She sends her apologies.”

    Agatha cursed under her breath. “Shit! Can you pick him up by chance?” “No I’m sorry. I have a doctor’s appointment in twenty minutes and it’s on the other side of town! I told you about this a month ago. Remember?” Agatha groaned. “Yeah! Okay… give me five minutes to figure something out. I’ll message you when I do.”

    “Okay.”

    Agatha hung up. She massaged her temples and sat back. She dialed Mrs Davis’ number. Waiting for it to answer. But when it went to voicemail for the third time she groaned.

    She scrolled through her contacts. Trying, hoping to find someone. One name stuck out in particular.

    She clicked on it.

    A few rings later the person on the other end answered.

    “Agatha! Hey what’s up!?”

    “I’m…” she sighed. “I need to ask you a favor. I’m sorry.” “Hey don’t apologize what do you need?”

    “My son’s school is letting out early. And I have no one to pick him up. I’d go but I have a very important meeting for my company in the half hour. And I mean really Important. I’ve been dreading this for months!” “Don’t worry! I got your back! I’ll pick him up! What’s the address of the school?”

    “I’ll text it to you! Thank you Rio! I owe you so much!”

    Rio looked around as she pulled up to the school. She didn’t see the boy outside with the other kids, so she parked and got out.

    Assuming he was inside, she headed toward the classroom Agatha mentioned and peaked in.

    She saw a few kids in the back playing a board game.

    A woman noticed her and smiled. She came to the door and greeted her. “Hello! Are you here to pick up Nicky!?” She smiled.

    Rio was confused. “H-how did you know?”

    She quirked a brow. “I don’t mean to assume. It’s just… You’re practically his twin. You must be his aunt?”

    Rio shook her head. “No um. I’m a friend of his mother’s. Agatha Harkness. Oh here.” She pulled out her phone and called Agatha, switching it to video. The woman picked up after the second ring.

    “Ms Sinclair! Hello! I apologize I was unable to pick up Nicky! This is a good friend of mine! Rio! She’s getting him for me!”

    The teacher nodded. “Alright! Thank you for letting me know Ms Harkness. And might I say your friend is the spitting image of your son! What a coincidence! Are you sure she’s not related to him!?” She chuckled. Agatha was taken aback by this but only chuckled in return. “It was nice talking to you Ms Sinclair. Hey Rio?”

    Rio smiled at the woman who retreated into the classroom to get Nicky. Before turning the phone back to herself. “Hey Aggie.”

    “I really am grateful for this! I’ll make it up to you!” Rio smiled. “Yeah? And how are you gonna do that Harkness?” She twirled some of her hair between her fingers.

    Agatha blushed. “Well… I could start by taking you out somewhere nice! And then a movie! Also, we could redo the escape room date! But this time bring Nicky with us! He’ll love it!”

    Rio beamed with excitement. “That sounds lovely! But can I pick the restruant this time?” She grinned.

    Agatha swooned. “Yes of course! Whatever and wherever you want my dear! I gotta go! But I’ll come down and see you two as soon as I’m done. There’s a cafeteria in the basement. If you come up to the top floor and talk to Lilia she’ll give you a card with my name on it and you guys can get whatever you want. Sound good!?”

    Rio smiled. “That won’t cost you anything will it?”

    Agatha grinned. “Baby, I own that building. You can have as much as you want. Okay? I can’t wait to see you both! Have fun together okay!” She winked.

    Now it was Rio’s turn to blush. “Okay Agatha. Thank you. You’re so sweet! Good luck at your meeting.” She blew her a kiss before hanging up.

    “Ms Rio! Hello! You’re picking me up today!?” Nicky said excitedly. His teacher waited for a moment behind him and handed Rio some papers. “These are some forms I need Ms Harkness to fill out.” She looked down at Nicky. “You almost forgot them honey. Remember I told you they’re important?”

    Nicky looked up at her. “I’m sorry! I even wrote a reminder on my hand! I don’t know how I forgot!” He showed her his hand.

    The teacher snickered. “It’s okay! Alright go on! Make sure you get your homework done though.”

    Nicky nodded. “I will! Momma will make sure of it! Bye Ms Sinclair! Have a good Monday!” He waved as they walked off.

    Rio smiled over at him as they made it to her friend’s truck. “Wow this is a really big truck! Where are we going Ms Rio?” Rio chuckled while buckling her seatbelt. “You can just call me Rio you know? You don’t have be so formal.”

    “Oh, alright!”

    “And we’re going to your mom’s work.”

    They drove in silence for a bit before Nicky decided breaking it. “Rio? Are you and my mom dating?”

    The woman’s heart skipped a beat at the question. “Oh? What makes you ask that?” She looked over at him for a moment before looking back at the road.

    He shrugged. “Mommas been really happy lately. She’s different, in a good way. Almost like she’s… complete.” He smiled at her. “I cab see it. Especially this morning, when she was with you. You make her happy. You must be really special to her. Momma has never gotten close to anyone other than me. She’s friendly with Ms Wanda and Ms Davis. But it’s different with you.”

    Rio smiled. “You’re a bright kid Nicky. And to answer your question. I…” she sighed. “I think you should ask your mother. That’s all I can say. Okay?”

    Nicky nodded.

    “But just know that I really care about her and we have a lot of fun together. And now me and you are gonna have some fun and hang out! You hungry? Your mom said we could have some food in the cafeteria.” Nicky bounced with joy. “Yay! I love the pizza there! I never get to see Mommas work much anymore. I used to go there all the time when I was little. But now that I’m bigger and Billy’s old enough, she just has him watch me instead of having me sit at the office with Ms Lilia. She was fun though to. She’d say the strangest things sometimes. Momma says her memories a little fuzzy from getting older. That saddens me. I really like Ms Lilia. She’s a really nice lady and really cool!”

    Rio chuckled.

    A few minutes later they pulled into the parking lot. Rio put the truck into park and turned to the boy. “You know, I brought something for us to do while we’re in the cafeteria.”

    Nicky lit up. “What is it?”

    Rio grabbed her backpack from the back seat and pulled out a case. “Well I brought my switch! We can play some games together! And I brought a sketchbook and some art supplies, so you can draw!”

    “Oh this’ll be so fun!”

    “I also brought my own sketchbook. If you’re interested in seeing my drawings, that is?”

    Nicky nodded. “Um yeah! You didn’t tell me you liked drawing too!” Rio chuckled. “I got a bit nerdy with art in high school and took some classes in college for fun. I mostly draw flowers and animals though.” She shrugged.

    She handed the boy her sketchbook before slinging her bag over her shoulder. “You can look at these while we walk inside. We’re going to speak to Lilia first. She’s going to give us a card so we can get whatever from the cafeteria.”

    Nicky nodded.

    Rio walked up to the front desk. The woman immediately recognized Nicky and smiled at them both. “You must be Ms Vidal. My name is Jen. Lilia mentioned you’d be on your way.” She gestured toward the elevator. “Take the elevator up to the fifth floor. Lilia will be right outside. Have a nice day.”

    Rio gave her a nod. “Thank you Jen! You too!”

    The pair went into the elevator. Nicky excitedly hit the button to go to the floor.

    They stood there in silence as he flipped through her sketchbook.

    Not less than a few moments later the elevator dinged and the door opened. An older woman looked up and smiled.

    “Oh hey! Lilia! I remember you from karaoke night! You were amazing!” Rio approached her. “I feel like we met before that though. Do you know where?”

    Lilia pondered for a moment. “It’s possible. Considering we’re both friends with Alice, but I’m not sure honestly. Plus my memory can be a bit fickle at times.”

    “But you also have the best instincts Lilia!” Nicky smiled at the woman. “It’s like you see the future! You even predicted I’d win the science fair last year! And! That Ms Wanda would have another baby!”

    Lilia chuckled. “Call it intuition. How are you Nicky? You’re looking as handsome as ever! I see you’re still growing out your hair?” Nicky nodded. “Don’t I look pretty? I love my long hair!” Lilia smiled and nodded. Though, something felt off for a moment. She squinted as she looked at the boy and then something hit her. She looked up at Rio and studied her face for a moment. Then back down at the boy. “Holy shit.” She muttered under her breath.

    Rio quirked a brow and tilted her head. “Are you alright Lilia?” “Oh! Yes! Sorry! Had a moment there! Getting older sucks! Never do it!” She winked at both of them. “Here’s the meal card.”

    Before Rio could say thank you, the doors behind Lilia opened and a woman came barreling out.

    “My darling boy! Oh! I have a minute! Let me see you!”

    “Momma!”

    Agatha crouched down and pulled her son into her arms. “Mommy’s sorry I couldn’t get you!”

    “It’s okay Momma! Ms— I mean Rio picked me up! We’re gonna have so much fun together. And look!” He held up her sketchbook. “She draws such pretty flowers! Isn’t that nice Momma!?”

    Agatha glanced over at the book. She took it into her hands and smiled. Then looked up at Rio. “They’re beautiful Rio. You never mentioned you could draw!”

    Rio shrugged. “I didn’t think it was worth mentioning.”

    Agatha scoffed then stood up. She pulled the woman in for a hug. “It’s a talent. And it’s obviously a part of you. I’d like to get to know as much as you’re willing to share.”

    Rio sighed and pulled the woman closer. “I’d like that.”

    They hugged a bit longer than appropriate for just two ‘friends’ especially at Agatha’s work.

    Nicky chuckled under his breath and gave Lilia a look.

    The older woman winked at him then went back to what she was doing before the pair entered.

    “Alright! You two enjoy the food! Have a good time!” She placed her hand on her son’s shoulder. “I’ll be an hour. Maybe a bit longer.” She looked back at Rio. “If something happens and it ends up being longer than planned I’ll have Lilia call you. And you can just take Nicky home for me?” Rio nodded. “Either way is fine with me. But I can totally run the little squirt home. Whatever you need.”

    “You’re awesome.”

    “I know!” Rio grinned.

    Agatha turned toward Nicky. “Alright honey Mommas gotta go work now. You be good for Rio okay?” She kissed him on the cheek before ruffling his hair. “I’ll see you in a little bit. Then we can three hang out.” “Okay Momma! Love you.”

    “Love you too buddy!”

    Nicky ran into the cafeteria. Giggling as the other woman ran after him. “You get back here!” Rio cackled.

    “Not a chance! I told you I’m super fast! My feet are like magic!” He beat her to the line and stopped to catch his breath. Rio shook her head at him with a grin. She wouldn’t tell him. But she totally let him win. She wasn’t even out of breath. “You getting pizza?” She nodded toward the food.

    He shook his head.

    “What? But I thought they had the best pizza here?”

    “They do! But they also have the best spaghetti! And it’s rare they have it! Looks like today is my lucky day!”

    Rio chuckled. “Well you get what you want. I’m gonna go find us a seat.” She handed him the card.

    “You’re not gonna eat?”

    “Maybe in a little bit. I had a snack before I came to pick you up. Besides, I’m in the mood to draw.”

    Nicky nodded. “Okay. Be there in a bit!”

    Rio smiled, then went and found them a seat in the corner. Her heart pounded in her chest as she pulled her sketchbook out and grabbed her bag of pencils.

    She couldn’t get the image out of her mind—it demanded to be put to paper. Biting her lip in concentration, she roughed out a sketch, her pencil darted across the page. Then, holding the book up at different angles, she studied it carefully, ensuring every line was symmetrical and perfectly proportional. She smiled and put the book back down. “So beautiful,” She breathed, “So sweet.”

    She got lost in the details. Especially when shading the eyes. She didn’t even hear it when the boy took his seat.

    “Is that my mom?”

    Rio jumped, then slammed the sketch book shut. “Huh!? Oh, no! Nope! Just… some flowers… yep! Some beautiful flowers.”

    Nicky shook his head, but smiled. “Yeah, beautiful… flowers.” He winked at her. “Sure. That’s what we’ll call it.”

    Shit! She’d been caught!

    She laughed awkwardly. “Yeah. So…. How was school today?” She gave a desperate attempt at changing the topic.

    Nicky didn’t seem to mind all that much. He shrugged. “Okay I guess. We were supposed to have a presentation today on a school project. I’m honestly glad the power went out. I was really nervous. I don’t like speaking in front of crowds.”

    “I get that. I was the same way at your age.”

    Nicky sat up. “Really? But you’re so… cool!”

    Rio chuckled. “I know. But I didn’t always use to be. Sometimes it takes a while to get to that point. To really grow into yourself I mean. Think of it this way. Your mom is doing a presentation right now. And it’s not for a grade. But to push her company forward. That’s gotta be really scary huh?” “Yeah. But Mommas always been tough! She has scars on her skin. She won’t tell me how she got em. But… I know it couldn’t have been good. And I know she sacrificed so much for me. I know she had dreams. But she had to give them up to make sure we had a place to live and food to eat. And… she’s different around grandma. She doesn’t let me see her much. I’m not so sure why. Basically, Momma’s always had courage. That’s why I don’t understand why I never had it. I must get it from my dad.” He sighed. Rio wasn’t sure what to say to any of that. And she definitely didn’t like the idea of Agatha having scars. She didn’t want to dwell on it though. It wasn’t her business. Agatha deserved the respect and privacy of that. If she didn’t want Rio to know then that that was totally fine. “Like I said it can take time.”

    Nicky nodded and slid her a bottle of water. “Here I got you this.” He took a bite of his pasta. “What games do you have for your switch?” The woman lit up at the topic of games. She pulled her case out of her bag. “I got a decent amount. I haven’t played in a while.” A partial lie. She played with Agatha last night. But she wasn’t counting that. “Being an adult doesn’t leave a lot of time for hobbies like this. I’m lucky I get to meet up with my band as much as I do.” She sighed.

    “Being an adult sucks.”

    Rio snickered. “It sure does! But the bright side is no more school! Downside is, work! But it doesn’t have to be bad. If you love the job you do you never work a day in your life! And honestly I enjoy my job. But that’s a topic for another time. Here.” She slid a game case over to the boy and opened it.

    “Woah! You have so many!”

    “It’s just six games.” She chuckled.

    “Yeah but I only have three!”

    Rio rolled her eyes. He probably only had three because he never plays anymore. “I have Mario kart, Mario 3D World, Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, Link’s Awakening and Cult of the Lamb.”

    “I haven’t played Cult of the Lamb before. It looks cute!” “It is! It’s my favorite game. I want to get more I just haven’t decided which ones. Only time I can really play is on my lunch breaks and occasionally after dinner at home. I have to catch up on chores. The rest of my free time goes to band practice.”

    “I wanna play an instrument. Can you teach me how to play drums? I really wanna learn. But Momma wants me to wait till I go to junior high to get me started on an instrument. She says I’m too indecisive and doesn’t want me to just give it up. She’s kinda right. I’m still deciding between band and orchestra. I really like the violin and piano. But I also really wanna play the drums. I’d also love to learn guitar, but they don’t offer it.” Rio nodded. “Yeah totally! Sounds like fun! I could even teach you guitar too! I have an acoustic guitar at my place! I could bring it over some time?” Nicky jumped in his seat. “Wow! You’re so cool! What other talents do you have!? You’re an artist and musician!”

    “Guitars more of a hobby. Drums are my passion. I guess… I enjoy knife throwing. But I don’t think your mom would like me teaching you that.” Nicky shrugged. “It sounds okay. If I had to choose I’d prefer archery I think!”

    Rio nodded. “Yeah that’s really fun! We did that in highschool! For gym class. I beat the whole class!”

    “Wow! Really! That’s so cool!”

    Rio chuckled and popped Mario kart in. “Oh I almost forgot. I love basketball. Do you like sports?”

    Nicky put a finger on his chin while he thought. “Kind of. I like to play them. I don’t like watching them though. I don’t really like football. But I like to play basket ball and baseball. And I’m not good at soccer. I’m not on any teams though. We played ping pong a few times in gym. That’s also really fun! But I have to be pretty careful playing sports because I get hurt easily.”

    “Ping pong is pretty sick! We could play that some time! It’s a safe game. Okay! Which character are you picking?”

    “Yoshi!”

    Rio groaned. “We’re gonna need to do rock paper scissors to decide who’s playing as him!”

    Agatha hurried out of her office. The meeting went a tad bit longer than she had expefted But not long enough to have Rio take Nicky home.

    She decided to take a half day for work. Wanting to spend some time with her son.

    She hurried down the stairs. The elevator wouldn’t be fast enough.

    Her heart was hammering in her chest. She also really wanted to see her again.

    She stopped in the entryway, her eyes widened as the scene unfolded before her.

    Nicky doubled over with laughter, squirming under Rio’s relentless tickling, as they played their game.

    She stayed there for a bit. Enjoying the moment.

    She’s never seen him so happy with another person who wasn’t herself. These two people they just clicked.

    Something about it… they…

    Agatha looked between them.

    Why was she feeling this way?

    Rio was so familiar. What was it!?

    She approached them and smiled.

    “Looks like you two are having fun!”

    “Momma!” Nicky jumped out of his chair and into his mother’s arms. “How was the meeting?” Rio asked.

    “Great actually. I got nervous for nothing. Most of those men cower when they see me anyway. I don’t know why I got worked up over it.” She chuckled.

    Rio looked up at her in awe. “You, Agatha Harkness are a force of nature. I never had a doubt.” She winked.

    Agatha blushed. “Thank you. You guys ready to head out?”

    “Yeah!” Nicky jumped with excitement, then headed for the door.

    That night went amazingly for Rio.

    They all had so much fun together. They even set up a day that Saturday to go to the escape room!

    But of course afterwards it’d just be the two of them.

    And now that’s where Rio found herself. Tapping her fingers away nervously. As they dropped the boy off; after an exciting day off fun together, at Wanda’s for the night.

    That was another thing too.

    Agatha would be spending the night at her place.

    Her roomie so graciously encouraged the sleepover. She even made herself scarce by staying at Alice’s for the night.

    “You sure it’s fine we’re seeing a horror film? We can see something else if you’d like.” Rio insisted.

    Agatha shook her head. “Nonsense! It’s just a movie how bad can it be?”

    How bad can it be?

    It was only dubbed the most frightening movie of the last decade.

    And now Rio wasn’t sure what she should do in this moment. She glanced over to see Agatha clamping her hands on to the armrests of the theater chair. Hyper focused on the film and shaking like a leaf. Rio reached out, but before she could touch her there was a jump scare. It did its job in making Agatha jump and scream.

    The younger woman clung on to Rio for dear life. Pushing her face in the crook of her neck, panting.

    Rio held her close. Placing a protective hand on her back. She could feel her heart pounding through her ribcage . She leaned towards her ear and spoke, “Why don’t we head out early? Hm? This movies lame anyways.” Agatha pulled back just enough to look her in the eyes. “What? No! You said you’ve been looking forward to this movie for a year!” Rio shrugged but smiled down at her. She pushed some of her hair out of her face. “I’m more interested in you right now. Come on. It’s getting late. I bet you’re tired. We can cuddle?”

    Agatha’s eyes widened slightly. She relaxed then smiled. She stood up and pulled Rio with her. Heading out of the theater.

    They ran out into the lobby giggling like teenagers. Hand in hand they made it outside. Both shocked from the sudden downfall of rain. “Shit! This weather!” Rio squealed.

    Agatha chuckled.

    They ran to Agatha’s car and quickly got in, catching their breaths. Agatha wrapped her arms around herself, shivering. Rio took notice and pulled out the jacket she had stuffed away in her bag and draped in across her shoulders then rubbed the side of her arms, trying to get her warmed up. All Agatha could think was how perfect Rio had been. Her eyes slid down to her lips for a moment then back up to her beautiful dark eyes. Rio smiled at the younger woman. “More unexpected rain! It’s super cold! Are you— mpfh!”

    Agatha kissed her.

    She couldn’t take it anymore. All of this affection and bliss! All for this woman! All this attraction and… dare she say lust! She caressed her face and held her close.

    The older woman’s eyes widened for a moment before relaxing. She slid her hands up to her hips and pulled her even closer.

    They stayed like that for a while, wrapped in each other’s embrace, sharing tender kisses.

    Eventually, they parted, both letting out a soft sigh.

    Rio smiled at her. “Wow!” She reached up and touched her own lips. “You’re an amazing kisser!”

    Agatha chuckled. “I should be the one saying that about you!” She glanced down at her lips for a second before looking back up at her eyes. Rio grinned. “You wanna… do it again?”

    Agatha snickered, she nodded but pulled away. “While I’d love to. I’m not sure I want to get stuck in the movie theater parking lot during a storm because…” she smirked at Rio. “We can’t keep our hands off each other.” Then put the key in the ignition.

    Rio nodded. “You’re absolutely right! Let’s get back to my place then! We can snuggle up and watch something a little less… intense?” She offered. Agatha nodded. “Yeah, I’d like that.”

    It became a habit. They’d have their date nights. Agatha would steal a kiss or two and then they’d have a family date night where Nicky would tag along.

    They’d text back and forth all the time. Neither able to get the other off their mind.

    And after one of their many dates their passion overtook them. The pair stumbled against each other as they kissed. Rio attempted fishing her keys out of her pocket to unlock the door. She chuckled as Agatha continued showering her in kisses.

    “Babe I gotta open the door!”

    Agatha whined. She moved away from her mouth and started sucking on her pulse point against the crook of her neck.

    She managed to pull a moan out of Rio and made her legs shook. “Shit! No fair! You’re driving me crazy! Aggie! Ughh!”

    Agatha slid her hands down Rios front. One hand move to rest against her hip while the other took the keys from her hand and slid it into the lock mechanism.

    She pressed her lips back to Rio’s and pushed her inside the apartment. Kicking the door shut she walked her back until she tumbled onto the couch, then climbed on top of her.

    “You don’t know how long I’ve dreamt of doing this!” Agatha sighed. “You’ve dreamt of me?” Rio joked.

    Agatha chuckled. She rolled her hips on top of her, making the woman gasp. “So many times!”

    “Aggie!” Rio whined. “I-I wait… honey!” She pushed the woman back. She didn’t want her to feel the hardening bulge in her pants. She could only keep it under control for so long. The kissing was getting too heated and intense.

    Agatha’s face fell and she sat back. “Did I do something wrong!? I’m sorry I—“ Rio shook her head. “No! No, baby! You’re perfect… I…” she sighed. What should she do? Should she tell her the truth? Ask for more time? She didn’t want Agatha to doubt her attraction for her or anything. “I just… I really like you. I want to take things slow.” “Oh.” Agatha slid off her.

    “I-Is that okay?” Rio asked in a panic.

    Agatha relaxed and softened. She reached for Rio and caressed her face. “Of course it’s more than okay! You have your boundaries. We don’t have to do anything tonight. We don’t have to do anything you don’t want to at all. I just… I like you. Okay Rio?” She rubbed her thumb against her cheek. “I just want this.”

    Rio smiled and leaned into her touch. “What is this? If I may ask?” Agatha hummed. “What do you want it to be?”

    “Hm… what do I want this to be…” she dragged out the sentence as if she were thinking. “Oh yeah!” She pushed Agatha down and kissed her. “I know what I want!”

    In a small voice Agatha asked, “Yeah?”

    “Be my girlfriend? Be my girl?”

    Agatha grabbed her hand and kissed it. “I already am your girl. Of course I’ll be your girlfriend. As long as you’ll be mine.”

    Rio nodded. “Absolutely!” She leaned down and kissed her again. “My girlfriend! I could get used to that.”

    Agatha hummed and pulled her down. “You better get use to it.” Then kissed her again. “You’re my girl too!”

    “Always!”

    Chapter End Notes I hope this one is okay. I had a small bit of writers block writing this one. But I really wanna finish it. I’ll be updating My Scars soon as well.

    Chapter 4: My heart is yours!

    Chapter Summary Basketball and fireworks.

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Rio dribbled the basketball in slow, measured steps, her sneakers scuffing the asphalt as Nicky darted in front of her, arms wide and grin even wider. The late afternoon sun cast long shadows over the driveway and the air hummed with the sound of cicadas and Nicky’s laughter. “Come on, Rio! Is that all you got?” he teased, his enthusiasm a mix of challenge and delight. Rio smirked, letting the ball roll between her fingers before launching into a feigned shot, only to pivot and glide past him, shooting the ball into the hoop.

    “Aw man that was sick!”

    She tossed him the ball, and he dribbled it a few times before lining up his shot.

    Lucky for him, he got the edge on Rio. Her eyes followed the ball’s arc as it swished through the hoop and thudded against the ground. “Not bad, kid,” she said, her voice light, but her heart warmer than she’d admit. She wiped the sweat from her forehead with her shirt. Then smirked when she sensed eyes on her.
