    “Nicky why don’t you come in and wash up. I made dinner.” Agatha called out to the boy, her eyes still currently trained on the sweaty and panting woman, in her front yard. She gazed through her eyelashes as she took in her well fit frame.

    She was a vision.

    Strong legs shown off in basketball shorts, those delicious arms exposed by her tank top. Her abs briefly visible as she lifted her shirt to wipe the sweat from her neck.

    Her face, beautifully flushed, with strands of hair stuck to her forehead. The way her mouth hung slightly open as she took in the cool evening air. And those dark eyes, meeting hers.

    Agatha’s own blue widened at being caught. She turned, now facing her boy who was in a similar shape to the older woman.

    He ran up to her with a bright smile as he caught his breath. “Mom! Rio is so freakin good at basketball! You should have seen her!” Agatha smiled with a chuckle. She chanced a glance in the woman’s direction. “I saw a bit.”

    Rio winked at her. Prompting the younger woman to look away and back down at her son. Her cheeks took on a shade of crimson while her heart pounded in her chest.

    “I made Salisbury steaks and mash potatoes!”

    “Sounds good! I’m gonna go take a shower! I’ll be down in a bit!” She watched him run inside and shook her head with a smile. Not expecting Rio to be inches away from her by the time she turned back, she jumped. “Shit! Rio! Do I need to put a bell on you!?”

    The older woman didn’t respond, only continued to gaze at the woman.

    Agatha’s blush deepened. “Y-you were pretty good back there! He looks up to you, you know.”

    Rio moved in closer and smiled. “You look so beautiful today!” Agatha snickered. “You said that earlier, remember?”

    Rio grabbed her hips and pulled her in. “Maybe it needs to be said again.” “You’re sweaty.” She stated.

    Rio gave her a look. “I’ll go inside and wash up then!”

    Agatha grabbed her arm before she could move away completely, and pulled her back in. “Don’t you dare!” Her eyes flickered down to her lips then back up to her eyes.

    “Oh?” Rio licked her lips.

    Agatha sucked in a shaky breath. Her hands slid up her body. She desperately wanted to feel her muscles. Her eyes scanned downward towards her abs. She pressed her hand against the thin material of the tank top and groaned. “God, Rio!” She slid a hand under her shirt. And oh! Touching her muscles directly like this was heaven!

    Rio leaned forward and littered kisses up her cheek. “Like what you see?” She whispered into her ear.

    Agatha nodded vigorously. “I do!” She breathed. “I really do!”

    Rio giggled then went in to kiss her.

    “Momma!” Nicky yelled from inside the house.

    The two pulled apart quickly as they heard his rapidly approaching footsteps before the front door flew open.

    “We’re out of shampoo!”

    Agatha had to catch her breath for a moment. Worried she almost gotten caught. But Nicky didn’t seem to have noticed a thing.

    “Honey, did you check under the sink?”

    “Oh no, I forgot about that! Thank you Momma!” The boy blushed before running back inside.

    Leaving the two women alone again.

    Agatha smiled at Rio and took her hand. “Come on let’s get you in the shower and then we can all eat.”

    Rio chuckled and wiggled her eyebrows at her making Agatha blush more. “Of course I meant alone. I’ll be busy setting the table.”

    Rio nodded.

    To be honest Rio wanted to.

    Really wanted to. But she just couldn’t.

    Not yet.

    Plus she still wanted to take it slow. She wanted it to be special. She just hoped they’d get that far and she wouldn’t wuss out. She knew Agatha would wait forever, but she didn’t want her to have to. She even said they never had to do anything if she didn’t want to. And that was definitely far from the truth.

    Rio wanted her so bad.

    Wanted to show her how much she cared.

    Feel her touch and affection.

    She leaned against the shower wall and let the water hit her back. It felt nice.

    She closed her eyes and allowed her muscles to relax, letting out a long sigh in the process.

    “Rio! I’m leaving spare clothes out for you! They’re on my bed!” Agatha’s muffled voice could be heard through the door.

    “Okay!” Rio shouted back.

    She allowed her mind to wander.

    How would Agatha react if and when she told her?

    Would she be mad?

    Disgusted?

    Indifferent?

    Rio wasn’t sure.

    But the thought terrified her more than anything.

    She really, really liked Agatha, and cared deeply for Nicky and they both had taken up residence in her heart. Rio wasn’t sure she could handle losing it all.

    Silent tears fell down her cheek, a drop landed on the shower floor. “Oh Agatha… I think I’ve fallen in love with you!” She clutched her chest as she whispered to herself. “And Im so afraid! Because I love you and Nicky so much!”

    Agatha hummed a tune as she swayed side to side, while plating her and Rio’s food.

    Nicky had already sat down for dinner and was currently digging in. “Momma this is so good!” Nicky shoveled a bunch a potatoes in his mouth and continued speaking. “You’re always so good at cooking!” Agatha turned and glared. “Nicky! What have I told you about speaking with your mouth full?”

    The boys eyes widened for a moment as he gulped his food down. “M’sorry! It’s a bad habit! I’ll try not to do it again!” Agatha shook her head with a smile. She just couldn’t stay mad at her boy. He was the sweetest kid she’d ever known. And she didn’t understand how she did so well by him, given how she grew up. “You’re lucky you’re cute!” “I know!”

    She stuck her tongue at him before going back to what she was doing. She wanted their plates to look pretty.

    A bright smile crept onto Agatha’s face as strong arms slid around her waist. She heard a small sigh, before a chin rested against her shoulder. “M’tired.” Rio yawned. “You smell good. Like cherry blossoms.” She nuzzled into her neck.

    “Awe Rio you’re such a nice friend to Momma.”

    Rio chuckled. “I know right?”

    The three sat at the table together, enjoying their meals. Random conversations would come up here and there.

    Mostly Nicky saying what popped into his mind at that very second. “So there’s this girl at recess and she won’t leave me alone!” Agatha’s head shot in his direction. “Oh? What does she do?” “She chases me around and tries tackling me! She also keeps calling me a cutiepie! I’m not cute!” He growled.

    Both women shared a look.

    Rio was smiling ear to ear.

    “Oh I see! I think I might know what your problem is!” Rio sat back in her chair as she took a sip of her water.

    “You do!?”

    She finished the glass and sat it down. “My sweet innocent boy, that girl likes you, silly.”

    Nicky’s eyes widened for a moment. “Oh…” He turned away from both women. The blush on his face was a dark shade of red.

    “Do you like her honey?” Agatha asked.

    Nicky shrugged. “Dunno. She’s… okay I guess.”

    Rio grinned. She glanced over at Agatha and gave her a look. Asking for permission, with her expression, to proceed with this.

    Agatha sighed but gave her a nod.

    “So if you wanted to Nicky you could ask her to be your girlfriend.” The boy looked up at Rio. “What!? I can’t do that!”

    Rio quirked a brow. “Why not?”

    “T-that’s embarrassing! The whole school will make fun of me when she tells me no!”

    “Why would she say no? You’re charming, smart, adorable! And given that you were raised by your mother, I know that you’re a gentleman! What’s not to like!? You’re the whole package!”

    He shrugged again.

    “Hey look at me buddy.”

    The boy slowly looked up at the woman.

    “Do this only if you’re comfortable, there’s no pressure by the way. I want you to write this girl a note, asking her if she likes you. Put yes or no a the bottom. Maybe draw her a picture or get her something. Like a chocolate bar. She’ll love it trust me.”

    The somber look on Nicky’s face shifted to something more akin to fondness. “Thanks Rio! You’re the best!” He got up and ran to her. Hugging her tightly.

    Rio pretended she couldn’t breathe.

    Promoting the boy to let out a couple giggles.

    His mother quickly snapped a picture. “That’s my new wallpaper.” She muttered.

    “Come on momma! We’re gonna be late! We need to get there in time to sit in the front row!” Nicky dragged his mother down the venue, by her hand. “I’m so excited!”

    Agatha smiled.

    They could hear music playing off in the distance. They wormed their way through crowds.

    “Honey we’re still early for the show. We’ll make it trust me!” Nicky shook his head. “Can’t risk it! Look it’s already packed! They’re gonna start soon.” He let go of her hand and bolted off. “Nicky!” She cursed under breath as she ran after him.

    He ran into the crowd practically disappearing from her sight. “Nicky!” She shouted, entering the tightly packed group. She moved quickly. Trying to not be rude and push anybody. But at the same time she was worried.

    “Agatha.” She felt someone grab her hand. “It’s okay. I got him.” She turned and was greeted by the beautiful sight of those obsidian eyes. “Rio!” She looked down and saw her son clinging to the older woman’s side.

    “Momma! Look Rio looks so cool!” He hugged her.

    Agatha let out a sigh of relief. “Baby you can’t run off like that! You scared me half to death!”

    “Sorry Momma! I just saw Rio and I got excited! It’s been a week since I saw her! I missed her!” He clung to her tighter.

    Rio chuckled as she held the boy close. “Shows about to start. Come on! I’ll walk you two to the front! After this we can go play some games or ride some rides! Sound good Nicky?”

    “Absolutely!”

    Rio smiled at Agatha and took her hand. Gently leading her towards the front of the crowd, who parted for her like the Red Sea. Agatha took note of this. “Why are they…?”

    “Fans! They know who am I!”

    “Huh.” Agatha hummed in acknowledgment.

    Rio ruffled Nicky’s hair and pinched his cheek. “You be good to your momma!”

    “I will!”

    “Oh hey what’s that over there!” Rio pointed off in the distance. “Where!?” Nicky’s head snapped in the direction of where she was pointing.

    Rio chuckled and quickly pecked Agatha on the lips. “Made ya look!” She pinched his cheek again before getting up on stage.

    “Ow! Stop that!”

    “Can’t! Not when you’re such a cutie!” Rio sang out as she skipped to her drum set.

    “Momma! Tell Rio to stop teasing me!” He took in her appearance. Her face was red. “Are you okay? You look weird.”

    “Huh.” She looked down at him. “Oh, I’m okay. Look they’re starting.” She pointed up at the stage. Rio had frazzled her was all.

    Rio started counting loudly while smacking her drum sticks together. Making a show of starting off the band. “1! 2! 3! 4!”

    They broke out into song.

    Alice sang lead vocals while playing piano. Jen; Agatha’s coworker and the newest member of the band, played bass and harmonized. Hela shredded on the guitar, adding backup vocals, while Rio drove the rhythm on drums. Agatha was pleasantly surprised when Rio started singing along with Alice. The older woman looked right at her as she began soloing the vocals of the most romantic line in the song they were covering.

    “This heart, it beats, beats for only you!

    This heart, it beats, beats for only you!This heart, it beats, beats for only you My heart is yours!”

    She continued leading the vocals, while the others joined in backup, while also impressively drumming fast, as the tempo sped up.

    Agatha felt like she was the only person there even though she was in a crowd full of people.

    Rio serenaded her and her alone. Giving it all of her emotions. All of her love written all over her face and dripping from her voice. Her devotion screamed as she continued playing seamlessly.

    Agatha didn’t know how she was doing it. How she was able to breathe and control her breath while moving so fast? All of that exertion and yet she continued to gaze longingly into Agatha’s eyes.

    Agatha felt her heart skip a beat.

    She loved her!

    Loved her with all of her being. This woman!

    Agatha knew it then and there! Rio was the one she wanted!

    They finished the song. The crowd broke out into cheers. Chanting for an encore.

    The band members looked at one another before Alice shrugged then nodded. She held up three fingers to her mates. They understood the meaning clear as day as they played their second song for the evening.

    This time a more upbeat and fast song. One you’d wanna work out too.

    Rio gave an impressive show once again with her drumming skills. Nicky was mystified by it all. The boy looked as if he was in heaven right in this very moment.

    Finally their second and last song finished off and the crowd once again cheered.

    The band took their bow, hand in hand then waved at everyone. Rio ran back towards the front and hopped off the stage and ran toward her two favorite people.

    Agatha pulled her in for a hug and held her. “You were wonderful baby!” She whispered into her ear and left a feather light kiss to her head. Rio pulled back and pushed some of her hair behind her ear. “You deserve every serenade!” She smiled.

    Nicky came over and hugged Rio again.

    “What did ya think bud?”

    “Um! That was awesome! I didn’t know drummers could play and sing at the same time! That’s amazing! You’re so good at everything Rio!” Rio chuckled. “Don’t worry! I’ll show you the ropes! Who knows, maybe you’ll surpass me in a year!”

    “No way! You’re super cool!”

    “Okay you wanna get some food?” Agatha asked, knowing Nicky would say yes and he did. She pointed at a food truck not too far, just in her line of sight.

    He ran off in the direction.

    Agatha giggled at his eagerness.

    “Ooh! I love funnel cakes!” Rio took a step forward in the direction towards the food truck. But before she could move anymore Agatha grabbed her arm.

    She reached up to her face and turned her head towards her, kissing her passionately.

    Rio’s eyes were wide for a moment; at her boldness to do this out in public before she relaxed and wrapped her arms around her neck.

    Agatha pulled back after a moment and sighed. “I love you Rio.” Rio jokingly huffed and stomped her foot! “I was supposed to say it first! I was gonna do it during the fireworks show!”

    Agatha chuckled. “You still can.”

    Rio shook her head. She turned to see if Nicky was looking and when she saw he wasn’t she turned back around. “Agatha Harkness I am absolutely in love with you!” Then she took her by her waist and dipped her into the most passionate kiss she’s ever given.

    Agatha’s hands shot up and around her neck as she let out a tiny squeal. Rio pulled back a bit and smiled down at her. She kissed her nose and cheek before pulling her back up.

    “Okay! You win!” Agatha chuckled.

    Rio took her hand. “I won the moment I earned your heart.”

    “Momma! What’s taking you so long!?”

    Both women giggled before walking off hand and hand towards the boy.

    Nicky pulled them both in the direction of the field.

    Both women laughing as they made their way through groups of people. “Gotta find a good spot!”

    But Rio reached out before he could go any faster and pulled him back. “Woah slow down buddy, what’s the rush?”

    He turned towards her with a panicked look on his face. “We’re gonna miss it!”

    Rio shook her head with a smile. “There’s still twenty minutes! Plus I’m sure your mother doesn’t want you falling over and busting your head!” Nicky quirked a brow. “You mean Momma?”

    Rio chuckled. “Yes. Plus I don’t want you getting hurt either!”

    “Nicky honey just relax. We’ll find a good spot I promise.” Agatha put her hands on his shoulders.

    “You promise?”

    Agatha held up her pinky. “Only the most sacred of promises!” Nicky lit up.

    Rio smiled at this and held hers up too. Interlocking it with Agatha’s. The boy held his up and curled his own in between theirs. His heart felt so warm in this moment! And so did the other women.

    And true to their promise they got the best seat in the house. Rio found a little hill off to the side for them to lay out on. She pulled the blanket she brought out of her bag. And two pillows she had ranger rolled. Agatha broke out into a fit of laughter. “Rio how! Did you fit those in your bag!?”

    “Boy Scouts!” She said it like it was the most obvious thing in the world. Agatha immediately stopped laughing. She didn’t know why she found that so… attractive!

    “Well… it was a coed thing. So we also sold cookies! It was awesome! Best of both I think!”

    “That sounds like so much fun!” Nicky beamed.

    Rio chuckled as she smoothed out the blanket on the ground. “Alright people, pick a spot!”

    “I call middle!” Nicky’s hand shot up before he practically threw his body perfectly in the middle of the blankets.

    Agatha smiled and laid down next to him. She kissed his cheek before glancing at Rio. She turned her head and held out her arm for the woman to join them.

    Rio smiled brightly and crawled over. And laid down next to Nicky, taking Agatha’s hand in her own and holding them over the boys chest. Nicky pulled them both close. Rio’s breath stopped for a moment. She’s never… experienced this before. To be together like this. As a family. Maybe one day her family.

    God knows she wanted to put a ring on Agatha’s finger. But it was still too soon. And she’d have to tell her before then.

    “Guys look up at the stars! They’re so pretty!” Nicky pointed up at the sky. They both looked up admiring the view.

    The sky was so clear tonight. They could see so much.

    Agatha smiled and looked back down at her son.

    “Beautiful.” Rio breathed.

    The younger woman looked at Rio. Expecting her to still be looking up at the sky. But instead she was looking directly at her.

    She blushed and pushed some of her own hair behind her ear. The two women gazed into the other eyes. Rio mouthed ‘I love you’ again. It made Agatha’s heart soar. She mouthed it back and squeezed her hand.

    “It’s starting!” Nicky shouted excitedly. Startling both women. They giggled at him and relaxed against the pillows fully. Looking off in the distance where they had started shooting off fireworks.

    It was beautiful!

    But still, Rio found herself constantly looking in Agatha’s direction constantly. Seeing the colorful lights reflect off of her blue eyes was a million times more beautiful than any supernova or star cluster.

    After a while Nicky started falling asleep. He cuddled into his Moms chest, clinging to her like a monkey on a tree. Agatha helped him close to her chest, and ran a hand through his long hair.

    Rio sighed as she watched them.

    So this was love?

    Agatha looked up at her and smiled. She grabbed Rio by her shirt and pulled her toward her until she was pressing her lips to hers. Rios eyes widened, she pulled back a moment and nodded down at Nicky. Agatha smiled but shook her head. She softly yanked on her shirt a couple times signaling to her that this was okay.

    Rio sighed then moved forward again, taking Agatha’s lips in hers. This was bliss.

    They whispered ‘I love you’s’ against the other’s lips, and sighed before pulling back.

    “I should get this boy home! He’s so tuckered out!” Agatha giggled and sat up. She attempting lifting up the boy but struggled. “God! Why can’t he stay little forever!”

    Rio reached forward. “May I?” She asked first.

    Agatha looked at her with stars in her eyes and nodded. “Just don’t pull anything grandma.” She joked.

    Rio rolled her eyes. “Please! I’m not much older than you!” She made it look easy as she scooped the eleven year old in her arms. Agatha glared for a moment before smiling.

    They walked back to Agatha’s SUV. Rio sat the boy down in the seat and buckled him in. She leaned forward and kissed his forehead before pulling away and closing the door.

    Agatha snuck a few pictures throughout the day. Knowing she’d treasure these forever. She smiled as she looked through them in the front seat. “I hope you got my good side!” Rio joked.

    Agatha gasped as she looked up at her. “You don’t have a good side! You’re whole face is perfect!”

    Rio grinned and posed for her. “Really? I am pretty sexy aren’t I?” She joked.

    Agatha playfully smacked her shoulder. “You’re unbelievable!” “And yet you love me! What does that make you then?”

    Agatha shook her head. “Unbelievably in love!” She moved forward and kissed her again. “Stay tonight?”

    Rio sighed and nodded. “I can. I gotta get up early for work though.” Agatha smiled. “That’s okay! I just want more time to with you.” Rio grabbed her hand. “And I promise you, you’ll have it, as long as you want it.”

    Chapter End Notes The song is My Heart by paramore btw

    Chapter 5: You know I love you so!

    Chapter Summary Campfire songs and ghost stories.

    Gifts and heartache.

    Chapter Notes Calm before the storm.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes

    There was a reason why Agatha didn’t allow her son to have a sleep over. Simply put, kids were loud and she usually had to get up early for work. Whereas her neighbor Wanda, was a stay at home mother; aside from a part time job she picked up, just for something to do.

    But considering it was seven in the morning and she was still in bed resting, one would normally expect a house to be quiet at this time. But for some reason there was a pattering of multiple footsteps and laughter! She groaned, pulling a pillow over her head in an attempt to muffle the sound. But it did nothing as the foot steps only got louder. She threw the pillow off before her eyes flew open. She sat up with a groan, rubbing her eyes then turned to glance at the clock.

    The pattering got even louder before there was a clattering and what sounded like something smashing onto the floor.

    Agatha hurried out of bed and threw on a robe quickly before running out of her room.

    “Nicky!?”

    She headed for the sound.

    “Oh no! Hurry! Clean it up fast!”

    She heard an all too familiar hushed voice from around the corner of the hall.

    She stopped out of sight to listen for a moment.

    “Oh no! I hope Aggie didn’t hear!”

    Came another familiar, but much younger voice.

    “Shush! As long as we’re quiet and fast Momma won’t know!”

    The woman shook her head and rounded the corner, placing her hands on her hips as she looked down at the two boys. Waiting for an explanation. Or an excuse.

    Nicky’s eyes widened when he saw her. He looked down at the broken potted plant and then back up at his mother before offering an awkward smile and chuckle. “Morning Momma…”

    “Don’t you morning me! Mister! What did you two do?” She glanced over at Tommy for a moment who coward away behind Nicky.

    Agatha couldn’t help but find the scene adorable. She glanced back over at her son and waited for his answer, tapping her foot impatiently on the floor. Nicky hung his head low in shame. “We were running and Tommy slid into the stand. B-But he didn’t mean to!”

    “And are you supposed to be running in the house!?”

    Nicky shook his head.

    “Then why were you!?”

    The older boy fiddled with his hands nervously.

    God! Why did this have to be so damn hard sometimes!? Nicky was a perfect kid. He hardly got in trouble and when he did it wasn’t that serious. But dammit! Why did he look at her like that!? He was so freakin cute! She always wondered where he got it from.

    “M’sorry Momma! I wasn’t thinking! I made a mistake! Please don’t ground me from playing with Billy and Tommy!”

    Agatha pinched her nose and sighed. “Baby, you aren’t being punished. You just need to think more about your actions before doing something, okay? Are you okay sweetie?” She moved toward them and gently took Tommy’s arm and crouched down to his level. “Let me see. Are you hurt?” The young boy shook his head. “Just a tiny bruise. I’m a big boy! It don’t hurt!” He smiled.

    Agatha smiled back at him and kissed his head. “You are a big boy Tommy!” She stood up and placed a hand on Nicky’s head. “Does Wanda know he’s here?”

    Nicky nodded. “She said she was going to text you to let you know he was coming over to play.”

    Almost on cue Agatha’s phone buzzed, off in the distance. She cursed under her breath and turned to her room to retrieve it.

    Wanda:Hey! I meant to let you know a bit ago, but Tommy came over. I hope that’s okay! If he’s too loud I’ll come get him.

    Agatha sighed again and glanced up at the boys.

    They were both hugging! Why were they so freakin cute!!? Agatha:No he’s fine.

    She watched the dots bounce before Wanda responded.

    Wanda:I have this sudden work retreat thing. They gave me no notice on it. Is it okay if you watch him? I’d have Billy do it but he’s on a school trip in D.C. and Vis is on a business trip. It’s important for my work. Agatha groaned. She really didn’t want to.

    But with how often Wanda had taken Nicky in and often on such short notice she’d be an asshole not to do this for her.

    Agatha:Yes of course! You’ve been my support all these years! It’s the least I can do! I’m here anytime, really!

    Wanda:Thanks! You’re the best! I’ll bring you back some cookies! I’ll let you know when I should be home!

    Agatha turned her phone off and shoved it in the pocket of her robe before exiting her room.

    “Okay Tommy you’re spending the night. Is there anything you need from your house?”

    Nicky jumped with joy. “Wait! Really!?”

    Tommy put a finger on his chin and glanced up in thought, “Hm… I need some things.” He started listing the items off on his fingers. “My stuffed bear, my blanky, and my night time undies.”

    Agatha groaned.

    He still wets the bed!?

    “He’s sleeping with you tonight son.” She pointed at Nicky. The excitement drained from Nicky’s face to that of terror. “No!” “I’m afraid so. Unless you want to sleep on the couch and he sleeps in your bed?”

    “He can’t sleep with you?”

    Agatha chuckled. She approached them and covered Tommy’s ears. “I don’t want him wetting my bed.”

    “Then can I sleep with you?”

    Agatha quirked a brow. “Afraid not. I’m having a sleep over with my friend.”

    “I don’t mind sharing with you and Rio!”

    “I do. You’re too big to sleep with me. And it’ll be cramped with all thee of us. Plus Tommy will be wearing leak proof underwear. You’ll be fine.” She removed her hands from his ears.

    The little boy wrapped his arms around Agatha and hugged her. “Yay! My first night at Aggie’s house!” His face beamed with excitement. Agatha almost squealed from cuteness overload.

    “And my first sleep over!” Tommy jumped.

    Well didn’t she just feel honored.

    Agatha fiddled away in her home office. trying to catch up on some work. She could hear distant laughter and the sound of a game console blaring. She didn’t know how many times she had to tell those boys to keep it down. Oh well.

    Boys will be boys.

    The sound of a pen scratching against paper filled the quiet space. She adjusted her glasses on her face as she continued filling out some paperwork for her job and a couple bills.

    She was lost in thought when her phone went off.

    She glanced over and read the caller id. Her face lit up as she answered it quickly.

    “Hello? Rio?”

    “Hey baby. How are you this fine day?”

    Agatha chuckled as she propped the device between her shoulder and ear. “Oh you know… just doing some bills and boring work stuff at home.” Rio giggled. “Is that so? Does that mean you’re unavailable to come camping with me and some friends?”

    The woman sat up. “Tonight?”

    “Yeah! I bought a shit ton of marshmallows! We’re gonna play music and tell stories it’s gonna be cool.”

    “I’ve got no one to watch Nicky and I’m babysitting the neighbors kid. This is the first time in a long time that I’ve watched one of her kids. Also it’s the middle of October!”

    “It’s the last nice day of the year! And that’s okay! They can come too! It’ll be awesome!”

    “I don’t know…”

    “Oh come on! It’ll be fun!”

    “Rio…”

    “Pleeease!” She dragged out the word. “With sugar on top? I’ll shower you in so many kisses and we can all snuggle up in my tent! It’ll be so nice! I’ll even go out and get sleeping bags for you guys!”

    Agatha took her glasses off and sighed. “Okay. But I will buy the sleeping bags! You save your money!” She demanded.

    “Yes ma’am!”

    She’s pretty sure Rio saluted on the other side.

    Agatha wasn’t sure why she liked that so much. “Ma’am? I’m younger than you. You dork!”

    “And? Doesn’t stop me from calling you Mommy either.”

    Agatha’s breath hitched.

    The sultry giggled that Rio let out made Agatha’s face redden. “Why do you tease me!?”

    “Because you’re cute when you’re flustered! I gotta go! But I’ll text you the deets! I love you baby!”

    “Love you too.”

    “I can’t wait to see you Mommy!”

    And before Agatha could say anything else Rio hung up.

    Agatha groaned again and put her face in her hands. “She going to kill me!”

    Nicky waited all too impatiently for his mother’s friend to arrive. He lit up when he saw the familiar truck off in the distance before it parked on the side of the road and a woman got out.

    Rio smiled as she noticed the familiar face in the window. She waved before waking up Agatha’s driveway. Her heart pounded in her chest, she was so excited for there little outing.

    The boy with long dark brown hair came barreling out of the house at full speed. Almost knocking the wind out of Rio when embracing her. “Rio!”

    “Hey kiddo! There’s my favorite little goblin!” She ruffled his hair. “I’ve got weenies on a stick with your name on it. You in or what?” The boy jumped excitedly. “Um yeah!”

    “Where’s this little child I’ve been hearing so much about?” Nicky giggled and turned waiting for Tommy to come out of the house. A moment later he did. Hand in hand with Agatha.

    Tommy waved at them with a big smile on his face. “Hello Ms Wio!”

    Rio smiled out how endearing this small child was. His mispronunciation of her name hit her right in her heart. She wished she could have had a child to raise.”You must be Tommy! I hear you’re super fast!”

    The blonde boy nodded. “Yeah! I’m like the flash!”

    Agatha chuckled. She handed Rio the boys backpack. The older woman quirked a brow. “My work called I need to head in for a few hours. But I promise I’ll meet back up with you guys as soon as I can. Is that okay? It was so sudden. But it’s important and this works out well.” Rios eyes widened for a moment. Agatha was entrusting her with her child and her neighbors kid. This meant a lot! She nodded. “Yeah! I can handle it. Plus I’ll have Alice, Jen, and Hela there.”

    “Alright. Just… call or text if you need anything okay?”

    Rio nodded.

    The three women sat close engaging in small talk.

    Alice was currently braiding Hela’s hair, while Jen brushed Alice’s.

    “Oh god what did I walk in on?” Rio joked.

    The three women turned. Their faces lit up when they saw the two young boys.

    Nicky ran over towards Alice. “Alice! I haven’t seen you in a while!” “You saw me at the harvest festival a couple weeks ago!” “Yeah but that was a long time ago!” He looked over at Jen. “Hi Jen!” He pointed at her necklace. “That’s pretty! Where’d you get it?” Jen looked down. “Oh my potion pendant? I got it at a thrift store a few years ago.”

    “Aw I wanted to get one for Momma! She’d look so pretty in it don’t you think Rio?” He turned toward the woman with bright innocent eyes. All three women smirked.

    “Yeah Rio! Agatha would look lovely in one of those necklaces wouldn’t she!?” Hela chuckled with a shit eating grin.

    The woman blushed and turned away. Pulling Tommy along with her. Nicky looked over at Hela and smiled. He held his hand out to her. “Hi! I’m Nicky Harkness! You were at the harvest festival!”

    Hela nodded and took his hand. “Well aren’t you just the gentlemen! And yes! Our band! I am the lead guitarist!”

    “I wanna learn how to play so bad!”

    Hela quirked a brow. “Oh yeah? I’m sure Rio could teach you.” Hela gestured behind her at the truck. “She did bring her guitar.” Nicky jumped with joy. “I wanna hear her play!”

    After an hour the sun started setting.

    Now it was time to prepare the fire. Alice and Hela worked to get it lit. Rio leaned back, wrapping a blanket snugly around Nicky and Tommy, the younger boy shivered against the lingering cold. Gradually, he began to warm up, nestled securely under her protective hold, with both boys cuddled close by her side.

    Alice and Hela snuck pictures the entire time. Knowing Agatha would be gushing over them later.

    “Wio when is Aggie coming back?”

    “Soon buddy. She said she’ll be leaving in a half hour.” “That’s a long time!” He whined.

    “I know honey. But it’ll be okay. You aren’t shy are you? You don’t need be shy around us! We’re all friends here!”

    Tommy shook his head. “I-I’m okay…”

    His shaky voice said otherwise.

    Nicky moved over to hug Tommy’s back. “It’s okay Tommy! Momma will be back soon! I’m here with you! You have nothing to be afraid of!” “T’ank you big bro!” He rolled over and hugged Nicky.

    “Who’s ready for some marshmallows!?” Alice asked.

    And almost as if nothing was the matter, both boys jumped up in excitement.

    “Me!” They said in unison, throwing their hands up in the air. Alice chuckled as the fire came to life. “Maybe Rio could play us a song in a bit.”

    “Maybe.” Rio said before making her way over to the campfire. “Or! We could tell ghost stories!” Hela chimed in, sitting down between Alice and Tommy.

    “Yeah!” Tommy bounced with excitement. “Scawy stowies pwease!” Hela chuckled before she tousled his hair.

    “No way!” Rio snapped. “We are not doing that sis! Agatha will kill me! And frankly, I don’t want to give the boys nightmares!”

    Hela rolled her eyes. “Look, I know you’re wipped for her. But I’m sure one little story isn’t gonna hurt. After all…” she smirked. “They’re big boys. They can handle it.”

    Tommy crawled towards Rio and gripped her shirt. “Yeah, Wio! We’re big boys wemember?”

    Rio sighed.

    “How about a song first?” Jen suggested. “And maybe after?” “I’ll do one now. I’ll think about later…” Rio stood up and went to the truck to grab her guitar. She opened the back door and leaned in, moving some things around to get to her case.

    Tommy followed after her like a puppy following its mother. “Wio gonna sing! Awesome!” He threw his hands up in the air with excitement. Rio smiled down at him and pulled back to pick him up. “You know Tommy, has anyone ever told you how adorable you are?”

    “My mommy all da times!” He hugged onto her neck. “You adowable too Wio!” There was a pause for a moment as Tommy took Rio in. “Aggie is amazing! And you are amazing! Nicky has such great parents! Rio gave him a look. “What do you mean why do you say that?” “Cause you are Nicky’s dada o’course!” He threw his hands out in the air excitedly. “My daddy says I’m super fast! I bet you and Nicky Wace all da times! You are super strong!” He flexed his arms jokingly. Rio couldn’t help but giggle at his antics. He must have seen them kiss in the yard before and that’s why he was saying these things. “Nicky is so fast! I can hardly keep up with him! His feet are like magic! But I bet you’re faster!”

    “Da fastest!”

    They made it back over to the fire and sat down. Tommy clung to Rio’s side for a moment before taking a seat on the log by Jen. “Hi!” He said enthusiastically. “You are pretty!”

    Jen giggled. “You’re pretty too!”

    Nicky bounced with joy before moving toward Rio. “What song are you gonna play!?”

    “Hm… not sure.” She looked up to the group. “Suggestions?”

    Hela was carving a figure out of a piece of wood when she looked up to offer her suggestion, “Play Never gonna give you up!”

    Rio rolled her eyes and looked around. “Any other suggestions?” Hela chuckled before going back to what she was doing.

    “Baby shark!” Tommy spoke up.

    “They need to be camp fire songs kid. But I promise I’ll do that one for you some other time.”

    “Okay Wio.”

    “How about Brown eyed girl? But change the lyrics to blue eyed girl!” Alice offered.

    Jen nodded. “I like this idea!”

    Rio sighed. “Fine. Blue eyed girl it is.” She moved her fingers around the fret board a few times. She had never played the song before so she was trying to get an idea beforehand. “Alright I got it.”

    She started to play and the group watched, mystified.

    They all hummed along to her singing. The women would squeal every time Rio said ‘blue eyed girl’. And every single time it grated on Rio’s nerves. The only thing keeping her from stopping was Nicky’s constant swaying side to side with a smile.

    Finally, she came to the end of the song. And the group broke out into claps and cheers.

    “Was that about Momma?” Nicky asked.

    Rio eyes widened at him for a moment before turning back toward the group. “How about that scary story huh?”

    Hela leaned back with a smirk. “Thought you’d never ask.” She grabbed a flashlight and turned it on, holding it beneath her face to make herself appear scary. “We’re taking about cryptids tonight.”

    The three other women groaned. But Nicky only look interested. Tommy didn’t understand.

    “And what better than a local legend!” Hela’s head snapped right at the boys with a wicked grin.

    The boys gasped.

    She gave a dramatic pause before starting.

    “The Devil of Northview!” She grinned at the sight of the boys jumping before continuing.

    “They say the woods outside Northview at night are no place for anyone to wander. But back in the 30’s, there was a boy named…” She looked between the two boys. Noticing Nicky’s interest and Tommy’s nervousness, her grin widened. “Thomas, who didn’t believe in ghost stories—or The Jersey Devil!” She growled out the last part dramatically. “Devil!????” Tommy squealed out clutching onto Jen for dear life. Hela chuckled again. “Oh yes! And on one summers night, he and his friends dared each other to sneak out. They headed deep into the woods, to see if the old stories were true.

    The moon was high, casting shadows across the wooded area, making the twisted trees seem taller than they actually were, there was a faint bit of light at the forest edge, but the deeper they went, the darker the forest became. Soon, they were unable to see their own hands in front of their eyes. It was too quiet, the only sound was the crunch of leaves beneath their boots. Then… a branch cracked. It felt as though the sound vibrated through their bones, like a gun shot! Thomas froze. ‘It’s just a deer,’ he whispered, but his voice was shaky.

    His friends were unsure. They pushed closer together, as the woods seemed to close in tighter. Suddenly, a shriek ripped through the trees, sounding like no animal they’d ever heard, high-pitched and guttural, chilling right down to the bone!

    One of the boys screamed before the others bolted back toward town, but Thomas stayed. ‘It’s probably an owl,’ he muttered, more to himself than anyone else.

    Then, he saw it.

    Just ahead, between the trees, two glowing red eyes appeared, hovering far too high to belong to any normal creature. A hulking figure emerged, its leathery wings unfolding with an ear-splitting snap. Its horse-like face twisted into a grin that revealed jagged teeth, and its cloven hooves scraped against the ground.

    Thomas tried to run, but it was faster. He felt the wind from its wings as it soared overhead, then a clawed hand grabbed his shoulder. His scream echoed through the woods. His friends could hear it far off, but they never looking back.

    The next morning, all they found of Thomas was his torn jacket snagged on a branch—and hoofprints burned into the ground where he’d been standing. They say if you’re brave—or foolish—enough to venture into the woods outside Northview at night, you can still hear his screams and the rustle of leathery wings above.” Hela paused for one last dramatic touch. “So… who’s up for a stroll in woods tonight?” She gestured toward the wooded area around them.

    Tommy practically let out a blood curdling scream and booked it over to Nicky.

    “Ah! I don’t want the monster to eat me!” He cried out.

    Rio pinched her nose and groaned. She stood up and reached for the boy. Lifting him into her arms and tucking him into the crook of her neck, she patted his back before speaking,. “Shhh, it’s okay sweet heart. It’s just a story. Hela made it up. I promise!”

    He sniffled before sitting back some to look her in the eyes. “You do? You mean it!? Not true?”

    She shook her head and offered him a small smile. “Trust me kid. If I put either of you boys in danger Agatha would kill me!”

    “I would?”

    The whole group jumped and screamed, all falling off their logs and chairs. Agatha squinted in confusion at their reaction. “Jeez! I know I can be intimidating at times! But come on! I don’t bite!”

    Hela sat up and smirked. “At least not that hard, huh Rio!?” Rio growled and glared at her best friend. “Hela! Don’t make me come over there!” She spoke through her teeth.

    Hela giggled. “Oh come on! I’m fun! Admit it! You love it!” Agatha quirked a brow but shrugged before taking a seat next to her son. “Momma! You just missed it! Ms Hela told an awesome ghost story!” “Oh? And about what?” She glanced over at the woman. “Nothing too scary I hope!”

    “No momma! Not bad!” He tugged on her sleeve. “I’m brave I can handle it. Tommy on the other hand…” he gesture toward the boy who was nuzzling into Rio’s neck.

    Agatha smiled at the woman and gave her a little wave.

    Rio waved back.

    “Aggie! You’re back!” Tommy turned and hopped down out of Rio’s arms and ran over to her. Practically knocking the wind out of her. “Umfh! Jeez! You okay bud?”

    “There’s a Devil in the woods! And it wants to eat me!”

    “Is that so? Well fear not little one. Nothings scarier than me! I won’t let it get you. I’m a big scary witch killer remember?”

    He nodded with a smile. “Yeah! The spirit witch!” He waved his hands up in the air. “Wio is a gween witch!” He pointed over at her. Agatha chuckled at the sight of Rio wearing a green sweater and green cargo pants. “I can see why you’d say that.”

    “Green witch? That’s the embodiment of death herself over there!” Hela joked. “But don’t be fooled for I am the goddess of death!” “I would kick your ass in a battle!” Rio chuckled. “A lowly goddess would never have a chance against a cosmic being!”

    “That’s hot.” Jen muttered.

    “Potions witch!” Tommy pointed at her.

    Alice and Hela erupted into laughter.

    “Damn! Boys got you pegged! You used to be a bartender too!” Jen rolled her eyes and took a sip of her beer.

    “What am I?” Alice asked.

    Tommy ran over to her. He took in her appearance. The fiery streaks in her black hair and red orange jacket gave it away to him. “Blood witch! You were born a witch! You protect people! And like fire!”

    The group was taken aback by how attentive this boy was. “Oh wow… I’m a security guard actually. Im going into the police academy soon.”

    “Yeah Alice is a great person! But don’t forget what a pyro maniac she used to be!” Hela smirked.

    “It was an accident! Are you never gonna let me live it down!?” “Nah! Not when you burned my first couch.”

    “Alright you two! Time for weenies and s’mores!” Rio came back over with all of the items they’d need.

    The boys ran over ready to eat.

    “Weenies and chocolate… what an interesting combo.” Agatha muttered. “I love weenies!” Nicky exclaimed.

    “So do I!” Rio said excitedly.

    Agatha gagged. “Ughhh! What is wrong with you people! I’m glad I brought my own pizza.”

    The boys heads snapped in her direction. “Pizza!?” They said in unison. She nodded with a smirk. “Yep! And it’s all mine! You boys have your weenies remember?” She teased.

    “We can have both!” Nicky chimed in.

    Agatha pulled the box out of her car and placed it on a box they were using as makeshift table.

    “Dominos!” Tommy smiled.

    They huddled around the camp fire together. Admiring the stars. They all enjoyed the silence. The only sound filling the space was the crackling of the fire and the sound of crickets all around them. Until Tommy broke it.

    “Rio sung about a blue eyed girl earlier! It was so pretty!” Rio’s face went flushed red when Agatha looked her way. “Really? Blue eyed girl?” She paused for a moment. “How interesting. Wish I was here for that one.”

    “Well, Rio could sing again.” Hela smirked in her direction. “Yeah Rio sing for us!” Jen butted in. She was starting to get bored. She needed drama. So she was definitely stirring this pot.

    Rio looked uncomfortable. She looked between the two woman and gave a nervous snicker. “Come on guys… I—“ “I’ll sing.”

    All heads turned toward Agatha.

    Alice lit up at this. “Oh yes! What are you gonna sing!?” Agatha smiled and looked across the fire at Rio. “Yellow by Coldplay. Can you play it?”

    Rio blinked for a moment before nodding and grabbing her guitar. “Good! Start us off and then I’ll jump in.” She winked at the older woman making her blush.

    Rio started to play.

    The group nodded along.

    Nicky leaned against his mother’s side as she started to sing. She kept her sharp and adoring gaze on the woman across from her. “Look at the stars, look how they shine for you!

    And everything you do!

    Yeah, they were all yellow.

    I came along, I wrote a song for you!

    And all the things you do!

    And it was called ‘Yellow’

    So then I took my turn, Oh, what a thing to have done And it was all yellow.”

    Rio softly gasped as she realized Agatha was singing to her. For her.

    “Ahhh, Your skin, oh, yeah, your skin and bones.

    Ohh, Turn into something beautiful.

    Aah You know, you know I love you so!

    You know I love you so!”

    Rio started tearing up. This felt like some kind of… proclamation. Agatha was being so romantic right now.

    The whole group was entranced as Agatha continued singing. But between the two women, it felt as if they were the only ones in the universe.

    At least for a moment.

    After a couple minutes the song came to a close.

    Rio set her guitar down and quickly wiped at her tears.

    “Why are you cwying Wio!? Did you get hurt?” Tommy asked with worry, crawling over to her.

    Rio chuckled but shook her head. “No buddy. I’m just… they’re happy tears is all. Aggie, is a really good singer. It was moving.”

    After a bit of chatting and laughter they all decided to turn in for bed.

    Agatha was nervous at the prospect of sharing a sleeping space with her son and her girlfriend at the same time.

    Even though Rio offered to just sleep in Hela’s tent, Agatha couldn’t do that to her. She knew Rio would miss them too much and Hela was probably annoying.

    They got their sleeping bags set out.

    Rio had a surprisingly nice and big tent to sleep in. Plus, really comfy mats to put their sleeping bags over.

    “I hope you guys sleep well! Don’t let The Jersey Devil bite!” Hela chuckled off in the distance, somewhere outside their tent.

    Tommy clutched Nicky tightly.

    “Ow can’t breathe! Calm down! It’s not real!” He whined. Agatha looked over at Rio, “Okay what were you guys talking about earlier?”

    Rio sighed, “Hela told a ghost story about The Jersey devil.”

    Agatha groaned and rubbed at her temples, “Seriously! She thought that was a good idea with a five year old?”

    “I told her! I’m sorry I should have stopped her.”

    Agatha’s face softened. “I’m not upset at you honey. It’s okay. They had fun today.” She gestured at the boys. “I…had fun today.”

    Rio smiled, “I’m so glad!”

    The morning came quickly as any other.

    It was supposed to rain at ten so they had to get up early and quickly pack. Tommy was sluggish as any child would be in the morning. And Nicky as the odd child he was, loved mornings.

    And so did Rio.

    So that’s how she found herself carrying a sleepy five year old while holding her tired girlfriend’s hand. Helping them to the truck. “Alice said she’ll take your car back to your house for you. You look way too tired to be driving.”

    Agatha grumbled unintelligibly while rubbing sleep from her eyes. Rio smiled, finding her morning grumpiness endearing as well as her adorable bed head.

    She buckled Tommy into his car seat and rubber Nicky’s head before climbing into the drivers seat and starting the engine.

    They drove in silence for a while.

    Nicky enjoyed the scenery while Tommy snored.

    Rio glanced over at her girlfriend. She could tell Agatha was cranky, from all the tossing and turning she was doing, unable to fall back asleep. Smirking, she decided to break the silence.

    “You drool in your sleep.”

    Agatha’s eyes shot open, mortification flooding her as she slowly turned to face Rio. Her pale cheeks flushed a deep red.

    “Excuse me!?”

    Rio looked back at the road with a smile.

    “Ya heard me.”

    “Um… I’m not sure I did. Unless you really said what I think you said!” “Mmhm!” Rio gave her snark, teasing the already grumpy woman. “Do you often wish to meet death Rio?”

    The older woman snickered. “You forget I am Death herself, remember?” “You’re also the green witch. But what am I?”

    Rio turned and smirked again. “Oh I know what you are!” She winked. She knew damn well what Agatha meant but decided to fluster her. “A cutie!” She turned back toward the road.

    More silence washed over them for a moment. Before Agatha spoke up. “You kick in your sleep!” She swatted at her arm before adding, “And you snore!”

    Rio giggled, “Ow!” She rubbed her arm and glanced over at the woman. Her mouth hung open with surprised excitement. “You did not!”

    “I did!” Agatha glared at her before throwing a crumbled up piece of paper at her head.

    “I am driving you crazy woman!”

    Nicky spoke up, “Momma! Please don’t get us killed over flirting!” Agatha gasped as her head shot in her son’s direction. “I am not flirting!” He rolled his eyes and looked back out the window. “Yeah! Yeah!”

    “I’m not!” Agatha repeated herself. But the soft hand sliding over her knee proved to her she was lying.

    A few days had gone by since the camping outing. It had been such a busy work week for Agatha. She hadn’t had time to sit and think let alone spend much time with her son.

    It made her feel empty.

    She had spent an all nighter at the office. Typing away in her laptop frantically. Her tired eyes constantly fluttered closed as she fought sleep. She pulled her glasses from her face to rub at her sleepy eyes. She sighed, before continuing her typing.

    A few minutes later the door swung open startling Agatha beyond belief. Sleep deprivation often made one skittish and jumpy, and right now her heart felt like it was going to burst from her chest.

    Her head shot up at the figure approaching her.

    It was Lilia.

    “Ms Harkness I tried to stop her but—“ “Agatha!” Rio came in right behind her practically shoving the older woman out of the way.

    The younger woman was confused. As to why Rio was busting down her office doors, looking angry but… holding flowers?

    “Get your ass outside and into my truck! I’m taking you home! Now!” She growled out.

    Agatha was flabbergasted. “What!? How dare you I—“ “Now!” Rio growled out again. “Your son is upset! He told me he hasn’t seen you in two days! You’ve been here this whole time!? Working!? You need rest!” She came to her side and grabbed her arm.

    “Hey! Let me go! Who do you think you are!?”

    “Your very caring and loving partner! Who is very worried about you! Who’s come to take you home so you don’t die of exhaustion!” She nudged Agatha toward her. “Who just held her crying son for twenty minutes because he’s worried about his mother!”

    Agatha looked up at her stunned. She looked over at Lilia who just shrugged. “I can finish up for you! She’s right! You need rest! Work can wait! And maybe you should take a day or two off.”

    “Lilia!”

    Rio pulled Agatha up before she could argue anymore. “Baby.” Agatha looked up at as if she was going to argue. But Rios softening expression stopped her.

    “Please.”

    She looked… worried.

    Agatha sighed and nodded. “Okay. I’m sorry. Take me home.” “Don’t say sorry to me! I’m not the one who cried there eyes out!”

    Rio drove her home, pulling in to the driveway. She quickly got out and helped Agatha out of the truck, who started to stumble from her fatigue. “Jeez babe!” Rio groaned before leaning down and scooping her up in her arms.

    Agatha’s eyes widened. “Ugh! I am not a child!” She grumbled but didn’t fight her.

    “Says the woman who can’t walk! Because she’s too tired!” Agatha glared at her for a moment. “Fine! Carry me! Like I’m your bride!” Rio snickered. “Don’t threaten me with a good time! Now! Time for bed!”

    Rio fumbled with the door before kicking it open.

    “Hey watch it! I paid for that door!”

    “And I’m saving your ass! The door will be fine!”

    “Momma!” A boy came running downstairs.

    Agatha’s face fell when she saw how red the boys eyes were. “Oh baby…” Agatha said as Rio laid her on the couch. Nicky flung himself into her arms right away.

    “Why were you gone so long! You always come back!”

    Agatha sighed. “I’m sorry sweetie I was just behind with some work that’s all. I… I promise I won’t do it again!”

    Nicky nodded as he sobbed into her neck. Agatha sighed and looked up at Rio.

    “Thanks.”

    “You don’t need to thank me.” Rio left for a moment before returning with the bouquet from earlier and a box.

    Agatha quirked a brow. “What’s that for by the way? It was very confusing seeing you so angry earlier, but holding those.

    “They’re for you!” She held them out to her.

    Agatha took them. Still looking up at her with confusion. “I called you Agatha. But you didn’t answer. So I spoke with Alice trying to see where you were. She wasn’t sure considering she was off, but then suggested you were doing something for your birthday.”

    Agatha’s face fell.

    “I was absolutely pissed!”

    “Rio…”

    “So I went out and got you something! And came here hoping to get an answer as to why you failed to mention when your birthday was or that it was coming up. You could imagine my surprise when I found Nicky here with that neighbor teen boy and he was crying his eyes out!” Agatha sighed.

    “Crying because he missed his mother and wanted to spend her birthday with her. Which apparently she missed.”

    She looked down. “I… would you believe me if I told you I forgot?” Rio scoffed before sitting down and pushing the box against Agatha’s chest.

    “What’s this?”

    “A surprise. So open it.”

    Agatha sighed. Nicky’s crying calmed down as he nuzzled against his mother, watching her open her present. “Momma Rio got you a present!” “I see baby.” She undid the very well done wrapping paper slowly, by peeling off the tape. She felt bad ruining it. It looked so nice. It even had a little bow.

    Rio groaned and rolled her eyes. “Oh jeez! Rip it!” She reached over and ripped a big chunk off for her to get her to hurry up.

    Agatha chuckled at her eagerness. She finished ripping it open herself and pulled the lid off the box. She gasped. It was a beautiful blue jacket with purple interior and on top was an amethyst necklace. She picked up the necklace and held it up to the light examining it.

    “Happy 40!”

    Agatha grumbled. “Ugh! Don’t remind me!”

    Rio huffed. She grabbed her phone and quickly started typing something in her notes and then held it in front of Agatha’s face for her to read. I am 42! There is nothing wrong with being 40! It’s hot! You’re hot! Get used to it!

    Rio wanted to kiss Agatha so bad right now, but Nicky was there, and it was too quiet to try and sneak one, he’d hear.

    She wasn’t sure when Agatha planned on telling him. So she was fine keeping it under wraps until then. It wasn’t like she was hiding their relationship as a whole. She pulled her phone away from her face and then ran her hand through Nickys dark brown hair. The same hair as his momma. Gosh he looked so much like Agatha! He was such a cute kid. The boy sniffled and shot up. “I’m gonna go get my gift!” Then ran out of the room.

    Rio chuckled, “That kid is so—“ Agatha yanked the woman on top of her by her shirt, and kissed her passionately.

    Rio was surprised only for a moment before relaxing into it. After a moment Agatha pulled back. “Thank you darling. You’re an amazing girlfriend. I’m so lucky to have you.” Agatha smiled. “Boy! Where did that energy come from!?” Rio chuckled.

    Agatha opened her mouth to speak but stopped when she heard rapid footsteps approaching. The boy was already in the living room before she could even react.

    “Momma! Here!” But the boy didn’t comment on Rio’s position on top of his momma. He just held his gift up to her.

    “Ohhh baby! This is so sweet!” She sat up and took his homemade card and read it.

    It was a drawing of their family. It had her and Nicky of course, and their pet rabbit and… Rio.

    It was such an innocent little drawing too. He was in the middle, holding both of their hands, while they all smiled.

    “Can I see?” Rio asked.

    Agatha looked at her, thinking for a moment before nodding and handing it over to her. She watched the expression on Rio’s face change and it broke her heart.

    Her bottom lip trembled before tears started to fall down her face. “Rio why are you crying!” Nicky went up next to her and hugged her from the side.

    Rio chuckled and quickly wiped away at her tears. “Boy! I’ve been doing that a lot, huh? I just really like your drawing that’s all.” Agatha reached out to her and took her hand in her own. “It’s such a beautiful card son! I love it! Thank you!”

    “Of course Momma! Happy birthday!”

    “Ms Harkness…” Lilia stuck her head in the door.

    Agatha looked up and noticed the somber look on the old woman’s face. Agatha’s brows furrowed as she took off her glasses. “Is everything okay?” The older woman sighed as she entered the office and closed the door. “The school called. It’s… Nicky. There was an accident. They took him to the hospital.”

    Agatha’s eyes widened as she shot up from her chair.

    Lilia flinched at the sudden rise in Agatha’s voice—deep, rough, and charged with anger and worry. It was a tone she’d never heard from her boss before.

    “What happened!?”

    Agatha weaved through traffic, driving far too fast and most likely breaking a few laws in the process.

    “Please, please, please!” she cried, her voice cracking as the call went to voicemail for what felt like the hundredth time.

    “Fuck!” she screamed, slamming her hands against the steering wheel as hot tears streamed down her face.

    All of her anger and frustration currently aimed at the hospital for not picking up their damn phones!

    Finally, she called her.

    “Hello? Aggie?”

    “Rio!”

    She heard a gasp on the other end.

    “Agatha what’s wrong!?”

    “It’s Nicky! I need you Rio! He’s at the hospital!”

    Chapter End Notes So I have a chapter that I meant to post for chapter four but I wanted way more stuff added in between it. So it got bumped to chapter 6. It’ll be an angsty one.

    Little hint for the next chapter, I’m introducing Evanora. That’s all I can say.

    Also the song Agatha sings is Yellow by Coldplay. And the song Rio sang in the previous chapter was My heart by Paramore

    Chapter 6: I’ll look after you!

    Chapter Summary Nicky gets hurt, Evanora comes over for early thanksgiving. Things take a turn Chapter Notes !!!Warning for violence in this chapter!!!

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Agatha never thought she could feel so much love. Her heart burned with a fire. Yearning for the one person who made her so happy.

    For weeks, she’d been carrying that warmth with her, wrapped in the moments she shared with Rio. The way her laugh filled the silence, the way her hand felt so right in hers.

    Their little dates had made her smile just thinking about them and when they brought Nicky along everything felt as it should be in their own little world.

    Just the three of them.

    But today, She realized her happiness could be taken away at any moment. Was she being tested?

    Her heart was frigid from the cold and it threatened to cease all movement. The phone call came in the middle of the afternoon, on a very busy work day. Lilia’s tone and expression tipped her off quickly that something was wrong.

    Before Agatha could fully process the words “hospital” and “accident,” she was already at her son’s bedside, her world narrowed to the beeping of machines and his all too-pale face.

    It was serious.

    He needed a blood transfusion.

    “Agatha!”

    The distressed woman looked up. Her eyes rimmed red with tears that had fallen long ago. Her hair was a mess and she looked beaten down. She was tired.

    So, so tired!

    “What happened, baby!?” She came to her side and pulled her into her embrace.

    Agatha wept into her shirt. “He passed out at recess and fell off the jungle gym at school and broke his arm! He was too anemic! The doctor said he’d need a blood transfusion! But they’re in short supply! They only had enough to give him, just to spare some time, so they can try and get more!” She choked on her words. “He has rheumatoid arthritis! He needs it! And I don’t have the same blood type as him! I…” She growled out in frustration.

    Rio kissed the top of her head, holding her close as she rubbed her arms and gently rocked her from side to side.

    “What’s his blood type?”

    “O-negative….“ She cried.

    Of course, his blood type was the highest in demand. Considering it’s the universal donor. That meant any other blood type could receive it. But the problem was that people with O-negative blood could only receive the same blood type and only that one.

    “I have the same type. I’ll donate mine.”

    Agatha sat back with wide eyes. “Rio I don’t know if I can ask you to do that! That’s a lot!”

    “I’m not offering! I’m telling!” Her voice was stern. “I don’t care for a moment of pain. If this saves him I’ll do it!” She looked back at the boy and sighed. She pulled away from Agatha and leaned over him to kiss his forehead. “I’m not just doing this for you. I… I care about him, so much!” She pushed some of his hair out of his face. “I’m going to let the doctors know. I’ll be right back.”

    Agatha nodded, “Thank you, my love!”

    After signing a bunch of consent forms they hooked Rio up to a needle and started drawing her blood.

    She didn’t want Agatha to know, but she hated getting blood drawn. She had a fear of needles as a child and while it subsided for the most part, stuff like I.V.’s and blood work still managed to get to her.

    It was funny considering she had a few tattoos on her body and her ears were pierced. She even had a nose piercing for a while.

    She let out a shaky sigh as her head fell to the side.

    She was starting to feel light-headed. Whether or not it was from getting the blood sucked from her body or the anxiety and stress… she wasn’t sure. But right now her vision was blurring a bit and she was starting to feel cold and prickly. She closed her eyes as she felt her mind drift.

    “Rio?”

    The worry in Agatha’s voice grabbed her attention. She hummed in response but didn’t open her eyes.

    Agatha furrowed her brows and grabbed her hand. “Hey, look at me.” Her voice was soft as she rubbed her thumb against her palm.

    “W-wha…” Rio took a deep breath. She just felt so tired. She wanted this to be over already. The needle was beginning to ache in her inner elbow. But she’d do this forever if it meant saving Nicky.

    “Baby, hey.” Agatha tilted her face toward her. “Open your eyes come on. It’s okay. I’m here.” She leaned forward and kissed her forehead. Rio felt so clammy, that it worried the younger woman. “Rio, do you need some water? Here.” She opened the bottle and held it to the woman’s lips. “Come on baby drink.” She supported her head and tilted it back some. Rio opened her lips and allowed some of the water pour down her throat. It helped relax her. She lifted her good arm and grabbed the bottle. Gulping the water down fast.

    “Hey, honey take it easy. I don’t want you to choke.” She reached out toward her.

    Rio wiped her mouth while catching her breath. Her eyes finally opened. She groaned. “Fuck! Ugh! I need a nap after this!”

    The younger woman wasn’t sure what to do. She felt bad that Rio was going through this pain for her.

    For Nicky.

    Her mind drifted, and she glanced at the floor. The guilt she felt etched across her features. But before she could sink deep into her pit of despair, a hand lifted her chin. Her blue eyes met a concerned brown. “What’s going on in that head of yours?”

    Agatha gave her a nervous smile. “It’s… nothing.”

    Rio shook her head. “Not nothing. You’re upset. Is it because of this?” She held up her arm. “It’s okay really. I chose to do this!” She slid her thumb across her cheek. “I’m happy to help. I mean it. It’s okay Agatha. Don’t blame yourself and don’t feel bad.”

    Agatha nodded. “Of course. You’re right. I’m just… you don’t know how much I appreciate this! I just wish I could make this less of a pain for you.” Rio offered a small smile. An attempt to comfort her. “I’m a tough girl.” Agatha sighed and moved forward to kiss her with all of the passion she could muster, to show her gratitude. She’d do anything for Rio! Anything for the woman saving her son.

    She pulled back just enough to press her forehead to the older woman’s and gazed into her eyes. “What do I need to do to show you how grateful I am?” “Hm…” Rio thought about it for a moment. “Oh!” She beamed. “Keep being your cute adorable self!”

    Agatha quirked a brow. “Seriously, Rio. What can I do to show you my gratitude?”

    Rio shrugged. “I just want you to be happy. I don’t need anything in return.” She paused for a moment. “Just your heart.” She looked over at Nicky. “And his.”

    It took a while for the blood to be processed and prepared for safe use. But luckily the small bag lasted them long enough until they were able to add another one.

    Agatha rested her head in her hand as she sat at her son’s bedside, muttering hushed pleas to no one in particular. She clung to his cold hand, squeezing it gently as if willing warmth back into him.

    Rio had left to get a change of clothes for Agatha and some food. Even though Agatha argued that she wasn’t hungry, Rio stressed the importance of consistent meals. She explained that not eating would only make her feel worse. The older woman begged and pleaded. But those damn puppy dog eyes were what got her!

    So she folded and allowed her to get her something to eat.

    The room was quiet, save for the faint sound of Nicky’s breathing, which brought Agatha a fragile sense of calm. She choked back a sob as she climbed into the bed beside her son, wrapping herself around him. Resting her head on his chest, she listened to the steady rhythm of his heartbeat. She started humming the melody of a lullaby she used to sing to him. She didn’t hear it when Rio walked in.

    The woman stopped in the doorway, feeling as if she was intruding. Like she was witnessing something that was meant to be private. She continued standing there until Agatha stopped humming, then moved the moment she heard a sob.

    “Baby I’m back.” She approached the bed and sat the bags down. Agayha wiped her tears quickly, before sitting up and offering the other woman a small smile. “Thank you for getting this stuff. You’re so sweet.” Her voice was strained from all of her crying.

    Rio sighed and sat down in the chair next the bed. “I’m here, okay? I’m not going anywhere. I’ll stay as long as you want me to.”

    Agatha nodded.

    Rio placed a comforting hand on her knee.

    They both ended up spending the night at the hospital. Agatha slept in the bed with Nicky, careful not to jostle his injured arm as she settled in beside him.

    Rio, slept on the convertible couch near the giant window, which overlooked a wooded area. It would have been a beautiful sight to admire, if not for the circumstances that had brought them there.

    Rio knew Agatha was struggling to sleep. She had been too nervous, to scared that something would happen while she was unconscious. The constant beeping of his heart monitor was the only thing keeping her sane in that moment.

    Rio made herself sleep. She knew she’d need to be well-rested in the morning.

    But eventually, the fatigue got to Agatha and she fell asleep.

    “Momma?”

    Agatha’s eyes shot open. She turned quickly and gasped when she saw her son’s eyes staring back at hers.

    “Nicky!”

    She hugged him.

    Rio was at their side in a moment. “Hey, buddy!”

    The boy groaned. “What happened? Where am I?”

    Agatha pulled back. “Baby you got hurt at recess. You got tired and fell. You broke your arm. But the doctors fixed it and put a cast on it. So it’ll heal in no time okay!”

    Nicky looked down at his arm. He hadn’t realized the cast was even there. He smiled and looked back up at his mother. “Can I have my classmates sign it!?”

    Agatha let out an amused chuckle. Of course, Nicky would find light in a bad situation. “Of course baby. I’ll get you some markers.”

    After getting looked over for a bit the doctor released Nicky. His anemia was now gone and all that was left was to allow his arm time to heal. They prescribed him iron supplements and a strong pain reliever before sending him on his way.

    He was excited at the prospect of being wheeled out of the hospital.

    When they arrived home Agatha made him a comfy bed on the couch so she could keep an eye on him. After he got comfortable she handed him a popsicle and combed her fingers through his hair.

    “So I don’t gotta go to school for a few days?” He asked, between licking the frozen dessert.

    Agatha nodded. “Yes. But that just means catching up on online classes mister!”

    Nicky groaned. “Schools boring!”

    “Oh come on! You’re good at your classwork!”

    “It’s still boring! I only like art and lunch! Sometimes gym!” “Well, you have to go. It’s important! Now, when you’re done with that I want you to lay back and rest! You need to allow your body time to heal!” Nicky nodded. He was still pretty tired.“Momma! My arm is hurting!” He whined.

    Agatha sighed and sat by his feet. “I know baby! But you have to wait to take your medicine! It’s too soon! They already gave you some in your IV at the hospital.”

    Nicky’s lip wobbled as he held back his tears. “It hurts!” Agatha held her head for a moment as she tried thinking. She reached out for her son and rubbed soothing circles on his legs. “I know baby! I promise you can have some medicine in a few hours! Just relax okay? Don’t think about it! Do you want me to bring Sẽnor Scratchy in here to keep you company?”

    Nicky nodded.

    “Okay, I’ll be right back.”

    The woman ran up the steps quickly. Before coming down with a large portable cage. She set it down on the coffee table and opened it. Nicky leaned forward to grab him but Agatha held out her hand. “Hey, wait. I’ll bring him to you.”

    Nicky groaned in frustration but sat back.

    His mother pulled out their pet rabbit and carefully sat him down on his lap. She rubbed his head to keep him calm. “There. Doesn’t that help?” Nicky nodded and sniffled. “Yeah! I missed him! My bunny!” “He’s our familiar, remember?”

    Nicky nodded with a smile! “Our coven of two! Plus Scratchy! The magical bunny!”

    Agatha chuckled. “That’s right! And this cutie has magical healing abilities to make you feel better! So believe in him and give him time for his magic to work.”

    Nicky nodded. “I will Momma.”

    She smiled before taking the rabbit back and putting him in his cage. “Okay, honey I’ll leave him here. But you get some sleep, okay?” Nicky smiled and laid back. “Okay, Momma. I love you!”

    “I love you too, baby!”

    Agatha struggled to relax. Her constant worrying clouded her judgment and any rational thinking.

    She ultimately decided to clean the kitchen and dining room; which were next to the living room. She constantly peeked in to check on him. Letting out a sigh of relief everytime she saw the rise and fall of his chest. She went back to the kitchen and swept the floor for the third time. It really didn’t need it. But what else was she going to do?

    Her mind constantly wondered.

    The worry and anxiety began to eat up at her.

    What if Nicky didn’t wake up?

    What if Rio didn’t have the same blood type?

    What if she hadn't even shown up at all?

    Her phone went off, pulling her back to relaity.

    She answered it without looking at the caller ID, assuming it was her girlfriend.

    “Rio? Did you make it home okay?”

    “Who? Agatha, it’s me, your mother!”

    All the blood from her face drained. Her mother’s voice was horribly nostalgic in the worst possible way. It‘d been a while since she’d spoken to her.

    “Oh, sorry. How… have you been, Mom?”

    “I heard Nicky got hurt! I’m coming up!”

    “Oh… there’s no need! He’s okay! Really!”

    “Nonsense! Besides, this works out for Thanksgiving.”

    “That’s in three weeks.”

    “And…? I’ll just stay with you until then. You do have a guest room, correct?”

    “I… yeah, but w-we could have an early Thanksgiving… if you want. It’s just, I have a lot of work to catch up on and I’d hate to leave you in this house all by yourself.” It was all a lie. Agatha just didn’t want her to come. “Oh, I’ll be fine! I could even help with some of your decorations! Bring something festive and fun to hang up. It’ll make Nicky smile. I also wanted to bring his Christmas gift and yours.”

    And yours?

    Her mother stopped giving her presents when she turned sixteen. The last thing she ever received was a blue backpack for school, even though she already had a purple one that she’d bought herself with money from her part-time job. It felt like she wasn’t allowed to like anything on her own— not unless her mother approved.

    Agatha groaned, her fists clenched until her nails dug into her palms. A headache was already forming at her temples.

    “Darling, I need to let you go,” her mother’s clipped voice cut through the line, tinged with impatience. “But I’ll call back in a bit.” “Okay… bye, Mom.” Agatha’s voice was flat, barely disguising her frustration. She hung up and let the phone slip from her fingers onto the counter.

    Pressing her hands against her face, she let out a slow, shaky breath. The thought of her mother coming over early—under the pretense of checking on Nicky’s injury—was enough to tie her stomach in knots. It wasn’t about Thanksgiving, or even concern for her grandson. Her mother would swoop in with that familiar blend of criticism and false cheer, finding fault in everything from the state of the house to the way she raised her son. Agatha scrubbed her face with her palms and muttered, “I don’t have time for this.”

    A moment later her phone rang, she sighed before answering it. “What?” She snapped, agitated that her mom was calling back so soon. “Agatha? I-Is everything alright? Are you upset with me?” Her face fell.

    It was just Rio!

    Her sweet and innocent Rio!

    “No! No, no! You’ve done nothing wrong!! You’ve been perfect! More than perfect! I’m sorry! I just got off the phone with my mother and I thought she was calling back.”

    “Oh? Its okay! Did something happen?”

    “She wants to come see Nicky and stay for the holidays.”

    She could hear Rio pause on the other end. Before she could even think to speak Agatha explained, “If you ask why that upsets me well… you haven’t met my mother. She’s controlling, to say the least.”

    “Do you wanna talk about it?”

    Agatha sighed. “Not in earshot of Nicky. She’s just… we didn’t get along much growing up. She tries to act like she’s changed since Nicky’s birth, but… I don’t want to believe in fairytales.”

    “That sounds tough. I don’t know her but if you think she hasn’t changed then maybe you should do what’s best for you and Nicky.”

    Agatha groaned. She peeked out into the living room to check on her son. He was still asleep, which was a relief.

    She went into the bathroom and closed the door so he couldn’t hear, in case he woke up. “The problem is I’m not sure. I mean she hasn’t exactly been around much. But I also never really wanted her here so I wasn’t surprised. I guess her not making an effort upset me a bit even if I didn’t want to see her. But every year she’d send Nicky a present for Christmas and his birthday. She’s even helped pay off some of his medical bills before I was able to do it on my own.”

    “Well if you decide to have her come over I can… be there for you. I-If you want? If you‘ like to introduce me to your mom? I’m interested in meeting the person who raised such an amazing woman!”

    Part of her longed to introduce Rio to her mother—to say, This is my girlfriend, the woman I love, the person who saved my son. She wanted her mother’s approval, even if she didn’t need it. But, she knew none of that was a good idea.

    “Trust me when I say I raised myself most of the time growing up. And whatever bible-bumping stuff she tried jamming down my throat I would just spit out the moment she looked away. She never wanted me to be my own person and I’m sure that’s still the case. She wants me to basically be a copy of herself or else I’m not perfect. If I’m not her definition of a saint then I’m evil.”

    “That’s ridiculous! In what universe are you, Agatha Harkness, evil? You’re so kind and generous. Even when you try to put on a mask. Don’t think I didn’t notice! You pay all your employees ridiculously well and give them amazing benefits. Not to mention your son is the definition of good! Maybe when she sees how happy you are she’ll forget about all that stuff?” “Did Alice tell you what I'm paying people!?” Agatha grumbled before continuing. “And that’s not how she works, I’m afraid,” she sighed. “I hate that Nicky hasn’t gotten to see his grandmother much. I’d like for them to have a good relationship, regardless of how she treated me growing up. Usually, bad parents try to make up for their mistakes by being better grandparents.”

    She paused, her breath unsteady. “The only thing is… Rio, I can’t—I can’t tell her what you are to me. She’s not accepting of the LGBT community, and she’d go ballistic if she found out.”

    Agatha’s voice wavered, her words tumbling out in a rush. “I’m not embarrassed by being with you, so please don’t think that for a second! I love you so much! I just… I don’t want her to hurt you too.” “I… I understand, baby. I’m not upset,” Rio said gently. “I can play the best friend.
