It wouldn't be the first time.” She let out an awkward laugh, reminiscing about her teen years. “It’s not easy falling for a straight girl, especially when she’s your friend.”

    The comment managed to pull a genuine chuckle from Agatha. “I can relate,” she admitted with a small smile. Then, her expression softened. “I just… I wish I’d met you sooner. We would’ve had more time together.” “I wish we had too,” Rio said, her voice steady. “But if we spend too much time looking back, we’ll miss what’s ahead. And believe me, I’m looking forward to our future. A long one. Like really long!”

    “Yeah? You proposing?” Agatha teased, her tone playful.

    Rio scoffed. “No way!”

    Agatha’s smile faltered, she let out a small sound of genuine offense. “Oh.” Rio panicked, picking up on the shift in her voice. “No, I didn't mean it like that! Ugh, I was going to say I want to take my time with you first! And I’d never do it in such a roundabout way—or over the phone! I’d ask the actual question and make it special.”

    Agatha exhaled, the clarification easing her sudden worry. “I don’t need a grand gesture, you know. Just asking would be enough.”

    “Yeah well… don’t be surprised if I propose on the Eiffel Tower or at Disney World! And definitely don’t be surprised if you find a ring in your champagne glass!”

    Agatha groaned. “Oh please not the hiding the ring in the food or drinks bit! It’s like your asking for your partner to choke!”

    Rio giggled like a little school girl with a crush. “You’re so cute! Hey! So, can you do me a favor?”

    Agatha quirked a brow. “Me? Cute? And sure what is it?”

    “Open your front door for me.”

    “Rio!” Agatha squealed excitedly, before running out of the bathroom.

    She ended up biting the bullet and agreed to let her mother stay for a few days. But stressed that it was only for a few days.

    She was nervous, to say the least.

    Nicky didn’t know.

    No one knew.

    Only she and her mother knew of the brutal treatment she received growing up.

    She covered her bodily scars the best she could. But she would never be able to erase the ones inside her heart and mind.”

    The two women stood in the foyer awaiting her arrival.

    Rio held Agatha’s hand tightly for a moment before stepping away. The younger woman opened the door and gave a small smile to the woman who birthed her.

    “There’s my darling girl!” Her mother smiled and moved in for a hug. Agatha flinched before relaxing. She hovered her hands over her back unsure what to do with them, before resting them lightly over her shoulders. She stared off into empty space.

    This was… weird.

    “Hello, Grandma!” Nicky said excitedly as he came into the foyer. Evanora pulled away and giggled. “Hello, little one! Oh, look how big you’ve grown!” She hugged him gently. “My poor boy look at you. Are you alright?”

    He nodded. “Yeah, I’m gonna have everyone in my class sign my cast when I go back! I was so strong! Rio told me so!” He smiled up at the woman who was standing off to the side, nervously.

    Evanora’s gaze followed and she squinted for a moment. Taking in the woman’s… style. Then she turned and glanced at Agatha, to see her daughter avoiding her gaze. “I don’t believe I’ve had the pleasure.” She turned back toward Rio and held out her hand. “Evanora Harkness. Agatha’s mother and Nicky’s grandmother.”

    Rio smiled and took her hand. “Rio Vidal! I’m Agatha’s… friend.” “Hm, and what do you do Ms Vidal?”

    “Oh, I run my own business!”

    Evanora quirked a brow. This interested her. “Is that so? And what kind of business exactly?”

    “Oh um…” Rio rubbed the back of her neck nervously. “I run… a funeral home and a flower shop with a friend of mine. I’m a mortician and a florist.”

    She expected the old woman to be put off by this. But instead, she just nodded. “Funerals are a tough time for families. Gives a person the opportunity to reflect on the time they've had with the one they’ve lost and to connect with god. A noble job. Not many could stomach it. But I’m sure you’re used to death.” There was a hint of judgment in her words. Before Rio could even respond Evanora breezed right past her. Agatha gave her a sympathetic look, and while her mother made her way into the dining room, she squeezed her hand and gave her a small smile. “I’m sorry.”

    Rio shook her head. “No apoligizing, I want to be here.”

    After a very tense dinner, they all retreated to the living room to relax. Evanora handed Agatha and Nicky their gifts.

    Agatha waited for Nicky to open his first before opening her own.

    He excitedly ripped the paper off but his smile fell when he saw what he got.

    Agatha held her head in her hand and suppressed a frustrated groan. “It’s an action comic retelling of the Bible! I know how you kids like your superheroes. And what better superhero than Jesus Christ himself!” His grandmother exclaimed excitedly.

    Nicky stared down at it. “Uh… thanks, Grandma.”

    She handed him another box. “Here one more.”

    It was smaller. Nicky opened this one hesitantly, unsure that he’d get something he liked. But was blown away when he saw what it was. “An iPhone!” He jumped up in the air excitedly. “Look, Momma!” He held up in front her.

    “Oh, I see it!” She said with an obvious agitation.

    To say she was pissed was an understatement. She didn’t want her son to have a phone, at least a smartphone. She was fine giving him a simple flip phone, but he never asked for one so she never worried about it. She just didn’t want to spoil him like and have him become addicted to it. Not to mention the inappropriate stuff he could potentially see on it. Not that she couldn’t parent lock it. But she had planned to get him one when he turned fourteen.

    “So you can keep in touch with your mother and watch those… what do you call them, tiktaks?”

    “TikTok.” Nicky corrected. “I’ve only seen a couple.”

    “Great! But who’s paying the phone bill?” Agatha suggested. “Why you of course.” Evanora smiled. “Merry Christmas my darling boy!” “Thank you, Grandma!” He jumped up and hugged her.

    Agatha eventually opened hers. She wasn’t surprised to see it was disappointing and not thoughtful at all. She knew that it was the thought that counts, but what’s the point if her mother was just going to give her something so ridiculous?

    It was a self-help book for women approaching their fifties. How embarrassing!

    Her mother even handed her a mini bible. Agatha took it and tossed it in the junk drawer near by while she wasn’t looking.

    Truth be told Agatha was raised Christian. And she didn’t think anything of it. But eventually, she found it wasn’t for her. She just didn’t understand how all of her fellow church members could preach these ‘nice’ ideas, but then turn around and do the opposite. And honestly, she just didn’t like the idea of there being some divine rule book. She didn’t need dead people to tell her how to live her life. But that didn’t mean she wouldn’t allow Nicky to believe in god if he wanted to. If anything she encouraged it, at least mildly. She just didn’t shove all the rules down his throat. If he ever came to her questioning it she’d just tell him to believe in what he wanted, regardless of what she thought. As long as he’s a good person that’s all that mattered.

    To attempt easing some of the tension Rio generously baked them some dessert. She made a homemade apple pie and boy did Nicky love it. He scarfed it down and asked for seconds.

    After a bit, Agatha suggested Nicky go to bed, he groaned but nodded. Rio offered to tuck him in and with a smile Agatha agreed. She gave her son a good night kiss before he went upstairs.

    It gave her mother the opportunity to say something.

    “His hair is long.” She muttered from across the table.

    “Yes.” Agatha replied simply, while pushing a piece of pie around on her plate.

    “He looks like a girl!” Her mother groaned.

    Agatha rubbed her temples before quickly responding. “No, he looks like a boy with long hair.”

    “That’s not right. You aren’t pushing… any alternative lifestyles onto him are you?”

    Agatha looked up at her in disbelief. “If you’re asking if I’m making my son trans or gay the answer is no! I’m allowing him to be himself!” “It looks ridiculous! I’m sure the other boys at the school make fun of him!”

    “A lot of his classmates like it actually. Not that he should need their approval.”

    “God this generation!” Evanaora threw her hands up in the air in frustration. “Why does it matter? Jesus had long hair and you love him!” “That was a long time ago!”

    “And yet you still preach old-fashioned beliefs! So which is it?” They sat in silence for a moment.

    Evanora tapped her fingers against the table anxiously before speaking, “Have you at least baptized the boy?”

    “No.”

    “Why!?”

    “Because I’m not worried about it.”

    “Fine.” She gave up. “He’s not my child. Do what you think is right!” Agatha wasn’t sure how to respond to that.

    “I just want what’s best for you two. Agatha, I… I’ve missed you, sweetie. You and Nicky.” She reached out for her hand. “I want to come around more. Be more involved in his life.”

    She’d never heard her mother say she missed her, before. “You have four days to prove to me you’ve changed.”

    She nodded. “Okay.”

    ——

    The next few days went surprisingly well. Evanora bonded with her grandson and daughter. It was like a dream come true. There were no fights. No tension. Just a happy family.

    The two Harkness women sat in the living room late one evening and chatted.

    “I’m proud of you Agatha. You’ve done amazing with the company. Your father would be proud.”

    Agatha looked down at her lap and smiled. “Thanks, mom.”

    The whole thing was a mixed bag. That was probably the first time her mother had ever said she was proud of her. But proud for something Agatha never wanted to do… it was confusing.

    “So tell me what have you been up to lately honey.”

    “Oh, you know just working and being a mom. Not a lot of time to do much of anything else.”

    “Aw, now you know how I felt raising you alone. Juggling a job and a child isn’t easy. It’s hard work.”

    “Yeah, but I love spending time with Nicky. He’s an amazing boy! I don’t know how I got so lucky!”

    Her mother hummed. “You did good raising him. He’s a smart and kind young man!”

    Agatha’s eyes sparkled. “Thanks, I appreciate it!”

    Things were going well. After their talk, Evanora stopped commenting anything passive-aggressive or on something Agatha did or didn’t do. She just spent time with her daughter and grandson.

    They were finally getting ready for their big dinner.

    Their own little Thanksgiving one.

    Evanora didn’t let her daughter see the small frown on her face when that woman came back.

    “Hey, I made macaroni! And more apple pie!” Rio said excitedly to Agatha. “Sounds deli—“ “Yes!!!!!” Nicky came running into the living room. Almost skidding to the side with how fast he was running. “Rio! What’s up!” He went in front of her and hugged her with one arm.

    “Aw, why don’t you hug me when my hands aren’t full, bud?” “Here I’ll take something.” Agatha reached for a bag so Rio could hug him back.

    “Dang, you found my weakness! Normally I’d carry these all myself, but I must hug this cutie pie!”

    Finally everything was finished and laid out beautifully on the table. Rio smiled brightly at the spread. “Wow! You guys did an awesome job!” “I helped!” Nicky said with a bright smile.

    Rio chuckled and tussled his hair around. “You did awesome kid!”

    And then ther was one small thing that agitated Agatha, but she just let it pass.

    “Let’s say a prayer.”

    “Sure.” She said flatly, with no enthusiasm as she extended her arm out for her mother to take.

    Evanora looked over at her grandson. “You too sweetie.”

    “Oh.” He had to shift awkwardly to take her hand with his good arm. “Maybe you could just touch his shoulder?” Agatha suggested, trying to help her son out, considering he looked uncomfortable.

    “Hm, you’re right. Relax darling.” Evanora leaned over a bit and rested her hand on him and closed her eyes.

    Nicky smiled at his mom before he reached for Rio’s hand. Rio happily took their hands and closed her eyes too. She rubbed soothing circles against Agatha's palm. The little sigh she heard made her smile. But even better was the little huff of air the younger woman let out when she slid her foot up her leg, beneath the table.

    She opened one eye and smirked. Seeing Agatha looking directly at her. Quirking a brow before smiling and shaking her head. She squeezed her hand, glanced at her mother for a moment to make sure her eyes were still shut, and turned to mouth ‘I love you’ to her. Rio happily mouthed it back but continued sliding her foot against the woman.

    “Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You for the delicious food and the wonderful people in our lives. On this day of thanks, all of my gratitude extends to You. I’m thankful for my daughter, my grandson, and the wonderful life they’ve built together. For the friends they’ve made along the w—”

    Thud!

    Agatha’s knee hit the underside of the table as her body jerked, cutting her mother off mid-sentence. The older woman glanced in her direction, her gaze lingering just long enough to notice the redness spreading across her face.

    But she said nothing. With a small pause, she continued on with her prayer. Agatha’s heart pounded in her chest, and she was thankful her mother didn’t notice the foot creeping beneath the hem of her sweater.

    “Thank you for everything you do Father. Amen!”

    Agatha and Rio said “Amen” after her, before they let go of each others hands.

    Evanora turned to Nicky, noticing her didn't say it. “Sweetheart, you’re supposed to say ‘Amen’ after a prayer.”

    “Oh.” He hesitated, then quickly added, “Amen.”

    This earned a chuckle from Agatha and Rio, but was short-lived by Agatha letting out a small squeal and jumping again.

    “Are you alright sweetie?” Her mother asked.

    Agatha nodded quickly, staring down at her plate.

    Evanora glanced in Rio’s direction, expecting to catch her doing something odd. But to her surprise, she was simply eating.

    Unbeknownst to her, Rio’s foot was pressed firmly against her daughter’s upper thigh, inching slowly towards her center beneath the table. Agatha grabbed her foot, stopping its slow but sure pursuit, and slid her hand inside her pant leg to massage the muscle there. She glanced in Rio’s direction and caught the corners of her lips lifting into a small smile as she ate. Acting as if she was doing nothing, absolutely wrong and she totally wasn’t playing footsie at the table.

    “Yum! Rio this pie is so good!” Nicky smiled as he shoveled a bunch of pie into his mouth.

    “Aw! Thank you! Learned the recipe in college.”

    The group enjoyed the meal together. Everything was fine and Agatha was pleasantly surprised. Evanora even gave her a compliment or two. Plus she mentioned how she found it impressive that Rio was able to have such a successful business right out of college.

    She watched her son tell his imaginative stories that he created, making everyone laugh at his charming antics, as he acted out the different characters and scenes.

    After a while the evening started to die down a bit.

    Rio headed for the door and sat down to put her boots on. “Nicky I think it’s time for bed honey.”

    “Aw, do I really have to go!?” The boy frowned.

    “Yes, I’ll tuck you in.”

    “I could do it. If that’s okay?” Evanora spoke up.

    Agatha turned, surprised at her mother’s offer. “Oh, uh.” She turned back toward Nicky. “You want grandma to tuck you in buddy?”

    Nicky looked at his mother unsure. He glanced over at his grandma and saw the hopeful look on her face then he turned back to his mom and gave her a small smile then nodded.

    “Alright, well say bye to Rio.”

    Nicky’s face lit up again.

    Rio adjusted her jacket on her shoulders while standing at the door waiting for the boy.

    He ran over to her and tried his best to hug her with one arm. “Bye Rio! Can’t wait to see you again soon!”

    “I’ll be counting the minutes bud.”

    The boy let her go and gave her one more smile before running upstairs. Agatha sighed. “Nicky no running! Especially with that arm!” Evanora chuckled lightly. “I guess that’s my cue.” She glanced over in Rio’s direction as she walked past her. Before turning and makimt her way up the stairs.

    Rio swore she saw her shake her head and sigh. But she didn’t want to start anything or stress Agatha out.

    They waited for the older woman to be out of sight and earshot before they moved in closer.

    Agatha giggled as Rio took her into her arms and swayed her side to side. “You look beautiful tonight! I really like seeing you in my clothes. You make my hoodie look so good! You pull it off so well!”

    Agatha snickered. “Yeah? I’m glad you enjoy it because you’re not getting this back!” she glanced down at her lips.

    Rio let out an amused chuckle before leaning in.

    Evanora peaked around the corner, looking for any sign of the young boy. She noticed a colorful light coming from underneath a door frame and sure enough, there were letters across the door that said ‘Nicky’ she knocked and waited for a soft come in, before entering.

    “Hi, Grandma.”

    “Hello, darling.” She looked around for a moment. She clearly felt awkward and out of place here, but she decided to just deal with the awkwardness and sit on his bed. She noticed the opened book on his nightstand and pointed to it. “Have you been reading honey?” Nicky followed her gaze and then smiled. He looked back up at her and nodded. “Yes, I have!”

    Evanora noticed some cartoony characters on the back. She wasn’t sure what it was. “That’s good darling. You’re doing well in school?” Nicky nodded. “Yes. I almost get straight A’s.”

    “Oh? Why almost?” She paused but noticing the nervousness on his face she decided to add. “I’m sure whatever it is you can work on over time. It’s not the end of the world.”

    “It’s… math,” He sighed. “Everything else isn’t too difficult. Boring, but not difficult. Math is overwhelming.”

    Evanora nodded. “I understand. Don’t worry honey you’ll get it. Can I ask you something?”

    Nicky nodded.

    “Is… that Rio woman... Is she nice to you?”

    Nicky’s face lit up at the mention of Rio. He didn’t pick up on her flash of distaste.

    “Yes! Rio is the best! She’s so nice! She’s Momma's best friend! We do lots of stuff together!”

    Nicky wasn’t suspicious of them? He didn’t know of his mother’s…. past preferences? Good. Evanora thought.

    “Oh, what kind of stuff do you do together?” She quirked her brow. “Lots of stuff! We went camping with friends! Sang songs and ate marshmallows! We went to an escape room and solved so many puzzles! One time we went to an arcade! Rio won a giant piggy for me! There’s more stuff too! She’s the best!”

    Evanora nodded, she heard all she needed. “Would you like me to read you a story before bed?”

    “Sure!”

    The pair smiled as she tried her best to act out the characters in the book. Nicky would even jump in for fun.

    After almost a half hour she sighed. “Well, I think it’s time for bed.” She closed the book and smiled. “You sleep well okay my dear.” Nicky nodded. “Thank you, grandma! I love you!”

    The woman froze at the admission before softening. “I love you too, my darling.” She kissed him on the cheek before shutting his door. She stopped at the top of the stairs trying to listen for any talking. When she didn’t hear anything she quietly made her way down into the foyer. She glanced around. Scanning the room for any sign of her daughter, when she caught movement through the little window beside the door. She squinted before making her way to one of the windows. She slid one of the blinds up and sneered when she saw her daughter outside kissing that woman. And it wasn’t a simple goodbye peck. They were making out. She snarled and looked away.

    Agatha giggled as Rio kissed her passionately. Then softly sighed into the kiss. “Rio, someone could see!”

    “Then let’s take it outside.” She smirked, tugging her girlfriend toward the door.

    Agatha’s breath shook before she nodded.

    They made their way outside but didn’t kiss right away. Instead, they just enjoyed each other's company surrounded by the stars.

    “It’s such a beautiful night!” Agatha smiled up at the sky. Rio couldn’t take her eyes off the woman. “Yeah,” She sighed, “so beautiful!” She noticed Agatha had her arms wrapped around herself and she frowned for a moment. She moved behind her and opened the front door to grab a jacket and draped it over her shoulders before shutting it. She didn’t back away. Instead, she rubbed her hands up and down Agatha’s arms to warm her up. “I don’t want you to catch a cold! Not on my watch!” Agatha hugged the jacket close to herself and smiled. “You’re such a gentlewoman!”

    Rio grinned, “I know I am, baby!” She slid her arms around her waist and pulled her in close.

    “Thank you again, Rio!”

    Rio tilted her head. “For what?” She had a feeling as to what it could be. Agatha snickered. “For coming to the hospital even though you were working. For saving my son’s life the other day.”

    Rio smiled and pressed her forehead to Agatha’s. “You needed me. Work could wait, you both come first. It’s simple, I love him, and I’ll always take care of you both. You call, and I’ll come. Okay?”

    A tear fell down Agatha’s cheek. How was this woman real? She was perfect.

    “Oh, baby don’t cry!” Rio wiped the stray tear away.

    “I love you!” Agatha breathed out passionately then pulled her in for a heated kiss.

    Rio was caught off guard for a moment before she relaxed into it. A small moan escaped from her lips encouraging Agatha further.

    “God, Rio! You’re amazing!” She slid her arms around her shoulders and littered kisses down her neck.

    Rio had to suppress a chuckle. She could see her breath in front of her from the cold. “Oh, Agatha!” She could handle this. It was dark enough, she was wearing thick pants. She allowed herself a moment of selfishness. She held her tighter with one arm and moved the other up to caress her face, bringing her back to her lips and pushing her against the front door. It was practically a battle of whose tongue could dominate who and Agatha was struggling. Her knees began to shake. Rio slid an arm down and groped her ass, pulling a shaky moan from Agatha.

    Agatha was losing it. She didn’t know what to do with her hands. She slid them in front of Rio and gripped at the material of her shirt. “Rio! My darling!” Her voice came out in a hushed whisper, she had to put a hand over her own mouth to stifle her moans as Rio moved to her neck to suck on her pulse point. She licked a sensitive spot that made her weak in the knees.

    She noticed this and continued. She groaned at the sounds of Agatha’s desperation and squeezed her ass even harder.

    The kiss was getting heated, fast. Rio was afraid she’d lose control. She needed to stop tat. But god she wanted nothing more than to comtinie! Agatha was warm! She smelled so good! Her sounds of pleasure were music to her ears! The way her body shook drove her insane! All of it!! She didn’t want it to end but…

    She sighed as her hand on her ass slid up to the small of her back and she pulled away from her neck. “As much as I’d love to keep doing this, we’re outside and…”

    “My mother’s inside.” Agatha sighed too. “I know.”

    Rio gave her a small smile. “I’ll text you when I get home. I love you, Aggie.”

    “I love you, my Rio.”

    They shared one last passionate kiss before Rio turned and made her way toward her truck.

    Agatha was all smiles when she walked back into her house. She felt like a schoolgirl with a crush. It was innocent, and not at the same time and she loved it. She had to slow her heartbeat before making her way into the kitchen to clean up.

    She hummed a tune as she put the leftover food away and the dirty dishes in the sink. She felt so light and free! Rio had that effect on her. She made her feel like she could do anything.

    “You’re cheery this evening.”

    The sound of her mother’s voice couldn’t bring her spirits down. The last couple of days have been… nice.

    “I’m having an amazing night!” Agatha smiled, her happiness filling her heart as she began to turn, ready to share more with her mother. But before she could, a sudden sharp pain shot across her cheek, sending her tumbling to the floor with a startled cry.

    She barely had time to clutch her burning cheek or even register the raging anger in her mother’s eyes before she was struck again and again. Each slap was a brutal reminder that her mother still hated her.

    “I thought we were past this! But no! I see you’re still a disappointment!” Evanora continued with her punishment. Each strike harder than the last. Agatha tried to move, but her mother gripped her hair tightly, slamming her hand across her cheek again and again as she growled, “I tried with you! So hard! I didn’t say anything when you got pregnant before marriage! Because at least I knew my daughter had finally done the right thing and picked a man! But now you bring that woman here! You let her do that filth where your own son can see! You’re a damn slut! A disgusting dyke! How many times am I going to have to teach you this lesson before you learn!?” The harsh sounds echoed throughout the house.

    Agatha whimpered with each blow, but finally, the pain became too much and she cried out loudly.

    Rapid footsteps approached the kitchen.

    “Momma!” Nicky screamed.

    Evanora turned and saw her grandson in the doorway, her eyes widened. Nicky was shaking, tears streaming down his face. Even in his fearful state he immediately rusher over to his mother’s side and cradled her beaten face in his arms, protectively. He shielded her with his cast. Endearing the pain to comfort and protect her.

    “Grandma! Why are you hurting momma!?” he shouted, looking up at her. The fury in her eyes hadn’t left. “Move!” She growled with a warning. “No!” He shouted back. “Stop it!”

    “Dammit, boy!” She held her hand up ready to hit him too. Nicky flinched and cried, covering his face with his good hand. “No! Please!”

    But when she went to swing her arm down, she couldn’t. A hand curled tightly around her wrist, stopping her movement. She turned her head, but before she could even process who it was, a hand pressed to her throat, shoving her against the counter off to the side.

    “Rio!” Nicky cried out.

    Rio got close to Evanora’s face, and with a shaky but eerily calm breath, she said, “Leave!”

    Her face, however, was anything but calm. Tears welled in her eyes, and she looked ready to kill Evanora. But still, her voice remained unsettlingly calm, though the venom beneath was unmistakable.

    “How dare you! You dy—“ She slammed her hand against the counter, her voice still calm and low as she spoke through her teeth. “I will not make a scene in front of him! Leave now or I will call the police!”

    The situation was unbearable for her, especially when all she could hear was Agatha’s quiet, painful sobbing and Nicky’s frightened whimpers. Out of the corner of her eye, she saw Agatha move to shield Nicky with her own body—a desperate act of protection. It infuriated her that Agatha even had to do that, especially from his own grandmother!

    From her mother!

    Evanora opened her mouth to speak, but before she could say anything, Rio cut her off. She moved close to Evanora's ear, her voice dropping to a threatening whisper, just loud enough for her to hear.

    "I will hurt you, if I have to!"

    Rio snarled, her lip curling as she spoke through clenched teeth, tightening her grip on Evanora's throat to emphasize her point. "Don't test me. We both know I'll win this fight, and believe me when I say, I'm holding myself back!"

    Evanora growled out. “You stupid bitch! I will ki—“ “Mother leave!”

    Agatha roared out. She had her hands clutched around Nicky’s ears and his face pressed to her chest so he couldn’t hear or see.

    They looked over at her.

    Tears streamed down Agatha’s beaten face. She was angry. So, so angry! “You’re not welcome here! Not around me! Or my son! You will not come into my house and disrespect my girlfriend either!” She breathed heavily as her voice cracked. She pulled her son closer to her body. There was so much more she wanted to say. But she would fall apart if she kept speaking. Rio's eyes widened as she took in the scene before her. Agatha's face was bright red, some of the skin bloody from the beating. The woman was trembling, clearly terrified for both herself and her son. Rio turned back to Evanora, her face darker than before. With a snarl, she grabbed Evanora's arm with her free hand and tightened her grip around her neck, dragging her toward the door.

    The woman flailed and fought her, but Rio was stronger. She was able to get her outside while keeping her retrained, and somehow managed to keep her still long enough to call the police.

    She waited.

    However long it would take she’d wait.

    “You piece of shit! You ruined everything! Agatha was done with that sinful bullshit until you came along! What did you do!? Seduce her? You filthy witch? You disgust me!” Evanora was able to break from her grip long enough to turn and punch her in the eye.

    But Rio managed to stay calm enough to get the situation back under control. The old woman continued fighting her for the five minutes it took for the police to show up.

    The police questioned the two women on the doorstep before considering to make any arrests.

    “Hello, I’m Officer Wilson. We got a call about battery and attempted battery. Is—“ he was going to ask his usual speel until he noticed Rio's black eye and Evanora’s aggression.

    “Arrest this bitch!” Evanora continued struggling. She maneuvered herself enough to slam the back of her head into Rio’s nose.

    The officer intervened and restrained Evanora. “Ma’am calm down!” Evanora continued arguing. “Why are you touching me!? Get your hands off of me! She’s the one you should arrest! She seduced my daughter this disgusting lesbian and she’s a danger around my grandson!” Rio growled at the prospect of her being a danger to Nicky. That was hilarious coming from the woman who tried beating him less than ten minutes ago.

    “Ma’am we are going to put you in the cruiser until you can calm down.” “What!? How dare you!”

    It took two of the officers to get her in the backseat. Technically they had reason enough to arrest her for failure to comply. But they wanted to get the full story so they could properly charge her.

    One of the officers stayed behind, outside the vehicle while his partner went over to talk to Rio.

    “Hello, could I get your name?”

    “Rio Vidal.”

    “And what happened here today, Rio?”

    “I was about to leave my gi— my friend’s house and was getting into my truck when I heard a strange noise. At first, I wasn’t sure what it was, so I stopped and listened. Then I realized—it was screaming. I ran back inside and followed the noise.

    “When I got there, I heard what sounded like smacking, followed by Evanora’s voice. She was screaming at Agatha, who was lying on the floor, her face bloody. She was crying in pain, and her son was screaming for his grandmother to stop.

    “I got there just in time—before she hurt him too.”

    The officer nodded, taking down notes of Rio’s account of the incident. “Was she using a weapon?”

    Rio shook her head. “No, she was beating her with her hands.” “And how long ago did this occur, exactly?”

    “About twenty minutes ago.”

    “And what is your exact relationship to… Agatha?”

    Rio's eyes widened for a moment. “Um… she—“ she let out a sigh. “She’s my girlfriend. But we haven’t told her son yet so please don’t say anything around him.”

    The officer nodded. “Of course. I understand. I have a nephew who is gay and I love him to death. I promise not to say anything in front of the kid.” Rio nodded.

    “I need to question the victim and anyone else who witnessed the fight.” Rio sighed. “Alright, but can you hang back in the foyer for a minute? I’m sure they’re shaken up. I need to let them know and make sure they’re okay.”

    The officer nodded. “Of course take all the time you need.” Rio led him inside the home, motioning for him to stay out of sight for the moment.

    Faint muttering drifted from the kitchen, making her frown. She stopped in the doorway, and her heart sank.

    Agatha was clutching Nicky tightly to her chest, with her face buried in his hair while sobbing. She hadn’t noticed Rio standing there and continued murmuring the same words: “I’m sorry, I’m sorry, I’m so sorry!”

    Nicky seemed to be crying too—silently. The only sign was the steady jerking of his small shoulders.

    Rio softly sighed before pressing her hand to her forehead. The pain from her injuries were starting to get to her.

    She tried not to think about it much. She wanted to be there for them, not worry about herself.

    She pushed away from the doorframe and crossed the room, her footsteps careful and deliberate. Lowering herself to their level, she crouched at their sides.

    For a moment, she hesitated, then placed a gentle hand on Agatha’s shoulder.

    Agatha flinched, her breathing hitched, and quickened with panic as she jumped.

    Rio recoiled, “I’m sorry! I didn’t mean to—”

    But Agatha cut her off, pulling her into a hug with Nicky nestled between them.

    “Thank you,” Agatha whispered into Rio’s hair before leaving a feather- light kiss there.

    “You don’t have to thank me. I will always protect you both.” She gently reached up and ghosted her thumb over Agatha’s cheeks.

    The younger woman whimpered.

    “My baby,” Rio whispered.

    Agatha gasped, she finally got a good look at her love.

    She was sporting a lovely black eye and bloody nose.

    Her mother was a tough bitch.

    Agatha reached out and caressed her face “Rio! Did my…” her lip quivered. “You’re bleeding!”

    “So are you.” Rio paused for a moment. “I’m okay. But, there’s an officer here. He needs to speak with you.” She sighed and looked down at the boy who was currently clinging to his mother. “Both of you.” She looked back up.

    Agatha nodded. “Okay… I just… I don’t want to go anywhere.” “He just going to talk to you here,” Rio reassured.

    Agatha had to think about it for a moment. She looked down at her son. “Nicky there’s an officer here. He needs to ask us a couple of questions, okay?”

    He nodded.

    Rio spoke up, “You can come in.”

    The cop entered the kitchen and frowned.

    Rio started helping them both to their feet, but Agatha wavered, forcing her and Nicky to steady her. The beating had left her disoriented. “Do you want me to call an ambulance?” The officer asked. Agatha shook her head, before stumbling more. The cop quickly came over and pulled out a chair. He ghosted his arms out; as they lowered her down, in case she fell out of their grip.

    “Okay, tell me what happened here.”

    Agatha sighed, she looked up at Rio and spoke, “Rio can you…” she trailed off as she nodded at Nicky.

    Rio nodded back and placed a comforting hand on his back. “Hey, buddy. Why don’t you and me go sit down on the couch for a couple minutes?” He rubbed the tears from his eyes with his good arm while sniffling. “B-but what about Momma?”

    “She’s okay, she just needs to speak with the officer.”

    He looked up at Rio and took in her honest expression before giving her a nod.

    They went and sat on the couch. Nicky didn’t say anything the whole time. He just fiddled with his cast and stared off into space.

    Rio frowned, but allowed him to just be.

    After a few minutes, the officer and Agatha came out. He assisted her over towards them.

    Rio stood up and held out her arms, helping her sit down next to Nicky. The officer smiled at the boy and crouched down in front of him. “Nicky, the officer is going to ask what happened. Do you think you can tell him?”

    Nicky took in the strange man. His breath shook, but he nodded. “Uh-huh.” “Hi, buddy. Your name’s Nicky? My name is Officer Wilson. I'm here to help you guys out. Can you just tell me a bit about what happened? You can take your time. There’s no rush.”

    The young boy turned toward his mother and moved into her arms. He spoke without looking at the man.

    “I-I heard screaming and then hitting sounds and grandma shouting mean words at Momma. I was really scared especially when I came into the kitchen and Momma was on the floor, bleeding! I begged Grandma to stop but she wouldn’t and…” his voice broke.

    Agatha rubbed his back. “She was going to hit me too. But Rio stopped her. She protected us! I just wanted to protect my Momma. Why did Grandma want to hurt me? Why did she hurt Momma?” He started crying again. The cop sighed and stood up. “I think I have all I need. I assume you wanna press charges?”

    Agatha pulled her son in and nodded.

    “Someone will be in contact with you in the next few days to follow up. Are you sure you don’t need an ambulance before I go?”

    Agatha shook her head.

    After the officer left, Rio took Agatha and helped her to the bathroom. Before even thinking to tend to herself, she focused on helping her first. She helped her sit down on the side of the tub before gently pushing her hair back, tucking it behind her ears and neck.

    Agatha’s eyes were red and swollen, her throat raw from what felt like hours of crying and shouting. Each swallow was a painful reminder of her exhaustion.

    The other woman ran a washcloth under the faucet, then gently dabbed it over her face. The coolness offered a moment of relief from the burning pain, but it faded quickly as her skin adjusted and began to ache again. Each touch felt like agitation, her raw skin screaming in protest. Agatha drew in a shaky, painful breath. Her hands gripped the edge of the tub as she fought against the fresh wave of tears threatening to spill.

    Rio shushed her. “It’s okay my love. I’ve got you.”

    She finished up.

    The bleeding stopped, and Agatha opted out of bandaids. She didn’t want her injuries to feel suffocated and burn more.

    Afterward, Agatha had insisted on helping Rio.

    The older woman didn’t have it in her to argue. Not when Agatha was looking at her with pain and sadness.

    Nicky came in to check on them. Clutching a teddy bear to his chest. “C- can I sleep with you tonight Momma?” His lip quivered. “Please! I know I’m too big but…”

    “Of course you can my sweet boy.” Agatha answered without needing to think.

    They got ready for bed.

    Rio wasn’t sure if she should stay or leave. She didn’t want to leave. But she also didn’t want to intrude. So she made a bed on the couch in the living room. The guest room was still occupied by Evanora’s things and she didn’t want to be around a reminder of her.

    Nicky said good night to her as Agatha walked them both upstairs.

    Rio sighed as she attempted to get comfy. Her head was pounding and the stiff couch definitely wasn’t doing her any favors.

    She wasn’t sure how long it had been, but eventually, she began falling asleep.

    She didn’t notice the soft footsteps coming down the stairs, but she definitely felt a hand slide around her waist and resting on her belly. A head nestle gently against her own, and an all-too-familiar voice whispering in her ear, “Come upstairs.”

    The words sent chills down her spine.

    Her eyes fluttered open before she turned. Sweet lips captured her own in a gentle exchange of appreciation and love.

    She hummed into the kiss and reached for her girlfriend’s face. Before they could get carried away Agatha moved back. She took Rio’s hands and pulled her up and off the couch. Leading her upstairs. “Are you sure?”

    “I’ve never been more sure.”

    Hand in hand Agatha pushed inside. Her son stirred unable to fall asleep without his mother.

    “Momma?”

    “I’m here honey.”

    “Did you bring Rio?”

    “Yes.”

    Agatha crawled in beside him. She kept her eyes on her love as she waited patiently for her to climb in.

    Rio felt unsure about this. Wouldn’t this tip Nicky off that they were a thing? Was this appropriate? Is it o—“ “Rio come snuggle.” Came Nicky’s voice.

    She let out a relieved sigh. That was all the push she needed and climbed in with them. Nicky was safely nestled between the two women, cuddled up to his mother with his back facing Rio.

    Rio stretched out over him a bit to drape her arm over Agatha. She held them both and stared up at the ceiling. So many thoughts running through her head. But mostly how she must protect them. Keep them safe from harm.

    Agatha clung to her, almost as if she was afraid she’d disappear. “I love you, Momma,” Nicky said breaking the silence.

    “I love you, sweetie.”

    There was a pause.

    “I love you, Rio.”

    Rio’s breathing stopped. She hadn’t expected to hear anything at all. Maybe a ‘goodnight’ at the most. But this…

    Finally, after all of the excitement of the day she started breaking down. “Rio?” Agatha asked with worry.

    “I love you too Nicky! And I-I love you, Agatha! I promise I’ll always look after you two! No matter what! You didn’t deserve any of that! I’ll protect you from this cruel world okay?”

    Nicky shifted, now this time he clung to Rio. “Thank you for saving me, for saving Momma. You’re my hero!” He leaned up and planted a kiss against her cheek then laid back against her chest.

    Agatha couldn’t believe her eyes, her two loves were bonding. She pressed her forehead against Rio’s and kissed her nose.

    “I’ve got you, both of you!” Rio’s protective hold tightened and she looked back up at the ceiling. She focused on their breathing and the feeling of their gentle heartbeats. It was enough to lull her back to sleep.

    As long as she had these two people in her life everything would be okay. And she'd make damn sure they’d never need to worry ever again.

    Agatha woke up again for the third time that night. She couldn’t help but stare down at Rio and Nicky’s sleeping faces.

    Her eyes flickered between them. Noticing their similarities. She shook the thoughts away. She was hit way too hard. She probably smacked her head against the counter.

    She sighed then attempted to fall back asleep.

    Rio pulled her in close. Cradling both Harkness’ in her arms. Finally, Agatha was able to sleep.

    Chapter End Notes The title is based off this song: https://youtu.be/DGwU9dipg3w?si=Qnqi50KWNAwu1Brv

    Chapter 7: Broken! You know that I’ve always

    been!

    Chapter Summary Nicky goes back to school.

    They have Thanksgiving.

    Then get ready for Christmas.

    A turning point.

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Since that terrible night, Agatha had been jumpy—more easily startled than ever.

    It had reopened something inside her, bringing old wounds to the surface. The mental scars her mother had etched deeply into her psyche now felt raw and exposed.

    She became cautious, hesitant in ways she hadn’t been before. Even the smallest gestures made her flinch, and it broke Rio and Nicky’s hearts to see her stumble back when they reached out to her.

    Agatha tried her best to hide it, forcing smiles and pretending everything was fine. But the cracks were too visible to ignore, even for her. Eventually, she realized she couldn’t face it alone. She needed help—real help.

    So, she started seeing a therapist.

    She even brought Nicky to a few sessions, giving him the space to talk about that night or anything else that might have been troubling him since. The night had affected him too—he’d been having trouble sleeping, his mind overwhelmed by nightmares.

    But the therapy helped him—more than she expected. The nightmares faded surprisingly quickly.

    She ended up keeping him home a few days longer than initially planned. Honestly, he was ready to go back. He was beginning to go stir-crazy being locked up all week inside. He wanted to be around other kids again.

    Things were improving pretty quickly, and it brought Agatha relief. She quickly threw his lunch together, spreading peanut butter on one slice of bread and jelly on the other.

    “Do you have homework in your bag from last week?”

    “Yes, Momma.”

    She glanced up at him. “You turned in all of your virtual assignments, correct?”

    Nicky nodded as he watched her hurry around the kitchen frantically. As if he’d miss the bus. Like she wasn’t the one taking him in that day and a little later than usual.

    He rested his chin on his hand. His eyes grew heavy as he began nodding off.

    “Nicky, watch it!”

    He jumped realizing he was leaning. His mother quickly grabbed him before he could fall off the kitchen stool.

    She caressed his face and looked into his eyes. “Did you not sleep well last night?”

    He shrugged. “I’m always a little tired in the morning. Guess more so today, s’all.”

    Agatha quirked a brow and stood back with a hand on her hip, looking him over.

    She noticed how uncomfortable he appeared.

    “Are you nervous to go back?”

    Nicky sighed but nodded.

    Agatha’s face fell for a moment. She pulled the stool next to him out and sat down.

    “Any reason why?” She said before she rested her elbows against the counter and leaned her chin on the back of her hands.

    Nicky looked away for a moment. “I've just… been gone for a bit. I’m always nervous going back to school after being away for awhile. It’ll probably happen after Christmas break and spring break too. And… yeah. That’s about it I guess.”

    Agatha’s face scrunched as she studied the boy for a moment. It looked like he wanted to say something else but she wasn’t sure.

    “Well, that sounds pretty normal. I can’t say I usually feel that way. But I definitely will be when I go back to work today.”

    Nicky looked up, shocked. “But you’re the bravest person I know.” “True, but I’ll be worrying my head off thinking about you.” She booped his nose making him laugh.

    “Can Rio come and drop me off at school too?”

    Agatha sighed and picked up her phone, checking the time. They had to leave in twenty minutes, which wasn’t much notice.

    “Nicky… I don’t know if—”

    “Please, Momma!”

    She looked back at her son and saw fresh tears welling in his eyes. “I-It’ll make me feel less nervous! Rio understands!”

    Damn, her son and his unintentional emotional manipulation! Agatha frowned, unsure what he meant by Rio understanding his nerves. How would Rio know? Agatha wasn’t even sure herself if Rio did. “I… She might be at work. But I’ll call her. You’re asking, though—I’m handing the phone to you. Got it?”

    Nicky beamed and nodded. “Yay!”

    Agatha grumbled as she quickly sent Rio a text, letting her know she was about to call and put her on speaker with Nicky. She hit the call button and waited. After a few rings, Rio picked up.

    “Hello?”

    “He—”

    “Hi!”

    Agatha had just started to answer when Nicky accidentally cut her off. He glanced at her with wide eyes. “Oops, sorry, Momma!” he said with a nervous chuckle.

    They heard Rio laugh on the other end. “And how are my two favorite people?”

    “Great!” Nicky giggled.

    Agatha blinked in surprise. It was almost as if the dark cloud hanging over her son had vanished in an instant, just from hearing Rio’s voice. “We’re doing good, ba— Rio. Nicky has something he wants to ask you.” “Oh? And what would that be, little man?”

    “I was wondering if you could come take me to school, Mommy?” Agatha’s eyes widened.

    “You called me to ask your mom if she could take you to school?” Rio chuckled.

    “No, I’m talking to you, silly! You and Momma!”

    The line went quiet. A faint, trembling breath broke the silence, followed by a soft, shaky exhale. Rio’s voice didn’t come right away, but the sound of her trying to steady herself—trying to hold back tears—said everything. “Mommy? Are you there?”

    “Yes! I’ll come! I just gotta…” she sniffled. “I need to put some things away and have my business partner finish some forms for me.” Agatha cut in, “Rio if you’re busy you don’t h—“ “I want to, Agatha. Seriously. I’ll be there in ten minutes.” Rio responded quickly.

    “Okay!” Nicky cheered.

    “Wait how?”

    “Oh, I’ll show you how in ten minutes!”

    They could practically hear the shit-eating grin on Rio’s face through the phone.

    “Rio I swear if you get into a car accident!”

    “I promise I won’t. Love you both. See you in ten. You can time me if you like.”

    “Oh my god…” Agatha groaned.

    “Okay challenge accepted!” Nicky stood grabbed the little analog timer on the counter and ran over to the couch to wait for Rio.

    “He’s waiting impatiently for you! I hope you know!”

    “Oh, I’m sure!”

    Agatha and Nicky’s jaws practically dropped as they stood in the driveway, watching Rio pull up. Both of them jumped with a startled “Ah!” as the kitchen timer—long forgotten—went off.

    “Oh? Did I nail the entrance or what?” Rio teased, pulling off her motorcycle helmet and shaking her hair free.

    Agatha quickly grabbed Nicky’s bag and used it to cover her face, hiding the deep blush spreading across her cheeks. Seeing her sexy girlfriend on a motorcycle, in a leather jacket no less, was almost too much. “Wow! You got a motorcycle? Are we riding it to school?” “No!” Agatha’s responded quickly, setting the backpack down as she spoke. Rio chuckled, swinging her leg off the bike and setting her helmet on the seat. “I don’t think all three of us will fit. Unless you want to sit on the handlebars, kid.”

    “Ugh! Can we at least go for a ride sometime?”

    Agatha’s eyes widened in terror at the idea.

    Rio smiled and placed a reassuring hand on her shoulder. “Sorry, bud. I think your mom would kill me. Maybe when you’re a little older?” “Oh okay!” He walked over to his mom and took his bag. “Come on moms! We need to go!” He ran off to the SUV and hopped inside. Agatha smiled as she watched Rio's eyes go wide as she looked off in the direction he ran.

    “Mommy…” she smirked getting the older woman’s attention, but before she could turn her head Agatha grabbed her face and pulled her in for a kiss. “Mm Mommy’s really good at kissing.” She said against her lips then pulled her in again.

    Rio whined against her lips. “Stop that!”

    But despite her words, she made no attempt to move away. Agatha gazed at her lovingly. “I had no idea he’d call you that.” She shrugged. “I guess get used to it. If it bothers you I can tell him to—“ “No!” Rio said quickly. “I… I don’t mind, I mean… he can call me whatever he wants.” She looked down at the ground, nervously fiddling with her fingers.

    Agatha sighed. She could see the faint outline of her concealed black eye from this angle. She lifted her chin to meet her gaze. “I love you!” She leaned in and kissed her one more time. “So much!” She whispered against her lips. “I don’t think you understand what you mean to me.” She glanced in the direction of the SUV. “What you mean to him.”

    Rio twirled her hair between her fingers. “I mean… I have some idea.” She smiled.

    “Mommy! Momma! Come on! I’ll be late if you keep talking!”

    Rio blushed. “You don’t think he—“ “I stuck his switch in his bag he was playing on it while waiting for you. I knew he’d get back on it. Plus I heard the faint tune of dahdahdah dada dah!”

    Rio nodded with a smile. “Ugh! I knew I heard Mario somewhere. I guess I just assumed it was coming from inside my head while you were kissing me!” she joked.

    Agatha playfully shoved her before breezing past. “Come on, beautiful, or he’ll be late! You don’t want to look bad on your first day dropping…” She turned and smirked at Rio. “Your son off, do you?”

    Rio’s smile brightened. “If I do, will you call me ‘bad mommy’?” She ran after her.

    “Absolutely not!” Agatha sprinted toward the car and struck a dramatic bow. “I am the victor! Now bow down to me!” she said as she rose. Rio snickered and glanced towards the back seat where Nicky was sitting. “Agatha… in front of your son?” She said jokingly as she glanced back with a blush and sighed. “Anything for you m’lady.”

    Agatha’s eyes widened when Rio quickly got on the ground at her feet and kissed her boots. “Rio! Those are dirty!” She looked up at her son to make sure he wasn’t looking. “And he could…”

    “He’s not looking remember…” she smirked quoting her words back to her. Agatha looked back down and saw the shit-eating grin on her face. Rio bit her lip and growled up at her before she grabbed her leg and slowly slid up. Agatha’s face flushed, almost as red as the morning sun, as she wobbled slightly. Rio’s arms quickly encircled her waist, steadying her. With a quick peck on her lips, before she darted away, opening the door and sliding into the middle seat with a mischievous grin.

    “I’m gonna get ya!” she teased.

    Nicky’s laughter rang out, bright and uncontrollable. “No! Rio! Mommy! No tickling! Ahh!”

    Agatha stood back, watching them with a fond smile, warmth spreading through her chest at the sight. She quickly took a picture before getting in the driver's seat. “Okay kids, time for school.”

    Rio and Nicky groaned in unison.

    “Hey! You’re not going to school!” Nicky giggled at Rio. “Oh, I forgot! Momma over there is a tough cookie. I almost thought I was in catholic school being scolded by the nuns again!”

    “Oh my god!” Agatha groaned as she backed out of the driveway. “Blasphemer!” Rio gasped.

    Agatha fished through her glove box before chucking a wadded-up piece of newspaper at her.

    Rio's mouth fell open in offense. “How dare you! That was uncalled for, Ms Harkness!”

    “Keep it up, Vidal! Keep it up!” Agatha warned.

    Rio’s heart felt light as she chuckled.

    Alright, so this is the class, right, kid?” Rio scanned the door for Class 5, the one with the big turkey on it.

    “Yep!”

    Nicky opened the door, not expecting a ball of auburn hair to come tumbling into him.

    Agatha arrived just in time to see the scene unfold.

    “Nicky! My darling! You’re okay!” A red-headed girl with thick, messy curls wrapped him in a tight hug before planting a big, wet kiss on his cheek. “I was worried!” she cried.

    The whole class gasped. “Oooh!” Then giggled.

    Agatha’s eyes widened in shock. There was her son, getting his first kiss on a random Monday morning, right in the middle of class, from a girl she’d never seen before.

    “Mayday!” Nicky groaned, rubbing his cheek in embarrassment. “Mayday? Is there a ship crashing somewhere?” Rio asked, looking around. The class chuckled at her comment.

    “No! That’s May Parker! She’s called MayDay because she’s a force of nature—or so her dad says!” Nicky added.

    May whimpered. “Aw, sweetie pie, why’d you rub my kiss away?” Nicky scrunched his brows in frustration and muttered under his breath, “My moms are right there!” He pointed toward them.

    The teacher chuckled at their antics before coming over. “Okay, back to your seat May. We should all give Nicky some space for a bit. He had a rough week.” She placed her hands comfortingly on his shoulders. “Nicky go on and hang your jacket and bag up out in your locker, then come take your seat.”

    He nodded, then turned and headed out to the hall, where the row of lockers lined the walls.

    Rio approached him with a bright smile. “Sooooo?”

    He grumbled out a response and turned away to hide the blush on his face. Rio put her hand to her ear and smirked. “What was that?” “M-my friend… who happens to be a girl,” he muttered.

    “Mmhm! That’s not what I saw! Friends don’t usually kiss each other on the cheek,” Rio teased.

    Nicky grumbled again.

    Rio leaned against the lockers and slid closer to him, giving him a playful look. “Speak up, little man! I’m old!”

    With an agitated groan, Nicky turned to her and said, “I said, you and Momma do it all the time, and you’re just friends!” He looked up at her challengingly.

    Rio mirrored his expression, both of them inches apart, growling at each other. It was as if they were looking in a mirror.

    Except Nicky was younger, a boy, and had flecks of blonde in his hair. They were snapped back to reality by the sound of a shutter. Both turned to see Agatha pointing her phone at them.

    “Sometimes I feel like you act more like Rio than me, Nicky. It’s cute,” Agatha said, laughing.

    The boy slammed his locker shut. “Not cute!” he whined.

    Rio pulled him into a hug. “You’ll always be cute to us, buddy!” She kissed his head.

    Nicky groaned but allowed it.

    Mayday is gonna be… handsy. I don’t want her to be. But… I-I like her. What do I do?” Nicky’s voice was quiet, but he trusted Rio’s judgment. Rio crouched slightly to meet his eye. “Hm, just let her know gently. If she respects you, she’ll back off. That’s just how some girls are, though. But if she makes you uncomfortable, tell her to stop, okay? Just be clear you like her so she doesn’t get the wrong idea.”

    Nicky nodded, his expression serious. “M’kay. Thanks, Mommy Rio.” He turned to hug her tightly. “Bye, Momma!” He pulled back to wave at Agatha. “I gotta go! I’ve already missed most of math! I don’t wanna fall further behind. I love you both!”

    The women waved, watching as he darted back into the classroom. Rio sighed. “I can’t believe he called me Mommy.”

    “I can’t believe he saw us kiss and didn’t tease us about it.” Agatha chuckled, stepping closer to Rio.

    “Well… he didn’t explicitly say kissing. Like, actual kissing. He compared it to cheek kisses, so maybe that’s all he saw?” Rio suggested. “Yeah, probably. Because if he saw us kiss on the lips, I know he’d bombard me with a million questions. He probably thinks cheek kisses are fine for friends.”

    “Yeah? Bestie?” Rio teased, bumping her shoulder lightly against Agatha’s. Agatha laughed, grabbing Rio’s arm and tugging her toward the exit. “Come on, I need help planning Thanksgiving dinner before I have to go back to work. And you’re helping me.”

    “Awesome! I’ll make the shit out of some mashed potatoes!”

    The day finally arrived when everyone gathered together. Agatha and Nicky followed their usual tradition of going to Wanda’s for Thanksgiving, but this time, Rio and Hela joined them. Alice was already there, as she was every year. The difference this year? She didn’t have to bounce between their dinner and Rio’s.

    Apparently, she’d also dragged Jen and Lilia along for the occasion. The house buzzed with chatter and laughter as the group mingled and worked on the multitude of Thanksgiving dishes.

    Meanwhile, the children entertained themselves—or at least, some of them did. Nicky and Tommy played energetically, while Billy sat nearby, visibly annoyed by their antics.

    As the adults finished up the last of the cooking, Agatha and Wanda enlisted Nicky and Billy to help set the table.

    Both boys protested equally against the chore, their groans earning amused smiles from the grown-ups.

    “Mom, I was gonna text Teddie!” Billy complained.

    “You can do that later! You’re helping set the table with Nicky!” “I’ll be doing most of the work! He has one good arm!” He gestured at the younger boy.

    “So? You’re capable!” She shoved a stack of plates in his arms. “Be a good influence on him! Or no apple pie!” She tapped his nose lovingly before going back to the kitchen.

    Nicky giggled as he moved to help set the silverware.

    Before long, the table was ready, each place perfectly set. Once everything was in place, everyone settled into their respective spots, ready to dig in. “Before we start, I thought it’d be nice if everyone went around and shared what they’re thankful for,” Vision suggested, glancing warmly at the group. Wanda smiled at her husband, her gaze filled with affection. “I’ll go first,” Vision offered. “I’m thankful for my beautiful wife, our two incredible boys, and the wonderful life we’ve built together over the past twenty years.”

    Wanda’s smile deepened as she mouthed, “I love you,” to him. The table responded with a chorus of soft “awws.”

    “I suppose I’d have to say the same,” Wanda began, pausing thoughtfully. “Though, I’m also thankful for Sparky—the adorable dog Agatha found for us.” She raised her glass toward Agatha. “And speaking of Agatha, I’m so grateful for the amazing friendship we’ve built. When I first moved here, I didn’t know a soul, but then you came along with your sweet son, and we just… clicked. You’ve been my rock for the last ten years, and I’ll always have your back. Mother to mother.”

    Agatha’s smile was warm and genuine as she met her friend’s gaze. “I’m thankful for my Momma, for Rio, and for Señor Scratchy!” The whole table erupted into giggles at Nicky’s cuteness. Each person took their turn sharing, and when it got to Tommy, he proudly declared his gratitude for his puppy and his huge Lego collection, which earned another round of laughter from the group.

    Next was Rio.

    All eyes turned to her expectantly. She hesitated, her nerves apparent, and instinctively reached for Agatha’s hand. The touch grounded her, giving her the courage to face the unfamiliar warmth of this family gathering. Agatha noticed and smiled, squeezing her hand reassuringly. “Would you like me to go first, darling? I’m next anyway—maybe I could help you out?”

    Rio looked at her with a mix of relief and gratitude. She nodded, her smile shy but genuine.

    She turned toward her son. “Well, I’d just like to say how thankful I am for my darling boy! He’s been doing so well in school! He had a tumble this month but he got right back up!” She looked back over at Rio. “And Rio, wonderful beautiful Rio,”

    The older woman’s eyes widened as she realized what Agatha was going to say.

    “She saved Nicky’s life. She came, in the middle of a service. The hospitals were short on blood supply. And she generously donated a heaping amount of her own blood for him.”

    The whole room listened in silence. Especially Nicky who was hearing this for the first time.

    “We also had a little… family incident. I won’t get into the details of it. But Rio came in. Like a knight and shining armor and saved the day, again. I mean she saved me and Nicky. She's always there for me when I need her. She’s been nothing but kind and supportive. Especially to Nicky.” She smiled over at her son and then looked back at her. “She’s been an amazing mother to him. I couldn’t have asked for a better partner. A better girlfriend.” She lifted her hand and kissed it.

    Nicky gasped. “Y-you are dating! I knew it!” He stood up and did a happy dance. “Momma and Mommy are dating!” He jumped around happily before running over to them. “When will you get married!? Ooh! Will I get a brother or sister! Can I be the ring bearer and the flower boy!?” He grabbed their hands and smiled at them.

    The two women broke out into laughter.

    “What’s so funny!?” Nicky whined, not understanding what was so funny. “We just love you, Nicky!” Rio pulled him in and kissed his cheek. Agatha wrapped her arms around him from behind. The three stayed like that for a moment before a shuttering sound broke the silence.

    Nicky peaked between them and pointed. “Billy!”

    The teen continued taking photos with his photography camera. “This is going to look amazing on canvas!” He muttered.

    Wanda winked at the boy for giving her an easy Christmas gift for her friend.

    “I think I deserve some thanks?” Alice crossed her arms and sat back smirking at the couple. “After all, your little love story wouldn’t have started without me.”

    Lilia muttered something under her breath in response.

    Alice quirked her brow but just ignored it.

    “Yes thank you for setting us up Alice!” Agatha held up her glass to her. “I would never have met Rio if it wasn’t for you.”

    “Or me!” Hela chimed in.

    “Hm…” Lilia hummed while eating a roll. “Things come full circle sometimes, I suppose…” she muttered something else under her breath, that no one could hear, before saying something in Italian. “Qualcosa è familiare.”

    Billy looked at the old woman with worry. “Mom! Lilia’s being weird again!”

    After the excitement died down they all dug in.

    Chattering picked up between the adults. As the children engrossed themselves in the food and only the food.

    Nicky swung his feet happily as he enjoyed Rio’s homemade Mac and cheese and Agatha’s stuffing.

    “My mommy makes such good devil eggs!” Tommy said through a mouthful as he smiled at Nicky.

    “Ew!” Nicky made a face of disgust at the little boys lack of manners. “Honey, it’s deviled eggs, not devil.” Wanda chuckled.

    “Oh, well dey are yummy Mommy! And I like the cwamberry sauce!” “It’s cranberry, dear.” Vision chuckled.

    Rio looked around and smiled. This wasn’t her first Thanksgiving—she’d had smaller ones with just Hela and Alice. But this was different. Now, she was surrounded by even more friends. She and Hela had grown closer to Jen and Lilia, and she had Agatha and Nicky by her side. Plus, there was Wanda’s family, welcoming her like one of their own.

    It was a moment she’d dreamed of since she was a little girl—being part of something big, warm, and full of love.

    “I’m thankful for you Hela…” Rio started.

    The whole table went silent and listened to her.

    Hela put her fork down and smiled.

    “You’ve always been there for me. My sister, my family for as long as I can remember. The only person I could turn to when I was in trouble or needed someone to take care of me when I was sick. And in turn, I did the same for you.” She wiped a stray tear from her eyes. “We’ve been through so much together and I wouldn’t have picked a better person to grow up with. You will always be my first-found family.”

    She turned toward Alice. “Alice meeting you in college was weird…” Alice chuckled.

    “I mean, you accused me of copying you in biology. I didn’t need to copy you. Trust me, I was doing just fine. We eventually fought over it but then we made up. You found me in the music room practicing my guitar and played along with me. You were my first real friend. And Hela wouldn’t leave me alone about befriending the girl who threatened to chuck a textbook at my head over some science questions.”

    Now it was Hela’s turn to chuckle.

    “Starting the band was a great change in my life. I've had so much fun playing with you guys! And of course, now that Jen has come along we have even more fun!”

    Jen smiled at the mention of her name.

    Rio turned toward Agatha and took her hands. “And yes I am so thankful for Hela and Alice setting us up. Three months ago I was… a less enthusiastic version of myself. You’ve brought something out in me that I never thought possible Agatha. You’re such a caring and thoughtful woman and I am so happy we met. I’m also grateful you called me back after leaving to deal with the SUV mishap.”

    Billy giggled at that one as Agatha rolled her eyes.

    Rio squeezed her hands. “I really am! And then meeting Nicky too! I never knew I could love two people so much! I just… I look forward to many more Thanksgivings with both of you! I’m just a call away when you need me! I promise I’ll always come when you call! I love you both!” She kissed Agatha’s hand and smiled over at Nicky.

    The group let out “awws.” as they clapped, making Rio blush.

    Agatha kissed her hand and mouthed “I love you.”

    The next few weeks were hectic, to say the least.

    Agatha was up to her neck in reports and meetings, as they approached the new year. They needed to get everything ready for their next sales pitch. Plus, they had to get ahead so they wouldn’t fall behind on their two-week paid break—Agatha generously gave her employees.

    Rio wasn’t fairing well either. The number of bodies being brought to the morgue were unusually high. She was overwhelmed in having to prepare them for their services and arrangements.

    While Hela worked tirelessly on finances before hosting the funerals. Rio was tired, she was ready for her break.

    She was fortunate enough to be able to take two weeks off. They wouldn’t be earning much income. But it wasn’t that big of a deal. They always save enough to get by.

    But this year was special.

    Rio had someone to spend it with. She was excited because soon she’d be able to wake up Christmas morning and watch Nicky excitedly open his presents under the tree before she and Agatha opened their own.

    The snow was coming down hard outside.

    Agatha peeked through the blinds and sighed, her breath fogging the glass. She glanced over at the sleeping figure in her bed and couldn’t help but smile.

    Carefully, she slid out of bed, moving slowly to avoid waking the woman. Though it was still early, Agatha knew she couldn’t ignore the storm. Being on holiday break didn’t mean she wanted to deal with the hassle of getting snowed in—or shoveling what would inevitably feel like mountains of snow.

    Groaning, she pulled on her boots and tugged her winter hat snugly over her head.

    “This is gonna suck,” she muttered under her breath.

    When she pushed open the front door, the sharp cold air hit her lungs like a crashing wave. She gasped, clutching her jacket tighter. “Ugh, it’s really coming down,” she groaned, yanking her hood over her head as she trudged toward the garage to grab her snow shovel. She panted as she continued to shovel for twenty straight minutes. Her fingers and toes were numb but the job needed down.

    She cursed under her breath and lifted her hat to wipe some of the sweat away. The icy remnants stuck to her glove scratched at her red and numb forehead making her whine in annoyance.

    It ached and burned. “Shit!”

    She penguin-walked over to the other end of the driveway, pushed the shovel down into the snow and walked forward, clearing another trail. She grunted as the air expelled from her lungs and she huffed in annoyance at the resistance she had encountered by the overwhelming amount of dense snow buildup in that one spot.

    She pulled the shovel back and went to dig in again—

    The front door swung open, slamming against the frame and startled her. “What the hell are you doing!?”

    Agatha raised a gloved hand to shield her eyes from the light spilling onto the snowy driveway. Squinting, she saw Rio standing in the doorway, a hand on her hip, shaking her head. Was that worry on her face? Annoyance? Agatha couldn’t tell.

    “Shoveling,” Agatha answered plainly, turning back to her work. “Why?!” Rio huffed, pulling a coat over her shoulders and hopping on one foot as she struggled to get her boot on.

    Agatha stopped mid-shovel and turned to Rio, incredulous. She threw her arms out in exasperation. “Because we’ll be snowed in otherwise!” Rio shook her head and slammed the door shut behind her, making her way down the steps. “No, that’s not what I meant. Why are you shoveling?” Agatha blinked, caught off guard by Rio’s obvious agitation. She repeated herself, this time with a hint of defiance. “Because it needs to get done!” She stomped her foot, punctuating her frustration.

    Rio let out a growl.

    Agatha’s eyes widened. “Did you just—“ “That’s my job!” Rio snapped, her fists clenching at her sides. Agatha raised a brow and shook her head, turning back to the driveway. “You’re ridiculous.” She muttered and pushed the shovel into the snow again.

    Rio huffed, marching over. Without a word, she grabbed the shovel from Agatha’s hands.

    “Hey!” Agatha reached for it, but Rio yanked it away and tossed it into a nearby snowbank.

    “Rio what are— ugh!”

    Before Agatha could finish, Rio swooped down, grabbing her and tossing her over her shoulder.

    Agatha squirmed, lightly smacking Rio’s shoulders. “What are you doing?! Put me down! I have to finish this!”

    “No,” Rio said firmly, trudging toward the house.

    “What do you mean, no?!” Agatha groaned, her voice filled with irritation. “You’re too cute!” Rio huffed, glancing at her like it was the most obvious thing in the world. “I take care of you!”

    With one final push, Rio opened the door and set Agatha down inside. “Rio I can do it my—“ Rio silenced her by peeling off her winter gear. Her gloves, hat, and coat were all quickly removed, leaving no room for argument.

    “H-hey!” Agatha reached for her coat and hat. “Stop it!” Now it was Rio’s turn to stomp her foot. “No! You relax!” She quickly shed her own coat and kicked off her boots. “You‘re freezing cold and I’m warming you up!”

    “Rio what has go—“ “I’m warming you up!” She said with finality. “End of discussion!” She lifted Agatha bridal-style and carried her up the stairs. “You’re ridiculous!” Agatha groaned. “I can do it myself! I’m fully capable! I’ve been doing it for eleven years!”

    “Well, now you’re not! I’m here, and I said it’s my job! So it’s my job! Now do yours and by my cute sweet queen and let me love you!” She dropped Agatha onto the bed with a huff.

    Agatha growled up at her. “I am not some helpless woman!” “I know! And you’re stubborn! Hardheaded! And bossy!” Rio listed them off on her fingers.

    Agatha sneered. “Hey!”

    “But that’s what I love about you!” She added before falling on top of her and pulling the comforter over them. “Now relax or I’ll be forced to punish you!”

    Agatha looked up at her challengingly. “You don’t have the guts! What are you gonna do!?”

    Rio smirked at her for a moment. The wicked look in her eyes startled Agatha, whose eyes were now wide.

    “Rio, whatever you’re ab— Ahhh! Hahahaha! Stop it!”

    Rio started tickling her lover mercilessly.

    Agatha attempted to roll away or push her off, but it was no use. Rio had the upper hand and she was using it to make her laugh.

    “No! No tickling! It’s horrible! Ugh!” Agatha struggled while gasping for air between her laughter.

    Rio smiled brightly. The sound of Agatha’s laughter brought her immense joy. She started chuckling along with her.

    “Rio, please! Okay, I give up! You win! You—mmph!”

    Rio cut her lover off with a kiss.

    The younger woman hummed into it, before relaxing and wrapping her arms around Rio’s neck, and after a moment they parted.

    Agatha smiled up at her girlfriend and blushed.

    “I love you, Agatha!” Rio kissed her one more time.

    “I love you, Rio.”

    With Christmas just around the corner, Agatha and Rio were out diligently shopping.

    “Hey! Look at this thing!” Rio held up a large Nerf gun. “I’m going to get this for Nicky!”

    Agatha groaned! “Oh no, you won’t!” She attempted to take it, only for Rio to yank her hand away.

    “Nuh-uh! You said whatever I wanted!” She stuck her tongue out at her. “I’m not sure that’s the best idea, he’s going to torture me with it! This is the third gift you’ve suggested that will bring absolute chaos to my house. I’m not sure you know how to pick out gifts!”

    Rio quirked brow. “Really? Because you seem to enjoy the gifts I got you for your birthday!”

    Agatha clutched at the amethyst necklace around her neck and hugged her blue coat to her body. “That’s different!” She turned away. Rio chuckled and sat the gun down in the cart. She moved forward to wrap her arms around Agatha’s back and kissed her cheek. “You’re so cute when you’re grumpy.”

    “Not grumpy.” She muttered.

    “Oh? Then what do you call this?” She pointed at her frown. “It’s called being a mother and…” she turned in Rio’s arms and faced her. “The woman you care so deeply for!”

    Rio smiled. “Mm, I do! I really do!” She leaned forward and kissed her. “I really don’t wanna poke the bear! But you’re just so cute!” She swayed her side to side!

    “Agh! I told you before I’m not cute!”

    “What was that? I didn’t hear you!” She kissed her cheek quickly and pulled away. “I’m gonna buy it!” She grabbed the gun and ran off. “Rio!” Agatha chuckled before pushing the cart after her.

    “Nicky! Come on! Are you ready for the Christmas festival?” “Yeah!” Nicky shouted before barreling down the stairs. “Where’s Mommy?”

    “Getting changed upstairs. She’ll be down in a second.”

    He nodded.

    She smiled at the boy as he fiddled with his tie. “Come here my love so I can fix your tie!”

    He skipped over toward her, cherry as ever. “Are Billy and Tommy going?” “Yes, your buddies will be there!”

    Nicky fussed as she re-knotted it. He always seemed to hate formal ware. The sound of footsteps approaching caught the pair's attention. Agatha turned and her eyes widened while she let out a soft gasp. “How do I look?” Rio posed with a smirk.

    Agatha approached her, taking the woman in. She looked gorgeous as always. But there was something so domestic and sweet about her wearing her own Christmas sweater. “Like the woman of my dreams.” She pulled her in for a kiss.

    “Ew! Stop kissing in front of me! My eyes are burning!” Nicky covered his eyes with his hands.

    Agatha chuckled against Rio’s mouth, giving her one more peck before turning back toward her son. “Oh, you’ll be fine!” She looked back over at Rio. “Did you steal that from my closet?” She smirked.

    “No…..” Rio dragged out the word, before looking away, with a smile. Agatha leaned in and whispered into her ear. “Lying will only get you on the naughty list.” She glanced over to make sure Nicky wasn’t looking before playfully smacking her ass, making Rio yelp, then continued whispering. “Be good or Santa won’t give you presents.” She kissed her cheek, then walked off before Rio could retaliate and get revenge. She heard Rio’s faint whimpering and smirked as she grabbed a bag of cookies, she intended to give out and headed toward the front door. “Do you have your cards, Nicky?”

    “Yeah!” He ran toward her with his bag of Christmas cards that they’d be handing out to people. Each card had a special and unique drawing. This was a tradition they started when Nicky was four and have done it every year since.

    “So, let me get this straight—you’ve been to this thing before?” Agatha asked as Rio walked up beside her.

    “Yeah, a few times,” Rio said with a shrug. “Hela and I usually kept to ourselves, but I know it started as a Christmas party hosted by Alice and her committee, or whatever. Then it turned into this big community event for the town. We always went to Alice’s house afterward, though.” “Hm, interesting. I guess I was the opposite—I’ve only ever gone to the West View Christmas Fest,” Agatha paused. “The party sounds nice, though. More personal and down to earth. The Christmas festival feels more like…”

    “Shopping?” Rio offered.

    Agatha nodded. “Yeah, plus some games here and there. It’s fun taking Nicky and all, but…” she bumped her hip against Rio’s. “It’s nice getting to have another person tag along.”

    “Well lucky you, we can all enjoy the party at least until eight. After that, it’s adults only!”

    “Yes, that’s right. I did make arrangements for Lilia to take Nicky for the night.”
