    “I get to hang out with Ms Lilia?” Nicky bounced with excitement. “Yes, darling.” Agatha set the bag down and helped him with his coat and scarf. “Here do it like this. I don’t need you getting a cold before Christmas!”

    “I’ll be okay Momma! Mommy wanna wear matching scarves!?” He held up a green one, matching his own.

    Rio smiled and nodded. She pulled her coat over her shoulders and then took the scarf. It smelled just like Agatha! Like vanilla and honey. She took in the sweet scent and sighed. “It’s lovely!”

    Agatha shook her head with a smile. “Let’s go before the streets get too busy!” She turned and flicked the tail of her coat dramatically as she stepped through the front door.

    Nicky snickered, then covered his mouth as if sharing a secret, leaning toward Rio. “Momma’s been doing that a lot lately.”

    Rio raised a brow, her gaze following Agatha. “Oh, has she?” She smirked, her eyes lingering a moment longer than they probably should have. Not her fault! She was pretty sure Agatha was swaying her hips like that, just to catch her attention—and it was working.

    Rio let out an appreciative whistle as she watched Agatha make her way toward the SUV. She was pretty sure she caught the sight of a smug smirk as she turned to get into the vehicle.

    The trio walked around for a while.

    The festival was packed full of people and activities.

    It was hard to decide on which to do first.

    That was until one booth in particular caught Nicky’s eye. “Can we try that Momma?” Nicky pointed.

    Agatha’s eyes followed in the direction of his finger and smiled. “Wreath making? Sure, looks fun!”

    They approached the booth and an elderly woman smiled at them. They were her first customers of the day. “Hello! Interested in making wreaths? Or just window shopping?”

    “Bit of both, actually.” Agatha fumbled through her purse until she found what she was looking for. Before she could hand the woman the cash, Rio had beaten her to it and was already sitting down.

    “Hm… Nicky, I think I may need your creative expertise on this one bud.” Rio patted the stool next to her.

    Agatha chuckled and shook her head. She sat on the other side of Rio and looked down at the supplies.

    The elderly woman smiled warmly at the group, her hands steady as she gathered sprigs of pine. “Alright, first thing’s first—start with a good base. I like to use a wire frame, but you can use a vine wreath if you want something more rustic. See how I’ve got this one here?” She gestured to the circle of wire in front of them. “Now, you want to lay down your greenery in layers, like so. Don’t worry if it’s a bit messy at first—it’ll all come together, just trust me.”

    Nicky’s eyes widened in wonder. “Can we make it super big, like the ones on the front door?”

    The woman chuckled softly. “Oh, yes, you can make it as big as you like! But for this, we’ll keep it a manageable size. Now, watch carefully—take your first branch, lay it flat against the frame, and secure it with some wire. Don’t worry if you can’t see it all at first. Just keep layering over it until it starts to look full.”

    She demonstrated by adding more greenery, carefully working her hands with the wire. “You just keep repeating the process. Make sure each piece overlaps a little, like a cozy blanket. That’s how you get that full, lush look.”

    Nicky leaned in, curious. “What about little ornaments or ribbons?” “Ah, that’s the fun part,” the woman grinned. “Once you’ve got the base all nice and thick, you can add whatever decoration you want! Ribbons, pinecones, little ornaments, flowers. The key is balance—don’t put all your decorations on one side. Spread them out, like you’re painting a picture.” Rio smiled softly at the boy, watching him focus. “I think I’m going to let you take the lead on this one kid!”

    The woman smiled kindly at Nicky. “Don’t worry, honey, you’ll do great. Just take your time and trust the process. It will all come together! I’ll be over here if you have any questions!”

    “Okay!” Nicky smiled at the woman. “I’m gonna make mine Halloween- themed!”

    Agatha quirked a brow. “If that’s what you want buddy, then have at it!” Nicky quickly got to work, eagerly adding the little trinkets at his disposal. Halloween was definitely his favorite holiday. Sure, Christmas was great for gifts, but there was something about the fall and spooky aesthetic that he just loved. “I’m so glad there are pumpkins and ghosts! Look at these pretty orange and black ornaments!”

    Rio’s face lit up as she watched him in his element, his tongue stuck out slightly as he focused on bringing his creation to life. “You’re giving me so much inspo! Ugh, Hela is so gonna love this!” Rio grinned as she leaned into the theme, working on a Halloween-inspired wreath of her own.

    The elderly woman watched them with interest, a warm smile on her face as she admired their creativity.

    “Rio, that looks so pretty!” Agatha said, her voice full of genuine appreciation.

    She and Nicky paused what they were doing to watch Rio work, curious to see what else she would add to her wreath.

    Rio chose black twigs and leaves, carefully weaving them into the frame. Then, she twirled some green Christmas lights through the wire and branches, adding a soft glow. For contrast, she tucked in a couple of purple and red flowers and placed a small skull in the center as a unique finishing touch. “Voila!” she said, holding it up proudly.

    “Wow! That’s awesome!” Nicky exclaimed, his excitement bubbling over. The elderly woman stood up from her chair and walked over with a smile. “Would it be alright if I took a picture? I love showcasing what people create!”

    Rio nodded enthusiastically. Nicky slid his wreath next to hers, and the two of them admired how well their creations complemented each other. They hadn’t even noticed that Agatha had quietly finished her own wreath as well.

    Rio and Nicky’s mouths dropped open when they saw Agatha’s wreath. “How did you do that!?” Rio asked, her tone filled with amazement. Agatha’s creation was shaped like a crescent moon, with a tiny cat in the center pawing at a dangling crystal. She had used black twigs and leaves, accented with small purple flowers and elegant black roses. “I used some wire cutters to reshape the wreath,” she explained with a small shrug. “Is it okay? I wasn’t sure if I did it right. Yours both look fuller and more eye-catching than mine.”

    Rio and Nicky exchanged a look, then turned back to Agatha with wide smiles.

    “Momma, this is the prettiest wreath ever!” Nicky exclaimed. The elderly woman approached Agatha and handed her a ribbon. Agatha blinked at it in confusion. “What’s this for?”

    The woman smiled warmly. “Didn’t you see my sign? I was holding a little competition for the most unique and well-made wreath. I’ve decided yours is the winner.”

    Agatha was genuinely surprised that she had won a ribbon. It was not her intention but it made her happy honestly.

    “Also you can pick from anything in my booth under fifty dollars, for free!” Her eyes immediately landed on two items.

    One was an intricate dragon wreath she knew Nicky would absolutely love! And the other, a beautiful skull vase with green and purple flowers inside. The elderly woman followed her gaze and smiled.

    Agatha turned toward her companions. “Rio and Nicky, could you two step out for a moment please?”

    The pair glanced at each other but nodded before heading out. Agatha smiled at the woman and pointed.

    “Ah yes. Well, I could strike you a deal, as the dragon wreath is a bit pricey. I’ll sell it to you for twenty dollars and you can have the skull and flowers for free!”

    “Deal!”

    The pair wandered over towards the next booth just to get a peak. They ogled the homemade candles and then took in their lovely scents. “Wow! This one is turkey-scented!” Nicky pointed, astounded that such a thing even existed.

    Rio snickered. “I’m not sure I’d find that appealing. Seems more like a gag gift or for someone who just really enjoys turkey!”

    Before Nicky could make a joke, Agatha walked over, beckoning them to follow before turning and heading out of the tent.

    The pair exchanged a glance.

    “Why is Momma acting all ominous?” Nicky asked, his voice full of curiosity.

    Rio smirked at his use of a big word. He must’ve picked it up at school. Shrugging, she gave him an amused look. “I don’t know. But I guess we’ll find out.”

    They exited the candle vendor’s tent and scanned the area, looking for Agatha.

    They spotted her waving from a set of tables near the food court. When they reached her, Agatha grinned, holding out two bags. “For you, my loves.”

    Their faces lit up as they eagerly opened the bags.

    “A dragon! Awesome!” Nicky exclaimed.

    “Aw, sweet! This is totally going in my office!” Rio said with a laugh. “Thanks, baby!”

    “Thanks, Momma!” Nicky added, his eyes wide with excitement. “You’re welcome,” Agatha said, arms open wide, a playful smile on her face.

    In an instant, both of them rushed into her, nearly knocking her off her feet. “Woah!” She chuckled.

    After dropping their wreaths off in the SUV they decided to check out more vendor stalls.

    Agatha had to be sneaky in picking up presents for Rio and Nicky. It wasn’t easy when they were all walking together. But she managed to sneak away enough times to collect what she needed.

    She was sure Rio was doing the same thing. She would notice that sparkle and wonder in her eye every now and again. So she knew she was up to something.

    Around lunch, they decided to meet up with Wanda and her children at the food court. That’s when they ran into Alice and Hela who were deep in conversation over their favorite Christmas movie.

    Alice’s was A Nightmare Before Christmas. Which wasn’t surprising in the least. And Hela’s was It’s A Wonderful Life. Which actually surprised everyone.

    They both turned toward the oncoming trio, wanting to know what they liked.

    Rio’s ended up being A Christmas Story. Which was adorable and Nicky’s was Jim Carrey’s Grinch Stole Christmas. Which Agatha knew considering he watched it every year.

    Agatha hesitated on hers for a moment. She didn’t really have a childhood movie she cared for considering her childhood kinda sucked. She pondered with a finger placed on her chin as she stared up in thought. “Happiest Season.”

    Hela and Alice went nuts and Rio stood there confused since she’d never seen the movie.

    “Are you kidding! That is so gay!” Alice laughed.

    “Yeah, I agree! And that’s coming from me!” Hela gestered at herself. Agatha groaned, annoyed. “Leave me alone! Riley was just so cute, okay!? And I was rooting for Abby!”

    “I wish I knew what you guys were talking about,” Rio said before taking her seat next to Hela.

    “It’s that Christmas movie I tried getting you to watch a few years back, but you told me you’d rather nap instead!” She made a mocking tone and face as she reminded the woman why.

    “Hey guys what are we talking about?” Wanda came over smiling ear to ear. “Christmas movies.”

    “Ooh, I love a bad mom’s Christmas!”

    Rio jumped in. “Oh my god me too! Carla is so hot in that movie!” “Ugh I know right!” Wanda swooned. “I love the bad girl archetype.” Hela cackled out before attempting to make her way to the auburn-haired woman’s side, only to be pulled back by Alice.

    “Oh no you don’t! That’s a married woman!”

    Eventually, as the day wore on so too did their time with Nicky and the kids for the day.

    Agatha showered the boy in kisses as Lilia so kindly took him and Wanda’s boys for the night.

    Both mothers repeatedly asked if it was okay.

    And Lilia would simply respond with, “I’m too old for parties anyway. Plus I can pretend they’re my grandchildren.”

    And Wanda and Agatha would just smile at her and tell her that they were her grandchildren.

    After all, Wanda’s parents had both passed a long time ago. And Agatha’s… well.

    Her mother was currently serving time for domestic violence, battery, and attempted child abuse.

    And her father had passed when she was just a child herself.

    So there was that.

    So yes Lilia was the honory grandmother as well as Sharon.

    The friend group made their way back to Alice’s for her annual Christmas party.

    “I miss your old place, Alice,” Rio muttered as she walked down her long driveway.

    “You say that every year, Rio.” She shook her head with feigned annoyance.

    “Well… it’s true.”

    “And it’s been ten years. You act like I got rid of a puppy or something.” “It might as well have been. I tended to that garden after all. It was my pride and joy.”

    Alice rolled her eyes playfully as they entered the home. The group quickly got to work and helped Alice finish setting up. Rio directed Agatha on where to hang up lights or where to set up tables. “So….” Hela moved to Alice’s side and wrapped her arm around her. “We finally making this a key party this year or…”

    Alice quirked her brow at her. She placed her hand on her hip and smiled. “Sure, Hela. And in the event you go home with a man… well let me know how that goes.”

    Hela’s face scrunched in disgust before taking the hint and walking off. “You know I still love you!” Alice called out to her retreating form.

    “Wanna know something funny?”

    Alice turned to see Wanda standing there holding up two cups. “Shoot.”

    Wanda smirked. “There was a key party scene briefly in the live-action Grinch movie.”

    Alice covered her mouth, in an attempt to stifle laughter. “No way!” “Yeah! It was at his mom’s house. Little baby Grinch witnessed a swingers Christmas!” Wanda broke down into a fit of laughter.

    And Alice soon joined her. “That little shit was freezing to death outside and his moms were getting it on with half of Whoville!?” “Yes!”

    Hela groaned as she watched them laugh.

    Rio came up beside her and smiled at the two women’s antics. “Don’t worry sis. They aren’t laughing at you. They’re laughing at the weirdly placed adult humor in children’s movies.”

    “No, they’re making fun of me,” Hela grumbled.

    Rio’s smile fell. She couldn’t help but think how much her adopted sister resembled grumpy cat at this moment. She thought on her feet quickly about how to rectify the situation. She grinned when the idea came to mind while looking over at Alice.

    “You know… a little birdy told me someone has a crush on you!” She said in a sing-song voice.

    Hela’s head snapped in her direction. “Who!?”

    Rio smiled at how easy this was. She turned away and acted nonchalant. “Well, I can’t say. I made a promise after all. She’d kill me if she found out.”

    Hela let out huff while grabbing her shoulder and turned her around. “I helped you find love! Now help me!”

    Rio was taken aback. With wide eyes she said. “Love?” Her face fell for a moment before immediately being replaced with a bright smile. “Hela you’re finally gonna settle down?”

    The other woman looked away nervously. “Maybe…”

    Rio put a comforting hand on her shoulder prompting her to continue. “Relationships are hard for me…” she looked down at her shoes. “Women like the awe and mystery of me. That I’m thrilling and fun. But once that flame burns out they leave. And that’s all I end up being, so why change it?” She shrugged and looked up at Rio.

    Rio shook her head. “No, Hela. That’s not all you are. You’re looking in the wrong places if that’s the kind of woman you keep attracting.” Rio sighed and turned her gaze in the direction of the two women, now deep in conversation across from them.

    Hela followed her gaze and her eyes went wide when she saw who she was looking at it. She blushed and turned around. She suddenly felt shy and decided to pull her turtle neck up higher to hide her face. “Rio… I don’t know. That’s… I can’t ruin what we have.”

    Rio frowned. “Who said you’d ruin anything? You haven’t heard how she talks about you when you aren’t around! Me and Jen are sick of hearing her say she’s going to do something about it. But then she flakes and runs away. I think you need to make the first step for both of your sakes.” Hela groaned nervously.

    “You have all night! If you excuse me I’m going to go find my girl before the party kicks off and guests start pouring in.” She squeezed her shoulder. “Don’t let it pass you by or you’ll regret it. Trust me. I’ve spent way too long being alone. It’s wonderful having someone.”

    “But I’ll wind up being a spaz around Alice!”

    Rio lifted a brow. “Oh come on! You’re great! Who could top you!? You’re the great person I know!”

    “Yeah, but Agatha’s awesome!” She grumbled.

    Rio sighed dreamily. “She is, isn’t she? But she’s all mine so don’t go getting any ideas!” She sang the last part of the sentence before walking off. “And have a little faith in yourself, Casanova!” She shouted over her shoulder while walking off.

    By nine o’clock, the party was in full swing. The mix of Christmas music and chatter created a festive buzz. The air was heavy with the sweet scent of freshly baked cookies—Alice had gone overboard, as usual, with about a thousand different varieties laid out on the table.

    Agatha stood off to the side, her beer cool against her fingers as she watched the crowd move around her. An awkwardness she always felt at gatherings like this began to creep in, like a quiet weight settling on her shoulders.

    She sighed and took another sip of her underwhelming drink. “You’re fine, Agatha. Just relax,” she muttered under her breath, hoping no one noticed her talking to herself.

    A tap on her shoulder pulled her from her thoughts, and she turned to find herself face-to-face with a familiar smirk and flirtatious, loving brown eyes. “Hey beautiful, you alone tonight?”

    Agatha quirked a brow at the raven-haired woman and shook her head with a smile. “No, actually. I’m with my ridiculously sexy girlfriend who’s way out of my league!”

    The woman mirrored Agatha, lifting a brow. “Oh? And where is this… sexy girlfriend of yours? I don’t see anyone here?” She spread her arms and looked around dramatically.

    Agatha chuckled at this little game. “She’s probably off flirting with middle-aged mother.”

    “Mm, I bet she’s a milf!” The woman purred.

    Agatha froze mid-sip. “What!?” She coughed, choking on the foamy liquid, as Rio burst into laughter.

    “Oh shit! Here, let me help you!” Rio pulled a handful of napkins from her pocket and dabbed at Agatha’s face with care. “I’m sorry I didn’t realize I was so charming that you’d choke on your drink.”

    “This wasn’t very good anyway…” Agatha stifled a laugh, her cheeks burning. “And I can’t believe you just said that!”

    Rio raised a brow with a smirk. “Said what? You want something else?” She gestured toward the drink in Agatha’s hand.

    “Are you offering to get me a drink from all the way over there? I think you’ll have to fight your way through a pack of wolves to get to it.” The concession table was crowded with a hungry, thirsty mob of partygoers. Rio smiled and bowed dramatically. “For you m’lady, I will claw my way through the trenches of hell if it means quenching your thirst!” “Such a gentlewoman!” Agatha pretended to swoon, pressing a hand to her forehead.

    Rio giggled, leaning in to plant a quick kiss on her cheek. “I’ll be right back!” she said before hurrying off.

    Agatha giggled as she watched her go.

    Neither of them noticed the sharp gaze tracking their every move, waiting for Rio to disappear into the crowd.

    “Hi.”

    Agatha turned to see a blonde woman she’d never met before standing in front of her. Something about her rubbed her the wrong way. She wasn’t sure why. Maybe it was the overly friendly smile or the way she was looking her up and down as if she was judging her. “Uh… hi.” She looked away again hoping she’d get the hint and leave.

    “So… was that Rio? Rio Vidal?”

    Agatha quirked a brow but didn’t meet her gaze. Why was she asking about her girlfriend!? Her hold on her cup tightened. “Depends… who’s asking?” “An old friend of hers.”

    Finally, Agatha turned and took the woman in.

    She was blonde, young-looking, with green eyes, and a nice smile. Charming, but in a way that felt manipulative and calculating. “Oh? And you are?”

    “My name’s Sarah. Rio and I went to school together. It’s been a while since I’ve seen her. I’ve just moved here recently and don’t know anyone, so I was pleasantly surprised when I caught the sight of a familiar face! Unfortunately, some weird guy over there wouldn’t take the hint, so I couldn’t make it over before she wandered off.”

    Agatha glanced in the direction Sarah had gestured but couldn’t identify which ‘weird guy’ she meant. Still, she sympathized with any woman trying to get away from a man who wouldn’t take no for an answer. “I’m sorry that happened to you. Rio’s my girlfriend. She just went to get me another drink—this one wasn’t very good.”

    The music grew in volume, forcing the two to speak louder, just to hear each other.

    Sarah’s expression shifted briefly into something Agatha couldn’t quite interpret before she smirked. “That’s adorable! Rio was always such a nice… girl.”

    There was a subtle edge to the way she lingered on the word girl. “She is,” Agatha said firmly.

    There was a pause. Sarah kept her gaze on Agatha, which made her uncomfortable.

    “So, what was Rio like in college?”

    “Oh, she hasn’t mentioned her past?” The amusement in Sarah’s voice was impossible to miss.

    “I’m not sure I get what you mean. We haven’t spoken too much about school or anything.”

    Sarah’s smirk deepened. “So I take it Rio hasn’t told you about her…. unique qualities?”

    Agatha furrowed her brow. She wasn’t sure what Sarah was hinting at. “What do you mean?”

    “So she hasn’t… interesting.”

    Agatha crossed her arms and waited, her patience wearing thin. “I assume you’re a lesbian, right?“ Agatha nodded.

    “Well I’m sorry to be the one to burst your bubble but you haven’t been with a real woman. Rio’s a liar. I should know—she lied to me.” Agatha’s face fell. She didn’t appreciate this woman calling Rio a liar, but a part of her needed to know what she was going to say. “What are you talking about!?”

    Agatha hadn’t noticed the music lower, but she and Sarah continued speaking at a high volume.

    Rio whistled as she made her way over to the concessions table. She had a huge smile on her face as she grabbed some punch for her love. Something had caught her eye and she glanced over. Her heart pounded in her chest at the sight.

    Hela and Alice were deep in conversation. Laughing and chuckling. They were standing pretty close and Alice even had her hand wrapped around the taller woman’s waist.

    The pair noticed the eyes on them and they glanced in Rio’s direction smiling.

    Hela nodded for her to come over.

    Which Rio did.

    “Hey, great party Alice! Though I don’t recommend the miller light.” Alice chuckled. “Yeah I didn’t pick that out. That was Jan from reading club.”

    Hela snickered. “You’re such a nerd!”

    Alice glanced up at her. “A sexy nerd!”

    Hela had to look away for a moment. Seemingly overwhelmed by Alice’s cuteness.

    Rio was so happy. That her two closest friends had finally found love in one another.

    “You know my dark and sexy goddess.” Alice walked her fingers up Hela’s chest, grabbing her attention. She bopped her nose as she turned her head to look back at her. “I have some things to attend to with some of my committee members. But I promise I’ll come right back over here to keep you nice and warm!”

    Hela blushed. “I’ll be counting the minutes!”

    Alice rolled her eyes but stood on her tiptoes, pulling Hela in for a kiss. Hela’s eyes widened before she relaxed and enjoyed Alice’s affection. All too soon she pulled away with a chuckle. “See you in ten, cutie!” She booped her one more time before leaving the two.

    Hela stood there in shock for a moment. Her arms still held up in the air. Where they had once been, clasping Alice’s waist.

    “Did I just witness your guys first kiss?”

    “Uh-huh!” Hela nodded. She finally relaxed and turned toward Rio. “How do you do it?”

    Rio lifted a brow. “Do what?”

    “Deal with the feeling of your heart almost exploding by receiving affections from your crush?”

    Rio crossed her arms. Amused at how panicked her sister seemed. “Usually you’re so confident. Huh. I’m sorry to say, sis. It doesn’t get easier.” “No?”

    “Nope. You’ll fall deeper and deeper until you can’t dig yourself out, but you won’t want to. Isn’t that wonderful?”

    Hela sighed and nodded. “That sounds amazing!” She smiled at the shorter woman. “Thank you, Rio.”

    “Yeah?”

    “Yeah. For the push. I… I asked Alice if she may want to go out sometime and she said yes! And well you saw what happened… I guess I’m hers now.” She rubbed the back of her neck nervously.

    “Looks like it. And we both know how possessive she gets. So just be prepared.”

    Hela swooned. “I know! Oh she’s so romantic!”

    Rio laughed. “She almost killed a guy for looking at her last girlfriend the wrong way.”

    “I know! She’s so passionate!” Hela giggled like a little school girl. “She’s perfect for you then.” Rio shook her head but smiled. They stood there for a moment, just enjoying the other’s presence. “I’m going to tell her.”

    Rio finally broke the comfortable silence.

    Hela’s face lit up. “You are? Oh! That’s great Rio! Agatha is amazing for you! You both have my full support! She’s perfect for you! I’m so glad you’re making this huge step!”

    Rio smiled but looked down at the drinks in her hand. “I’ll tell her. But lot till after Christmas. I don’t want to… risk ruining anything.” Hela’s face fell for a moment. She moved forward and pulled her sister in for a hug. “Rio that woman loves you with every fiber of her being. I promise you everything will be alright. And in the very unlikely chance it goes south I’ll be here for you! But that won’t happen! I can tell, Agatha is a good woman.”

    Rio’s smile grew. “I love her. So much! And Nicky! I love them both! I mean it! Hela I want to…” she sighed. “We haven’t been together that long. But I want to marry her! I am so in love with her and I’ve never loved a kid so much! Something about him feels… familiar! They’re my home!” A couple tears fell down Hela’s cheek. “I know darling. You go get your girl okay? I’ll be here.”

    Rio smirked. “With your girlfriend!”

    Hela blushed. “Yes… I guess so. With Alice. My girlfriend.” Rio patted her shoulder before making her way back to her love.

    “What do you mean Rio is a liar! Who are you to come in here and tell me —“ Sarah gave her a feigned sympathetic look before cutting her off. “Honey, Rio is a fraud and a liar. She has a penis— a real dick and set of balls.”

    Agatha’s eyes widened in shock. “Wait, wha—“ Before she could even finish, a noise cut her off. Agatha looked over the blonde’s shoulder and saw Rio standing there, wide-eyed, tears streaming down her cheeks. The drinks she had just brought were now scattered across the floor.

    The music stopped, and murmurs filled the air. All eyes were on the three women, but mostly Rio.

    Sarah turned with a smirk, casually waving at the raven-haired woman. A flash of genuine fear crossed Rio’s face as she took in the crowd. She could hear the whispers clearly.

    She didn’t hear the people expressing their concern for her. Because only one sentence stuck with her: ”Did that girl just say what I think she said? That’s actually a thing? That’s gross.”

    Agatha stepped forward, her voice soft but urgent. “Rio, wa—” But before she could finish, Rio backed away.

    Agatha reached out, but the force of Rio’s sudden departure sent her tumbling forward.

    “R-Rio!” Agatha shouted before running after her. “Rio!” Chapter End Notes Thank you for reading! I’ll try and update soon! I’m still working on the next chapter. These just take a while to edit.

    The title is based off this song https://youtu.be/CrUM4tVpmRc?si=ImqiOJqMYBqigU6y

    Chapter 8: Behind these hazel eyes!

    Chapter Summary Agatha chases after Rio…

    Chapter Notes !!!!Warning of a transphobic and intersex-phobic character!!! See the end of the chapter for more notes Hela’s fists clenched at her sides, nails digging into her palms as she replayed Rio’s tear-streaked face in her mind. Her chest burned with rage, and before she could think twice, her arm swung back. Coming into contact with the blonde's chin as she punched her.

    Sarah staggered back, her eyes wide with shock as she cradled her face. “What the fuck is wrong with you!?” she screamed, her voice shaking. “You made Rio cry, you bitch!” she spat on her. She stared her down with a glare sharp and venomous.“That’s my sister! My family! And you go and ruin her happiness!? Get the fuck out of here! Or I’ll show you real pain!” The girl stood up and moved toward Hela.

    Alice stepped forward, her eyes blazing. Her voice, usually calm and steady, came out sharp as a knife. “Get out of my house! You’re not welcome here!”

    The blonde turned toward her. Her intense gaze was now fixed on the host of the party. She moved toward her. But Alice wasn’t alone. Three others, faces grim with anger, stood behind her prepared to step in if needed. Hela was one of them.

    It was rare when Alice ever got angry. But here she was ready to kill someone for hurting one of the people that meant so much to her. The blonde girl scoffed before running toward the front door. The room fell silent, the air thick with unease. No one dared move until the slam of the front door echoed through the house.

    Hela started to panic. She paced back and forth quickly. “Shit! I… I gotta go after her!” Hela turned to leave, but before she could Alice grabbed her. “Hela, wait!”

    “Alice! Rio needs me! She—“ “Agatha went after her! She’ll handle it! Just trust her, okay!” Hela searched her eyes, looking for any hint of doubt. When she found none, she let out a breath and relaxed. Pulling out her phone to check the time, she groaned and buried her face in her hands.“I swear if something happens I’m killing that bitch!”

    Alice patted her shoulder. “And I’ll be at your side helping. But it won’t come to that. Just trust me.”

    “Are you—“Before Hela could finish speaking her phone vibrated it was a text from Lilia. Her eyes widened. “Alice, can we take this conversation somewhere more private? Lilia is teasing me! And I need somewhere quiet to think!”

    Alice nodded. She looked around at her guests and in an attempt to ease everyone’s worries she smiled at them. “Everything is fine, guys. Just go back to having fun. I’ll be back in a bit.”

    With that, the two made their way to Alice’s bedroom. They could hear the faint sound of Christmas music coming back on as they entered her most sacred space.

    “What did Lilia say?” Alice asked before sitting down.

    She felt exhaustion creep in as she yawned and settled back into bed. Before closing her eyes, she sent Agatha a goodnight text, a small smile tugging at her lips at the thought of her darling girlfriend. Sleep soon overtook her, her mind drifted and she started to dream of a life where she and Agatha had met years ago.

    “Rio, meet your son.”

    Agatha’s voice trembled with joy as she held the newborn up to her. Rio’s face lit up, tears streaming down her cheeks. Her darling wife had just endured hours of harsh labor and now held their beautiful baby boy. “My love, he’s beautiful,” Rio whispered, taking the infant into her arms. “I know,” Agatha said softly. “He has your face.”

    Rio blushed as the baby’s eyes fluttered open. At first glance, they seemed brown—then green—then she realized they were actually a perfect swirl of brown and blue, a blend of their eye colors.

    They’ll probably darken over time, Rio thought, though her heart swelled with pride. “And look at his thick brown hair,” She said with a grin. “Just like yours! I can already tell he’s going to be a little spitfire! Just like momma!” She winked at her love.

    Agatha snickered. “No, I think he’ll be a sweetheart and maybe a little shy —like his mommy.”

    Rio glanced up, her smile widening. “So, i’m Mommy?”

    Agatha nodded, her expression tender. “Yep and I’m Momma.” Rio raised a playful brow. “Ooh! Mamacita!” she teased, grinning at her the younger woman.

    “Rio!”

    “Hm!?” Rio groaned, rolling onto her side to escape the annoying voice. “You got a package!” Hela’s muffled voice drifted through the door. “Are you decent?”

    Rio sat up with a growl, rubbing the sleep from her eyes. The memory of her dream quickly fading away, but she remembered the basis of it. “If only that were true…” She muttered under her breath, then checked the clock, six a.m. At least it was morning. “Yeah, come in.” Hela pushed the door open, her messy hair sticking up at odd angles from sleep. Her smirk was all too suspicious.

    “What?” Rio muttered, her tone edged with annoyance.

    Hela took her time, dragging out the moment as she slowly brought something out from behind her back.

    “It’s six a.m.! This couldn’t wai—” Rio’s voice caught when she saw the bouquet of flowers.

    “Flowers and a card!” Hela said in a sing-song voice, as she approached the foot of her bed. “Wonder who they’re from?”

    Rio crawled to the edge, snatching the bouquet from Hela’s hands, her cheeks already burning, as she tore open the card. Grumbling up at the woman for waking her up before looking down to read it.

    These flowers aren’t as beautiful as you, my darling. But I hope they put a smile on your face as you have for mine every day! Sincerely yours, -A.H.

    Hela nudged her with an elbow. “Ehh, look at you! Getting flowers delivered to the house at six a.m. I don’t even know how someone managed that. And in the middle of winter!”

    Rio glanced up, suspicion narrowing her eyes. “Do you know something I don’t?” She clutched the bouquet to her chest, inhaling the earthy scent that instantly relaxed her.

    “Maybe…” Hela’s voice trailed off as she turned her head, poorly hiding a sly smile. “Maybe not.”

    “You do! What is it?” Rio shot to her feet, determination burning in her gaze. She needed answers.

    “Hmm…” Hela tapped her chin theatrically. “I mean, how does someone deliver flowers at six in the morning in the dead of winter?” She grinned, eyes twinkling. “Especially when the main florist in town is closed for the season?”

    Rio planted a hand on her hip, glaring. “Easy, go to Walmart and deliver them yourself!”

    “Bingo!” Hela pointed at her with a triumphant laugh.

    Rio’s face lit up in realization. A second later, she bolted out of the room, leaving a laughing Hela behind.

    Her heart pounded in her chest as her bare feet thudded against the wooden floor. She skidded to a halt at the front door and yanked it open with enough force to nearly unhinge it.

    “Oh, finally! I’ve been wa—”

    “Baby!” Rio squealed and launched herself into her girlfriend’s arms. “Oof! Hey to you, too!” Agatha chuckled, stumbling slightly as she wrapped her arms around Rio. “Did I surprise you?”

    Rio pulled back just enough to hold Agatha at arm’s length, her face glowing with excitement. “Yes! You could’ve just texted or called, y’know!”

    “I know, but this way was more fun.” Agatha grinned and leaned up to kiss her.

    Rio hummed in contentment before grabbing her hand and pulling her inside. “Want something to drink? Coffee? Tea? Water?” She moved toward the kitchenette, excited to be the one to treat Agatha as the guest this time. “Tea would be nice,” Agatha said, taking a seat at the counter. Rio nodded and poured hot water from the coffee maker into a mug, adding a tea bag. “Sugar or honey?”

    “Hmm, both.” The younger woman laid her cheek against her hand while she gazed at her love, hard at work for her.

    Rio finished preparing the tea, stirring in the sugar and honey before sliding the mug across the counter. She turned to brew herself a coffee, glancing back over her shoulder. “So, what brings you to my neck of the woods?” She leaned back against the counter, arms crossed, smirking. “Well…” Agatha tapped her nails against the mug, her tone teasing. “I was hoping to invite you over to help me wrap some presents. If you want to, that is.” She took a sip.

    Rio smiled. “Of course I just need to get dressed. Where’s the little monster?”

    “At Mrs Davis’. I told her I needed some alone time to do some Santa work.”

    Rio chuckled. “She’s so sweet. We should hang out with her again sometime. She was so fun! I’m sure her and Nicky are getting into so much trouble!”

    Agatha giggled. “He’ll be the one keeping her in line. Nicky isn’t the biggest trouble maker.” She took a sip of her tea. “Unlike me.” “Oh?” Rio was intrigued. “You were a…” she trailed off, her voice now low. “Bad girl?”

    Agatha blushed. “Oh, Rio…” she was taken aback by the other woman’s flirtatious demeanor. “Your roommate’s here. Are you wanting to start something?” She glanced around for a moment, making sure no one was listening before focusing her attention back on Rio.

    “Hmm…. Tempting. But, I think I’d like it to be somewhere a little more private. Like I said,” Rio smirked, “I’m loud. And you’re louder than me, so…” she trailed off. Allowing Agatha to fill in the gaps. Agatha grinned and swayed side to side, fiddling with her amethyst necklace. “Well… we have all the time in the world.” She bit her lip. “Last night was fun by the way.”

    “Yeah? You were definitely being a naughty girl last night.” Rio tapped her fingers against the counter, she leaned forward, her robe slid forward allowing Agatha a close view of her cleavage. “I think next time we have our little sexy time I’ll be sure to punish you.”

    Agatha’s breath wavered. “I-I look forward to it.”

    Rio was satisfied with the woman’s flustered state. She turned and finished brewing her coffee, then took a sip. Apparently, that was all she needed because right after she set the mug down. “Okay, I gotta go get dressed.” Agatha blinked, not expecting the urgency. “Can I come?”

    “You hoping my resolve will slip?” Rio glanced up through her lashes, a teasing smile on her lips as she rounded the counter, her gaze never leaving Agatha.

    Agatha’s cheeks warmed at the implication. “No, I just want a proper look at your bedroom. Last time I was there…” she paused just long enough to smirk. “I was… distracted.” Her voice dripped with playful suggestion. Rio chuckled, shaking her head. “Fine, come on.” She waved her on before leading the way.

    As they stepped into her room, Rio let out an agitated groan. Her roommate was sprawled across the bed, fast asleep.

    With an eye roll, Rio walked over and tugged at the bedding. “Don’t mind her. She probably tossed and turned all night—she’s been struggling with sleep apnea.” She sighed softly, adjusting the comforter to pull it over Hela then brushing some of the hair from her face.

    Agatha leaned against the doorframe, a warm smile spread across her features. Rio’s tenderness never failed to melt her heart. She truly was the kindest person she had ever known.

    Well… next to Nicky she was.

    “I’m gonna go change in my bathroom,” Rio said, gathering up an outfit. “I’d give you a tour, but…” she balanced around. “There isn’t much to see here, I guess. But I don’t mind answering any questions you have.” She gave Agatha a serious look. “Just don’t look in my closet.” She wagged her finger at her then kissed her cheek before shuffling into the bathroom to change.

    Agatha swooned, her cheeks flushed at the brief touch. She took in the small room, letting her eyes wander over the cozy space.

    Rio’s full-size bed had an emerald green comforter, currently thrown over Hela, and she was lying over white and grey striped sheets. She remembered how they felt—soft and warm, they smelled just like Rio. A mixture of apple and cinnamon. It was nice.

    Beside the bed, two potted plants sat, their leaves vibrant and well-tended. They were clearly well cared for.

    Above the bed, a couple of vinyl records hung on the wall, likely for the record player she had seen out in the living room.

    The walls were painted light green and adorned with vines, leaves, and twinkling fairy lights, that added a whimsical charm. The room gave off an adorable earthy vibe.

    A sleek brown desk stood near the corner, with a large, black computer on top. She noticed the flickering rainbow lights glowing softly inside the transparent side, that was adorned with stickers. She had never seen anything like it before. Perhaps she’d look into getting Nicky something like that when he was a bit older.

    Beside the desk was a very familiar acoustic guitar propped up in the corner and a bookshelf that brimmed with knickknacks and books, giving Agatha a glimpse of Rio’s interests.

    She glanced at the book titles on the shelf. There was a book about botany, a few Stephen King novels, and some brightly colored covers she recognized as manga. The only reason she knew what they were was because she’d bought a couple for Nicky in the past. On the top shelf were little trinkets—figurines of a wolf and a fox. And characters from media Rio loved as well as a mini succulent, and a small framed photo. It was of Rio, herself, and Nicky, taken on the day they went to the harvest festival together.

    Each detail made the room feel uniquely hers—a reflection of the woman she absolutely adored.

    “Anything catch your eye?”

    Agatha glanced over her shoulder to see Rio standing in the doorway buttoning up her pants. She couldn’t help but think how cute her girlfriend looked in her jeans and oversized hoodie with her hair thrown up in a messy bun.

    “Well I can certainly tell you have a thing for plants.”

    The corner of Rio’s lips lifted at that. “Yeah. It’s cause they don’t judge me when I tell them my problems.” She went and stood next to her gazing around her room. Imagining what it’d be like to see it through fresh eyes. She noticed Agatha’s eyes lingering on her guitar, and Rio smiled as an idea for a gift popped into her mind. “So, what do you plan on getting Nicky for Christmas?”

    Agatha shrugged, her tone thoughtful. “Hm… I bought him a PlayStation. Maybe then he’d want to have Billy and Tommy over more.”

    Rio bumped her shoulder playfully. “You’ll definitely be the cool mom!” Agatha turned, her smile soft as she looked up at Rio. She took her hand and led her into the living room, careful not to disturb Hela’s rest. “What’s in your closet, anyway?”

    “Wouldn’t you like to know?” Rio teased, her grin mischievous. Agatha stopped mid-step, raising a brow.

    “It’s a surprise,” Rio said, rolling her eyes at the look on Agatha’s face. “I don’t want you spoiling Christmas.”

    Agatha leaned up and kissed her cheek, her voice dropping to a near whisper. “You’ll stay for both days, won’t you?”

    Rio nodded. “Absolutely!” She smirked, leaning closer. “Maybe then I could…” Her voice dipped lower as she whispered into Agatha’s ear, “get into Ms. Claus’s panties.”

    Agatha hummed, her breath catching. “You planning to make the Yuletide gay?”

    “Oh, I absolutely will,” Rio murmured, her lips grazing Agatha’s pulse point. “So, am I on the naughty or nice list, Ms. Claus?” Her hands slid down Agatha’s back.

    A chuckle bubbled up in the back of Agatha’s throat. “Hm… that depends on where those hands of yours end up.”

    Rio’s hands froze at her hips, and she pulled back just slightly, her breath warm against Agatha’s skin. “You know what sounds really good right now?”

    Agatha’s breath hitched. “What?”

    Rio’s lips curved into a smirk as she leaned closer and whispered, “Chicken and waffles.”

    Agatha groaned at the thought, the tension dissolving into laughter. “Yes, please!”

    Rio pressed a quick kiss to her cheek. “Anything for you.” “Alright, but after that, we’re going back to my house to wrap presents.” “Deal! And we can watch a Christmas movie!”

    Chapter End Notes Just a little something until I post the next chapter. I wrote this before, during and after my small vacation. So that’s why it took a bit. But I had already started the next chapter. This was going to be the beginning of the next chapter but I decided to make it its own.

    Chapter 10: Getting high on love! And Christmas!

    Chapter Summary Rio makes a new friend, hijinks ensues!

    Christmas comes!

    There’s sweetness, angst and family love!

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes Rio had exactly three hours to decorate Agatha’s whole house and she was freaking out.

    She told Agatha she’d decorate the inside as a favor, except the Christmas tree. They’d do that together.

    But Rio wanted to surprise her and decorate the outside of the house too. Nothing overwhelming. Just some Christmas lights on the roof and candy canes aligning the walkway.

    But the only problem was that Rio didn’t know how to put up Christmas lights. She’s never had to do it before. And sure she was pretty handy. She could fix her own damn sink and toilet without needing a plumber thank you very much! And you better know she knew how to change a tire! She’d even consider herself a gas monkey. She enjoyed cars. She could figure out the problem and fix it herself if she needed.

    But never owning your own house and living in apartments and rentals meant no nails in the wall or roof.

    She paced the front yard as she fiddled with a strip of lights.

    “You’re going to pace away the snow at the rate you’ve been going!”

    Rio jumped. Not expecting for someone to be standing right there. She turned, it was just Wanda. Sweet, kind, and helpful, neighbor, Wanda! She grasped her chest as she caught her breath. “You could warn a chick before sneaking up on her!” Rio groaned and looked away for a moment. “I’m too old for this I’m gonna have a heart attack.”

    Wanda chuckled. “Sorry, didn’t mean to startle you. We haven’t really had a chance to talk. Just one on one.”

    “I guess not. Always so busy in a group setting.”

    The two women stood there for a moment in a semi-awkward silence. Wanda had her arms wrapped around herself. Maybe from the cold or maybe she was just shy. She kicked some snow around trying to find something for her body to do.

    “I’m glad you’re with Agatha, by the way.” She broke the silence adding in a small smile.

    Rio looked up in surprise. “Oh! Yeah? I’m glad to hear it!” Wanda chuckled. “I mean it. You’re good for her. I haven’t seen her this alive in a long time. I’ve never seen her hang out with anyone since before Nicky was born. Ever since it’s just been those two against the world.” She took a breath. “I mean I’ve been there. Trying to help her through her tough time adjusting to being a single mother.”

    Rio nodded. Unsure what to add.

    Wanda cleared her throat. “But I didn’t come out here to talk about that. Do you want some help with that?” She gestured toward the light strip. Rio seemed to have forgotten why she was even out there, to begin with, and that she was even holding the lights. “Oh, yeah.” She glanced down at them. “I… don’t really know what I’m doing. I’m sure Vision taught you how to do yours?”

    Wanda lifted a brow. “I taught him, actually.”

    “Oh! Sorry, I didn’t mean to assume I just thought… you know what I’m just going to shut up!”

    “It’s fine!” Wanda waved her off. “I love my husband but he isn’t the most… handy of men. I’ve always taken to crafts and doing things myself so I just watched my old neighbor do it. Well… more like I forced him to show me.”

    “Oh, I bet he was impressed by a mom wanting to put up lights?” “I hope not. I was only ten after all.”

    Rio’s eyes widened. “You’re… a very interesting character.” “So I’ve heard. I’d say it was my Sokovian upbringing that made me so independent. But I’m not so sure it was that exactly. So,” she placed a hand on her hip. “I can show you the ropes and we could have a drink or two later?”

    “Sure! Er, I actually have—” Rio checked her watch, “two hours and thirty- three minutes to get this done. And I was wanting it to be a surprise. Plus I still have the inside to do.”

    “Well then,” Wanda smirked. “Let’s get to work!”

    The two women worked in tandem. Surprisingly well together. Almost as if they had been doing this for years.

    “You know Rio you’re a very quick learner I’m impressed.” Wanda smiled as she finished stapling in the last strand of lights.

    “Well,” she rubbed the back of her neck shyly. “Don’t wanna brag but you could say I’m a bit of… stereotype.” She blew at the end of the stapler as if it were a gun.

    Wanda nodded. She was amused at Rio’s words. “Ah yes. A stereotypical lesbian. Because a woman can’t just be independent unless she is uninterested in men.” She joked.

    “Apparently. I don’t make the rules. Society does.” She shrugged and then smirked. “You, however, don’t strike me as the type who is only interested In men.” She pointed the stapler at the auburn-haired woman. “I’ve seen the Chappell Roan poster in your… woman cave.”

    Wanda rolled her eyes. “Craft room. And sue me! She’s a great singer and songwriter!”

    “You have a PlayStation one in there! And you have a copy of The Price of salt!”

    Wanda snickered. “Am I not allowed to enjoy some crash bandicoot from time to time? And it was a gift.”

    Rio nodded. “Mhm. Was the crocheted pink, purple, and blue blanket on your couch a gift? Or did you make that yourself?”

    Wanda smirked. “Touché. But I don’t care for labels.”

    “But the blanket?”

    The younger woman shrugged. “Pretty colors? I also enjoy the lesbian flag. But you see who I’m married to, so.”

    “Yes, I do. And he’s a nice guy. I won’t pry. I was just curious. You’re not an open book. But you’re very interesting when you get a peak inside. I can see why Agatha has taken to you.”

    “You say that as if me and her met yesterday.”

    Before Rio could reply, Wanda grabbed the latter and moved it closer. Making sure it was still stable.

    “Before we get too deep into the conversation we should probably get inside. I don’t want to freeze to death. I know where Agatha keeps the good booze.” She glanced at Rio from over her shoulder. “Don’t worry I’ll buy her more. I’m no mooch.”

    The two women descended the ladder before making their way inside. They stomped the snow off their boots and brushed their sides off. Wanda shed her winter attire with practiced ease. “Alright so outside is all done. Now for the inside.” She glanced around the entryway. “I guess we’ll have to find the Christmas box.” She sighed then without another word proceeded into the home.

    Rio was in the middle of taking off her own boots, hopping on one foot as she pulled her first boot off. “Wanda, wait up!” She groaned as she yanked her second boot off and then hurried out of her coat. “Ugh! You’re weirdly fast!” She dashed after her.

    “Alright, I forgot, Agatha is sparse with the decor. So we’ll make some just to fill in what she doesn’t have.” Wanda sighed.

    They both looked down at the singular box of decorations. Most of it was ornaments and garland for the tree. Not much else. Aside from some stockings, a snowman here and a reindeer there. Wanda laid out some construction paper and hurriedly started making snowflake chains.

    “I’ll show you how to do snowmen next and we can also make cute little presents and a tree!”

    Rio nodded. She worked diligently to finish these quickly.

    They finished up with their paper projects and quickly put them up around the house.

    “I also bought some things to put up. You don’t think it’s too much do you?” Rio asked, worried that it’d come off as overbearing or something. But Wanda only shook her head with a small smile. “Let’s see, what do we have.” She held out her arms and took the bags before rifling through them. Her smile brightened. “No, dear. These are lovely. Nothing’s too much when it comes to Christmas!”

    Rio let out a sigh of relief. “Okay, good.”

    “Where will you put this?” Wanda smirked pulling out a mistletoe. Rio blushed and snatched the little piece of green. “By the front door of course!”

    Wanda chuckled. “You don’t think that’ll cause problems?” Rio shook her head as she hurried over toward the doorway. “I think it’ll score me a bunch of kisses! And also potentially be an entertaining way to stir up some mayhem!”

    This answer honestly amused Wanda. “Alright Romeo, why don’t we finish this!”

    They hurried finishing up the decorating. With just thirty minutes to spare. Wanda put her hand on her hip and gazed around triumphantly. “Now this, will surely blow Agatha away!”

    “You’re sure? She won’t think it’s a lot?” Rio's nervousness still got the better of her.

    Wanda smiled. “Like I said before, nothing is too much on Christmas! Besides, I’m sure this will make the Harkness’ a very happy duo. I know this will bring up their spirits!”

    Rio nodded listening thoughtfully. Happy that her efforts would be worthwhile.

    “How about that drink?” Wanda mentioned before heading for the kitchen. She opened the highest cabinet in the kitchen and pulled out a bottle of wine. “I’ll be sure to get Agatha more booze. I’ve got connections, so it’s not hard for me to get her the good stuff!” She pulled out two glasses, handing one to Rio. “You a white whine or red whine kind of girl?” Rio blinked, unsure of what to say, “Um…”

    Wanda lifted a brow. “Not a big drinker?”

    Rio shook her head. “Not really. I don’t mind having some on occasion. I just don’t have the best experience with it. You wouldn’t believe how many people working in foster care love to drink. And I mean a lot! Unfortunately for me, a good portion of my foster parents had something they were dependent on. Alcohol abuse was one of the many vices I had to grow up around.”

    “I’m sorry, Rio. That couldn’t have been easy.”

    The older woman shrugged. “It’s in the past. Growing up around it made me who I am today. Though… it ended in me having to stay at a convent which I didn’t care too much for.”

    Wanda perked up at this, curious to know more. “Oh, yeah? What’s that like?” She nodded for Rio to come sit at the table with her. The older woman followed, watching the auburn-haired woman pour their drinks.

    “As you’d probably expect. Strict, old-fashioned to a degree. They weren’t monsters or anything. But I got sent there because I was seen as ‘unruly’ mostly because I wasn’t the most feminine girl and I wasn’t attracted to boys. Honestly, it was better at the convent than with the families. At least the nuns were honest and weren’t trying to ‘sell’ themselves like the foster families were, just to make a quick buck off me.”

    “What kind of things did they teach at the convent?” Wanda was genuinely curious. Such. Foreign world to her.

    Rio sighed before answering. “Lots of things. The place wasn’t exactly foreign to me. Most of my general schooling took place there. I just lived with low-class families outside of it. In the end, I spent the rest of my childhood there. Got kicked out of general foster care at thirteen. Never looked back. But what’s nice about the programs is they prepare you for life” Rio tapped on her glass. Before continuing.

    “The older you get the more likely you are to age out of the system. And at a certain point, your chances of even getting adopted are practically zero. Most people want babies or young kids. They don’t even look at tweens or teens. And a lot of the nuns were foster kids themselves. It was personal for them. They made sure we were star-studded students all around. We learned everything. From the basics, of math, English, science, and history… to life skills, such as culinary, sewing, and finances. Just to name a few… I mean these weren’t introductory! Me and Hela know how to cook! We’ve made costumes! We do our own finances with everything! They really prepared us for life!”

    Wanda nodded along. “Did you get to have hobbies?”

    Rio nodded. “Oh absolutely! The nuns pushed us to find the things we were passionate about! From arts, sports, and music! Hell, they even had computer science programs if you can believe it! I actually learned the drums there! Granted it wasn’t for the music I do now! Church stuff. But it was fun! I learned how to draw and paint! To write to sing and dance! I was even on the basketball team!”

    The auburn-haired woman smiled. “All things considered your childhood sounded amazing!”

    “It was… I just wished I had a family like the kids I’d read about in books! But I was used to it! I had Hela and I knew no one would ever want me.” Wanda was unsure what to say. She had parents. Granted she lost them at a young age, but still she had them. What was the phrase? Is it better to love and lose than to never love at all?

    “I don’t mean to be a bummer! It’s in the past! And I’ve more than accepted it!”

    Rio paused and took a sip of wine, humming at the taste.

    “Good?” Wanda hoped she enjoyed the flavor. “Has a sweet note to it? Or is it sour?”

    Again Rio shrugged. “It’s… alcohol. I guess. Tastes like sparkling grape juice with a touch of poison.” She took another sip, this time taking more into account the ‘sweet’ note Wanda was talking about. She clacked her tongue as she let the taste ruminate. “Meh, I don’t get the hype on this stuff.”

    Wanda tilted her head. “Didn’t you get drunk off your ass on your first date with Agatha?”

    A blush spread across Rio’s cheeks. “Oh, she told you… well… that was different. I was nervous and excited. Needed the help. Y’know?” Wanda chuckled, nodding. “I get it. Seems as though you don’t need it as much. You’re comfortable around her. That’s a good thing. Honest.” “Yeah, she’s been great.”

    “Agatha’s an amazing woman. She’s beautiful and once you get passed that tough shell she’s incredibly kind. So that’s no surprise.” Rio sighed. Taking in the woman’s tone as she said Agatha. “I hope this isn’t too forward or… anything. But did you… do you like Agatha?” Wanda sighed again. “I suppose it wouldn’t be wise to lie.” Rio’s face fell.

    “I’ll admit it’s come and gone, here and there. But I love my husband, and Agatha is my best friend. I don’t have any interest in pursuing any relationship that isn’t what we already have. I promise you I’m no threat. It may sound weird but at this point she’s like a sister to me.” Rio tilted her head. She could understand that surprisingly. It was similar with her and Hela. Granted Rio was too young at the time to understand her confusing emotions, plus Hela was all she had. What was probably an innocent crush evolved into a sisterly love over time. So it wasn’t entire implausible.

    She nodded with a small smile. Content with her answer. The two women sat in a comfortable silence for a bit. Just enjoying the others presence. Rio swished the wine around in her mouth trying to find whatever it was Wanda was talking about in this stuff. Honestly it didn’t taste different from any other wine she’s drank. But it was making her feel relaxed and carefree. So she was fine with its tartness.

    She swirled the liquid around in the glass. Watching it make a little whirlpool. It entertained her for the moment. When a thought came to mind. “What was Agatha like when you met her?” She broached the subject. Sitting up really wanting to know.

    Wanda sighed, setting down the glass. “I’m gonna be honest, we did not! Get along!”

    Rio was honestly surprised at that. “I thought you two ‘clicked’?” “We did. Just not right away. Agatha had just moved in next door with her baby. I was nervous to say the least. I had a hard time making friends and I was fairly new to the area myself. Having only lived there for a year. Ms Davis had apparently been so busy that year, helping her daughter prepare for her own delivery. So I didn’t have the pleasure of meeting her yet.” She took a breath. “Agatha was… to say the least, cold and distant. She was overly attentive to her son and would even take him with her to work. I hadn’t even introduced myself yet. I only watched from afar. But one day I couldn’t take it anymore. Her struggling. I could tell how tired she was. So I… just walked over and said hi.”

    Rio nodded. Very interested in this side of Agatha.

    “She… was awkward to put it lightly. But still, she said hi back. We introduced ourselves and got to talking. She noticed my son, Billy running around in the front yard and that seemed to draw in her interest. We actually managed to hit it off. Eventually she opened up to me. Telling me she was going through a tough time alone. She had inherited her mother’s company and having to juggle that with being a new single mother… was tough. But I started offering to watch him. I had to convince her that everything would be ok. She was so worried about every little thing. First time mother problems really, on top of some other things. But then we fell into a routine. We grew closer and… that was that.”

    Rio smiled. “Huh. Makes sense I guess. She’s in a good place now.” “Oh yeah! And believe me! She was going through things at the time. She was recovering from the tough pregnancy and her mother breathing down her throat wasn’t helping.”

    Rio lifted a brow. “Is that…”

    Rio sighed. “You know what sure. But I’ll take a third of it. I don’t need to have a bad trip. This isn’t gonna fuck up my anxiety meds will it?” Wanda shrugged. “How would I know? I’m not a doctor.” She chuckled. She ripped the head off the bear and tossed its body in her mouth, sighing in delight at its sweet taste before chewing and swallowing it. She held out the head to Rio. “I’m sure it won’t harm you, just this once. It’s not like crack or anything. But I’m not going to peer pressure you. I’m a firm believer in consent.”

She groaned out in annoyance, rifling through the sink cabinet to pull out mouthwash. Luckily Agatha kept little paper cups next to it for Nicky to use. She gargled some of it then spit.
