Our familiar is so dapper!” He reached out and almost on command the rabbit hopped up into his arm and crawled into their lap. “Good boy!”

    Rio couldn’t believe her eyes. “Wow, this rabbit is star quality!” Her eyes widened when the rabbit's own brown ones looked right into her own. “Agatha! I think this rabbit has the soul of a person inside it!” She sunk down in the chair feeling spooked out by the animal.

    “Oh come on Señor Scratchy! Stop scaring mommy!”

    Rio wasn’t sure if she should be more or less scared by the fact that the rabbit listened to the boy and turned away.

    “Alright, Nicky. Time for you and Señor Scratchy to go to bed!” Nicky nodded. “Yay! Santa’s comin' buddy! I hope you were good this year! Maybe he’ll bring you some carrots and lettuce!”

    Rio shook her head with a smile. She stood up and carried the boy and his rabbit to his room.

    Agatha followed happily along.

    “Can you read me a story Mommy?” Nicky asked fluttering his eyelashes at her.

    “Sure, I could read The Grinch That Stole Christmas?”

    Nicky nodded excitedly. “Okay!”

    The day was finally here.

    Christmas!

    And Agatha couldn’t have been more happier.

    She had Rio snuggled up in her bed. And now they’d just wait until six a.m. when they would open presents with Nicky.

    Rio started stirring.

    Agatha’s smile widened as she pulled her lover closer to her chest. “Riooo.” She said her name softly in a sing-song voice. “You gonna wake up?” Rio only hummed and nuzzled closer in response.

    This pulled a chuckle from Agatha. “Come on baby. Don’t you know what day it is?”

    Another hum in response.

    Agatha rolled her eyes with a smile. She held Rio still as she slid down enough to kiss her lips. It was only to soften the blow before she made her attack. Her hand drifted south towards her belly and pushed beneath her shirt. Giving feather-light touches with her nails over her skin. “Agatha….” Rio groaned with a drawn-out suspicion.

    Now it was Agatha’s turn to hum in response.

    “I swear if yo—“ Rio whined as she scrambled to get away. “No, no, no! You wench!” She broke out into uncontrollable laughter as Agatha tickled her mercilessly, she rolled them so she was on top, trapping Rio beneath her.

    “Are you awake now?” Agatha asked with a smirk, continuing her assault. “I yield! Please, my love!! Mercy!”

    Agatha lifted a brow. “What’s the magic words?” She slowed her assault enough to give Rio a moment.

    Rio looked up at her with confusion before smirking. “Praise be thy Queen” She declared before her hand came up to grope Agatha’s chest. “With such supple bosom!?”

    Agatha shook her head and continued her assault. Somehow, Rio managed to keep her grip on her chest, which only amused her further. After a minute of torture, Rio finally gained the upper hand by hooking her legs around Agatha’s waist and flipping their positions. But she was too weak to torture her love in return. Instead, she forced her hands above her head and trapped them there with her own.

    “What? No tickling back?” Agatha asked tilting her head in curiosity. Rio couldn’t help but think how much she looked like an adorable puppy. “No, I, unlike you don’t find pleasure in torturing my partner,” She challenged.

    Agatha snickered. “Well… a queen must make an example of her subjects.” Rio lifted a brow. “Oh? What does that make me?”

    Agatha found amusement in the question, especially since Rio had been the one to refer to her with the noble title first. Biting her lip, Agatha let her eyes scan down Rio’s body for a moment before moving back up. “My royal handywoman. I just can’t seem to… stop finding things broken in my castle.” Her voice took on a breathy and charged tone. “I require the assistance of a…” her eyes dragged down again, “Strong, beautiful woman to help me in my time of need.” She met Rio’s gaze once more. Rio let out a groan of approval, clearly enjoying her role in this little fantasy of theirs. “Beautiful? What, am I going to charm the issues into fixing themselves? I can’t exactly charm the pants off household items.” Agatha gave a low throaty chuckle. “Oh, but you have many a time for your queen. At least, you’ve charmed my dresses off.”

    Rio’s grin widened, and she leaned down to nuzzle her nose against Agatha’s.“Merry Christmas, my queen.”

    “Merry Christmas, my love,” Agatha replied, her voice soft and full of affection.

    Rio giggled deviously as her eyes flickered to her lips.

    Agatha took notice and with a small chuckle she pulled Rio down ready to take her lips into her own and—

    “Merry Christmas!” Came Nicky’s sweet voice as the door to her bedroom swung open.

    Rio threw herself off of Agatha before fumbling to yank the comforter over her head.

    Nicky watched in amusement and confusion as Rio finally managed to cover herself. Hiding from her embarrassment and shame.

    Agatha sat up fast, her face flushed with her own embarrassment at almost being caught kissing in bed! At least they weren’t… in the middle of something else.

    “Nicky, it’s not six yet!”

    Nicky glanced between them in confusion before shaking his head and choosing to focus on what was important. “Yes, it is!” He pointed at the clock on Agatha’s nightstand.

    To which she immediately looked over. She smirked at the digits clearly saying 5:59.

    Rio peeked out from her tent of shame and chuckled. “Awww gotta wait one whole minute!” She said pretending to sound upset about it. But not a second later Agatha’s alarm went off on her phone. Making everyone but Agatha jump, who was used to the alarming sound. In a flash the boy came barreling into her bed, attacking his mother in a barrage of hugs and snuggles. “Merry Christmas Momma!”

    He giggled when she tickled him.

    “Merry Christmas my baby!”

    Rio snapped a few photos quickly.

    Nicky noticed and instead of allowing her to take more photos he gently went over to her and hugged her.

    “Hey, why doesn’t she get assassinated?” Agatha asked incredulously. “It wouldn’t be much of an assassination without the element of surprise.” Rio chimed in playfully.

    “Because I don’t want to scare Rio away…” Nicky muttered, not meeting either woman’s gaze, but continued latching onto Rio.

    Agatha and Rio exchanged a look, unsure how to respond at first. Before Agatha could respond Rio spoke first. “Aw, I wouldn’t leave you, buddy.” She combed her fingers through his hair with a warm smile. “I’m afraid you and your mother are stuck with me!”

    Nicky smiled up at her. “Like a parasite?”

    Agatha blinked, alarmed by his phrasing. “Nicky! Wha—“ But Rio seemed to enjoy it, laughing as if she were proud of the odd statement. “Yes! Exactly like a parasite!” She booped his nose. He beamed at her expectantly before looking over at his mom. Agatha couldn’t take it anymore. He was just so freakin adorable! “Fine! Let’s go!”

    “Yay!” He cheered before bolting out of his mother’s bed.

    Rio got up and before Agatha could even blink she was at her side of the bed offering her hand. “M’lady?”

    Agatha lifted a brow. “Come on Rio! I’m not that old yet.” She snickered before taking her hand.

    She wasn't prepared for the cool slide of silver against her skin. Her breath hitched as Rio fastened a bangle around her wrist—its amethyst stones sparkled from the moonlight that seeped in through the blinds and at its center, an opal crescent moon sat, absorbing the starlight and twinkled like little galaxies.

    “Merry Christmas baby,” Rio smirked, satisfied with her smooth surprise. "Rio." Agatha breathed, lifting her wrist to examine it. When she turned it over, her heart caught in her throat. Engraved on the back, in delicate script, were two words: Mi Luna.

    "You are my light in the darkness. I know I can always look to you to find my way home."

    Agatha lowered her hand to see Rio crouched on the floor gazing longingly up at her. “Oh, Rio… please tell me you didn’t spend a fortune on this?” Rio hesitated, her eyes widening before she lowered her gaze, looking down at the floor. “Oh, no actually. I mean… not with this. I just… I couldn’t afford anything fancy so I—“ She paused, the trembling in her voice was hard to miss. “I made it myself.”

    “You made this!?” Agatha asked in shock as she held up her arm. Rio looked back up at her, wincing almost as if she was expecting it to be thrown in her face or something. “I hope that’s okay. I mean if not I could— “I love it!” Agatha interrupted her voice firm.

    Rio’s face softened. “You do? You mean it!? You’re not just saying that!?” Agatha sighed at the worried look on Rio’s face. Who could have ever hurt this woman? She’s so precious in every sense of the word. Clearly, she’d been through a lot. With how cautious she’s been around her. Agatha cradled her face between her hands. "Rio, listen. I only asked because this looks expensive, like something out of a boutique." She gestured toward the bracelet. "But knowing you made this... That means more to me than anything you could've bought."

    A few stray tears fell down Rio’s face.

    Agatha softly gasped and wiped up her tears. “Oh baby, don’t cry! I love it! I mean it!”

    Rio sniffled and quickly wiped up her own tears. “Sorry. I’m just… they’re happy tears!”

    Agatha softly sighed before leaning forward and pressing her forehead to Rio’s. “¡Te amo, mi corazón!”

    Rio’s eyes widened at the sweet sound of Spanish. “¿Has estado aprendiendo español?”

    Agatha nodded. “Un poco. No genial.” She laughed nervously. “Just knowing you’re making an effort is enough for me. It’s a wonderful Christmas present.”

    Agatha lifted a brow. “Darling if you don’t think half of those gifts under that tree aren’t yours then you’re sorely mistaken.”

    Rio’s face brightened, she leaned up, ready to kiss her love and start this day off right and maybe—

    “Mom!” Nicky shouted.

    Both women chuckled at the boy's impatientness.

    “Coming buddy!” Agatha shouted back.

    Agatha sat by the fire, her arm draped around Rio’s shoulder, watching Nicky excitedly tear into his presents. She occasionally sipped hot chocolate from her mug.

    “Can I have a sip?” Rio whispered into her ear.

    Agatha nodded and handed her the mug. “Careful, it’s hot.” “It’s okay. I’m used to hot things!” Rio winked playfully before taking a sip.

    “Gross!” Nicky commented.

    Agatha stuck her tongue out at the boy then smiled. “Adults flirt. You’ll be okay. What about that one over there?” She pointed over at the large box in the corner. Curious about what was inside. She honestly couldn’t remember if she had gotten that for him.

    Nicky scrambled to his feet to read the label. “It’s for me from mommy Rio!” He said excitedly.

    Rio continued sipping on the sweet hot beverage while giving all her attention to the boy.

    Agatha glanced over at her for a moment then back again. Wondering what in the world she got her son.

    He tore open the Christmas-themed Pokémon wrapping paper and gasped. “Is it…” he quickly opened the case to see a mahogany Yamaha acoustic guitar inside. “A guitar!”

    Agatha looked over at Rio who just shrugged with a smirk while sipping on the hot chocolate.

    “Rio….” Agatha dragged out the words.

    Rio looked away, hiding her smile.

    “You’ll spoil him mi amor.”

    Rio responded with another shrug.

    “Momma, this one’s yours!”

    Agatha turned back to her boy, who was holding up a small box with both hands. “Oh?” She took it from him, casting one last glance at Rio, who now sat watching them expectantly, her mug set aside.

    With a soft sigh, Agatha unwrapped the gift.

    Inside was a plain cardboard box tied with twine. She carefully unraveled it and opened the lid.

    “What is it?” Nicky asked, bouncing on his toes as he tried to peek inside. Agatha’s breath caught.

    It was a handcrafted wooden box, its lid carved with a crescent moon and a tree. When she lifted the lid, soft music played—a familiar tune that made her heart swell: Ballad of The Witches’ Road.

    Inside the box were three treasures.

    On top lay a single purple rose, its petals soft and perfect. Beneath it was a small framed photo of the three of them together, the day they went camping.

    And at the bottom—

    Agatha gasped.

    Nestled snugly in the velvet lining were two matching rings. A large obsidian heart sat in the middle, shimmering between rows of white diamonds. She pulled them out looking them over. The inner bands gleamed with an opalescent hue. One word was etched inside: Promise. Tears welled up in her eyes. She sniffled and wiped at her face. “What’s wrong momma? You don’t like your gift?” Worry flooded Nicky’s tone.

    “I love it!” She looked over at Rio. “I absolutely love it!” She slid toward Rio and pulled her in for a passionate kiss.

    The sound of Nicky gagging made them giggle.

    “Here’s yours Rio!” The boy came over and nudged her shoulder with a huge box. “This one’s from Momma!”

    Rio turned and glanced down at the box. “What do we have here? Come to mommy!” She grabbed it excitedly, not expecting it to be so light, as her hands pushed up expecting to support more weight. And just to torture Agatha she opened the gift meticulously slow.

    She did it for a minute straight before Agatha finally got fed up. “Rio rip it!”

    “I’m sorry! You’re just really good at wrapping! I wanted to savor it!” She giggled. Mocking the way she had opened her birthday gifts a couple months ago.

    Inside was another wrapped box. Rio turned and glared at Agatha, but she gave her the benefit of the doubt. She opened it, but surprise, surprise there was another wrapped box.

    Agatha snickered as she drank her cocoa.

    Rio groaned as she opened that box and, again, inside was another wrapped box!

    “Agatha!”

    “Come on you’re almost there!” Agatha bumped her shoulder with her own. “Just a few more to go!”

    Rio grumbled under her breath as she continued opening box after box. “I mean really! What a waste of wrapping paper!” Rio snarled. “It’s absolutely worth it!”

    Rio looked up noticing Nicky filming her.

    “Have you been doing that the whole time!?”

    He nodded excitedly, an amused smile shined over his features. “Just a little Christmas gift to myself is all.” Agatha snickered. “Go on darling, I promise there’s not many left.”

    “Yeah, yeah…” she opened the box and sighed a sigh of relief when she saw a black envelope inside. She wasn’t expecting Agatha to tell the truth on this. “If I open it and there’s another envelope I swear—“ her breath hitched in her throat when she pulled out three tickets to Wicked, which, had been sold out for months, and Rio had been doing nothing but annoying Hela about it. She jumped out of her seat and squealed. “No way!” Agatha drank her coco smirking. She had a feeling this was how Rio would react. “Nicky be a dear would you?”

    “Yes, mother.” He stopped filming to go and grab five more boxes from the tree.

    Rio stopped, her attention on the boy. “Agatha!!!!” She looked over at the woman who was now spoiling her.

    Agatha simply shrugged while smiling into her mug.

    “Here’s the first one!” Nicky said excitedly as he handed Rio a rectangular box.

    “You’ll need something appropriate to wear to the show, dear,” Agatha said wearing her pride across her face.

    At that, Rio tore into the box quickly. Gasping loudly when she saw it was a green leather jacket! “Oh yes!”

    Before Agatha could comment she noticed one of the presents she meant to keep in her closet. She kept calm to not rouse suspicion. “Can I have the one wrapped in green wrapping paper, son?” She asked holding out her hand.

    Nicky nodded and handed it to her.

    “We’ll open this one later.” She turned and winked at Rio, who flushed nervously.

    “This one looks neat!” Nicky handed her a gift wrapped in Minecraft wrapping paper.

    “Oh, whoops. I didn’t mean to use that paper. Oh well.” Agatha chuckled. Rio took it with a smile. “Is this another item to wear?” She asked looking over at Agatha, who simply shrugged.

    “‘Dunno. Why don’t you open it?”

    Rio let out an excited squeal before unwrapping it. This time a bit slower, but not nearly as slow as the first one. “Aw sweet! These are sick!” She held the leather boots up, taking them in. They had plenty of buckles and straps. They didn’t serve much purpose other than looking cool!

    “Ok, last two!” Nicky handed her the last two boxes, seeming as if he were growing a bit impatient. Probably wanted to open more of his own gifts. She took them happily. The third gift was a lovely framed photo of the three of them that said ‘family’ on it. Rio teared up looking at it because it really did hit her now, that she did indeed have a family. One that she always wanted. One where she could have family dinners with, take their child to school, and open Christmas gifts together.

    The family of her dreams. And it was finally hers.

    The fourth and final gift was a signed pair of drumsticks by The Lorna Wu. “I wasn’t sure how exciting those would be. I assume you’ve met in person before?”

    “Actually no! Weird to say! But I have spoken to her a few times on video call! These are sick! Thank you, baby!” Rio bounced excitedly. Agatha nodded and hummed. “Take them out of the case and turn them around.”

    Rio’s face brightened up and she squealed when she did. “No way! Is that…”

    “Idina Menzel’s autograph.” Agatha mentally patted herself on the back. “It is.”

    Neither Harkness’ was prepared for the excited scream that would erupt from Rio’s lungs. Or the fact that she’d immediately bolt from her spot, to run around the room.

    “Hey! No running!” Nicky scolded her as if he wasn’t the child. “You’re going to get hurt or break something!”

    Now Agatha couldn’t contain herself at the interesting role reversal. “You tell her baby! Rio! Come back over here to me! Nicky still has a few more gifts to open! Afterward, we’ll make cookies! Come on! Get it out of your system already!”

    Rio squealed joyfully. She turned at a sharp angle and headed right toward her girlfriend, barreling into her in the least graceful way she possibly could have, burying her face in Agatha’s soft plush sweater.

    Agatha grunted from the impact while cradling her girlfriend’s head against her chest.

    “Ahhhh! I’m so happy!” Rio squealed then laughed uncontrollably. Nicky’s eyes widened at the awkward position and turned away, covering his face. “Can I open my other gifts now!? Please?”

    “Oh, Rio sweetheart, you’re scaring the boy.”

    The older woman’s eyes widened and she pulled away. “I’m sorry! I didn’t mean to attack you!” She turned toward Nicky. “I’m sorry buddy! The craziness has left the building.”

    “Promise!?”

    Rio nodded. “Yeah, open up your other gifts! Let’s see what Santa brought!” She clamored off the couch and crawled over toward him. “Bro what if—“ she grabbed his shoulders and had him face her. “He brought you the one thing you’ve been asking for!?”

    The boy's eyes widened. “You don’t mean—“ his eyes flickered toward his mother.

    Agatha rolled her eyes with a smile before pursing her lips and looking away. She held her head high and shut her eyes. “I have no idea why you are looking at me. Do I look like the big man in red?”

    Rio glanced over her shoulder. “Hm… me thinks you’re more of a… Mrs Claus!?”

    Agatha peeked one eye open at her girlfriend and smirked. “Alright then, you’ll be Mr Claus in this scenario.” She teased hoping to agitate Rio. But the woman only seemed to enjoy said title.

    She threw her arms up in the air triumphantly. “Yes! And Nicky can be our elf and Señor Scratchy can be our sleigh bunny!”

    “What’s happening?” Nicky muttered. “You haven’t gotten into Billy’s funny gummy bears, have you? Cause I’ve seen what that stuff does to him and he gets weird.”

    Agatha's eyes widened and she shot out of her seat. “No! Of course not! We don’t touch that stuff huh Rio!?” She placed her hand at the back of Rio’s neck to get her attention.

    “Oh, absolutely not! Bad stuff all around! Wouldn’t touch it with a thirty- nine-and-a-half foot pole!” The raven-haired woman chanced a glance at her partner and smiled. “Right babe?”

    “Not even a forty-foot one!” Agatha joked, lightening the mood, she rubbed her hand at the back of Rio’s neck getting her to relax. She had started to tense and Agatha really didn’t want her to go through another self- deprecating panic episode again. She needed her love calm and happy. And the kneading motion she was pushing against her muscles seemed to be helping immensely.

    Rio sighed, melting into her girlfriend’s touch. “What about that box bud?” She pointed at a small one to start with. “With the cute bunny paper.” Nicky smiled, happy to be back on track. “Aw, they all look like Scratchy!”

    Finally, after an hour of opening gifts, Agatha worked on getting breakfast together as Rio helped Nicky set up his PlayStation that he had been waiting very patiently for. And given his impressive grades Agatha was more than happy to give it to him.

    “Aw, sick! Your mom went all out and got you five games too! What are you gonna play first!?”

    “Astrobot probably! Then I’ll play a bit of crash bandicoot!” “Ah, man that was my favorite game as a kid! I used to play it all the time at my friend’s house!”

    “You wanna play with me!?”

    “Aw I would little man but you only have one controller.” “Oh shoot I knew I forgot something!” Came Agatha's voice from the kitchen. She shuffled quickly through the living room and went straight into the entryway and opened the front closet where they stored their extra jackets and shoes. She rifled through the back and with an “Ah-ha!” She pulled out the little box she was looking for. “Baby catch!” She tossed the box over to the pair.

    Rio’s eyes widened and she booked it forward, to not let the box hit the floor. She caught it but had to lower herself toward the floor. “Agatha! You’re lucky I’m fast! But damn! Did I not mention I tore my ACL in college!?” She groaned rubbing at her knee.

    Agatha covered her mouth before running over to Rio. “Oh shit! Honey, I’m sorry!” She got down on her knees and wrapped her arms around her lover. “Are you okay? You didn’t get hurt, did you? I didn’t mean for that to happen!”

    “I’m tough, I’ll live! Don’t worry, I know you didn’t mean it!” She smiled at her love.

    “I’m getting you an ice pack!” She left no room for discussion before getting up and rushing to the kitchen.

    “Are you okay Mommy!?” Nicky rushed over to the woman who was still crouched on the floor.

    Rio glanced away for a moment but nodded. It was a lie. The cold weather wasn’t doing her joints any favors. It was something she had dealt with since she was little. It just didn’t bother her until she got much older. Sometimes she could do physical activities such as sports or… more intimate ones. And be fine. But then at the same time, she’d try to do something small but quick and it’d fuck her up more than it should have. Agatha returned. She noticed the painful look on Rio’s face and crumbled toward the floor at her side. “Rio, hey! Put this on it!” The younger woman’s face filled with worry.

    “Mommy you promise you’re okay?”

    “I-I…” Rio couldn’t answer. She wouldn’t lie to him. Of course, she wouldn’t die, but her knee was honestly starting to kill her right now. She didn’t mean for the whimper to slip from between her lips. She looked down at the floor trying to avoid both pairs of worried eyes on her. Agatha started tearing up. Feeling like she had hurt her love. “I’ll be okay… it’s not the first time this has happened. Won’t be the last.” “Do you need to go to the hospital?”

    Rio shook her head. “No, I’m okay.” In all honesty, it’d probably do her good. But her insurance wasn’t great and she didn’t want to ruin everyone’s Christmas.

    “Rio…”

    The older woman shook her head. She suck up the pain and tears and turned toward Agatha with a smile. “I’m good!” She paused, mustering the courage to lie to her love. “Promise.” She sniffed the air. “The food smells amazing honey, but I think it’s burning.”

    Agatha’s eyes widened. In her state of worry, she hadn’t allowed her senses to take in the smell of burning food. She took the bate however and got up, running to the kitchen to turn off the stove. She needed to start all over on the food. She groaned in annoyance.

    Rio sighed in relief. She turned and faced the youngest of the trio. He continued staring at Rio. “I do that sometimes…” he trailed off. “Huh?” Rio was confused.

    “Pretend I’m okay when I’m not. Because I don’t want to worry Momma or ruin anything.”

    Rio shook her head. “I’m not…”

    “She’s just worried about you. You won’t ruin anything. Promise. She just wants you to feel better. It’s just how she is. She’ll worry and worry and worry some more. It sucks because momma always puts me above herself. I’m sure she’d do the same for you.” His gaze lowered to her knee. “It sucks being in constant pain. Doesn’t it?”

    Rio’s gaze softened. She nodded. Why did this boy understand her so well? “You hide it well. But I’ve noticed. Wasn’t entirely sure. But… it’s one of the reasons I’ve felt so comfortable around you, so fast. I’ve never met someone who understands me the way you do. I feel like… we’re the same in a lot of ways.” He paused, taking a breath. “Is that weird?” Rio shook her head. “No. I get it. I… never put a whole lot of thought into it. But I’ve felt it too.”

    Nicky smiled up at her. “I’m really happy you care for my momma. She needs someone. And you make her happy. My momma hasn’t done anything for herself since…” he looked down at his hands. “Well since I came along. I know it’s what mothers do, but… I feel like…” she sighed. “I feel like I burden her, I—“ “Nicky…”

    “Honestly, I do… she hasn’t gotten to have her own shred of joy because of me. I just… I wish I could be an adult already so she didn’t have to take care of me anymore. To worry about me anymore. I just want my momma to be happy. I don’t want to hold her back like I have been. I…” he wiped the tears from his eyes. “I know she loves me, but I just… I feel like her life would be easier if I wasn’t…” he chanced a glance at her then looked away. “Never mind. It doesn’t matter.”

    Rio gasped and her eyes widened. She reached for the boy. “Nicky what are you saying!?”

    “N-nothing…” he wiped his eyes. “Just.. forget I said anything. Please don’t tell momma. I don’t want her to worry. I’m not… I’m not gonna do anything. I promise. I know it’d only hurt her more.”

    “Nicky, listen to me!” She forced him to look at her. “Your mother loves you with her whole heart! And that will never change! You are not a burden alright!? It doesn’t matter how old you get she will never stop caring and worrying about you! It’s her job! And she does it well! You are her whole world! Her everything! Please don’t say those things! Think those things! I know it’d only tear her up inside! She just wants you to be happy! Because that makes her happy!”

    Nicky nodded. “I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to ruin Christmas.” Rio shook her head. “Hey, buddy, you can talk to me whenever you need okay? And your mother. I know sometimes it’s different and you need a different set of ears, but your mother is the best person for you to talk to! She’s in your corner! By your side! Through every step of the way! And she loves you! I love you! If you ever get those thoughts again, please! Tell her! Or me! Or someone, you can trust! Will you do that for me? Promise me?” He nodded. “I promise, I’m sorry.”

    She sighed and pulled him in close.

    Neither of the two noticed the figure standing off in the distance. Not until they heard sniffling. They both pulled away and saw Agatha crying in the doorway.

    Rio and Nicky spoke at the same time.

    “Agatha!”

    “Momma!”

    “I’m sorry! Nicky! I’m sorry you’re sick and in pain all the time! It’s my fault!” The woman crumbled to the floor.

    The pair sprung up and was at her side in seconds.

    “No, it’s not Momma!”

    “Agatha, hey!”

    Agatha shook her head. “Who else would it be!? It’s my job to take care of you! You’re always hurting and now you… When have you started thinking these things!? I don’t want you to leave me, Nicky! Please promise me you won’t ever do anything so terrible!? Please!” She grabbed his arms and pleaded with him.

    Nicky held himself together from breaking down. “I promise Momma! I didn’t mean it! It's just how I feel sometimes! I just hate that you worry about m—“ “It’s my job to worry! I love you! You’re my son! My baby! My pride, my joy my love! You’re my world! Okay!? It isn’t your job to take care of me! I take care of you! And I’ll never stop doing it! I’ll never stop caring! Not even when you’re an old man! Do you understand me!?” Agatha wiped the tears from her eyes and pulled her son into her.

    Nicky nodded. “I do. I’m sorry mother. I just needed to talk about it.” “Thank you for telling someone, honey.” She glanced over to Rio and mouthed thank you to her.

    Rio softly smiled and then nodded. She felt like she was intruding. And even though she was in pain she went to stand, but the hand gripping her wrist prevented her from leaving. She glanced over and saw Agatha looking at her with desperation. She tugged her arm toward them, pleading her with her eyes not to go.

    Rio sighed, a second pair of eyes glanced at her. The same desperation screamed back at her. She crawled into their embrace, allowing them to hold her as she held them. She kissed both of the foreheads and pulled them close.

    If this wasn’t what Christmas was about she didn’t know what was. Being there for family. Even when it was tough. This was hers, and she’d be damned if she allowed anyone to interfere or take it away. She’d protect these two with her life if she had to.

    “Bud you sure you wanna stay up?” Rio asked as she hovered her hands behind the wobbly boy.

    “Y-yes… w-wanna make it to the new year. Eat cheese and crackers!” It came out in a mutter of slurs.

    Hela laughed. “Ah jeez! Kid looks like me when I’m wasted!” Rio gave her sister a look. “You gonna stand there and make jokes or help me catch the kid when he falls over?”

    Hela rolled her eyes. “Relax. I know for a fact you got this! You’re the strongest chick I know!”

    “I’ll toast to that!” Agatha held up her drink with a smirk. Hela lifted a brow. “Is that… apple juice?”

    The younger woman pulled her glass away offended at the accurate accusation. “Maybe… I’ve been… under the weather. Not in the mood for alcohol.”

    “Yeah, Hela don’t peer pressure the woman.” Alice joked coming up to her side. “Maybe she’s taking a break. Y’know New Year’s resolutions and whatnot.” She eyed the woman.

    “If this is about my pin collecting hobby! Not addiction, then I don’t wanna hear it! Besides, I don’t believe in New Year’s resolutions! Why wait for a specific day to change? Sounds like a bad excuse! Why not just do it now!” Alice gave her a look. “Okay! Then make the change to be financially more responsible, now!”

    Hela rolled her eyes. “I have more than enough money saved up thank you very much! Maybe you could deal with toning it down on the guitar collection! At least my hobby is cheaper and takes up way less space!” She stuck her tongue out at the woman.

    “At least my hobby serves a purpose other than to just sit there and look pretty!”

    Hela gasped in offense. “I serve a purpose and I look pretty all the time!” Agatha groaned, pulling her son and girlfriend away before the two could really get into it.

    “Okay wow! Was not expecting that!” Rio muttered as she was being moved toward Wanda and Lilia.

    The two women were lost in conversation, but when the eldest woman’s eyes landed on Agatha she winked.

    Agatha tilted her head and squinted out of confusion.

    “Momma!” Nicky whined pulling Agatha’s curious gaze away from her assistant.

    “Yes, sweetie?” She crouched down to his level.

    “Dunno if I can stay awake… ’m tired.”

    “Awe thought you wanted to partake in the charcuterie board!” The boy groaned, rubbing more and more sleep from his eyes. “I’ll take him up, sweetie.” Rio leaned in and kissed her girlfriend’s cheek. “Don’t gotta stress. Your amazingly strong and cool girlfriend is here for you!” She picked the boy up with ease. “Save me a kiss for midnight though?” She ended the sentence off as a question when it didn’t need to be. “Always.”

    “Ewwww! Please take me to bed already! Before I barf!” The boy grumbled shoving his face into Rio’s neck to hide away from the piercing LED’s of the kitchen lights.

    “How much did you have to drink young man?” Rio chuckled before waking off with the boy in her arms.

    Agatha smiled after them. But she couldn’t ignore the constant feeling of eyes on her. She turned and saw her old assistant quirking a brow in her direction.

    “Something on your mind, Calderu?”

    Lilia glanced over to make sure Wanda had walked off before shuffling over to Agatha. “Hard cider?” She eyed the beverage.

    “Ah yes! Because who doesn’t drink booze from a SpongeBob cup!” Lilia shrugged. “I don’t know, a mom would. So… virgin cider?” “It’s just apple juice, hun.”

    “Hm…” Lilia hummed thoughtfully before taking the woman in. Glancing her up and down. “So how have you been Agatha? With Rio I mean. You two are quite the couple! Makes my old heart believe in love again! You two are fated lovers! In a constant cycle of love and rebirth! Even when you think you’ve lost her she’ll always come back to you.”

    Agatha gave her a nod. “Is this one of your card readings? I remember you mentioning once that you used to work as a fortune teller in Sicily.” “Do you see cards?” She gestured out in front of her. “I just have eyes, dear. But… for a dear friend, I don’t mind having some old fun tonight.” She pulled a stack of tarot from her pocket.

    This amused Agatha. She went to open her mouth, but before she could ask her question Lilia answered.

    “The craft never leaves me. They’re also a good tool for guidance. Helps with my mental slips… and makes me feel a bit grounded when I feel myself… falling.”

    “Oh Lilia… you know my doors open, you can always talk to me if you’re having a hard time! I’m here for you my darling! Jen and Alice too!” Agatha pulled the older woman in for a hug. She knew she was lonely in life. Losing your family at a young age couldn’t have been easy and even more so the trauma it left her. But she had friends now. And Agatha would always be there for her. Lilia was one of her first friends after Wanda, Jen, and Alice. She just wished she’d realized that sooner.

    Seriously, it’s not like she hadn’t known Lilia for the last thirteen years! Even though Wanda was her first friend. She had known the three other women longer than aged known the redhead.

    It was ridiculous how long it took for her to actually open up to them. But when she needed help for her work they were the first three people she contacted for their respective jobs.

    Lilia’s face softened as took a seat in front of the coffee table. “I’m going to shuffle the deck a few times, then I’ll hand it to you to shuffle. Then you pull three cards from the top and set them face down from right to left.” The elder woman tapped against the table, festering about where to put the cards.

    Agatha smiled and took a seat across from her. She noticed Jen and Alice come over, most likely curious as to what they were doing. “Ooh! Mystical stuff! Should we shut some lights off? Maybe set out some candles?” Agatha joked before taking a sip of her juice.

    Lilia lifted a brow. “Depends… you finally making a move on lil ol’ me?” She smirked at Agatha’s reaction of choking on her juice. “Don’t die on me yet! I need to know your past, present, and future!”

    Agatha rolled her eyes and held out her hand to take the stack. “Alright Momma, let’s see what we got here!” She took the deck in hand and shuffled it herself. She made an obnoxious show of it, earning an eye roll from the ex-fortune teller herself. “Alright, right to left, bam, bam, and bam!” She smacked the cards down dramatically one by one. Making the old woman jump.

    “Alright! Gentle! They don’t make this set anymore!”

    Agatha chuckled. “Sorry, hun.”

    Lilia shook her head before pulling the first card, and laying it face up on the table.

    “The Ten of Wands —your past.”

    Agatha froze. The card showed a figure overwhelmed with heavy wands, struggling under their weight.

    Lilia tilts her head. “This is a card of burden. Struggle. Carrying more than you should. It’s about feeling overwhelmed, maybe by expectations or responsibilities that weren’t yours to bear.”

    Agatha looked away, her jaw tightening “That… sounds about right.” Lilia watched her closely, her voice softening. “Anything you want to share?”

    “My mom. She always wanted me to be… something I couldn’t be.” The older woman reached out giving her hand a squeeze, not pressing further. Instead, she flipped over the second card.

    The Empress —your present.”

    Agatha furrowed her brows. The card depicted a regal woman surrounded by lush greenery, a symbol of abundance and creation.

    “This is a beautiful card. It’s about love, nurture, and creation. Motherhood, even.”

    Agatha laughed nervously. “Well, I am a mom. And things are… really good right now. Better than I ever thought they could be.” Lilia’s eyes narrowed slightly, a spark of curiosity lit in them. “You’ve been feeling okay, though? I mean, you’ve seemed a little… off lately.” Agatha hesitated, her hand unconsciously moving toward her belly. “I’ve just been tired. Probably nothing.”

    Lilia hummed, her fingers hovering over the final card.

    “And your future…”

    She placed the card down slowly, almost as if the weight of it would shatter the table.

    “The Two of Cups.”

    Agatha leaned forward, studying the card.

    Two figures faced each other, exchanging cups under a caduceus—a symbol of unity and connection.

    “Ah, This is about partnership. A deep, soulful connection. Harmony. But it’s also about balance—things coming together in ways you might not expect.”

    Agatha blinked, unsure of what to make of it. “What… what does that mean, exactly?”

    Lilia shrugged, but her eyes gleamed mischievously as if she knew something more than she was letting on. “Hard to say. Maybe something in your life is about to surprise you, or someone. Or maybe, you’re about to figure something out about them. Either way, it’s good. It’s love. It’s fate.” Agatha sat back, chewing on her lip. Something about the cards stirred an uneasy feeling in her chest, unsure as to why.

    Lilia, meanwhile, stared at her friend, her suspicion growing. She muttered softly to herself. “Things are getting interesting.”

    Agatha winced unsure of what she had just said. “Huh?”

    Lilia waved her off. “Oh, nothing! Just a crazy old woman muttering to herself! Now,” she reshuffled the deck. “Rio,” she turned her gaze landing directly on the woman in green who was now approaching the living room. “Free reading?” She shook the cards up in the air.

    Rio lifted a brow and glanced over at Agatha.

    “Hey, she’s the best in town! Seriously! She’s scary good!” Agatha assured her.

    Rio shrugged, “Sure why not.” She took her seat next to Agatha. “What was yours? All good I hope.”

    Agatha nodded. “For the most part… I mean the past one was… y’know. But it’s the past and—“

    “Hey Agatha can you help in here real quick?”

    Agatha glanced over her shoulder, seeing Wanda shuffle out of the kitchen waving a mitten-clad hand, spatula between one of them, and a mess of flour on her apron. “Sure, yeah!” She looked back at Rio. “Be right back.” She kissed her cheek and wandered off, Jen and Alice followed in tow to help with whatever monstrosity Wanda was cooking up.

    “Leaves just you and me.” Lilia chuckled as she shuffled the deck again for good measure.

    Rio sighed and glanced up at the old woman “I don’t know about this, Lilia. I’ve never done this before.”

    Lilia smiled back at her, finding her sudden nervousness endearing. “It’s not scary, I promise. Just a little fun. Past, present, future—you know the drill.” Rio glanced toward Agatha, who was in the kitchen fanning away smoke but laughing away. Seeing her happy always settled Rio’s nerves, so when she turned back she nodded.

    “Alright. Hit me!”

    Lilia stopped shuffling and pulled the first card, laying it down between them.

    “The Five of Pentacles —your past.”

    The card depicted two figures trudging through the snow outside a church, their expressions weary and pained.

    “This is a hard card. It’s about loss, struggle, and feeling left out in the cold. Poverty, isolation… even abandonment.”

    Rio’s lips pressed into a thin line as she leaned back in her chair, her arms crossing over her chest. She let out a long sigh. “Yeah. That… tracks.” Lilia’s gaze softened, and she spoke carefully. “You don’t have to talk about it, but it’s clear you’ve been through a lot. This card doesn’t just mean hardship, though. It’s also about perseverance—finding strength when it feels like the world’s against you.”

    Rio said nothing, her jaw only tightened. She nodded, her eyes flickered back over to Agatha. Needing something to ground herself. Lilia sensed the weight of the moment, and instead of saying anything more she simply pulled the second card.

    “The Ten of Cups —your present.”

    This time, Rio leaned forward, her curiosity piqued. The card showed a joyful family beneath a rainbow of cups, their arms raised in celebration. “This is one of the happiest cards in the deck! It’s about love, harmony, and emotional fulfillment.” She paused, getting Rio’s full attention before adding, “Family.” This seemed to make the younger woman relax. “This card says you’ve found your people, your home.”

    Rio let out a peaceful sigh. “Agatha. Nicky.”

    Lilia smiled at her bliss. “Exactly. Things are good right now. Really good. This is a card that reminds you to enjoy it, to appreciate the happiness you’ve built.”

    Rio’s smile faltered, her self-doubt began creeping in, and she glanced to the floor. “They are. I just… I don’t know if I deserve it.” Lilia tilted her head but didn’t press. Instead, she pulled the final card. “And your future…”

    Rio looked back up, fiddling with her hands with worry.

    Lilia placed the card down slowly, her lips parting slightly as she took it in. “The Judgment card.”

    Rio frowned, studying the image. A figure blew a trumpet as people rose from their graves, their arms outstretched.

    “This card is about awakenings. A reckoning with the past. It’s about truth coming to light and making peace with it. And it’s about second chances— starting fresh.”

    Rio’s face went pale. “Truth? What kind of truth?”

    Lilia hesitated, her gaze flickered toward the kitchen where Agatha stood, laughing away at Wanda’s antics before flickering back to Rio. “Something big. Something that changes everything. But it’s not bad, Rio. This is a card of redemption. It means moving forward, stronger than before.”

    Rio stared at the card, her mind racing.“Does it… say what kind of truth?”

    Lilia sighed. “No. But I think you’ll know when it happens. Just remember, it’s something you can face. And you won’t face it alone.” Rio sat back in her chair, her hand absently rubbing her wrist. The sound of the party buzzed around them, but she felt like she was a million miles away.

    From across the room, Agatha caught her eye and smiled.

    That smile…

    So full of love, it steadied her heart. She spoke quietly, turning back toward the older woman, before glancing back at the floor.

    “I guess we’ll see.”

    Lilia shuffled the deck again, her mind lingering on the Judgment card. She didn’t know exactly what lay ahead for Rio, but something told her that whatever it was, it was already in motion. Her eyes flickered back toward Agatha who was bellying over in laughter. Her gaze specifically locked on her arms clutched around her belly.

    “Rio…” Lilia started before glancing back.

    “Yes?”

    “I know sometimes when you have something, something wonderful you want to hold on to it for dear life. Preserve its innocence and happiness for as long as possible. But please know that the tighter you hold on to something… the more likely it will hurt when it slips from your grasp.” Rio furrowed her brows, unsure of what to say. “I…”

    “Don’t put so much weight on the past, or get caught up worrying about the future,” Lilia took a breath. “If you do you’ll miss what’s most important.”

    “And what’s that?”

    “The now, baby.”

    Lilia let out a wavering sigh before continuing.

    “The present is all we have. Sure, we learn from the past, and yes we can look forward to, or dread our future. But if you stay stuck in either one, you’ll miss out on what’s right in front of you. I know how much family means to you, I’d understand more than anyone. But holding guilt for something that’s long past will only drag you down.”

    Rio tilted her head, confused. “Carrying guilt over what?” Lilia hesitated, glancing away for a moment before shaking her head. “Ugh! I’m getting ahead of myself,” she muttered, adding something under her breath in Italian. Taking a deep breath, she looked back at Rio. “My point is this: just be with them. Don’t try so hard to be perfect, because to them? You already are.”

    Rio smiled, her chest easing at the words. She knew she had a tendency to overthink, to try too hard to hold on to the people she loved. Lilia’s words meant a lot. They reassured her. “Thank you, Lilia. You’re always so wise. What would the group do without you?”

    The old woman shrugged. “Oh… you would have gone bankrupt in Vegas had I not intervened that one time.”

    Now Rio was really confused. “Are you talking about Fall Guys in Vegas? That Canadian independent film, from the mid-90s?”

    “Huh? Oh… oh! Yeah! That was a good one! I took Jen to see that when she was a youngster! That was wild!”

    “I was twelve you goober!”

    Jen’s voice could be heard directly behind them.

    “Is twelve not a child’s age Jennifer?” Lilia asked a little too seriously, for what she meant as a joke.

    Jen almost didn’t take it as such until the old woman started chuckling at her seriousness.

    Rio only shook her head at their antics before turning toward the kitchen. Blue eyes were already on her. Shining so bright with that… kind and beautiful smile!

    Oh!

    Her heart skipped a beat.

    “¡Dios, no soy tu soldado más fuerte!”

    Alice’s voice pulled Rio out of her head.

    “Hey, guys! Get over here, the countdown’s starting!”

    The music dipped as everyone crowded around the TV, their voices buzzing with excitement.

    “Yes, let them balls drop, baby!”

    Agatha choked on her drink, coughing as Hela’s joke echoed above the laughter.

    “Ugh! Babe!” Alice groaned, swatting Hela lightly on the arm. Rio smirked, shaking her head at the couple’s antics.

    The group began counting down.

    Agatha snuck over behind Rio.

    “10! 9! 8! 7!”

    She slid an arm around Rio, pulling her close. Rio stiffened in surprise for a second before relaxing into the warmth.

    “6! 5! 4!”

    Agatha’s voice joined the chorus, but it sounded softer now, just for Rio. “3! 2! 1! Happy New Year!”

    Before Rio could even react, Agatha turned, her lips brushing against her loves in a kiss that was timer perfectly.

    The chaos of the room seemed to melt away. For a brief, blissful moment, it was just them—hearts pounding in unison, the world spinning in celebration.

    “Happy New Year, Rio!” Agatha smiled against her lips.

    Rio never knew such bliss. This was what it was like to have someone to kiss on New Year's!??

    “I love you! Agatha Harkness!”

    If there was one thing Agatha Harkness prided herself on it was her independence. Sure she had a decent support system. But for the most part, she survived as a single mother for nearly 12 years.

    Nothing could bring her down or stand in her way! She’d fight through anything. Solve every new problem that life threw at her. Whether that’d be juggling motherhood and a career, on top of taking care of a house!

    Especially motherhood! It’s not like she had anyone to prepare her for that. She had left Salem behind for a good reason. And that meant leaving behind someone who potentially had some answers.

    But that’s what Google and first-time mother-for-dummies books were for! Plus friends.

    Wanda and Sharon! They were her original support system!

    Things probably wouldn’t have turned out half as good as they had if it wasn’t for those two.

    But now here she was, nearing break and she was stumped!

    Things were coming apart around her, currently.

    What started out as just an obnoxious dripping in her downstairs bathroom sink became a leak fast.

    All she was trying to do was tighten a couple screws!

    What happened!?

    And on top of that, there was something up with her fuse box and she wasn’t getting electricity to certain areas of the house.

    “Shit! Today of all days!”

    She grumbled to herself as she paced back and forth. She placed a pile of towels beneath the sink to help with the slow but sure stream of water coming out of the loose pipes.

    She was so preoccupied with her thoughts she almost didn’t hear her phone buzz.

    Not until maybe, the fifth time.

    She jumped and picked it up.

    It was just her sweet girlfriend. She answered it quickly. “Hey, hun! What’s up?”

    “Aggie! Whatcha up to? I’m catching up on some reading at home, I couldn’t get my mind off you though.”

    The little giggle on the other end made Agatha’s heart flutter., “You’re so sweet. And not much, just trying to fix some things around the house. What are you reading?”

    Rio perked up at this. “Fix? Is something broken? And… it’s…” she chuckled. “It’s kinda… geeky I guess. It’s about the history of plant life and its prehistoric ancestors!”

    Rio sounded ridiculously excited for a topic so… interesting?

    “That sounds like… you. I’m sure you’re having a wonderful time! And it’s just a little leak and some power outage. It’s got me stumped I’ll admit. But it’s alright. I’ll just call a guy and—“ “What!? N-no! No guy! I can do it!”

    “Uhh… you sure? I don’t want to burden you, I know you just want to relax today.”

    The woman groaned on the other end. “Of course, I’ll come help! Never call a guy! Or a random girl! I’m here! I’m queer! And I’m ready to get to fixin'!”

    The sound of metal groaning caused Agatha to jump. She glanced over with wide eyes and saw that the pipe had burst and now there was a huge leak. “Shit! Rio, I gotta go! It got worse! If you’re coming over then get here asap! Or you’ll be swimming to get to my lifeless body!”

    The sound of fabric rustling and a door slamming cracked through her phone's speaker. “That will not happen! I will get there in five minutes! But if I have to dive in then give you mouth to mouth then I will!”

    Five minutes!?

    “Rio! We’ve talked about this! Do not be reckless for me! And how are you getting here!? Did you permanently commandeer your friend Ralph’s truck!? You better not be taking that death trap! It’s still winter you know!”

    “Oh relax! And in a manner of speaking, I have! Dude does stand up, he’s on a tour right now on the West Coast. I’m just keeping an eye on his baby till he gets back.”

    The relief Agatha felt when Rio finally arrived at her place was immense. She wasn’t sure if she should have been relieved that the five minutes she promised had long passed or not.

    Because either that meant she was taking her time, or she ended up in a head-on collision!

    Agatha practically yanked the door off the hinges when she heard that damn thing pull into her driveway.

    Rio though, somehow managed to beat her to the door. But Agatha pulled her in just before she started knocking.

    “Get in here! Before I have a heart attack! I need to feel you!” Agatha pulled her in for a tight hug catching her off guard for just a moment before her body relaxed and she wrapped her arms around her love. “You’re lucky you’re so cute! And hot! And beautiful! And all of the things!” Agatha shoved her face into the crook of her neck. “You’re going to give me an early death I swear.”

    This earned her a chuckle. Rio patted her back and kissed her head. “Awe don’t worry, mistress death won’t allow it!”

    Agatha hummed. “Mistress, huh? Is that a self-proclaimed title? Or did you earn that from your past girlfriends?”

    Now Rio really did laugh. “Girlfriends!? As in plural? I wish I had the balls to—“ Agatha pulled back and quirked a brow at her.

    “Wrong choice of phrasing. I meant to say, I wish I had the ovaries to go on dates when I was younger. But I’m glad I didn’t because those choices led me to you. And I don’t want anybody else. I don’t need anybody else.” “Awe aren’t you just the sweetest.” Agatha stood up on her tiptoes and kissed Rio. “I’m glad you didn’t either. Besides, the thought of you with other women… with anyone else, doesn’t sit well with me.” Rio softened and wrapped her arm around Agatha’s shoulder. “My sweetheart you have nothing to worry about. Now, where's this leak!? I should get to work, I don’t want Nicky to come home to a fish bowl!” She wiggled her toolbox up in the air with a smirk. “Daddy’s got tools, mentally and physically to fix the problem.”

    Agatha’s hands came up to cover her mouth. She hadn’t noticed the toolbox before and now she finally took in her girlfriend’s attire. Denim overalls with one strap unbuckled, over an old Evanescence Tee, that was covered in colorful flicks of paint. To top it off Rio had her hair pulled back in a messy bun sticking out the back of a cute, deep forest green washed baseball cap.

    “Why are you so cute!?” Agatha gushed, immediately pulling out her phone and snapping a couple of pictures. She let out an overwhelmed cry at how excited Rio looked to help her with this! But also, “is this what you wear when you… paint?” She lowered her phone and smiled at the woman. Rio looked down at herself then looked back up at her. “No, I do my taxes in these.” She paused for effect. “Of course, these are my painting clothes! But like I said! No more wasting time! Let’s fix this leak!”

    The two women headed for the bathroom. Rio’s eyes widened the size of saucers at the sight of the damage. The plethora of buckets and towels Agatha had laid out were becoming overfilled and drenched. “Wait you were serious about it flooding!? Why didn’t you shut your water off?” Rio immediately booked it toward the kitchen where the door to the basement was.

    “Wait, you can do that?” Agatha followed after her. Incredulous that she had never learned that.

    “Yes! I thought you were over-exaggerating and would be shutting the water off after you hung up!”

    “I always had a guy come do it for me! I never asked questions. He always just plugged the holes then tightened the pipes and I paid him.” Rio stopped in her tracks and turned, her eyes wide at Agatha’s phrasing unsure if she was messing with her or not. “Who have you been calling over here!? Are you aware there’s also a shut-off valve under the sink!? I can’t use though because of how rusted up it is!” She turned and continued on her way down the stairs. “And no one else needs to be plugging your holes!” She muttered the last bit to herself.

    Agatha shook her head in amusement at her girlfriend’s obvious frustration and jealousy.

    “Look right there!” Rio pointed over toward a set of pipes in the corner of her basement near her washer and dryer. “See this here? This valve?” She twisted it. The sound of a congested gurgle along with a couple of seconds of thumping sounded throughout the basement. “There! Water shut off. Now, next, I’m going to see how fucked your pipes are.” She turned and headed back upstairs.

    Agatha decided she wanted to tease at this moment. She waited until Rio pulled out her flashlight and bent down, leaning toward the sink cabinet before she made her move.

    “Oh, but I want nothing more than for you to fuck my pipes, you always do such a good job too.”

    “Huh!?” Rio went to turn but hit her head on the cabinet in the process. Her hand went to her head as she groaned. “Ugh! God dammit!”

    The feeling of guilt ran through Agatha. She moved toward Rio’s side and reached for her head, only for her to move away. “I’m fine, really.” The younger woman studied her face, making sure she was telling the truth. She saw no deceit so she relaxed and sat back on her heels. “I’m sorry. I shouldn’t have teased you while you were crammed in such a tight space.” Rio’s face fell. Her unamused look burned through Agatha who was trying not to laugh. “If you want your sink fixed then stop cracking jokes like that.”

    Agatha’s laughing stopped and she nodded. “Okay, I’ll be good!” The other woman relaxed. With a nod, she turned back around and examined the pipes. “Jesus! How did it crack open this badly!? Seriously!? Who was servicing these before!? They need to be fired! I’m not even a plumber and I can see that!” She pulled out her wrench and started undoing the washers to remove the section of pipe. “I’m going to need to get you a new pipe. I’m not filling this with anything. The damage is too much, it’ll just bust from the constant fluid and pressure.”

    The younger woman’s hands flew to her face and she turned around shuffling as far away as possible without leaving the room, trying her best not to laugh.

    But Rio could hear her struggle. She decided not to comment on it, instead reacting with an eye roll and smile before turning to get up. “I’m going to the hardware store. I’ll be back in a bit.”

    Agatha nodded with a thumbs up but continued struggling from the floor.

    By the time Rio came back, Agatha had finally composed herself enough to be semi-helpful. She listened to Rio explaining what it was she was doing. So Agatha could have some knowledge on what it was she needed to do if it happened again.

    “I don’t mind being your handywoman, honey. I like it in fact. But it’s best for you to know how to do these things for yourself too. Especially if I’m not here to help.” She continued tinkering around.

    Agatha watched with interest. Mainly because of the amazing view. Rio’s cute butt stuck out of the cabinet, wobbling side to side as she worked.

    It got Agatha thinking. She really enjoyed so many qualities about Rio. Her favorite physical trait was probably her eyes. They were striking and gorgeous. Eyes you could just get lost in for hours.

    She sighed.

    Rio’s face was just perfect all around! She had an intense look and demeanor. That was sure. But Agatha herself was intense. Even though she knew she didn’t look it without trying. It was just so adorable to learn what a juxtaposition Rio’s personality was from her natural resting face. Another one of her favorites was her raven hair that fell in gorgeous waves, framing her face! Perfect round eyes… her plump lips! She was so jealous of them! Her cute nose! Her fucking dimples! And dammit she had the most endearing tooth gap!

    Don’t even get Agatha started on her body!

    She bit her lip. She needed to relax she was getting too worked up about it. She was familiar with Rio’s insecurities. Or at least… the biggest one. She wondered if there were others hidden beneath the surface. Agatha couldn’t understand it. Through her eyes, Rio was a vision of perfection—inside and out.

    But Agatha was no stranger to insecurities herself. Her biggest ones were her scars. Even though they were less noticeable, thanks to the tattooing. Though, they still served as a constant reminder. If you knew to look for them, you could see them clearly—etched into her skin and memory alike.

    Her mind drifted. To her other insecurities…

    Agatha sighed softly, inching closer to her. She cupped Rio’s face in her hands, hesitating for a brief moment before pressing their foreheads together.

    “Don’t apologize. I shouldn’t have shouted,” Rio murmured, her voice shaking. “I never wanted you to see me like that. I promise it won’t happen again.”

    Agatha sighed again, her thumb brushing up and down Rio’s cheek in soothing strokes. “Do you want to talk about it?”

    Rio exhaled deeply, her shoulders slumping. “I should be asking you that question.”

    Agatha shook her head. “It’s… probably PTSD from my mother. The abuse… it never left me, obviously. But you aren’t her. You’re nothing like her. You love me, you treat me like a queen, and now you’re upset, and I just want to help you.” She slid closer, pulling Rio into a tight embrace. “What happened, honey?”

    Rio’s voice broke as she spoke. “I-I… the bank… they’re taking back the building where I work.”

    “What!? Why!?” Agatha asked, her disbelief evident.

    “Because some rich guy wants to buy the property for his own businesses,” Rio explained, her voice thick with anguish. “And I’m only renting to own. But he can afford to buy it outright—hell, and then some. He’s made a few sleazy dirtbags richer, and they couldn’t care less who they hurt in the process. I… I can’t do anything about it. I’m done for.”

    She pulled away from Agatha, burying her face in her hands just as Agatha had moments ago. “And now I have to tell Hela that our dream is being ripped away and I couldn’t even… even fight for it.” Her sobs broke free again. “I’m a loser! A fucking loser! Why wouldn’t I lose this? My life has always been destined for misfortune! Ever since I was born! God, why me!?”

    “Rio, you’re not a loser,” Agatha said firmly, reaching for her. But Rio startled her when her hands fell from her face and she snapped, “How the hell am I not!?” Her words came out louder and sharper than she intended.

    Agatha flinched, instinctively raising her hands defensively to shield her face, bracing for an oncoming strike. But it never came. She waited, expecting insults, expecting to be told how worthless she was—just like her mother used to—but nothing happened.

    Agatha heard a sharp gasp instead of the expected shouting. “Agatha! F-fuck… I-I…” Rio stammered, panic in her voice. She wanted to comfort her but couldn’t—not when she was the one causing the fear. “I did it again… but at you… I didn’t mean… oh my god! What is wrong with me?”

    Peeking around her trembling arms, Agatha saw Rio with her face buried back in her hands, weeping harder than before.

    Agatha had enough. This was spiraling out of hand, all over something beyond either of their control—and a misunderstanding above all else. This wasn’t about Agatha. Rio didn’t mean to hurt her. The real villain here was whoever was trying to rip Rio’s business away, someone who clearly didn’t care about the lives they were affecting.

    “Rio, come here.” Agatha’s voice was firm but soft as she opened her arms. Rio fell into her embrace like a lifeline, clinging to Agatha as if she might disappear. Agatha held her tightly, stroking her back and kissing her forehead, trying to ease her pain.

    Rio sobbed into her neck, her voice breaking. “I’m going to lose everything! I can’t… this is all I know! It’s what I love! What am I without this? I’ll lose my apartment! I’ll be homeless! Hela will be homeless! I can’t do that to her! I promised her we’d never end up like that.” Agatha gently rocked her, shushing her softly. “Then you’ll both live with me. Or I’m sure Alice or Lilia would help Hela if she doesn’t want to stay here. And Rio, you’re more than just your title. What about the florist business?”

    Rio shook her head, tears still streaming. “The building is attached to the funeral home. And if I can’t work, I can’t afford to order flowers to sell. I’ll run out of money in two months or less. This is my purpose, Agatha. It’s how I help people. I don’t have anything else.”

    There was a pause before Agatha’s small voice spoke up.

    “You have me. You have Nicky.”

    She spoke softly before continuing. “Hela and even Señor Scratchy, not to mention all your friends.”

    She paused again, before adding, “You have a home here, with me.”

    “I can’t just impose on you like that!” Rio protested. “I’d be a burden, I—” “You are not a burden, Rio.” Agatha’s voice was firm, unwavering. “You never have been, and you never will be.” She squeezed her tighter, her conviction clear. “Besides… maybe I can help. Do you remember what I do?”

    Rio sat up quickly, blinking. “You work for an investment firm!” Agatha chuckled, taking Rio’s chin in her hand. Her voice took on a teasing ton, practically purring. “Oh, baby. I don’t just work for one. I own one. Don’t you remember? I’m the CEO of my own company.”

    Rio wiped her tears, her heart softening despite her despair. Agatha’s flirtatious tone caught her off guard, but it was comforting—a welcome distraction. “Oh yeah, that’s right. I don’t know how I could forget. You… can help me? That’s okay for you to do?”

    Agatha smiled, stroking Rio’s cheek. “Well, I don’t know if I can save that building. I’ve heard of Stark, and once he’s got his claws in something, it’s hard to pry it away. But I can invest. I can help you find a new home for your business. And if we can’t find one, we’ll buy a lot and build one from scratch.”

    Rio clutched her hands over her chest. “You’d do that? For me? You won’t get in trouble?”

    Agatha’s grin widened. “In trouble? From who? Myself? It’s my business— I make the rules. I invest in worthwhile ventures, and yours is definitely worth it. But…” She hesitated, her expression turning serious. “The issue is that if I offer my services and expertise, I have to charge a fee. I can lower it, but it’ll still look bad if I utilize my resources and funding without any payout. It wouldn’t be good for the company’s reputation… you understand?”

    Rio nodded. “I do. And that’s okay. I don’t expect you or your people to work for free.”

    Agatha frowned. “But I don’t want to take from you. Ugh!” “Well… how much of the earnings are we talking?” Rio asked cautiously. Agatha sighed. “It’s not a fixed percentage for every business, but the average deal is 60-40. You would get the 60%. But that’s way too steep for you. I know it wouldn’t be fair to the other businesses if I gave you special treatment, but this is personal to me. Call it nepotism—I don’t care.” She groaned, rubbing her temple. “I’ll cut the fee. How does 80-20 sound?” “Jeez, babe, that’s a huge cut for you!” Rio’s eyes widened. “I know, but I refuse to charge you my normal rate. And don’t try to talk me into it!” Agatha shot her a pointed look.

    Rio held up her hands defensively. “I wouldn’t dream of it. And even though I feel bad—because I do—I couldn’t afford the regular rate anyway. Even with the 80-20 deal, things will still be tight, but I’ll manage. So yeah, I’ll take the offer.” She extended her hand to Agatha with a determined smile.

    Agatha arched a brow at Rio’s outstretched hand, then let out a surprised laugh. “Are you kidding me? Just seal it with a kiss, damn it!” She yanked Rio in and kissed her deeply, her tone softening when she pulled away. “You’ll stay here, won’t you? At least until we find a new place for your business and get you back on your feet? Maybe even help you find a new apartment?”

    Rio hesitated, then smiled. “That could work. And it’ll be nice waking up next to your room every day.”

    Agatha blinked and winced. “Next to my room? No, Rio. Next to me. In my bed! Why on earth would you take the guest room?”

    Rio shrugged sheepishly. “I just… assumed it might be tiring, seeing me every night. It’s a big change. I mean… would Nicky even be okay with it? Even if it’s just for a while?”

    Agatha gave her an incredulous look. “Rio, that boy adores you! He’d be over the moon. And…” Her cheeks flushed, and she glanced away before meeting Rio’s gaze again. “Maybe you could just… I don’t know… stay with me? Even after we get everything settled?” She fiddled with her fingers nervously. “I’d love to have you here. Nicky would too. And I’m serious—I’ve been thinking about it for a while.”

    Rio’s eyes widened. “Wait, are you asking me to… move in with you?” She swallowed hard.

    Agatha nodded, smiling shyly. “Yes, I am. Will you move in with me, Rio Vidal?” She paused before adding her little joke. “Be… roomies?” Rio burst into giggles, her tension melting away. “Oh, aren’t you just a great… bestie!”

    “If besties raised a kid together.”

    Rio blinked a few times. Did she hear that right?

    “Together?”

    Agatha smiled, “Yes baby. Raise our son together. If you’d like that. I mean, he already calls you Mommy, Nicky’s already adopted you as his other mother. As long as it’s not too fast for you?”

    Rio had to take a breath. “N-no! Not fast!, I’d… I’d really like that. Raising him with you. Being his… mother with you would mean… the world to me. ”

    Agatha sighed dreamily. Rio was just so… perfect! “I love you.” “Oh, I love you, baby!” Rio’s eyes fluttered shut as she leaned in to connect their lips. But instead of soft lips, she kissed skin. Her eyes opened, realizing she was kissing the back of Agatha’s hand.

    “Down, girl!” Agatha chuckled, pulling back with a smirk. “I need to get the house tidy, and you need to talk to Hela about our business deal. Honestly, you should have gotten her consent before agreeing to my terms.” Rio sat back with a small pout. “I just planned on letting her know. She left me with the business side of things—she hates dealing with that stuff. I think she’ll be perfectly happy with the decision, considering we have no other option. Besides, she’ll love teasing me about you being our boss.” “Well, I wouldn’t exactly say boss…”

    “Aww, but I had so many naughty ideas with that!” Rio crossed her arms, huffing like a child.

    Agatha placed a finger over Rio’s pouty lips and laughed softly. “Well, we can definitely explore those fantasies—behind closed doors.” She leaned in and pecked her lips in a chaste kiss. “Anything else you need to talk about, my love?”

    “No, I’m just happy you saved me. Is there anything you need to talk about?”

    Agatha shook her head. “Maybe later. I just need to decompress right now. I promise I’m okay. We’re okay. And I’m not upset with you. Let’s just move past this, alright?”

    Rio nodded, her expression softening. “Of course, Agatha. Anything for you.”

    It was moments like this where Agatha swore she won the lottery in life. Sure there were pitfalls and slip-ups. But no one’s life was perfect.

    But to her, this sure felt perfect.

    Agatha leaned her cheek against her palm while watching her two loves giggle, telling stories of their favorite shows, over a hearty portion of beef stew and biscuits.

    “So when he gets splashed with cold water he turns into a girl! Isn’t that neat? It’s a really cute show! I ship Ranma and Acané! I haven’t watched the original one. But the remake is really pretty!” Nicky’s cheery voice rang through the room.

    Rio nodded while listening along to the boy gushing about his new favorite show.

    “It sounds neat. I wouldn’t have guessed you like romance anime, kiddo.” “It’s not exactly a romance anime. I guess there is romance in it. But it’s mostly… drama and fighting I guess.” He shrugged taking a sip of his water.

    Agatha sat back, smiling, watching these two oddly similar people chat away.

    Rio’s face lit up before leaning forward in her chair. “Oh, so I started watching this one anime, and let me tell you…”

    And speaking of similarities…

    Agatha’s eyes flickered between the two.

    That feeling came back to her.

    She studied their faces, their laughter.

    It was almost like—

    Before she could finish the thought her hands flew up to her mouth, she pushed her chair back, and the feet of it squeaked against the hardwood floor startling the pair as she stood up abruptly.

    Similar eyes looked up at her with worry.

    Then they both spoke at the same time.

    “Aggie?” “Momma?”

    “Oh god!” She ran to the bathroom nearby, to throw up for what felt like the millionth time.

    As she did the image of their faces continued rattling in her mind.

    And that feeling intensified, this time it localized in her lower belly.

    She hadn’t felt this sick since…

    Her eyes widened.

    “Babe! Are you okay!? Should we take you to the doctor?”

    Rio asked from the doorway.

    Agatha shook her head, wiping her face and smiling up at Rio to calm her down. “Oh, absolutely not. I will be okay. I feel better already!” “A-are you sure?” Rio was taken aback by her calm response. Agatha nodded. “Yes, I promise. I have to use the bathroom. So I just need a minute.”

    Rio nodded. “Okay, honey. I’m out here if you need anything. Just call if you need me okay?”

    Agatha nodded.

    Rio sighed giving her one last look before shutting the door.

    The moment it clicked Agatha moved toward her sink. Yanking each drawer open before rifling through them.

    “Where are you? Come on I know you’re in here!” After a minute of looking, she finally found what she needed. “There you are. I’ll need to thank you, Wanda. And your emergency scares later.”

    She did what she needed to do, then waited. Her heart thundered in her chest as she stared down at it. This was the longest three minutes of her life. She had to look a way for a moment. It was too much. She glanced at her phone and saw that five minutes had passed. She mustered all of her courage and turned.

    Her hand shot up to her mouth in disbelief.

    “Oh! Oh my god! No! No! No! I am way too old for this! Oh my god! What am I going to do!?”

    Agatha couldn’t believe her eyes. She stared down at the little symbol on the pregnancy test in shock.

    Because right there on the little screen was a tiny blue plus sign. Chapter End Notes Thank you for reading I hope you guys enjoyed this chapter. Let me know what you thought of it.
