    Chapter 13: There’s no coming back from this!

    Chapter Summary Agatha deals with her realization, finally she makes a decision. A turning point in her relationship.

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes The news had been weighing on Agatha’s mind for days, a heavy secret she wasn’t ready to share.

    At least it explained the nausea, mood swings, and sudden weight gain. She was a little over a month into the pregnancy but had no idea how to handle it.

    Not to mention, she was alone.

    If she told anyone, it would be Rio. But she wasn’t ready yet. It had been twelve years since her last pregnancy. In some ways, it felt like yesterday; in others, a lifetime ago. The experience felt distant, like a faded photograph in the back of her mind. She hadn’t documented much of it back then—why would she? She never expected to find herself in this situation again.

    Yet here she was.

    Pregnant.

    With Rio’s baby.

    It… was Rio’s.

    How was she supposed to feel about that?

    She pressed her palm against her forehead, desperate to ease some of the throbbing pain behind her temples.

    She picked up her fork, absently pushing the vegetables around on her plate, hoping the distraction might help.

    It didn’t.

    And neither did Nicky’s sudden piercing laughter.

    She groaned, shutting her eyes and covering her ears.

    It was a shame. Nicky’s laughter, a sound that usually brought her so much joy, was now adding to the pain.

    Agatha could hear muffled voices but was unable to make out what was being said.

    Then, a hand rested gently on her shoulder.

    She opened her eyes to find Rio crouched in front of her, worry etched into her features.

    Agatha slowly lowered her hands, allowing herself to hear Rio’s words. “—ou look pale. Are you okay?”

    Agatha’s gaze flicked to Nicky, who was watching her with the same concern.

    Rio sighed, clearly understanding. Turning toward Nicky, she offered him a reassuring smile. “Hey, bud. Think you can give your mom and me a minute to chat? I’ll buy you a candy bar as thanks.”

    Nicky hesitated, his eyes darting between his mom and Rio. But Agatha forced a reassuring smile, and it seemed to do the trick. With a small nod, he excused himself to the living room, where the sound of the TV soon filled the quiet space.

    Only then did Rio turn her attention back to Agatha. Her voice was soft but firm. “What’s wrong? You’ve been out of it for days. You’re scaring me.” She took Agatha’s hand, lifting it to her lips, and placed a tender kiss there. Agatha tried to keep her expression neutral. She wasn’t ready to tell her— not yet.

    “I’m fine, my love. I’m not sick, I promise.”

    Which, technically, was true.

    Rio sighed, her shoulders sinking. She clearly didn’t believe her but chose not to push. “I’m here, okay? If you ever need anything. I love you. You know that, right?”

    And damn Rio for that sweet and sincere smile! And for those kind and understanding eyes that always seemed to see right through her. “I know, my darling. And I love you. You’re so sweet.” Agatha cupped Rio’s face, her thumb brushing gently across her cheek. With her other hand, she swept a stray raven lock away from Rio’s forehead.

    And that’s how it went for a week.

    Rio allowed Agatha to just be. Staying patient, hoping, when Agatha was ready she would come to her about it.

    But it didn’t help that the younger woman didn’t get much time to see her love or her son, as of late. A relentless work week had swept her away, leaving little room for family time.

    At least this time Nicky didn’t have to stay with Wanda.

    Because Rio had officially closed her business, moved the property into storage, and left her apartment behind, to move in with them. And Nicky couldn’t have been happier—he was thrilled that he’d get to see Rio every day now.

    Hela, on the other hand, had mixed feelings about the change. But she trusted Rio above all else and decided to embrace it.

    When Agatha offered her a place to stay, she politely declined. She didn’t want to interfere with Rio’s new family dynamic. She wanted her little sis to spread her wings. They’ve lived together long enough and as nice as it was, she was ready for the younger of the two to move on. Plus, she had a super cute singer offering up her bed for her to sleep in. And how could Hela possibly refuse such a tempting offer?

    It made Agatha so happy, to see Rio’s things around the home. At first, Rio suggested putting most of her things in storage. When Agatha protested, Rio relented—but only slightly—offering to stow them in the attic or basement instead.

    This annoyed Agatha even more.

    Rio wasn’t trying to argue; she simply didn’t want to impose. She even suggested setting up her things in the guest room, offering the idea of it being her office or personal space.

    And while Agatha was fine with the idea, she refused to let all traces of Rio be confined to one room.

    Agatha had said things like, “I don’t mind if you hang your records in the living room—Or your plants! Keep your guitar in our bedroom or your new office space if you’d like. Put your figurines wherever you want! Do whatever makes you comfortable. This is your home now too!” Despite her reassurance, Rio remained bashful. Agatha could see it in the way she moved like she still felt like an intruder in a space that wasn’t hers.

    “I’m sorry! If that looks bad there, I’ll move it somewhere else! O-or I can just put it up in the attic! It’s no problem, really—”

    “Rio, baby, relax! It looks great there! Look, Nicky won’t stop staring at it!”Agatha sighed, tapping her foot against the hardwood floor as Rio fretted over where to hang her various paintings.

    Nicky had taken a particular liking to one of Rio’s works—a breathtaking painting of a blossom tree in the foreground with a city skyline in the distance. The detail was mesmerizing. Rio truly had a gift, though she seemed too shy to acknowledge it.

    She held up another canvas, avoiding Agatha’s gaze. Her hands trembled slightly, “I-Is this okay? I-I made this one for you.”

    Agatha’s breath caught in her throat as she took in the vibrant scene: a family of rabbits snuggled together in a pile of multicolored leaves. A rusted bucket sat in the corner of the foreground, and a pitchfork leaned against a tree further back.

    The level of detail was astounding, and Agatha marveled at Rio’s craftsmanship, even as Rio looked embarrassed by it. Agatha understood; that an artist’s eye is often its own worst critic. As a writer, she felt the same way about her stories and poems.

    “Rio, it’s gorgeous!”

    After plenty of back and forth, everything finally found its place. So Rio took the role of stay-at-home wife and mother, which had excited Agatha to no end.

    Rio was able to watch Nicky, instead of Agatha having to dump him on the neighbors.

    And getting to come home to the both of them every day… It meant the world to her.

    Currently, Agatha was buried in her work, the pulsing migraine she’d been battling with was doing her no favors.

    She had to check in with Rio every few hours, convincing her that working overtime was fine. It was the only way to keep the older woman from storming into the office again—like she had before.

    But, of course, Agatha lost track of time—and of the promise she had made about being home for dinner.

    And she knew how important dinner time was to Rio. It was a moment to sit down as a family and spend quality time together. Talking about their days, what books they were reading, shows they were watching. How they were doing at work or school.

    Agatha agreed wholeheartedly, but she hadn’t meant to push herself to the brink of exhaustion just to pass out at her desk.

    She didn’t hear Rio storming into the office or her voice calling her name. It wasn’t until she was shaken awake that she registered anything. “Agatha! Hey, wake up! Let’s go home, honey. Please! You promised me— you promised Nicky!”

    Agatha groaned, groggy as she came to. The realization of where she was— and who was speaking—hit her all at once. Embarrassment burned through her. She hadn’t just stayed late; she’d fallen asleep and started drooling. “Oh, crap!” She rubbed her eyes quickly. “I’m sorry, sweetie! I didn’t mean to fall asleep. I set an alarm, and—”

    She grabbed her phone but faltered mid-sentence, her stomach sunk when she saw that it was actually the calculator app open, and not the clock app. Rio covered her mouth to suppress a chuckle. “Oh my god, that’s ridiculously funny!”

    Agatha groaned. But couldn’t help feeling her bliss at hearing Rio’s sweet little giggles. “Is there still time to make it to family dinner night? Or have I ruined the evening?”

    Rio offered a small smile but shook her head. “I’m afraid not. It’s late and Nicky was practically starving to death. I couldn’t bear to tell him to wait. So he ate and now, he’s asleep at home. Billy was sweet enough to stay over at the house while I came to pick you up. But if you’re up for it, we could eat together. Unless you’re too tired… I’d understand. I just want you home.”

    Agatha sighed as she nodded, turning to shut off her computer and laptop. Grabbing her purse, she pushed her chair back and stood up. Her legs, still half-asleep, wobbled beneath her, and a surge of panic rose. The last thing she needed was to fall—especially in heels. But before she could, Rio’s arms wrapped securely around her waist, steadying her before pulling her in close.

    “Oh, honey, let me help you. Just relax,” Rio spoke so softly. Agatha let out a startled squeak as her girlfriend effortlessly swept her up into her arms, bridal style.

    Heat rushed to her cheeks as she instinctively rested her hands on Rio’s shoulder and chest. “Oh! I forget how strong you are!”

    Rio giggled, allowing herself a little reward as her eyes roamed over Agatha’s figure, appreciating her stunning work attire.

    She wore a crisp white blouse with the top three buttons undone, teasing a hint of cleavage beneath her amethyst necklace. A tight black pencil skirt hugged her curves, paired with sleek black stockings that led down to black stilettos, which sat loosely on her feet.

    “Gosh, you’re so beautiful in your work clothes! I should bother you at work more often!”

    “No! Ugh, I’ll never get anything done if you do that!” Agatha huffed. Rio chuckled, amused by how easy it was to rile her up. Without hesitation, she turned and began carrying Agatha toward the office door. “Come on, sleepyhead. Let’s get you home—I made zucchini spaghetti!” Agatha’s stomach growled in response, making Rio grin. “Oh, that does sound delicious! Wait—oh crap! Rio, people are still here! They’ll see!” Agatha frantically reached for the doorframe, trying to stop her. “And? It’s not like they didn’t see me do this the first time. What’s the problem? They’ll just see how much your partner cares for you! Besides…” Rio smirked. “Do you really want to walk right now?”

    Agatha grumbled, slumping in defeat. “No, not really.”

    “Then it’s settled. If anyone says anything rude, I’ll pummel them. How’s that sound?”

    “No, Rio! This is a workplace—I’d like to keep it a violence-free zone, thank you very much!”

    “Fine,” Rio teased. “Then I’ll settle for glaring at them.”

    And glare she did. For the few who dared to glance their way with raised eyebrows or curious stares, Rio’s sharp look was enough to send them scurrying. The sight of it honestly amused Agatha, who couldn’t help but smile to herself as they made their way out.

    And Rio only continued being amazing when they got home. She had kept the pasta warm on the stove on a simmer. Serving Agatha up a hefty portion before plopping down on the couch next to her to watch a movie. “Rio, this is an absurd amount of food for one person!” Agatha stared at the plate in shock before picking up the large slice of Texas toast, next to the huge pile of zucchini noodles. She glanced up at her girlfriend who had the same sized plate.

    She shrugged before shoveling a large forkful into her mouth. Agatha’s jaw dropped at the amount of food she consumed in one go. She wasn’t disgusted—far from it. She was astounded at Rio’s ability to even be able to shove all of that down her throat at once! And the fact that she was doing it without shame in front of somebody else.

    Is this what being domestic with someone was like? To just be truly comfortable around the person you cared for the most?

    It was nice.

    Rio noticed Agatha’s gaze, turned her head, and stopped eating, before gulping down the large portion and setting the plate down on the coffee table. She looked away bashfully, wiping her mouth with the back of her hand. “Oh uh… I-I’m sorry… that was rude of me.”

    Agatha sighed, setting her plate down, and moved closer to Rio. “What was rude? You’re just enjoying your delicious food. Nothing wrong with that. Why’d you stop? Aren’t you hungry?”

    Rio looked back at her. “I mean yeah… I just… I forgot I’m not living with Hela anymore. I… I didn’t want to weird you out I guess. It didn’t bother you?”

    Agatha shook her head, running her fingers through her hair. “No sweetie. Come on, let’s enjoy our dinner and watch a movie. Then we can snuggle.” Rio’s face softened. “Okay!” She said happily before grabbing her plate and resumed eating. This time though she made sure not to grab huge forkfuls. Agatha shook her head at Rio’s antics. This woman surely was interesting. She grabbed her plate as well. Still shocked at the amount on there for herself. “But seriously! Why’d you fill my plate!? You gave me way more than yours!”

    “Oh, well… I didn’t want you to starve.” Rio’s smile was all too pure as she spoke. “So instead of giving you too little, I gave you a lot! Good idea huh?”

    It was… but still!

    “Are you trying to make me fat, Rio?”

    “No! I just don’t want you to go hungry! Eating is important! Especially the right amount!” There was conviction in the older woman’s voice. Agatha hummed in response. “Would it bother you if I was?” Because soon that would be somewhat a reality, and Agatha was scared to death about all of it.

    “Huh?”

    “If I gained weight. Would that bother you?”

    Rio shook her head quickly. “No! I don’t care! You’re sexy no matter what! Eat my yummy food! Or I’ll eat it myself!” Rio reached for the plate, but Agatha moved away.

    “No!! If I don’t finish it you can have the rest! But I want to indulge myself tonight! Now back away you!” Agatha pointed her fork at her. “Mine!” She added with a little growl.

    “Sheesh! Okay!” Rio joked back. “You’re so moody when you’re hungry. Remind me never to poke the bear. I want to live!”

    Agatha suppressed a sigh. She wasn’t moody because of the lack of eating. Well… maybe a little.

    But most of it was from…

    She looked back over at Rio, who was lost in her food and the beginning of a film Agatha hadn’t even bothered to pay attention to.

    When should she tell her? There’s no time like the present, but… Agatha’s heart thudded in her chest.

    It definitely didn’t help when Rio broke out into laughter at something that happened in the movie.

    The same laugh her son had.

    Oh!

    She’ll tell her tomorrow! She had the day off.

    She could do it!

    …She couldn’t do it.

    Not when she had seen a pop-up ad for single mothers, online. “Why does this have to be so hard!?”

    She groaned.

    The day was on the verge of ending. They would be going to bed soon. Fuck!

    How should she even bring it up?

    There was so much here! And she was the only one who knew!

    She sat on a stool in the kitchen, staring out at the night sky. She could hear Rio and Nicky’s muffled voices and laughs from upstairs. She was telling him a bedtime story. No doubt they were having a good time. The sound warmed her heart.

    “Fine, I can’t take this anymore.” She stood up and headed for one of her many little safes that she kept hidden around the house. This particular one was kept at the back of their shoe closet beneath the stairs. She punched in the code and then ruffled around through some old and expensive jewelry that she kept in here. This was her least used safe. The others were vastly more important. The one in her closet held her and Nicky’s passports and any identification, like birth certificates and social security cards. As well as some gun ammo and a bunch of cash in case she needed it for an emergency.

    She kept the actual gun in her nightstand, unloaded, but still there to ward off any intruders and the actual ammo stored away in case she really needed it.

    The other one was in her study and held important documents she needed for work that had personal information on them.

    Other than that, that was it. But she decided she wanted to keep her positive pregnancy test somewhere Rio wouldn’t think to look.

    Not that she would. Considering she had no idea.

    She grabbed a little slipcase that was normally used for glasses that she kept the cleaned pregnancy test in and slipped it into her back pocket. She whispered words of encouragement to herself as she headed for the downstairs bathroom, figuring that would be the most private room in the house that wasn’t near Nicky’s bedroom.

    “Rio! Could you come here please?”

    Chapter End Notes Cut this one short. Wanted it to end on a cliffhanger. Update should be soon-ish!

    And will be angsty.

    Chapter 14: Baby, please don’t run away!

    Chapter Summary Agatha has a much needed discussion with Rio…

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes “Rio, could you come here, please?” Agatha called out from the bathroom doorway.

    She waited for a reply but heard nothing. Her hands trembled as she called out again.

    “Sweetheart?”

    “Be down in a minute, honey!” Rio’s voice drifted down from upstairs. Agatha sucked in a shaky breath as she took a seat on the closed toilet lid, her heart pounded in her chest and ears.

    “Aggie?”

    Her head shot up at the sound of Rio calling for her. “In here! The bathroom,” she replied, her voice unsteady.

    Footsteps approached and finally, Rio poked her head in through the doorway.

    “Oh? Are you okay?”

    “Can you come in here? Shut the door and lock it,” Agatha asked barely above a whisper.

    Rio hesitated, studying her for a moment before nodding. She stepped inside, gently closing the door behind her, turning the lock with a soft click. “What’s going on? Are you okay?”

    Agatha closed her eyes, exhaling shakily before shaking her head. “Well… I… it depends.” When she opened her eyes, they glistened with her unshed tears.

    Rio’s brows furrowed with concern, she knelt down to Agatha’s level and reached for her hands. “Hey, what’s wrong?” Her voice was gentle and soft. “Rio…” Agatha’s voice wavered as she took another shaky breath. “You… I…”

    She needed some space to do this so she stood abruptly, slipping her hands out of Rio’s grasp and turned away. Crossing the small bathroom to face the wall, with her back to the very woman she loved.

    Rio stood up fast, clutching her chest as her heart hammered against her ribs. The panic began to well up inside her. Her mind raced with questions. Had she done something wrong? Why was Agatha being so distant? What was causing this trepidation?

    But she said nothing. She just stood there, waiting. Waiting for the woman she loved to speak.

    “Rio, did you go to Alice’s birthday party? Her twenty-second birthday party? When she lived in Eastview? With the huge garden in the front?”

    Rio hadn’t expected that question, she had to think about it for a moment. That was a long time ago. “I…” she thought about the garden… it brought back some memories of the party, after a minute a light bulb went off. “Oh, yeah. I was there. Were you there too?”

    Agatha nodded. “That was… twelve years ago if I’m not mistaken.” She muttered under her breath.

    Rio had to strain her ears to hear her. “Oh? I guess so…” she took a breath before taking a step toward her, reaching out. “Hey Agatha what’s g—“ Agatha turned around suddenly, and the sight of tears streaming down her face knocked the breath from Rio’s lungs. The older woman froze, her hands twitching with the urge to hold her love. But something told her to wait. To listen.

    “Do… do you remember me? From… that night?” Agatha’s voice wavered. Rio brows furrowed as she blinked. She looked up again, trying to scrub her memories as best she could. “I… I don’t know. It was a long time ago! And I was probably drunk. Maybe… I—“ “Dammit, Rio! Think!” Agatha snapped, not meaning to startle the poor woman, but she was getting frustrated. “You really don’t remember me? Remember that night?”

    Rio was so confused. There were flickers… of something… gorgeous blue eyes… a purple dress… sweet laugh…

    But that was only ever a dream, wasn’t it?

    “I… I didn’t even know you were there. It was a long time ago. I’m having a hard time remembering anything about it. I was really drunk.” She moved closer to reach out for Agatha. “Honey are you feeling—“ “Rio!” Agatha jerked her body away like Rio’s very touch would burn her. Rio dropped her hand and stood back. Why… why was she acting like she was afraid?

    Or disgusted…

    Was she—

    “Agatha did I do something…” her voice fell away. She couldn’t even ask the question it hurt too bad. “What did I do wrong? How can I fix it?” She offered. Maybe she did do something wrong and couldn’t remember. All she knew was she couldn’t let this get out of hand.

    But the frustrated look on Agatha’s face told her she hadn’t said the right thing.

    Agatha’s voice was small, but it trembled with emotion. “I… I was having a hard time piecing it together! Maybe I would have, eventually, without that damn photo, but it would’ve taken me so much longer! Lilia found a photo —from that night. At Alice’s party. You really don’t remember!?” Rio shook her head as her confusion deepened.

    “It was you!” Agatha’s voice cracked, as she finally said the words she had been wanting to say for days.

    “Me?” Rio took a step back, she was still so confused and Agatha was walking toward her with an strange look in her eyes. “What are you tal—“

    “You! It’s always been you!”

    Agatha’s voice broke again. “You got me pregnant that night! It’s been you this whole time!” Her finger jabbed against Rio’s chest with every word, her voice sharp but trembling. “How can you not remember!?” Rio blinked a few times, stunned.

    Agatha half expected Rio to panic, maybe yell or deny it outright. What she hadn’t expected was laughter. “Why are you laughing!?” She asked incredulously.

    Rio shook her head, her laugh shaky and nervous. “Because that’s insane, Agatha. I’m a woman. I can’t get anyone pregnant!” But the words came out too fast, too defensive, her voice was cracking under the weight of the whole thing.

    Agatha’s jaw clenched as her anger overwhelmed her. She couldn’t control her temper anymore, her voice rose, carrying all of the hurt and frustration caused by Rio’s denial.

    “Yes, you can!”

    Agatha pulled the pregnancy test out from her pocket and held it up like it was the most important thing in the world. Her hand trembled as she pushed it toward Rio. “Rio, I’m pregnant. And you’re the only person I’ve been with! The only one in the last twelve years!”

    Rio’s quiet and awkward laughter died in her throat. Her eyes locked on the test, her expression shifting from disbelief to dread, as the color drained from her face. “Is that…”

    “It’s yours,” Agatha said, her voice breaking as she tried holding herself together.

    Rio opened her mouth, fumbling for something to say. Instead she blurted out the first thing that came to mind—even though it was the lousiest thing she could have uttered, “There has to be someone el—”

    Agatha slammed her hand against the wall as her anger erupted. Her voice was piercing and raw as she screamed, “I HAVEN’T BEEN WITH ANYONE BUT YOU!”

    Her words carried the weight of her emotions. How could Rio even suggest that she’d been unfaithful? The accusation was like a dagger, sharp and cruel, plunging straight through her heart! Her chest heaved as she fought to catch her breath.

    Rio flinched from the sheer force of Agatha’s fury. Her gaze dropped to the floor, unable to meet the eyes that once held so much kindness, but now burned with betrayal and anger.

    But Agatha wasn’t done. She panted, struggling to steady herself, then spoke again—this time at a normal volume, though the fire still burned in her tone.

    “Don’t you dare suggest I’d lie about something like this!” They were on the verge of sobbing, but Agatha managed to steady herself, her voice softened as she tried to reach the older woman with her words. “How can you not see it?! You both have the same allergies, the same eyes, same face, same laugh, the same damn blood type! He even has the same preferences in food as you! He’s more like you—than he has been or ever will be—like me!”

    She paused, her voice continued to tremble as she restated the undeniable truth.

    “Rio, you! Are the father!”

    The room fell silent.

    Rio couldn’t breathe. Her chest tightened, as her wide, tear-filled eyes locked onto Agatha’s tear-streaked face.

    Agatha’s breath came out gravelly as she tossed the test in the trash, then turned back to Rio, waiting—pleading—for her to say something… anything!

    Rio had to have gotten the picture now, right?

    Because Agatha could grasp if she was having a hard time accepting that she could even reproduce. Maybe this was all just a mis—

    “I… there’s no way… I-it can’t be me! It can’t be!”

    Even after all of that…

    Rio still didn’t believe that it was her child!

    That they were both hers and—

    Oh.

    After enduring a such brutal beating Agatha’s heart finally shattered into a million pieces.

    Rio didn’t want to be the father did she?

    She didn’t want their baby...

    Her mind began to spiral.

    She was going to have to raise this baby alone, just like the first time. But this time she knew exactly what she’d be losing…

    The love of her life.

    The room was heavy with silence, broken only by Rio’s labored breathing. The tension felt suffocating.

    And then, Agatha’s small, broken voice pierced the quiet.

    “Y-you don’t want me anymore?”

    She took a breath then continued.

    “You don’t want your son, or your baby? Am I going to have to raise this baby alone, again!?”

    Her legs gave out, and she collapsed to the floor. Clutching her chest, she gasped for air as panic consumed her, each breath more labored than the last.

    This was it!

    She was losing Rio!

    “Why am I so hard to love?” Agatha choked out, covering her face with her trembling hands. “Why doesn’t anyone want me?” Her sobs filled the room, raw and heartbreaking. “What am I supposed to tell my boy?” Rio’s eyes were wide with horror at the sight of her love falling apart. “A- Agatha, no! That’s not it!” she cried out, dropping to her knees in front of her.

    “Baby, please, no! I love you! With everything I have! I want you! I want Nicky! I just—” She grabbed Agatha’s wrists, gently pulling her hands away from her face.

    Her breath hitched when she saw the fear and anguish in Agatha’s bloodshot eyes. “Don’t cry,” Rio whispered, but her own tears continued to fall. “Please! I’m sorry! I’m so sorry! I shouldn’t have reacted like that!” She tried wiping Agatha’s tears with her thumbs, but the effort was futile as more continued to fall.

    Agatha’s lip quivered. “Then why are you denying them? I’ve never been with anyone else! I’d never do that to you, Rio! These are your babies! Why don’t you believe me!? Why can’t you remember that night—the night we first met?”

    Rio pressed her hands against her own aching head as her voice rose with desperation. “Because! That wonderful night had to have been a dream! How could anyone want me like that!? I-I… and if they’re mine…” Her voice cracked as she continued. “If they’re mine, then that means I’m the reason your life fell apart!”

    Agatha froze at the realization of why Rio was having such a hard time grasping this. “Rio…”

    The rest of Rio’s words came barreling out, unrestrained, with all of her pain and guilt now layered over top of the part of herself she already hated. “It means I’m the reason you had to quit school, to give up your dreams! The reason you thought you betrayed yourself, thought you’d slept with a man! The reason you got sick! The reason you almost lost Nicky!” Her voice grew hoarse, shaking under the weight of her confession. “And I’m the reason he’s even sick in the first place! He gets it from me, Agatha! I’m the one who passed it on to him! Every bad thing in your life—it’s because of me!” She pointed at her own chest with her thumb as she spoke. Agatha reached for her, but Rio pulled away, trembling. “I wasn’t there!” She whispered, her voice breaking, before it rose much louder. “For eleven years, I wasn’t Fucking there!” She looked down at the floor, gripping her head hard. “I missed his first steps, his first words… I wasn’t there to help him through being sick and in pain!” She looked back up at the woman she loved. “I could’ve helped him, Agatha. He didn’t have to go through it alone. You didn’t have to be alone! And I wasn’t even there!” She curled in, sobbing. “I’m a coward. I became the one thing I swore I’d never be! Someone who abandons their family!”

    Agatha couldn’t take it anymore. “Rio, stop!” She shouted with desperation, to break through the storm of guilt swallowing her love.

    Rio listened, she wasn’t sure if she had the strength to argue further anyway. Agatha moved forward, grabbing her loves shoulders with trembling hands. Her grip was firm despite the shake in her fingers. “Of course I wanted you! That part of you, you hate so much! It never once bothered me and it didn’t back then!”

    She took a shaky breath before continuing. “And we couldn’t have known, Rio! I know you would’ve stayed if you had. If I could change the past, we would’ve shared those eleven wonderful years together! But I can’t! You’re here now, in his life—and I want you to stay… for the rest of mine.” Agatha’s voice softened, her tone hopeful. “You came back to me, to Nicky. That has to count for something! And now we have this baby, one we can raise together! And be together!”

    She drew in a shaky breath, steadying herself, her voice barely above a whisper. “Don’t you want that, Rio? To be with me? To raise our baby together? Nicky’s still so young—he needs you. I need you.” The raw vulnerability in Agatha’s voice made Rio’s heart ache. Did she really make her think she’d abandon them, again!?

    Rio nodded, her voice breaking as she spoke. “Of course I want you—all three of you.” Her hand trembled slightly as she reached out, resting it gently on Agatha’s belly, her touch tender and full of love. She glanced down while rubbing her lovers belly. “I want this more than anything. I want this family, this life, with you.”

    Her eyes met Agatha’s, steady and unwavering. “I would never leave you— especially not over this. You’re my everything. You, Nicky… and now this little one.”

    Agatha’s lips trembled, but instead of a frown, they curved into a small and relieved smile. She sniffled and wiped away her tears, a soft giggle escaping her before she spoke. “You were wearing a green dress… it sparkled, just like your eyes.”

    Rio’s eyes widened, her breath catching.

    “Your hair was longer back then, too,” Agatha continued, her voice warm as she remembered it fondly. “It fell in these gorgeous waves. You had so many people around you, but you still looked so… alone. You were magnetic. I’d never seen anyone so put together and yet so lonely.” Rio let out a shaky breath, her chest tightening as fragmented memories began to stir and come together.

    Agatha laced their fingers together, her touch steady and grounding. She gave Rio’s hand a gentle squeeze before continuing. “I was wearing a purple dress. Some… stupid name-brand thing.”

    This pulled a giggle from Rio at the reminder, the sound brought a comforting warmth to Agatha’s heart.

    “My hair was up. I was already drunk out of my mind, but none of that mattered. All I wanted was to talk to the fascinating woman who was surrounded by so many, yet looked so utterly alone.”

    Rio let out a soft laugh, though it wavered with emotion. “Wow… I must have looked pretty pathetic. You must’ve taken pity on me.” Agatha shook her head, her quiet laugh carrying warmth. “No. I’ve never seen anyone so strong and resilient.” Her smile grew, her eyes glistening with tenderness. “So… divine and ethereal. ”

    Rio’s breath hitched as realization settled over her like a wave. Her voice came out in a whisper. “Agnes O’Conner…”

    Agatha chuckled, a light flush coloring her cheeks as she nodded. “In the flesh. Just… a little older now.” She shrugged, her smile softened as it grew warmer.

    Rio reached out, her fingers gently brushing against Agatha’s face, her touch filled with tender love and adoration. Her voice trembled, but her words were sure and full of awe. “And yet, you’re still as beautiful as the day I met you.”

    Agatha chuckled, caressing the hand against her cheek, her eyes fluttered shut as she leaned into it. “I should be the one saying that.” She hummed in content while she nuzzled Rio’s hand. She peaked an eye open, making Rio giggle.

    After a moment of just resting, and gazing into the other’s eyes, Rio went to talk. She let out a heavy and somber sigh.

    “Agatha… I am so sorry. For the way I reacted—and suggesting you cheated. That was…” she looked away for a moment, just to gather herself before looking back. “That was horrible of me. You didn’t deserve that.” She sighed again. “I know you would never do that. I’m sorry! I’m so sorry!”

    Rio’s tears started to fall again, she tried to hold back her sobs. Agatha reached out, wiping her tears and pulled her in close to lay her head against chest.

    Rio planted feather light kisses against her sternum, her other hand never leaving Agatha’s belly where she rubbed soothing circles there. Agatha swayed her side to side, humming a tune. “It’s okay. Rio. I expected something would happen. I shouldn’t have screamed at you, even if I was mad. I forgive you okay? This is all just a complicated situation.” “Aggie, I understand why you screamed. And… I honestly I deserved it. I wasn’t listening to you. I was terrible. I knew deep down you were telling the truth, I was just scared. I… of putting you through everything… of putting you through it again.”

    “But you’re here with me. You’re staying aren’t you?”

    Rio sat back and pulled Agatha’s face close so their foreheads were touching. “I’m never leaving, my love, you’re stuck with me. But… I’m still worried about your health. For our babies safety. You’ll have to go through the pain of labor or C-section. It may be ours, but you bear all of the burden. I just… it’s not fair.”

    “We’ll take it day by day. I can’t promise I won’t get sick, but I’ll fight for this child! Nicky is here today. This baby will be too and born healthy!” Rio nodded. “But…” she glanced away, speaking under her breath. “What if… Nicky is disappointed? T-that I’m his other biologically parent? That I don’t live up to his expectations… or… that he hates me for abandoning him. I just… I can’t…”

    “Rio… that boy loves you more than anything! He wants to be just like you. Ge already calls you mommy! If anything he’ll be happy, to know that you’re his father. Nicky is so pure, I promise everything will be okay.” Rio glanced back up at her love. “But… how… how will we explain it to him? How it works? And… the other parents at school will figure it out and his classmates… he’ll get bullied because of me! What if—“ “Rio.”

    Agatha kissed her lips to get her to stop spiraling. “It’s no one’s business but ours! And we’ll just sit him down and explain it to him, or we won’t until he asks. Fuck everyone else! I promise this isn’t going to become some broadcasted thing. And even if people do find out I’ll kick anyone’s ass who tries to say anything bad. I love you and I’m not disappointed by being with you or carrying your children. I want people to know that you’re the other parent. I want them to see that you’re loved and appreciated.” “Y-you… mean it? You aren’t embarrassed by me? T-to have my babies?” Agatha sighed. “Rio I am so in love with you and will scream it from the rooftops! I’m honored to carry your children and raise them with you! You’re my favorite person next to Nicky and now this little one.” She slid her hand over the one pressed against her tummy. “I have never been or ever will be disappointed or embarrassed by you. Okay? Don’t worry about other people, just… be here with me. I love you as you are, I mean it.” Rio wiped at her tears, what were once tears of fear and sadness were now happy tears. “Oh Agatha! You’re perfect!”

    Agatha smirked. “I’m aware. I am pretty great, huh?”

    Rio giggled, she went to open her mouth but before the words could come out they heard a pounding at the door, that startled the both of them before a small panicked voice muffled through the wood.

    “Momma!? Why were you screaming!? What’s going on? Where’s mommy? Are you okay? Did something bad happen!? Mommy didn’t leave did she!?”

    The panicked words flew out of the boy at lightning speed. His sobs were evident in his voice.

    “Baby, I’m okay! Hold on, Momma will open the door! And Mommy’s here with me okay?” She quickly got up and went to the door, unlocking it. As soon as she did it flew open, and she had to jump back to avoid getting hit by it.

    “Momma!” The boy cried out, pulling her in for a hug. “You sounded so angry I was so scared! I heard you two fighting. I waited for it to calm down. I didn’t know what was happening and then I didn’t hear anything.” He peaked over at Rio, relief flooding his features. “I was afraid! I thought you left us!” He ran towards the older woman practically tackling her to the floor.

    He clung to her desperately, as if the thought of letting go would end the world. “Please don’t go Mommy! I love you so much! You make me and Momma so happy! I love you! I-I’ll give you all my toys if you want! And my PlayStation! As long as you promise not to leave! You’re part of our family! I can’t lose you!” He wept into her shirt, his little body shaking, afraid that one of his favorite people would abandon him. Rio softly gasped at his admission. Her arms tightened their hold around him and she buried her face in the crook of his neck. “Leave you? How could I possibly do that? You and your Momma are my everything! I love you two more than you could ever know! I’m not gonna take your toys! And I’m not going anywhere! I don’t want to! As long as you’ll both have me I’ll never leave! I promise! I promise buddy!”

    Nicky let out a sigh of relief as he wiped tears from his eyes, his smile prevalent as he hugged Rio. “I love you forever, Mommy!”

    “I love you too, Nicky! Sweet boy!”

    The pair laid on either side of Nicky, running their fingers through his hair, whispering words of affections and assurance that everything was okay and that their family wasn’t breaking up.

    His breathing eventually evened out as he finally fell back asleep in Rio’s arms.

    Agatha softly sighed, she helped weasel Rio from his grip without waking him up before tip-toeing to the door.

    The moment it shut behind them she rubbed her head and groaned. “I think I need to soak in the tub for a while an—woah!”

    Rio scooped her up in her arms, kissing her passionately. “Is it okay if I join you? Or do you need some alone time? I understand if you do. That whole thing was… intense, to say the least.” Agatha’s shoulders relaxed, she reached up and caressed Rio’s cheek. “You may join me. But no funny business.” She poked her in the chest. “Not with Nicky in the house.”

    Rio nodded, “I promise to be good!”

    Agatha lifted a questioning brow at her.

    “Cross my heart.” Rio muttered before carrying Agatha off to the bathroom. Once in she set her down. Agatha reached up to start unbuttoning her blouse but Rio placed a hand over hers to stop her.

    “Let me do that for you. You’ve done a lot today, I wanna take care of you, it’s the least I can do.”

    Agatha sighed, then nodded. “Alright, I suppose.”

    Rio got to work gently undressing Agatha, kissing every inch of skin she could see, before moving to fill the tub. She crouched down by the faucet, testing the water with her hand, making sure it wasn’t too hot or too cold. “Want bubbles?”

    “Meh,” Agatha muttered, “I just want to lay in the warm water.” Rio nodded. After a minute she was more than satisfied with the temperature. “Perfect, its ready. Wanna get in?” She glanced over her shoulder at Agatha, with a smile so soft.

    “Yes, I’ve needed this all day!” Agatha replied, climbing into the clawfoot tub with a sigh of relief, as the warm water surrounded her, she leaned back, finally feeling relaxed after two weeks of stress and worry. Rio rolled up her sleeves and stood behind her, placing her hands on Agatha's tense shoulders to knead her gently, her thumbs working over the knots with practiced care.

    Agatha groaned, leaning back into her touch. “I thought you were gonna get in with me?”

    “In a bit.” Rio murmured, focused on pampering Agatha. “Wanna love on you first.”

    “You can love on me in the tub, I miss your warmth.”

    Rio chuckled. “I’m right here, darling.”

    “I know but I want you closer. I want you to hold me.”

    Rio paused, brushing a strand of hair from Agatha’s face before planting a gentle kiss on the crown of her head. “I know, baby. Just let me finish working these knots out and then I’ll climb in.”

    “Alright.” Agatha murmured, taking a deep breath. And Rio wasn’t kidding about her knots. She was already melting into her lover’s touch.

    Rio moved from her shoulders. Now pressing her thumbs into the base of her head, applying just the right amount of pressure. She knew this was where Agatha often carried most of her tension, and a good massage always helped her feel better.

    "Oh, my love, that feels wonderful," Agatha groaned, her voice heavy with her relaxation.

    Rio smiled before peppering soft kisses along the side of her neck. They stayed in a comfortable silence for a while, just savoring the intimacy, until Rio spoke.

    "How long have you known?"

    Agatha sighed, her body began to tense again at the dreaded question. "Almost two weeks..."

    The admission hung in the air between them. Agatha braced herself, worried Rio would be upset from the long hesitation to even tell her. But Rio only hummed softly in response. She kissed Agatha's shoulders, her hands shifting to rub slow, soothing circles in the crook of her neck. "I get it," she said gently. "I understand why you kept it from me. I'm not mad, okay? I promise. That couldn't have been easy, holding onto all that, by yourself."

    Agatha shook her head.

    The moment Rio heard a sniffle come from her she knew she was done and ready to get in. "Alright, hon," she said firmly, standing up. "I'm coming in."

    She stripped quickly, her movements calm and purposeful. Agatha shifted forward in the tub, making space for her to slide in behind her. The moment the older woman’s arms wrapped securely around her, Agatha felt a wave of relief wash over her.

    She let out a long, contented sigh and closed her eyes, leaning back against Rio's chest. She finally felt safe and okay.

    The fight was something Agatha never wanted to relive. She couldn’t bear the thought of losing Rio—not after everything they’d been through. Especially now, knowing Rio had always been Nicky’s father. And the father of the infant growing inside her.

    “Fate has a way with things, doesn’t she?” Rio murmured softly, her lips brushing against Agatha’s ear before pressing a kiss into her brown curls. “Call it cliché or corny, but I think you were always meant for me.” Rio tightened her arms around Agatha’s waist, snuggling closer. “It still blows my mind, you know? All those years of wishing for a child of my own, and it turns out I already had one. And not just any kid—the greatest kid ever.” Her hand moved to rest over Agatha’s belly, warm and steady. “And soon, we’ll have two of the greatest kids ever.”

    Agatha chuckled softly, her laugh vibrating against Rio’s chest. “This one better look and act more like me this time!” she teased, a smile tugging at her lips.

    Then she paused, turning slightly to meet Rio’s gaze, her hand sliding up to curl around the back of her neck. “Though, I can’t complain. Not when you’re so amazing. Honestly, I wouldn’t mind having another Nicky, considering he’s your mini-me.”

    Rio let out a playful huff, her fingers trailing up to curl around Agatha’s forearm. “Mini-me? You think Nicky’s my mini-me? Am I the only one who thinks he looks more like you?”

    Agatha blinked, shocked by the question. She twisted around fully in Rio’s arms, making Rio release her as she turned to face her. “Think about it for a second,” her voice was firm but amused. “His smile, his eyes, his nose— he’s 99% you! The only thing he got from me is my brown hair and maybe a hint of blue in his eyes.”

    Rio’s brow furrowed as she tilted her head, genuinely considering it. After a moment, she shrugged. “I guess I can see it… a little.”

    “A little?” Agatha gasped, mock-offended. “Oh honey, I swear I will make a comparison chart to show you how much he looks and acts like you!” Rio looked away for a second, a small smile tugging at her lips. She couldn’t deny it anymore—Agatha was right. And honestly? That realization made her heart swell.

    “It does make me insanely happy that he looks like me,” Rio admitted, her voice softening. “But for the past few months, all I’ve seen is your face in his. It’s part of why I took to him so quickly. Aside from, you know… parental instincts. He’s just… amazing. Who wouldn’t love him?” She paused, her voice dropping. “It just saddens me that y—”

    Agatha interrupted, a wry smile crossing her face. “That I carried him for nine months, went through hell and back with nausea, only for him to pop out looking exactly like his father? Oh, trust me, I’ve thought a lot about it.” She’d been feeling this way since Nicky’s birth, but what once brought her so much frustration was now bringing her so much joy.

    Rio bit her cheek, unsure of what to say. She let out a sigh, her gaze dropping to the bathwater. “Yeah, I get that. It’s almost like God thought it’d be funny. But hey, when she comes, I know she’ll be just like her Momma! I promise! And if I have to raise her myself for eleven years and then come back to you for her to be just like you, I—”

    Rio stopped mid-sentence at the unsettled look on Agatha’s face. Her hands shot up in the air in surrender. “I’m just joking, honey! I swear! I want to raise this baby with you!”

    Agatha tried to hold back her laughter but couldn’t. Then, as her chuckles subsided, something Rio had said caught her attention. “Wait a second— you think it’s a girl? Why not another boy?”

    Rio blinked, her eyes widening. “Oh, did I say ‘she’? Well…” She hesitated, rubbing her thumbs gently over the slight swell of Agatha’s belly. “I guess it just feels right to say. You’d think it’d make sense—we’re both women, so you’d expect a girl, right? Especially with my chromosome makeup. I know there’s still a chance for another boy. It’s just… I have a feeling it’s a girl, you know? Not that it matters either way. It’d be nice to have one of each, but honestly, I’m happy as long as they’re healthy.” She chuckled softly. “Still wild that our first kid turned out to be a boy, though.” Agatha arched an eyebrow. “Chromosome makeup?”

    Rio nodded. “Yeah. It’s the reason I am the way I am. I have XXY chromosomes instead of the standard XX most women have. So, biologically speaking, it’s kind of surprising we had a boy the first time. Statistically, it’s less likely, but clearly not impossible.” Agatha smirked. “What if I think it’s a boy again? Hm?”

    Rio sighed, her smile teasing. “Well, I guess we’ll just have to see. Do you want it to be a surprise when they’re born? Or should we do one of those gender reveal things?”

    Agatha groaned at the thought. “I don’t know about those. Oh, those parties are ridiculous. Especially when someone ends up disappointed by the baby’s sex, that’s horrible for a child to see. Plus most people are just excited regardless of what gender! I mean, I get why some people enjoy them—they can be fun, sure—but it’s gotten out of hand. At the end of the day, I don’t care. I just want my baby to be healthy.” She paused, her gaze softening. “But personally… Im leaning toward them being a boy.” “What if…” Rio hesitated, her voice soft with worry. “What if they’re like… me?”

    Agatha’s expression was gentle and warm. She reached up, brushing a hand along Rio’s cheek. “Then we love them, no matter what.” Her smile deepened as she added, “I love you, Rio. Exactly as you are. That doesn’t change with our child. I promise. However our child comes out, they’ll be ours and they’ll be perfect!”

    Her words brought tears to Rio's eyes. What Rio had always wished her parents had said and done for her, Agatha was already promising to do for their baby.

    "You have no idea what hearing that means to me!" she whispered, her voice trembling.

    Leaning forward, Rio pulled Agatha into a passionate kiss, pouring every ounce of her love and gratitude into it.

    She took Agatha's hand and pressed it to her chest, letting her feel the rapid beat of her heart. "Oh, Agatha Harkness! You're amazing! How did I get so lucky to find someone as wonderful as you?"

    Agatha smiled softly, her voice warm and sure. "By being your sweet and perfect self, my beautiful girl."

    After their relaxing bath, they cuddled in bed, whispering sweet words and promises to one another.

    Rio held Agatha tightly, murmuring reassurances that she wasn’t going anywhere.

    They both stared up at the ceiling, smiling at the little glowing stars that Nicky had begged them to put up in every bedroom.

    “I know it’s still early to even think about this, but… any names on your mind?” Agatha asked before rolling over to face the older woman. Rio met her eyes and shrugged. “Not sure. I always liked the idea that my kids name would have meaning behind it. What made you choose Nicky’s name anyway?”

    Agatha smiled, remembering the wonderful day she met her son. “I… I’m gonna be honest, I had no idea what I was going to name him. But the moment I saw his beautiful face I just… knew.”

    “That’s… actually wonderful.” Rio’s face lit up, imagining Agatha lying in a hospital bed holding baby Nicky. For a moment the light behind her eyes flickered out, still she wished she had been there for them. “It is? You don’t think it’s… thoughtless? Or… impersonal?” “No, why would it be? A name’s a name. You make it what you want! And he’s your baby. You had every right to do it how you wanted.” Agatha sat up, correcting Rio on her wording. “Our.”

    Rio tilted her head in confusion. “Hm?”

    Agatha sighed, reaching for her face to run her thumb over the arch of her brow. “Our baby. He’s our baby boy. Remember?”

    Rio’s face fell for a moment, realizing her mistake before returning to her cherry demeanor. “Oh yeah, I’m sorry. Of course he’s our boy! I guess it’ll take some getting used to.”

    “It’s okay, my love.” Agatha laid back against her pillow pulling Rio back down with her to lay on her chest, so she could play with her raven colored locks. “You don’t have to answer if you don’t want to, and I understand if you don’t even know, but I was just wondering…” She trailed off, nervous to continue.

    “Yes, sweetie?” Rio asked softly, as she slotted an arm around Agatha’s side, pulling her even closer as a way of reassuring her that she could ask her anything.

    “Do you know why your parents picked Rio?”

    “I… yes, actually.” Rio took a deep breath. She was fine talking about it. It wasn’t like it was a secret. “Rio in Spanish means river. And my last name, Vidal, means life. So, River of Life… that’s what my name means. But…” She hesitated for a moment. “They named me that because they thought I was a boy. I mean it worked out regardless, Rio is a gender-neutral name, but it clearly sounds like a boys name. But yeah… that’s me. That’s all I know.”

    “River…” Agatha sighed. “You have such a beautiful name, Rio. I think it fits you perfectly.”

    “Really? Me? Death? Bringer of the end of all life?”

    Agatha chuckled at that, then flipped their positions so she was laying on top of Rio instead. Continuing to comb her fingers through her hair. “Oh, my beautiful girl, you merely assist humans to the afterlife, and I think that’s wonderful.”

    “Yeah? You don’t think it’s ironic? That I’m a mortician? It’s like I’m tainting my namesake.” She turned her head toward the wall, unable to meet Agatha’s piercing gaze. This topic was a little… messy for her. She’d thought about it a lot—about who she was supposed to be.

    Agatha sighed and cupped her cheek, gently turning her face so their eyes met once again.“First of all, you’re also a florist. You literally help plants grow. You have a green thumb, you love animals, and…” She leaned close to her ear, her voice dropping into a breathy tone. “Who do you think put this baby inside of me to begin with, hm? Mistress Death?” Rio’s face burned bright red from Agatha’s flirtatious and seductive tone. It didn’t help that she was trailing her finger down the middle of her chest in a teasing manner.

    Agatha giggled, clearly aware of the effect she had on the poor woman. She stilled her hand, sliding it up to rub soothing circles on Rio’s forehead in an attempt to help her relax. “I have one more question,” she said, planting a kiss on her cheek to pull Rio out of her flustered state. “Go on, shoot.”

    Agatha smirked, “If we have a girl, can we name her Nicole?” “No!” Rio answered quickly, her tone unusually stern for the tender moment they were having.

    “No? Why? You don’t think it sounds nice?”

    Rio glared at her girlfriend. “We have a son named Nicky! We don’t need a daughter named Nicky too!”

    “Oh, come on! We could just call her Nicole.”

    “Absolutely not! I will not be one of those parents who gives their children the same name. Nicky deserves to stay the only Nicky in the house. Our baby deserves their own name, not a recycled one!”

    Agatha smiled. She brought a hand up to her own mouth trying to stifle her laughter. “Oh! I’m sorry! You’re just too cute!” She took a second to calm down then continued, “I love how thoughtful you are of our children.” “Of course I am! My babies deserve the best!” Rio huffed out with her agitation before it faded back into bliss.

    Agatha pressed her forehead to Rio’s gazing into her eyes. “Oh Rio, I love you.”

    Rio sighed, pulling Agatha close to kiss her. “And I love you, Agatha.”

    Before Agatha's alarm could go off, little feet pattered quickly toward the bedroom.

    Without knocking, Nicky burst into the room, clutching the doorknob. "Mommy! Are you still here?" he shouted, panting and wide-eyed with panic.

    Both woman sprung awake, terrified and confused.

    "Mommy! You didn't leave!" The boy ran and jumped onto the bed, flinging himself into Rio's arms. Relief washed over him as he saw her tangled in the sheets beside his mother.

    "Of course I'm here, bud. I told you I wasn't going anywhere." Rio's arms encircled him protectively.

    "I had a nightmare that you left! That you didn't want to be part of our family anymore! Momma was crying! I was crying! I don't want that to happen!" His voice broke as he clung tighter to her.

    Rio's face fell. She rubbed his back and stared down at the sheets, guilt pooling in her chest. She felt ashamed for how she'd acted last night for making Agatha cry, and now Nicky too.

    The moment Agatha saw Rio’s tears she didn’t hesitate. She pulled both of them into her arms. “Shh,” she whispered, kissing their foreheads. “I love you both so much. Everything’s going to be okay.”

    "Nicky, Mommy isn't going anywhere.

    I promise," Agatha spoke gently, "We just had a little... heated discussion. But we're okay now. We're not breaking up. We're a family, and family’s stick together."

    The boy sat back slightly, rubbing at his tear-streaked cheeks. "Yeah... but —“

    Agatha took his face in her hands, her thumbs brushing away any lingering tears. "You trust me, don't you?"

    He nodded quickly.

    “Then trust that I’m telling you the truth. Trust that Rio—your Mommy—is telling the truth. No one’s leaving. Nothing bad is happening. If anything, she and I are even closer than before. You’re both my loves—“ Agatha’s gaze shifted to Rio, meeting her sweet brown eyes with her own blue, full of adoration and affection. "And I'll fight to the ends of the earth to keep us all together."

    She pulled Nicky close again and reached for Rio's shoulder, drawing her back into their embrace.

    After reassuring Nicky for the second time, they all got up and began getting ready for the day.

    Rio diligently made breakfast while Agatha helped her son pick out an outfit for school.

    The eldest of the three danced freely around the kitchen, singing along to the music playing on her phone as she cooked. Completely unaware of the two sets of eyes watching her—until she felt arms wrap around her waist and soft kisses trail along her neck.

    “You dance so beautifully, my darling,” Agatha whispered into her ear. “Ew! Momma! Not in front of me!” Nicky groaned, his face scrunching in exaggerated disgust as he rushed off to the living room to watch cartoons until breakfast was ready.

    Agatha and Rio giggled at his reaction to his mother being affectionate with someone else.

    Once Nicky had turned on the TV, Agatha leaned in closer and whispered, “Should we tell him now? When do you want to do it?”

    Rio sighed deeply, setting her spatula down. She gripped the counter at the sides of the stove, her gaze dropping as she thought. “I just… I need a bit of time to figure out what I’m going to say. Should I tell him about how I am? I’m just… worried.”

    Agatha leaned into her, resting her chin gently on her shoulder. “My love, you know he loves you. We won’t tell him until you’re ready, but I’m sure he’ll be nothing but thrilled. We don’t have to get into specifics if you’re not comfortable. If he asks one day, we can tell him. But honestly, what matters most is that he just knows it’s you.”

    Rio’s voice wavered, “But… what if he hates me? Because I wasn’t there? Because of how I am… I think my heart would break if he did.” “We both know that was out of our control,” Agatha said softly. “I’ve told him I don’t know who his father is, and he never questioned it. He won’t be mad—I know that for a fact. That’s just not who he is. And if it makes you feel better, I’ve raised him to accept people for who they are. Do you think he cares that his mom is dating a woman? Nicky doesn’t judge people on things like that. He judges them by their heart. And he adores yours. So if you decide to tell him how you were born I promise he won’t hate you for being different. Trust me, he’ll be more focused on the fact that you’re his father.”

    Rio nodded slowly. “That… makes me feel a lot better. We’ll tell him soon. I just want it to stay between us for a bit. Is that okay?” She turned, meeting Agatha’s eyes. “Just our secret.” She slid her hand to her love’s belly. “Just for a little while longer?”

    “Of course, darling. I won’t do anything you’re not okay with. This is your baby too.”

    “You have infinitely more say in it than I do. You’re the one carrying the little bundle of joy after all. But I appreciate you considering me.” Agatha cupped Rio’s cheek, her touch was gentle as she spoke softly. “I want us to be equals in this. We’re a team—we work through everything together. I’ll never do anything without consulting you.” She pressed her forehead against Rio’s. “I want you involved as much as I am. Okay? It’s you and me, always.”

    Rio nodded. “I love you so much. I love her too.” Her eyes flickered to Agatha’s belly.

    “You mean him? Darling? Our sweet little boy?”

    Rio glanced back up with a mischievous smile. “Wanna make a bet?” Agatha lifted a brow. “Oh? Pray tell, what would you get out of this if you won?” She crossed her arms over her chest, smirking.

    Rio looked her up and down before replying, “Well… I haven’t thought about it yet. We’ve got time, considering we’re waiting for the baby to be born. Right?”

    “Yes. I think it’ll be more fun that way. Though we should get the baby’s gender in an envelope and give it to Wanda, so our friends can get the proper colors for the baby shower.”

    Rio chuckled. “So, we’d have the baby shower after the baby’s born? And are we really going to follow gender color norms?”

    “I guess your right on that, we’ll have to think it over with Wanda and Hela. And no on color norms. But don’t you think our little girl would look positively adorable in pink or purple? Emphasis on the purple!” Rio laughed. “Oh, so now you’re agreeing it’s a girl? And we’d have to throw in some green to even things out!”

    “My darling, I’m humoring you. I’ll dress my boy in purple if I damn well please!”

    “And green?” Rio asked, her innocent eyes full of hope.

    Agatha smiled, caressing Rio’s face. She adored how excited she looked at the prospect of motherhood.

    “Especially green!”

    Agatha said softly, standing on her tiptoes to kiss her love.

    After both women dropped Nicky off at school, they made their way to Alice’s for brunch, taking advantage of the rare occasion they were all off during the day.

    Lilia was already lounging in the living room, her feet propped up on the coffee table as she sipped from a Family Guy mug.

    Rio raised a brow, trying and failing to stifle her laughter. The old woman rolled her eyes in response. She pointed at Agatha, curling her finger to beckon her, before heading toward the back of the house. Rio gave Agatha a questioning look, but the younger woman only shrugged before following after the eldest.

    “Aw man, Agatha got called to the principal’s office already.” Hela shook her head and clicked her tongue playfully, startling Rio. “Guess you’re dating a bad girl now, kid.” She patted Rio on the shoulders. Rio cringed. “Are you high!?”

    Hela’s neutral expression didn’t waver as she closed her eyes and took a long, exaggerated sip of hot cocoa from her Rick and Morty mug. “Mmm! So good!” Her eyes fluttered open, she held the mug out to Rio, offering to share with her sister.

    “Want some?”

    “No, you dork!”

    “Are you finally gonna do it, Lilia? Take out your old boss? I knew this day would finally come. Just tell my kid I love him and not to look in my closet,” Agatha joked as she stepped into the bathroom, where she saw Lilia retreat to.

    Lilia rolled her eyes. “Har-har. No, I’m not offing you. None of us are taking the easy way out! I actually have something important to tell you.” She took a deep breath before continuing. “I may have known for a while, but I needed concrete proof. And now…”

    Agatha sighed, raising a hand to cut her off. “Lilia, look, I—” “I don’t know how, but I think Rio is Nicky’s father!” Lilia blurted out, holding up her hands. “I know it sounds insane. Maybe she’s transitioned or —”

    “Lilia, I already know she’s his father.”

    “Wait, you do?” Lilia’s eyes widened.

    “Yes. Your little picture tipped me off. I noticed a few things before that, but yeah.” She shrugged. “We talked about it. Everything’s good. It’s really good, actually! Rio is so happy about the baby and—” Agatha froze, her eyes widening as her hands flew to cover her mouth. She wasn’t supposed to tell anyone yet. She and Rio were planning to announce it together. Nicky didn’t even know yet!

    Lilia’s eyes widened as she rushed toward Agatha, grabbing her shoulders. “You’re serious?!”

    Agatha nodded. “You can’t tell anyone, okay? I haven’t even told my son yet! Please, promise me you won’t say anything!”

    Lilia held up her hand, miming the motion of zipping her lips. “I promise! I won’t tell a soul! I’m so happy for you!”

    “And Rio isn’t trans…” Agatha added.

    Lilia looked up, thinking about it before saying, “So she’s in—“ Before she could finish, Agatha cut her off. “You can talk to her about it, but not until I make the announcement about the baby. It’s her business, and if you didn’t hear anything about the party, I’m not saying a word without her knowledge or consent.”

    Lilia nodded, understanding. It didn’t take much to figure out what the only other option was, but she wouldn’t push the matter if Agatha wasn’t comfortable taking about it. Both of them loved and respected Rio to even think to talk about her behind her back.

    “Of course. It doesn’t change anything. Rio’s a sweet girl, and I’m so happy for you both. I wish you a lifetime of happiness together!”

    Back in the dining room, Hela thought it’d be great to start cracking jokes while high.

    “So, so this girl walks into a bar and—“ Rio groaned. “Did you seriously wake-n-bake!? I thought you stopped smoking!?”

    Hela rolled her eyes. “Relax, sis. It was just a little gummy from Wands. No biggie. I was having a bit of anxiety last night and she had given one to Alice. She didn’t mind so I took it.”

    “And it’s still in your system? Was it a THC one? Are you seeing Freddie mercury right now? Maybe Michael Jackson? God? Santa Claus? The tooth fairy!?”

    Hela’s eyes flickered behind Rio’s shoulders, she let out a whistle. “I don’t know about all that! But right now I’m seeing a damn sexy piece of ass right now!”

    When Rio heard an all-too-familiar voice say, “Excuse me!?” she jerked her head around. She saw Agatha standing there, frozen, bent over in the middle of untying her shoes. Rio’s protective instincts kicked in. She turned back to Hela, grabbing her by the collar, raising her fist, and shouted, “What the fuck is wrong with you!? Don’t talk about her like that!” Hela panicked, she tried to get away from her but fell out of her chair in the process. Rio hadn’t let go, instead she moved with her now towering over her with her fist still pointed at her.

    Hela threw her hands up in surrender. “W-wait! Shit! I thought it was Alice! You gotta believe me! I’d never speak about a friend like that! Especially your girl!” Her eyes flickered over to Agatha. “I’m sorry Agatha! I mean it! I really thought you were Alice!” Then she glanced back to Rio. Rio continued seething with anger while looking down at her. “Rio! It’s okay!” Agatha grabbed her arm, lowering her fist, and slid a comforting hand over her shoulder. “Calm down, baby. It’s alright, look at me.” She gently cupped Rio’s cheek and turned her head, locking eyes with her.

    Rio immediately softened, those blue eyes had quite the effect on her. She glanced between Agatha and Hela before sighing and letting go of her sister’s collar. “You’re lucky I love you Hels! Otherwise you’d be six feet under saying shit like that!”

    Hela looked over at Agatha mouthing ‘thank you’ before speaking out loud. “Oh man! Woo!” She grabbed at her head trying to steady the rush she was feeling. “That was crazy! At least I know you’re a sweet and protective girlfriend, Rio! You make me proud!”

    Rio rolled her eyes at her sister’s smirk. “You’re lucky I didn’t give you a black eye.”

    Now it was Hela’s turn to roll her eyes. “Wouldn’t be the first time! I’m sure it won’t be the last!”

    Agatha gave Rio a look. Who just shrugged back at her. “What? Sisters argue. We got into it a lot a growing up.”

    “And I won every time!” Hela grinned.

    “Hela!”

    Hela jumped, her eyes widening as she turned to see Alice standing there with her hands on her hips.

    “I thought I told you to keep the roughhousing to a minimum? I’d like to keep my house in one piece!” Alice pointed her finger at her girlfriend disapprovingly, making her cower.

    “Yeah! Hela! No rough housing!” Rio stuck her tongue out at her before she sat back down at the table.

    “Why am I always the one getting in trouble?” Hela muttered as Alice helped her up. “You guys are mean to me!”

    “No! We just care about you, babe!” Alice tried reassuring her, she pinched her girlfriend’s cheek, doing it harder than normal.

    Hela’s hand flew to her face from the sharp sting. “Ow! Babe! what the—“ “That’s for calling my boss a sweet piece of ass!” Alice’s words came out in a growl.

    “Sweet what? What’d I miss?” Lilia asked as she came back from using the restroom.

    “Hela mistaking Agatha’s ass for Alice’s apparently.” Rio grumbled, still agitated by the whole thing.

    Lilia shook her head at the absurdity of it all.

    “I’m not even gonna ask!”

    They didn’t start brunch until Wanda and Jen arrived. When they did they were able to set the table.

    Agatha was practically drooling at the sight of the large spread. She was eating for two now so she could indulge a bit, right? After getting everything dished up the group dug in.

    Rio and Hela continued cracking jokes at each other. Their demeanor relaxed after the rough morning, Rio had long went back to her sweet and relaxed self and Hela to her goofy and charming self.

    Agatha propped her chin on her palm while she gazed longingly at her girlfriend as she enjoyed a price of French toast that was smothered in a hefty amount of berries, syrup and whip cream.

    And when she got a bit of cream on her nose Agatha wiped it off with her finger before taking some into her own mouth, humming in delight at the taste. The act made Rio giggle.

    Wanda watched the two with a fond smile.

    “Hey Ags you gotta try this! It’s so yummy!” Wanda offered her a glass filled with an orange colored liquid.

    And Agatha seemed interested. “Ooh that looks good! Is it Pineapple and orange juice?” She took the glass and raised it to her mouth. Rio turned, watching as she did.

    “Yeah, a delicious mimosa.” Wanda finally stated.

    “No!” Rio quickly grabbed the glass pulling it away before Agatha could swallow any of it down.

    Agatha blinked, confused at what happened. “Wait… it’s… there’s alcohol in it!?” She panicked for a moment at the close call.

    “Well yeah! Why? You aren’t drinking anymore? It’s not high proof or anything. Have you sworn off drinking or something?”

    “Uh…” Agatha looked between Wanda and Rio, unsure what to say. Lilia stifled her laughter that quickly turned into a fit of coughs. Which Jen quickly tried to alleviate by patting her back.

    The group could feel the awkward tension from Agatha’s lack of response. Rio hiding her face behind her hands only made everything all the more suspicious.

    Wanda spoke up, unsure how to break the awkward tension. “If the problem is it’s early then who cares? Besides, I mean it’s not like you’re pregnant…” Agatha and Rio panicked for a second before steeling their features. Unfortunately for them their friends had already noticed the flicker of emotion, tipping them off.

    “Oh! Wow! What a shock! I had NO idea at all!” Lilia blurted out. Earning a weird look from Alice and Jen.

    Hela turned from Wanda, seeing Rio’s clear panic. She reached over the table and grabbed Rio’s ear, yanking it between her fingers making her sister squeal pathetically. “What did I tell you!? If it rains wear a damn coat!” She slammed her free hand against the table startling everyone else.

    Rio tried to turn her head away to avoid her sister’s disappointed gaze. “Look at me! You didn’t wear protection!? Didn’t I teach you better than that!? Do I need to remove your nuts?” Hela pointed between her legs, making Rio jump, thinking she was gong to twist them or worse and tried getting away.

    “I-I… I wasn’t thinking! I didn’t think I could… I didn’t mean to! I didn’t have— I-I“ she squealed again, squeezing her legs together. “Why do you gotta put that image in my head you’re a monster!”

    Agatha got up and removed Hela’s hand from Rio’s ear, whose skin was turning red. “Alright that’s enough! We’re both adults and made a conscious decision! And I knew what I was doing! So don’t go putting all the blame onto Rio! Regardless, I’m fine with it and she is too, so lay off her!” She snarled at the other woman as she leaned in close. “You really don’t wanna poke the bear!”

    She didn’t care who it was, no one lays a hand on her Rio! Hela threw her hands up in the air in defeat. “Okay-okay! I yield! Forgive me! I’ve practically been Rio’s guardian since we were little. It’s a gut reaction. But…” Hela sighed, facing Rio. “You aren’t a kid anymore. I’m sorry, Rio. I’m happy for you both.”

    Rio sighed, “Let’s call it a draw. We’re even.”

    The room fell in silent for a moment before someone squealed making everyone jump.

    “Oh my god! You’re gonna have a baby!!?” Wanda beamed with joy, pulling Agatha into a tight hug. “I’m so happy for you, honey! You’re gonna to be such a great mom again!” She turned to Rio, her smile softening as she took her hands. “And this time, you won’t be alone. You’ll have Rio to help with everything—someone to be there for your first ultrasound, when you’re sick, when you’re in labor. You won’t have to give birth alone. Or juggle preparing everything by yourself.” Rio’s heart sank at Wanda’s words, the weight of the hard truth settled heavily on her shoulders. No one knew she was Nicky’s father. No one knew she was the reason Agatha had to endure those hardships alone in the first place—navigating every step, every challenge, without the support she should have had. This was another harsh reminder of how deeply she’d hurt the woman she now loved.

    While Rio had lived a carefree life with Hela, Agatha had bared the full burden of raising a child on her own. The guilt stung, carving another wound into her already heavy heart.
