    Rio’s eyes widened and she sat back against her pillow. “I…” she tapped her fingers against each other, unsure what to say.

    Agatha sat back, triumphantly. “Gonna listen to me know, Rio?” “I…” Rio stared down at her sheets and gripped them. “I don’t know if I want to now…”

    Agatha threw her hands up in the air. “Oh for the love of— what does that even mean?”

    Rio’s head shot up and before she could stop herself she blurted out, “It means you’re so hot when you get like this and it’s unfair! And I feel conflicted because I wanna be good for you, but I also wanna know what happens if I’m not.”

    Agatha’s face was actually red now. She had to take a breath and get up for a moment.

    Rio panicked, thinking she had said something wrong or that what she had said disgusted Agatha. Her hands shot up as she scrambled to follow. “W-wait! Don’t leave! You aren’t gonna leave, are you!? I’m sorry! I’ll be serious! Don’t leave! Please, I’m sorry! I won’t say it again!” Agatha’s eyes widened as Rio took a step toward her, only to sway unsteadily. Without a second thought Agatha rushed back to her. “Rio! What are you doing!? You have to lay down!”

    “I-I don’t want you to go!” Rio’s tears returned, pouring down her face staring up in fear as Agatha pushed her back down in bed. How had Agatha been so… ignorant? Not realizing the magnitude of how broken this woman truly was—how unstable her emotions were, how insecure she was, to the point where she genuinely believed the slightest upset would lead to the downfall of their relationship.

    This was going to take serious work…

    Work Agatha would gladly shoulder.

    “Rio! I wasn’t… I just needed a moment. You were flustering me that was all!”

    “I’m so—“ Agatha placed her finger over her lips. “No more apologies! Seriously! I’m not mad! You just caught me off guard with what you said! Why would you think I’d leave you over that?”

    With upturned eyebrows and sad eyes, Rio opened and closed her mouth a few times unable to explain the irrationality of her emotions, before finally shaking her head and attempting to look away.

    “No, look at me.” Agatha grabbed her chin to bring her eyes back to her own and pressed her forehead to her own. “Breathe. You’ve had a stressful day. You need to relax. You’re getting yourself worked up and it’s worrying me.”

    “I’m—“ “Rio!” Agatha snapped then quickly calmed herself. “Baby.” She took a breath. “When you feel less about yourself I want you to come talk to me about it okay? I will reassure you a million more times if I need to. I’m not going anywhere. I don’t blame you for anything. You’re absolutely perfect the way you are and I will never want anyone else. Are we clear?” Rio took a breath and then nodded. “Yes. I’m—“This time Rio caught herself. “I… just… don’t know what to say now.”

    “Well…” Agatha leaned in and pecked at her lips. “Start by telling me what you love about yourself.”

    Now Rio was truly caught off guard by this. “Oh… I’d rather talk about you and—“ Agatha shook her head. “No. I want you to talk about you. Tell me, my love.” She ran her fingers through raven locks. “Tell me what my pretty girl loves most about herself.”

    Rio blushed. She attempted to look away again but Agatha kept her face in her grasp.

    “Rio, breathe for me. Come on. At least three things. You can do it.” What… she loves about herself?

    But she’s never really said it out loud. At least seriously. More in the sense of a joking manner or just to lighten the mood. She slumped against the bed.

    “Um… I-I like that we’re together and I like my son and…” “Rio, honey I said about you. Not like that. What are some qualities you like about yourself? Things you do? Or something about your appearance? Those kinds of things.”

    “I…” she gulped, searching for something. “I love… my taste in clothing?” Agatha lifted a brow. “Is that a question?”

    A blush dusted across Rio’s cheeks. “Um… n-no I guess not.” “Then continue.” Agatha kissed her cheek. “Keep talking. I wanna hear you say wonderful things.”

    “I-I love my taste in music.”

    “You do have pretty good taste.” She kissed her other cheek. “What else?” Oh!

    What else?

    Rio started to shake. “M-my… abs.”

    Agatha moaned. “And what about those… deliciously… sexy things?” Her lips hovered over her neck.

    “I-I love my abs.”

    “Oh me too!” Agatha leaned in and kissed a fairly sensitive spot against her neck, pulling a whine from her. “Tell me more, darling.”

    “Y-you said three.”

    Agatha pulled away from her neck and looked into Rio’s eyes. “Well, now I want more! You gave me three, you can give more.“ “I don’t know if I have… more.”

    “Yes, you do.” Agatha kissed her forehead. “How about this? You tell me something and I’ll tell you something about myself?”

    Rio lit up at the idea. “You promise?”

    Agatha chuckled and nodded. “I do. Here I’ll start. I love…” Agatha racked her brain for a moment. “How smart I am. I’ve always been at the top of my class. Whether or not that gave me an ego I don’t care. I’ve become successful because of it. Your turn.”

    Rio swooned. “Oh, you are very smart! Too smart!” She leaned forward and kissed Agatha’s cheek. “I love my passion for music. But it’s second to my love for plants and botany.”

    “Now that’s something I can definitely agree on. I love listening to you play, and go on and on about plants.”

    Rio squealed with joy when Agatha pecked her lips again. This time twice since she said two things.

    Agatha stayed, hovering inches from Rio’s lips. “I love my femininity and the care I put into my outfits. I love commanding the attention of a room. Not necessarily because of my looks but because of—“ Agatha smirked, “The power.”

    Now it was Rio’s turn to moan. She rubbed her thighs together and leaned in to kiss Agatha. “Oh, baby! Fuck! You have no idea how sexy it is to see you take control of your workspace! God, you’re such a bad bitch.” She leaned in to kiss her again, but Agatha stopped her.

    “Your turn, beautiful.”

    “I love my kindness, towards people, animals, and plants. I love my thoughtfulness and how I take the time to make sure all of my clients feel valued when I give them their service. I love how much care I put behind every single one of my gifts to my loved ones. I love my attentiveness to detail. I love how far I’ve come in art. I love painting and drawing especially with my son! Our son! Oh, I love that I can take care of you two! I love that I can be there for you and help around the house and fix things. I love that I can support you both.”

    She took a breath before continuing. “I love that I, Rio Vidal was able to earn the heart of Agatha Harkness! I love that I found you both again! I love our family! I love that we have another child on the way! I love my love for you! For Nicky! Fuck! Agatha I know this is about me, but I love you both so much! And now this little one is coming and I can’t imagine my life any other way! And I love that I have the greatest family ever! I love that!” Her voice wavered and tears rolled down her face. “I love what I was able to create with the part of myself I’ve hated for so long! I love that it brings you joy and… maybe it brings me joy now, too! Because of this!” She reached for Agatha’s belly and placed her hand there. “And because of Nicky. I’ve hated it for 42 years, but knowing that I was able to bring you joy and make wonderful babies with you makes me hate it a bit less. I…” She took a breath. “Agatha! I love our life together! I love who I am when I’m with you!”

    Agatha shot forward taking Rio’s lips into her own, kissing her senseless. “If we weren’t in a hospital I’d take you right here!” Agatha breathed against her lips.

    The sound of the heart monitor picking up a bit pulled Agatha back. “Oh, I’m getting you way too riled up.”

    Rio didn’t seem to care even though she was starting to feel lightheaded again. “Oh you definitely are and I’m in heaven. Please don’t stop my angel.” She leaned in for another kiss but Agatha stopped her. The sweat pouring down Rio’s face prompted Agatha to place her hand over her forehead. “Rio! You’re burning up! I need to get a doctor in here now!” “B-but I-I’m f-fi….” Rio trailed off as her eyes started to roll back and she slumped against the bed, her breathing slowed greatly. She struggled to keep conscious. “A-Agatha I-I’m s-so tired…”

    “Jesus, Rio! Doctor! Nurse! Help!”

    Apparently getting all hot and bothered after fainting hours prior wasn’t the best course of action. And Agatha was still kicking herself for it. But at least she knew Rio was okay. After getting her stable enough and allowing her the rest she needed—before waking her for blood tests, she was eventually released to go home.

    Agatha waited to hear back about the results while she ran her fingers through Rio’s locks.

    She gazed down at her love’s sleeping face against her chest and leaned forward to kiss her forehead.

    Luckily this all managed to happen while Nicky was away with Wanda and Tommy on a little museum trip for school.

    Agatha would have more than enough time to look after Rio before he got home. Before she’d have to tell him that Mommy had a little spell. Oh, and that she may also have the same ailment as him.

    “H-he looked just like me… Agatha…”

    Agatha sighed. Hearing Rio’s broken voice always made her chest ache. “What happened when you went to the restaurant?”

    Rio took a moment before responding.

    “My parents were there but… they weren’t alone. There was a whole group with them! I… I wasn’t the only child! They had to have been my sister, brothers, and nephews. But… Agatha one of them looked just like me! I felt… something when I saw him, a familiarity! I have a fucking twin! Which means they hadn’t abandoned their only child. They had abandoned me! They didn’t want me because of how I was born!” Rio cried out against Agatha’s chest.

    Agatha held her close.

    “That’s why I was scared you’d leave me! If my own parents didn’t want me why would anyone else!? Why am I not good enough!? What did I do to deserve to be unloved and unwanted? Why did I have to be born like this!?” “Rio no! Please, honey! You are so loved and wanted! Me and Nicky love you so much! Hela! All of our friends! Hell, señor scratchy! And our baby! We all love you! With everything inside of us! Baby! I can’t tell you why your parents did what they did. But I can tell you that you’re more than worth it. You deserve so much love! Rio! You deserve the world and I will give it to you! You aren’t alone! We aren’t going anywhere! You’re ours and we love you!”

    Rio squeezed Agatha tighter. Almost fearing if she didn’t this would all just… fade away. “I just… I can’t believe it. All these years… wondering if they had really gotten rid of me because of how I was born and… I-I was right.” She sniffled wiping the tears from her face. “I guess some good came from it. I met Hela. And I probably wouldn’t have met you and I don’t think I want to live in a world where I don’t know you.”

    “I don’t think I could either. Especially if that meant Nicky wouldn’t exist.” Rio sucked in a harsh breath. The very thought did something to her that she did not like. “I can’t… even imagine that. I can’t live without him… you.”

    “I agree.” Agatha planted another kiss on Rio’s head. “Will you try again? Reaching out to your parents I mean?”

    “I… should I?” Rio raised her head, meeting Agatha’s eyes. “That’s entirely up to you. But you don’t have to if you don’t want to.” “I… it’s not that I don’t want to. But… I’m scared of what they will say to me. I wonder if… my siblings— my brother, if they even know about me. The shock of having any siblings at all is surprising. I guess I can deal with younger ones. But the fact that they already had another one when they abandoned me just hurts so much. I’m scared of what he— my brother might think of me. I’m sure they’re all mad I stood them up.” “No! Don’t worry about what they think. Your parents lost the right to care about that when they gave you up. If you don’t want to do it then you don’t have to. But I understand it if you need to.”

    “I… just want to be present for our family right now. That’s enough for me.”

    Agatha caressed Rio’s face, pushing a strand of hair away from her eyes. “You’re mine, Rio. You’ll always be. You’re Nicky’s mother. You. Rio Vidal. You have no idea how happy that boy makes me! How happy he has made me for the past eleven years! I felt so alone in this world and you gave me the greatest gift I could have ever asked for! You gave me family! Someone who loves me unconditionally. You gave me a piece of my heart that I didn’t even know I was missing.”

    Now Agatha was tearing up too. “But still,” she pulled her closer. “I had felt like I was missing something. You may have unknowingly filled my cold heart with warmth but it was still yearning for its other half. Being Nicky’s mother has brought me nothing but joy for eleven years, but I still felt a bit empty and that’s because I didn’t have you there to complete our family. I had my heart, but I didn’t have my soulmate. I didn’t have you.” Rio’s lip quivered. She grasped the hand against her cheek and brought it to her lips, kissing it. Her breath shook as she spoke. “Soulmate? How sappy of you, Agatha.” She smiled when she heard Agatha giggle at her joke. “But I guess it’s the only proper word to describe this feeling.”

    “And what is that feeling, Rio?”

    “Home.”

    “Momma! I’m home!” Nicky came barreling in through the door, with his little souvenir in hand that the museum handed out to each kid for free. He was a whirlwind of excitement, wanting to tell his moms all about his day. He hurried out of his coat, haphazardly tossing it in the shoe closet even though he knew it was supposed to be hung up by the door for easy access, and discarded his snowy boots directly in front of the door. “Momma! I got some candy from the museum! It’s got bugs in it!” He shouted but still, received no answer.

    He sighed, he knew better than to run upstairs now. He really didn’t want to risk seeing… that again!

    So instead he got comfortable in the living room, slipped on his headphones, and turned on a movie.

    Eventually, he fell asleep.

    The smoke alarm going off was what woke both women up from their nap and they jumped.

    “Shit, Nicky!”

    Agatha and Rio sprung out of bed, making their way to the stairs and down them in a flurry.

    “Nicky! Honey are you okay!” Agatha shouted. But at the same time, Rio stumbled, missing a few steps, if Agatha hadn’t been in front of her she would have fallen down them, instead she smacked into Agatha’s back. “Oh my god, Rio! Baby, you weren’t supposed to— ugh! Come here!” She slid her arm behind Rio’s back and under her armpits and helped her down the rest of the way. “Nicky! Are you okay!”

    The boy still didn’t answer, only worrying both women even more. Especially Rio who, even though was in no shape to be running head first into danger did so anyway, pulling out of Agatha’s hold, against her protests, and bolting straight into the kitchen.

    There was their boy, trying frantically to figure out how to turn the oven off. “Mommy! I’m sorry! I just wanted some pizza! I got hungry!” He cried, visibly shaken as he watched Rio shut the oven off and grab mitts to pull out the chard remains of food. “Please don’t be mad at me! I-I didn’t mean to!”

    Her strained coughing echoed throughout the room and her legs shook as if she was struggling to stand, but still, after getting the situation under control she turned to Nicky and pulled him against her into a tight hug. “Rio! Honey wait for— Nicky, honey, are you alright!?” Agatha rushed to her family's side and checked him over for any burns or injuries. At least the parts of him that weren’t shrouded by Rio’s body.

    “I’m fine! I’m sorry Momma I just wanted something to eat and— Mommy!” The older woman fumbled to the floor, the boy attempted to keep a tight grasp on her to steady her but struggled with their difference in size.

    Agatha moved quickly, scooping Rio up and instructing Nicky to head to the living room with her.

    “What’s wrong with Mommy!?”

    Agatha sighed as she laid her girlfriend out on the couch. “Mommy just had a little tumble today, she’ll be okay. She’s just not feeling good.” “Is it like when I fell off the jungle gym?” He asked as he moved close to look at her face.

    Rio chuckled, “Kinda. Looks like me and you might be twining with our illnesses bud.” Her chuckle fizzled out awkwardly before she looked away altogether.

    Unable to meet her son’s gaze, fearing he may blame her for his ailments and injuries.

    But instead, all he did was embrace her. “I just want you to be alright Mommy! I know how it feels, I don’t like it when I get lightheaded either.” Rio sighed and turned to face her boy. She returned his hug. “I’m more worried about you, you didn’t burn yourself, did you? I think my heart would shatter if you had.”

    He shook his head.

    “Nicky what were you doing trying to use the oven by yourself, you know you could have gotten me to help you.”

    He struggled to meet his Momma’s gaze. “I know… b-but last time I barged into your room um…” his face turned red and he struggled to meet either of their gazes.

    Rio looked over at Agatha, mortification filling her to the brim. But Agatha only seemed to chuckle. “I guess you’ve learned your lesson about knocking?”

    He nodded frantically. “Yes. I’m sorry! For both things!” “Don’t be. Momma should have been awake for when you got home. I’m sorry.” She leaned forward and pulled him into a hug.

    “Oh! That reminds me!” He pulled away from his mother and grabbed the little bag of gems and suckers he received from the museum. He held them out proudly to his parents. “Look! Aren’t these rocks pretty!? And these suckers! Mommy they have bugs in them! Isn’t that gross!?” Agatha was visibly disgusted.

    “Awe eww! Sick! Lemme see that!” Rio reached out taking one and inspecting it. This particular one had crickets inside and a couple of larvae. Both Harkness’ eyes widened as they watched her unwrap the strange confection and start sucking on it. They stiffened in horror as they heard the crunching of the crystallized candy, and then crunching of a different kind. “Rio! Oh my god!” Agatha’s hands flew to her mouth. “I’m gonna throw up! Babe! Why!?”

    Nicky only chuckled. “Oh eww! Mommy! Even I wouldn’t have tried that!” He looked at her like she was crazy, but then relaxed as curious fascination washed over him. “What does it taste like?”

    “Hm… well… the candy itself is watermelon, but the crickets are quite salty and the larvae taste like nothing. Almost like a soft popcorn kernel without any flavoring.”

    “Rio! Stop talking!”

    “Hand the lime and scorpion over, son. I wanna try it.”

    Agatha couldn’t take anymore, she bolted straight for the bathroom. “I can’t with you two!”

    Agatha frantically racked her brain for something nice she could do for Rio, to take care mind off the messy events from a few days ago. She continued bouncing between Guitar Center and Hot Topic but continued coming up empty.

    She wasn’t sure how, but Nicky just seemed to know what she was thinking.

    “Are you trying to find Mommy something to cheer her up?” The young boy poked his head over his Mother’s shoulder, curiously looking down at her phone.

    Agatha sighed and nodded. “Any ideas?” She had a feeling of what he was gonna suggest, especially since it had been the only thing she kept coming back to.

    Nicky smiled and leaned forward whispering his answer into her ear.

    And of course, she was right.

    “Oh boy.”

    Rio chuckled as she was being driven to her ‘surprise destination’. It was just her and Agatha today.

    “Come on babe! Where are we going? I wanna know!” She pouted and kicked her feet like a child.

    Agatha only smiled and rolled her eyes while keeping her gaze locked on the road. “Patience dear. It wouldn’t be a surprise if I told you, now would it?” She turned and looked over at her girlfriend, quirking a brow at her with an amused smirk.

    “Oh! But I wanna know now! It’s eating me up inside!”

    Agatha playfully scoffed and turned back toward the road. “You aren’t getting a thing out of me! Now, just sit back, relax, and enjoy the ride, Rio.” The older woman crossed her arms and turned away with a ‘hmph’. “Keep acting like that and I might just have to pull this vehicle over.” Rio giggled from her empty threat.

    “Am I finally meeting my end?” Rio joked as she was being led toward some unknown location with Agatha’s hands over her eyes.

    Agatha groaned at the over-dramatic accusation. “No, Rio. But stop for a second. I need to pull my hands away. But no peaking!”

    “Okay, okay. I’ll behave.” Rio was good and listened, keeping her eyes closed as Agatha moved around her.

    Agatha sighed and shook her head. She pulled a door open and pressed her hand against the curve of Rio’s back, gently pushing her forward. “Go on, but keep those pretty eyes of yours shut.”

    Rio was buzzing with joy. Excited beyond belief at what her surprise could be. She was tipped off though when she heard a bark.

    With a quirk of her eyebrow, she spoke, suspicion filled her tone. “Agatha…?”

    Agatha walked around her. Her heart skipped a beat at the huge smile on her love’s face. She couldn’t help it and instead of telling her to open her eyes she gave her a quick peck on the lips, making the older woman blush, then whispered against her lips. “You can open your eyes now, pretty girl.” Rio’s eyes fluttered open. The first thing she saw was Agatha’s blue eyes before the younger woman backed away. Then she glanced around. “No way!” She moved forward taking it all in.

    It was a pet store!

    A freakin pet store!

    Rio spun around to face Agatha. “You’re serious? I can get a pet? We’re not just here to look?”

    Agatha nodded and gestured for her to proceed.

    However, she was expecting the older woman to head toward the cats or dogs, maybe even the rabbits. What she hadn’t expected was for her to head toward the more… exotic animal section of the store.

    “Rio… the pets are back that way.” Agatha gestured toward the cute fluffy animals in the opposite aisle.

    But Rio shook her head. “There’s more back here too!” She said way too excitedly.

    Agatha’s shoulder slumped and she let out a groan.

    Rio tried reassuring her. “Oh come on! These guys are cute too! Look at him! He’s got such a handsome little smile!”

    Agatha lifted a brow. “Rio.” She paused for a moment then glanced at the woman. “That’s a snake!”

    “A handsome snake!”

    If it wasn’t for the fact that Rio was beaming Agatha would have pulled her out of that section altogether.

    It really hadn’t helped when they reached the… Creepy Crawlers section and Rio only became more excited.

    Agatha shivered.

    “Oh my gosh! Look at her!”

    Rio ran over to a little tank in the back and Agatha swore she felt her heart drop to the floor. “Oh Rio… please! God please not that one!” “She’s perfect!” Rio knew this was the one. She looked back over at Agatha completely missing the fact that the woman had gone pale. “Baby! This is the one I want! Isn’t she cute!?” She turned back toward the tarantula and began speaking to it like it was a child.

    “Look at you! Who’s a pretty girl!? You are! My precious little baby!”

    “Oh… man,” Agatha whispered to herself.

    The whole ride home was tense for Agatha. She continued glancing over at Rio who was giddy as could be while holding her little terrarium complete with one whole tarantula inside.

    Even still, Agatha couldn’t help but smile at her love’s joy. She hadn’t seen her this happy in days.

    “What are you gonna name her?”

    “Matilda!”

    Agatha had to do a double take at the spider. “So… like the movie?” Rio shrugged. “Not really. It’s just… felt right. She looks like a Matilda.”

    “How do you know it’s a she?”

    “Well females are bigger than males and she’s pretty big, so I just assumed. That, and I asked the store owner and she confirmed. Come here you.” Agatha’s eyes shot open. She felt her whole body stiffen. She could hear the sound of the terrarium being opened and see Rio pull the… thing! Out of its cage, in the corner of her eye. “Rio! Please, not In the car!” “Aw, but she’s so snuggly. Look. She’s latching onto my chest.” “I can’t. Please. Just… wait till we get home. Please.”

    Rio sighed but listened. “Alright come here, princess. Go back into your home. I promise I’ll get you a much bigger one when we get back.”

    Agatha let out a sigh of relief.

    The whole time back Agatha kept her distance from Rio’s office space. She knew all too well what was in there.

    Her stomach churned at the thought and before she could control herself she booked it to the bathroom to release the stress from her body.

    Rio could hear Agatha’s gagging from all the way upstairs. She quickly put the spider back in its cage before rushing downstairs.

    “Agatha!?”

    The younger woman continued to gag.

    “Honey! Oh, honey!” Rio crouched down at her side, pulling her hair behind her neck, and rubbed her back. “Get it out sweetie. It’s okay. I’m here! I’m not going anywhere.”

    Tears streamed down Agatha’s face. This was a rough one. She couldn’t breathe and the dry heaving was excruciating. She let out a cry, leaning her weight forward on her hands as she propped herself directly over the toilet and wept.

    “Baby, don’t cry! You’ll dehydrate fast! Just relax!”

    “I hate throwing up!” She whimpered. Thankfully the worst of it seemed to be over. She leaned back and grabbed toilet paper to wipe her mouth off with. “I’m so disgusting.”

    “No, Agatha. You’re human.”

    Agatha groaned and grabbed her head. “My head is pounding.” She turned toward Rio who softly gasped at the sight of her red eyes and pale complexion. “Can you do me a favor, Rio!”

    Rio lifted a brow. Agatha’s tone was… odd. “Depends?”

    “Kill me.”

    “No.” She answered simply. “But I can get you Tylenol.”

    “I think death would be a mercy.”

    “Not to me. Now come on. I’ll fix you up.” Rio got up and held out her hand.

    Agatha couldn’t help but let out a smile as she took the offered hand. “Carry me?”

    Rio lifted a brow but let out a chuckle. “Man, you’re lucky you’re cute and I bounce back fast. Alright, c’mere you.” She scooped her up in one go, carrying her out into the living room. “You look tired. You wanna nap? We could nap together? It’d be nice. Then when the boy comes home we could help him with homework and I’ll cook something yummy. How’s that sound?”

    Agatha sighed, placing her hand against Rio’s chest. “It sounds lovely sweetie, but I had plans to cook anyway. Especially since you haven’t been feeling well.”

    “Yeah, but you aren’t feeling great either. And you’re hard at work carrying our baby. We can cook together if you want. But I don’t mind doing it myself. I enjoy it, honestly.”

    Agatha hummed, “Okay,” in acknowledgment.

    Rio glanced down, not realizing that the younger woman had started drifting off.

    “Awe, my darling is sleepy. Come on you. Let’s get you to bed.” She kissed her forehead before ascending the stairs. “My sweet love. What would I do without you? Mi bella durmiente te amo. Anhelo comprarte un anillo. Te mereces el mundo. Tengo la intención de dártelo. Eres mi familia, para siempre.”

    “Where is it?” Agatha tossed a few pillows around in her bedroom as she searched high and low for her favorite bracelet. The very one Rio had gifted her at Christmas.

    “Come on! Please! You can’t be gone!” A tear slid down Agatha’s cheek. But she really didn’t get much time to be upset.

    Not when—

    What is that!?

    Matilda’s in the bed!

    Agatha let out a blood-curdling scream.

    “RIO!!!!!”

    The tarantula jumped at the sudden noise, attempting to scatter away.

    Agatha jumped back, she wanted to vacate the room, but she didn’t want anything bad to happen to the damn spider either!

    She kept her eyes on it but kept her distance.

    She heard rapid footsteps approaching and a faint “Agatha!? What’s wrong!? Are you okay?” Come from downstairs.

    “RIO! Get your damn bug!” She shouted as the door flung open. Rio was taken aback by how… ridiculous Agatha looked, standing on top of the chair in front of their vanity, holding out a hairbrush in front of her as if it was some kind of holy weapon, with her hand shaking.

    But the implications struck her and she hurried over to her precious companion and picked her up. “You weren’t gonna hurt poor Matilda with that were you?” She turned toward Agatha and pouted, genuinely saddened by this development. “She won’t hurt you. She might bite a little if you scare her. But so would Scratch! She doesn’t wanna hurt you! Look!” Rio held her out a little closer.

    Agatha took in the genuine and sad expression on Rio’s face and softened. She lowered the brush and got down from the chair. “I’m sorry. But you have to admit these aren’t… Matilda isn’t exactly friendly-looking. And I’m not exactly fond of spiders.”

    “B-but she’s so cute! Look at her face! She wouldn’t hurt a— okay not a good analogy. She won’t hurt you, I promise. Just treat her how you’d treat Scratch.”

    Dammit!

    Rio was giving her The puppy dog eyes.

    Agatha teared up at the sight. “Rio no!”

    Then her lip started to quiver.

    “I’m warning you!”

    And a tear trickled down her cheek.

    “Rio!”

    “Please, for me?”

    “Oh for the love a—“ Agatha wiped her own tears pouring down her face. “Come here, you!” Without caring for the spider she pulled Rio in, kissing her now tear-stained cheeks. “No tears! Please!”

    “You’ll hold her?” Rio asked with hope in her tone.

    Agatha pulled away with wide eyes. “I’ll what!?” She asked flabbergasted. “Hold her?” Rio held the spider out to Agatha. “And then when Nicky comes home he can too.”

    “You’re gonna put me in an early grave!” She held out her hands but squeezed her eyes shut and tensed up, bracing for the spider to touch her skin.

    But when it finally did she was shocked at how… soft it was. “Agatha just breathe. Look, she isn’t even doing anything, she’s just standing there taking you in.”

    She peaked one eye open to see the fluffy tarantula just… looking up at her. From this angle it was kinda… cute…

    Huh.

    It wasn’t so bad.

    “Why isn’t it biting me?”

    “Because she isn’t hungry.”

    Agatha looked up with terror in her eyes.

    “I’m joking. She’s not aggressive. She’s a curly-haired tarantula. They aren’t known to be aggressive by any means and they only eat worms and roaches for the most part. Sometimes crickets. They’re a great starter tarantula.”

    Agatha glared at her for the choice of words.

    “I don’t intend on getting more if that’s what you’re worried about, besides.” Rio reached out to pet Matilda. “This cutie is more than enough for me! I just hope she enjoys the cute skull I got for her enclosure!” “The what!?”

    “A skull. It makes their home look super cool! It’s not real! But I’m considering ordering a real deer skull. It’ll be cleaned of course. Uhh! Nicky is gonna flip!”

    “Yeah, just like I did.”

    “You think so? I get the feeling he’ll be excited.”

    “Hm, well considering he’s just like you he might just be.” “I hope so! Matilda is a very affectionate girl. She needs all the love she can get. Even Scratch likes her.”

    “You let this bug around my ba—ahhh! Rio, it’s moving!” Agatha whined. She tried not to move as the tarantula crawled up her arm and onto her shoulder, Matilda stopped and poked Agatha’s cheek with her leg. “Awe she’s just giving you kisses.”

    Agatha pleaded with her eyes, begging for Matilda to be removed. With a sigh Rio relented. “Alright my darling daughter, come here, Momma is shy right now. But we’ll get her to warm up to you in no time! Wait till you meet your brother!”

    “I don’t recall birthing that monstrosity,” Agatha muttered as the spider was being removed, she shivered as she felt its appendages attempt to cling to her for one last time.

    “No, but you did adopt her with me!” Rio lifted the arachnid close to her face, Agatha’s eyes widened in shock when Rio kissed it.

    “Oh, you have now tainted those sweet lips.”

    Rio chuckled. “Don’t be dramatic. I keep my baby clean, huh girly? Tell Momma see ya later!” She softly poked at the hairs behind Matilda’s legs encouraging her to turn around and face Agatha.

    And then Matilda waved one of her little legs at Agatha, like a person! “Rio, what the—“ Before she could even finish her sentence Rio burst out laughing.

    “No way she just did that! Oh, man! That was wild!” She had to wipe a few tears from her eyes. “Looks like we have another pet here who has a knack for picking up on commands! Just like Scratch!”

    “Listen here you—“ Agatha pointed her finger at Rio. “Señor Scratchy is a dapper little man, he shall not be compared to that… thing.” She glared at Matilda, who now seemingly coward back against Rio’s hand as if saddened by Agatha’s tone and glare.

    With a gasp, Rio put her hand over Matilda and pulled her away. “You don’t wanna love her? Fine! Me and Nicky will! You don’t deserve Matilda’s snuggles anyway! Meanie!” She stuck her tongue out at her. Agatha clenched her fist at her side in frustration. Unsure of what to say. Rio looked like she was joking on the surface as to keep the mood light, but Agatha could tell she had upset her with the rejection and dislike she threw at Matilda.

    So she relaxed her fist and relented fully. Her shoulders relaxed and she sighed. “I’m sorry, I… can I try again?” She held out her hands, hoping maybe Rio would give her a second chance. “I don’t want to upset you, the point of this whole thing was to make you happy, I’m being selfish making this all about me. Let me make it right. Let me make you happy.” Rio shouldn’t have been surprised by how considered Agatha was being right now. She really shouldn’t have. But this woman continued to surprise her again and again with her dedication and love. So she smiled at the younger woman.

    “What would make me happy is if you could find it in your heart to love Matilda the way I do.” Rio placed her back into Agatha’s hands. “I just want both my girls to get along and Matilda really is sweet. If you can get past my rough exterior and love me I know you can for her.” Rio smiled down at Matilda, watching her poke at Agatha’s palm. But Agatha continued to look at Rio’s face, her sadness now strewn across it. What had she done? Behaving like a child when this was her choice. Her gift to Rio and she was ruining it. And… “Rio, you’re beautiful. Why would you say you have a rough exterior?” Agatha’s voice was so soft. To help lighten the mood a bit more Agatha took a breath then placed the spider against her chest, cradling it close to her heart.

    Rio seemed to have missed the question and instead fawned over Agatha hugging Matilda to her chest. “Awe! See! She’s a little sweetheart! You just gotta give her a chance is all. Tarantula’s can love too.” “Rio…” Now Agatha’s tone was serious, prompting the older woman to finally look up, her own smile fell away at the sight of Agatha’s saddened expression.

    “I… what’s wrong honey? Why do you look sad?” Rio reached out to her. “I… just said that you’re beautiful. I just wanted you to know that.” She offered a gentle smile.

    “That’s all?” Rio lifted a brow.

    Agatha was hoping to just drop it. She didn’t want to soil the moment any more than it had been. “I can’t find the bracelet you gave me. It’s been driving me insane. I guess it’s still weighing on my mind.” “Oh, no honey, it’s in my office. I saw that it needed polished a bit. I was letting it air out. I’m sorry, I thought I had told you. It’s safe and sound I promise.”

    Agatha let out a sigh of relief. “Thank goodness.”

    “I guess it’s a good thing you thought it was missing. Although I’m saddened that you were upset by it, you found Matilda and I hadn’t noticed that she’d gotten out and I would have been tearing the house apart trying to find her. I love her so much. She means a lot to me.”

    The spider skittered a bit, then latched onto Agatha’s chest making her let out a squeal before she relaxed. This was gonna take time! “I-I know, baby. I’m happy she makes you happy.”

    Rio giggled. “I can see you’re at your limit.”

    “N-no I’m fine, I swear.”

    “It’s okay Agatha. Really, I’m just happy you’re making an effort. That’s more than enough for me. Now let me get this girl back in her enclosure, she’s probably all peopled out by now. She needs some personal time!” Rio encouraged Matilda to crawl into her hand, smiling ear to ear before making her way to the door of their bedroom. “Nicky should be home soon. I’m so excited to introduce you two!”

    Agatha watched her go, deciding not to press Rio about it and to just let her go about her business. She had been stressed enough as it was. She didn't need Agatha prying for more information. So instead she followed after her, opting to spend a bit more time with her before their loving boy came barreling through the front door.

    The school bus came to a creaking stop in front of the Harkness and Maximoff residence.

    Two boys booked it out, both heading for their respective homes. “See you later Tommy! Tell Billy I said hi!”

    “Okay!”

    Nicky ran excitedly into the house, frantically trying to take his shoes off in a whirl. “Is it a puppy!? Is it a kitty!? A turtle? what is it!?” He bounced up and down, his Momma looked amused by his excitement.

    Her arms were crossed and she lifted a brow, continuing to just stand there until he hung up his coat and backpack.

    “Go ask your other mother. I’m sure she’ll be more than happy to show you.” She waved him off, she really couldn’t take more spider time right now. But just before he could bolt she put her hand in front of him, stopping him. “Wait, do you have homework?”

    The boy deflated at the mention. “Just one. It’s a word scrambler.” “Alright well after you go meet Rio’s new friend come right back down and get started on it. I’d prefer you do it now, but I can see you won’t be able to focus unless you go see what Rio picked out.”

    “Thank you Momma! I love you!” He pulled his mom into a hug before rushing off to go see the new pet.

    “Mommy! Are you in your office slash gaming room?”

    Rio smiled, hearing the boy small feet patter up the stairs. “I am.”

    Her door creaked open, and pretty brown and blue eyes peaked in just enough to see where Rio was.

    Rio giggled at him. “What are you doing?”

    “I don’t wanna let whatever is in here, out.”

    “You won’t, come on in. Let me introduce you to someone.” She waved him in.

    The boy beamed ear to ear. “I’m dying to know what you got! Is it an axolotl?” He asked noticing the corner of the tank.

    “No, but those are cute. I’m sure you haven’t guessed. Come meet her.” Nicky’s smile faltered for a moment. “Did you get a hamster? Where is it?” “She’s under her little hideout, right there.”

    The boys eyes widened.

    Agatha jumped when she heard her son scream. She ran toward the landing and yelled up. “Everything alright up there?”

    “Momma!”

    She heard rapid footsteps approaching. She started smirking, so she finally had something in common with her son.

    “It’s okay, honey I know it’s—“ “She’s so cool!”

    Her son stopped at the top of the staircase beaming more than when he came in, if that was possible.

    “Oh, of course you’d think that.” She face palmed herself. He was an eleven year old boy for Christ sake and Rio Vidal’s son. Of course he’d be amused by a bug.

    “Momma! I love Matilda so much! Mommy is so good at picking pets! She’s awesome!”

    Agatha smiled and nodded in agreement. “She’s the best.”

    “Hey buddy come look! She’s drinking her water!”

    Nicky eyes widened before running off. “Ooh! I gotta see!”

    “Those two cuties.” She shook her head in disbelief, but still she was so full of love and adoration. How lucky was she? To have such an amazing family. An amazing and caring partner. Sweet and kind son. And to top it off a sweet bundle of joy on the way.

    She felt a strange sensation in her belly. She grasped at it. Huh, odd. It was still too early to feel kicking, or anything at all. Her phone buzzed, pulling her out of her thoughts. She reached into her pocket and scoffed.

    Alice: Hey boss lady, I got a lovely shipment of condoms heading your way! The hormones are only gonna get worse from here! Love ya! P.S. Lilia is running this place with an iron fist! Can’t wait to see you back here on Monday! Hope Rio enjoyed her gift!

    “What th—” Agatha groaned in annoyance. She knew all too well that her hormones were on the verge of sky rocketing. She didn’t need the reminder. “Momma come up here! Mommy is being funny with Matilda! You gotta see!”

    She chuckled before ascending the stairs.

    Chapter End Notes I had a hard time figuring out mistresses deaths family dynamic. If you guys are familiar with the Endless from Dc that version of death is easier to understand in regards to her siblings. It doesn’t seem as straight forward in the marvel universe. I made some changes with characters relationships because yeah.

    I’ll expand a bit more on it, but I don’t know how deep I’ll go into it. I plan to make like a two shot after this series ends, maybe I’ll put something in there about them more. But at the very least I will have Rio learn their identities and their connections to her. Sorry for the little tease though, it just didn’t feel like time to introduce them fully, yet.

    Ch16 translations: Mi bella durmiente te amo. Anhelo comprarte un anillo. Te mereces el mundo. Tengo la intención de dártelo. Eres mi familia, para siempre. (My sleeping beauty I love you. I long to buy you a ring. You deserve the world. I intend to give it to you. You are my family, forever.)

    Chapter 17: Write your name in a heart with the

    hemorrhage!

    Chapter Summary Work stressors, Eating out at work, Valentines, New friends, and Exes. Chapter Notes I apologize for the late post, I meant to post this on Valentines Day but life got busy for me, and I also wanted to add more to the story. I hope it doesn’t feel all over the place, I didn’t have an overall plot for this chapter but more of a bunch of smaller ones. I hope you enjoy and as always thank you for reading!

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Agatha was livid. Work had been terrible. It was bad enough that she somehow got stuck doing group projects with freakin Stephanie Layton and the group of lackeys that followed her around—ugh! She hated doing business with that bitch. But she was her second most valuable client! On top of that, Agatha had to deal with her infuriating engineering team, who, were having issues with their computer system and had started a fight down on the basement level with tech support. Out of the whole team, there were only three people she could tolerate—and one of them she actually liked.

    Her tires came screeching to a halt before she put her SUV in park. With a groan she lugged her purse out of the car and made the arduous journey to the front door before bursting inside ready to just be done with the day. “Honey? Nicky?” She called out as she entered her home, setting her keys down on the little table next to the door in the foyer. Expecting to hear someone call back to her, or even rapid footsteps come her way, but was only met with silence and a dark house.

    She sighed as she entered the home, shutting and locking the door behind her.

    This was not what she wanted to come home to. Nothing…

    Her nerves were fried, and her hormones were all over the place. It made her overly emotional, and whether she wanted to scream into the void or break down altogether, she held it all in. She had been doing it all day—for the sake of professionalism and to avoid scaring some poor intern. But now she was home.

    And alone…

    A feeling struck her.

    What would her life be like if she never had Nicky? If she never had that faithful night with Rio? Never met Rio for a second time? Would it be like this?

    Coming home to an empty and dark home?

    Because if so she wanted no part in it.

    She didn’t give a crap if she would be working her dream job or… whatever. Wherever her life would have taken her.

    It didn’t matter.

    Nicky and Rio were her life.

    They were always meant for her.

    But her very emotional and hormonal mind clung on to the idea of truly coming back to an empty home.

    No son…

    No girlfriend…

    Just…

    Alone.

    She felt her legs give out beneath her and before she could stop herself she crumbled to the floor. Her hands came to her face and she wept at the horrible thought.

    “Nicky! Rio!”

    She couldn’t handle this alone.

    She’s not sure she’s ever come home to an empty house like this. Why was it hitting her so deeply?

    Regardless, her heart was breaking over a scenario that never happened and wasn’t happening—yet she had conjured it up as if it were. Maybe she just needed to let it out.

    Maybe she just…

    The front door opened and before Agatha could righten herself and erase all traces of her emotional break down, she was already caught. “Baby?” A look of concerned plastered itself onto Rio’s face as soon as she spotted Agatha on the floor crying into her hands.

    Agatha looked at her in horror then sniffled while quickly wiping away her tears. “Oh, Rio! I was just…”

    “Momma we’re ho— Momma!” Nicky came up from behind Rio, his smile falling away before bolting over to his other mothers side. “Momma! What happened are you hurt!?” “No no! Baby! Momma’s okay! I promise!” She faked a chuckle hoping to reassure her boy.

    But she wasn’t sure he bought it, and clearly Rio didn’t either who was at her other side kissing away the tears from her cheeks. This managed to pull an actual chuckle from Agatha.

    “H-hey! Rio! That tickles!”

    Before Agatha could even attempt to get away Nicky mirrored Rio’s actions, showering his mother’s other cheek in kisses of his own. “Hey! Ahaha! S-stop it you two!”

    Rio slid her hand across her girlfriend’s belly with a sweet smile while nuzzling her nose against her cheek and whispering into her ear, “Let me help you up sweetheart! I’ll hold you and we can talk, okay?” Nicky ceased his kisses and instead snuggled against his mother, allowing her to finally think properly.

    She nodded.

    Somehow, in a marvelous show of strength, surprising both Agatha and nicky, Rio scooped them both up at the same time, carrying them to the living room couch.

    “Wow! Mommy is super strong!”

    Agatha was reeling from this. She wasn’t weak herself, she could carry Rio from time to time, as long as she hyped herself up enough too. But both of them!? Where did Rio hide all her muscle!? And where did she put it? Agatha swore Nicky was heavier than the eldest of the three, somehow, considering Rio was still a foot taller than him.

    “Rio, how!?” Agatha asked with a perplexed tone.

    Rio grinned, “Magic!” She set her girlfriend and son down on the couch, then stood up straight and flexed her biceps. “Magic muscles!” She blew on them as if blowing smoke out of the barrel of a gun.

    Agatha swooned, while Nicky admired them.

    “Wow! I hope I have cool muscles when I’m big like you mommy!” “Well… considering you’re my son you probably will.” Her face switched to something serious for a moment, as she pointed at the boy. “But I didn’t get these muscles by genetics alone young man. I worked hard for them and I ate good!” She booped his nose. “And drank plenty of water! And got good adequate rest! I’m sure it’ll be a lot easier for you by the time you’ve hit puberty. You’re a boy after all. They’ll grow faster.” Her grinned turned feral. “You’ll have all the ladies swooning after you! Or… boys.” She shrugged.

    Nicky looked at her like she was crazy and Agatha scoffed. “Mommy I want to be strong like superheroes! I don’t care about what girls and boys think! And I don’t think I like boys. I think I like girls, like you and Momma. Boys are gross. Girls are less gross, I guess.” “Rio our son is not vain. I didn’t raise him to be.” Agatha held her head up high, feeling prideful of her son’s lack vanity and need to be the best out of all the other kids. She just wanted him to be the best version of himself he could be.

    Rio’s macho persona deflated. “Well, I’m just happy you aren’t growing up as fast like I assumed most kids your age are.”

    “Why would I wanna grow up? Being a grown up doesn’t sound fun. School isn’t fun, but then you have to work and pay taxes! And make sure you don’t go homeless!”

    Rio chuckled, taking her seat next to her son. “I suppose you’re right. But it doesn’t have to be all bad. When you’re an adult you have way more freedom. But it also comes with a butt load of responsibility.” “Like me?” The boy pointed at himself.

    Agatha giggled. “Especially you!”

    This whole interaction was making Agatha feel so much better. And Rio seemed to notice.

    “Hey buddy, mind giving your Momma and I a moment? Maybe go work on your homework in the dining room? I’ll get dinner started in a bit and then we can watch a show before bed. How’s that sound?”

    Nicky smiled. “Okay! My homework is easy tonight! It’s color by numbers but I have to solve the problems to get the right numbers first! Can I listen to a story on your phone Mommy?”

    Rio smiled and nodded. “Yes, as long as it doesn’t distract you.” She pulled her phone from her pocket, unlocked it and handed it to him. “No scary ones though. You kept getting nightmares last time.”

    “Okay, I promise I won’t.” He smiled, kissed Agatha on the cheek then headed off to go do his homework.

    Agatha smiled in his direction then turned to face Rio, who was looking at her fondly. The older woman leaned in close and pushed some of her hair behind her ear. “What’s the matter mi amor? What’s got my girl upset? Do I need to go beat someone up?”

    Agatha chuckled but shook her head. “No… it was just… a stressful day at work. And well… the pregnancy is making me emotional. I started thinking some… not so good things. And I guess I just broke down.” Rio sighed, scooting closer to her girlfriend, pulling her in for a kiss. “Wanna talk about it?” She ran a comforting hand down her head. Agatha tensed, which Rio seemed to take notice and began massaging her shoulders.

    “I… imagined what life would have been like without you two…” she looked down at her lap. “I didn’t like what I saw. There were flickers… of me, working some dream job. I was rich…I was successful… on the surface. It was lonely… horrible. I was a terrible person. Bitter, angry, hateful, like my mother! My life without Nicky—without you! Was horrible! I just… I know it’s stupid I—“ Rio shook her head. “Not stupid. Not at all. But it’s far from true. We’re both here. Nicky and I. And you’re still you. Generous and… I know you hate to admit it but you’re kind. It’s okay to be stressed. Your family is here for you.” She kissed Agatha’s hand. “Your son is here for you. We both love you very much.”

    Agatha nodded. “I know.” She let out a deep sigh. “I need a good stress relief.” She ran her hand over her own face, not noticing the devilish smirk appear on Rio’s face.

    The older woman leaned in whispering into Agatha’s ear, making the other woman’s face go red.

    “Wait, what about—“ “I’ll give him his headset, put on a movie. He’ll love it! I’ll be fast! What do ya say?” Rio licked her lips, her gaze turned dangerous. “Or I can be slow. I can make it… really good for you, baby. Really good! I’ve gotten pretty good at it myself! But I can always use more practice to perfect my technique!”

    Agatha’s face flushed from how flustered she was but she chuckled anyway. “You’re a dirty dog!”

    Rio hummed in agreement, she leaned in and whispered her response into Agatha’s ear. “Last time I checked you love it when I hump you. But tonight will be all about you! And I wanna use my mouth! Come on baby, let’s go make you feel good.” Rio kissed her cheek, flashing her a wink then took off before the younger woman had a moment to respond. Agatha’s heart thudded against her chest as she listened to Rio tell Nicky he could watch a movie before dinner.

    “Oh my god. She’s gonna eat me alive!” Agatha groaned before bolting upstairs.

    “…But yeah, I just don’t get it! All these couples hooking up! Having meaningless sex! It’s just not my thing! It’s never been! I just don’t understand how anyone can meet a stranger and be comfortable enough around them to take off their clothes and show them their insides! Let alone let them stick it in!” Agatha waved her hands around as she spoke, disregarding the dice she had dropped moments ago.

    Rio’s face fell. “Yeah… I totally agree. But how did we get from the topic about new movies coming out to meaningless sex…?While playing board games?”

    The agitated look immediately melted off of Agatha’s face as she blinked a few times, looking at her group of friends who were waiting for her to take her turn, but were now just flabbergasted at the sudden topic change. “What!?” She glared at all of them.

    Sharon thankfully broke the tension by chuckling. “Aw! You’re so sweet, Agatha! Honey, you’re such a romantic! But I’ll tell you—there’s nothing more thrilling than meeting a strange but handsome man and then letting him—”

    “Ahhhhh!”

    Everyone but Hela groaned in unison, seemingly she was the only one interested in hearing the rest of the story.

    “Oh! You kids! It’s almost Valentine’s Day! You can’t tell me you aren’t looking for someone to spend it with?”

    This time Agatha was the only one to groan at the mention. Which surprised Rio. It stuck with her. So much so that the following week, on Valentine’s Day itself, she found herself wanting to bring it up while they were in the kitchen, preparing lunch.

    She watched Agatha stir something in a pot, waiting for the perfect time to give her girlfriend her gifts.

    Agatha hadn’t even said Happy Valentines, and Rio avoided saying it for the time being. But she really wanted to.

    “So… today’s Friday.” Rio brought up, nonchalantly, leaning against the counter, crossing her arms trying to look cool.

    “It is.” Agatha responded plainly, without glancing her way. Rio tensed, Agatha didn’t get her hint here. Ugh, she’d need to try and push a bit more. “It’s also almost the weekend…” she added.

    “Mhm…” Agatha hummed, seemingly just to respond as to not be rude. Rio bit her lip with agitation. “Got any… plans?”

    Maybe Agatha was going to do something for them the following day? “No, was just gonna stay in, read, catch up on some shows, help out with the house chores, just a plain boring Saturday.”

    Rio nodded. “Hm… okay. Sounds… relaxing, I suppose.” She suppressed her sigh, her shoulders slumped and she tried staving off her disappointment.

    Agatha seemed to notice this and stopped stirring the food then turned facing Rio completely. “Something on your mind, honey?”

    Rio avoided her gaze and just shook her head. “It’s… nothing, was just making… small talk.” She shrugged.

    Agatha was unsure how to feel. She took Rio’s hand in hers and kissed it. “You sure?” She rubbed circles on the back of her hand with her thumb.

    No! Rio wasn’t sure!

    “Well… it’s just… y’know…” she chanced a glance back at her. “Valentines… and all that.”

    Agatha groaned at the mention. “I know! Such a stupid corporate holiday! That suckers love sick individuals into buying their crap! Like! I don’t need Walmart telling me when to spend a day with my significant other!” She crossed her arms and shook her head, fuming at the mention. Rio felt her heart crumble and she glanced down at the floor. “Oh…” Agatha took notice of her unenthusiastic response, and immediately felt concerned.

    The older woman fidgeted nervously with her hands. “S-so…you don’t want…my gifts? I didn’t have much money to spend, but…” her voice broke as she tried keeping her emotions together. “I made you some things…” she added the next part under her breath. “I just wanted you to be… my valentine.” Her lip wobbled. Why was this hurting her as much as it was? It was… just a… “You know what, it’s fine. It’s just a stupid day and—“ “No! Rio! I had no idea you felt that way. Honey!” She grabbed her chin bringing her face up to meet her eyes. Her heart shattered when she saw the heartbroken look in her lovers teary eyes. “I’m sorry! I shouldn’t have expected you to feel the same! That doesn’t reflect my feelings for you I…” she groaned. “I’m an idiot! This is important to you! I’m sorry! Of course I’ll be your valentine! You made me something?”

    Rio sniffled but nodded. “It’s really okay, you don’t have to do this for me. It’s not that important and—“ “Rio, please. I’m an asshole! A jerk! I’ve always dreaded this day because I never had anyone to spend it with. But I have you! I…” She sucked in a shaky breath. “I had gotten you something as well… I was just going to wait, I…”

    The smile blooming over Rio’s features took all the air out of Agatha’s lungs.

    “You did?” She asked under her breath.

    Agatha couldn’t help but smile herself, a tear fell down her own cheek, she was upset at herself for neglecting Rio of this experience. “Yeah. I guess even though I… dislike this day so much I just… couldn’t avoid doing something. I…” she shook her head, willing herself to find the right words to make it right. “Rio, will you be my Valentine?”

    Rio lit up and nodded. “Y-yes!” She jumped with joy then pulled Agatha in for a hug. “I’ve never had one before.”

    And that was what destroyed the younger woman. Here she was wallowing about the fact that she had never had a damn Valentine and unknowingly ruining it for Rio who had always wanted one. But before she could sink into her pit of despair Rio kissed her.

    Agatha sighed into it, relaxing into her loving embrace, just being present with her love. She pulled back just enough to speak. “Do you want to… um… exchange gifts?”

    Rio nodded vigorously.

    They each made their way to the places they hid their gifts, then met back in the living room. Rio jumped with joy as she hid her own gifts under a blanket while Agatha came down the stairs with her gift behind her back. With a nervous sigh, Agatha began. “Alright, my love, you’ve waited long enough. Happy Valentine’s Day, beautiful.” She handed her a small gift bag, a rose peeking out from between the tissue paper.

    Rio squealed as she took it, opening it quickly—she had never had this experience before. She had waited her whole life for this, and— She froze.
