    Agatha rolled her eyes and uncrossed her arms. “I was not! I was merely pressing a throw pillow to your face, that was all. I barely applied pressure.”

    Rio lifted a brow. “Yeah, keep telling yourself that.”

    Agatha growled. “I would never hurt you!” She looked away with a ‘hmph’!

    Rio couldn’t help the smile over her face. Agatha was just so… cute! She opened her mouth to speak, before she could their darling boy was barreling into the front doors.

    “Momma! Mommy! I got an A plus on my math test!”

    Rio jumped for joy. “Oh honey that’s fantastic! I told you could do it! Let me see!”

    The days were getting longer and longer. And as of late Rio enjoyed her own personal time. When it was just her, Matilda and Scratchy. With her Girlfriend at work and son at school it left her with a lot of free time.

    She had caught up on cleaning and ran out of things to fix. She wasn’t interested in reading anything at the moment or play a video game. And scrolling mindlessly on her phone sounded mind numbing and not in the good kind of way, at least in that moment.

    So she decided to get fresh air. And enjoy what mid spring had to offer. It was sunny, warm but not hot, and a gentle breeze blew through the air, which felt soft and crisp.

    The leaves were almost completely back and flowers were blooming all around.

    It was perfect!

    Especially the warmth her skin was soaking up.

    Her phone buzzed, she sighed and stopped her pace.

    She had a feeling of who it could be.

    She grabbed it and pulled it out and of course she was right. Her father…

    He had been apologizing for months since that day.

    Rio didn’t go into too much detail, but he had a feeling as to why she was upset with them. And finally too… he acknowledged her as a she. Rio wasn’t sure when he figured out. Maybe someone from the group saw her when she was outside the restruant. She wasn’t sure.

    Regardless, she didn’t need this right now. Not when she had her own family to take care of, and a beautiful baby on the way.

    They came first.

    She slipped her phone back in her pocket, opting to shooting him a quick message later.

    She still needed to keep in contact a small bit. A part of her did feel bad. He did really seem sorry.

    But she’d give it more thought after the baby.

    Speaking of, Rio imagined her family together.

    The four of them.

    She grinned from ear to ear as she resumed her pace.

    What a comforting and wonderful thought!

    Especially imaging the baby having beautiful blue eyes! Dark brown hair, a smile that resembled her Momma’s!

    Rio really could not wait!

    Especially when—

    “Ah!”

    She stumbled when she nearly tripped over something. Something small, loud, and jerky.

    Looking down, she spotted a little black void on the sidewalk and— “Meow!”

    A large black kitten gazed up at her, and Rio swore she felt her heart melt. Those blue-green eyes!

    “Oh, what beautiful eyes you have! And aw! Look at your little socks!” She bent down, cooing over the kitten’s mismatched white paws and charming clipped ear. “Well, what’s your name, little one?”

    She squealed as the tiny creature purred and bunted its head against her knee.

    “Oh my god! I’m going to die from cuteness overload!”

    She snapped a few pictures. “You look so cool! So pretty and cute! And— ah! I can’t possibly leave you here!”

    Without hesitation, she scooped up the little feline and headed back toward the house.

    It wasn’t far—just around the corner, really.

    She smiled when she spotted Nicky playing in Wanda’s front yard with Tommy.

    “Mommy! I just got off the bus and—oh my god! Is that a kitty!?” He ran up to her, practically bouncing at the sight of the tiny black fluffball. “Can I pet him? Where did you find him? Are we getting another pet? Can he sleep in my room!?”

    “Whoa, there, bud! One question at a time. And yes, you can pet the kitten. I found this little cutie just around the block. As for keeping her, that’s up to your momma—it depends on what she says. She is the queen of the house, after all.”

    “Oh, I am so telling her that!”

    Rio jumped at the sudden voice behind her.

    Spinning around, she glared when she saw Wanda smirking at her. “Queen of the house? You’re such a simp, it’s not even funny.” Rio groaned. “You young people and your slang!” She rolled her eyes dramatically.

    Wanda snorted. “Oh, don’t give me that B.S. I’m in my mid-thirties—I’m not that young. And you’re not exactly the most… grown-up person.” “I am much more mature than you, thank you very much!” Rio huffed, turning away from Wanda with an exaggerated hmph Unaware of her son trying to sneak his hand around her, in an attempt to pet the kitten.

    Wanda scoffed playfully. “What do you got there? A hairball?” Rio gasped, looking deeply offended. In response she cradled the kitten closer to her chest and angled her body away so Wanda wouldn’t have the privilege of gazing upon such cuteness. “How dare you! This is a beautiful child, and you will treat her with respect!”

    Nicky groaned in frustration. “Mommy! You said I could pet the kitten!” Still holding her glare on Wanda, Rio relented. “Alright, my boy, my apologies. Here—be good to Blaire.” She carefully handed the kitten over to him.

    “Blaire? But… isn’t he a boy?”

    Wanda chuckled at his confusion. “Did you check, Rio?”

    Rio nodded firmly. “I did. She’s a beautiful girl.”

    Wanda crossed her arms, lifting an eyebrow at the tiny new addition. “You really think Agatha will let you keep it?”

    Rio smirked. “You think Vision will keep letting your son’s boyfriend climb in and out of your house every Friday night?”

    Wanda’s smile immediately dropped. Her arms fell to her sides. “What?” Rio grinned wider. “Oh—oops. Wasn’t supposed to say anything. Agatha made me promise. Something about a deal they struck… I don’t know.” Wanda shook her head, flabbergasted. “Billy!!” she shrieked before stomping off toward her house.

    Rio snickered at her victory. “Hehe, serves him right! No one disrespects my queen! The little twerp’s so getting it!”

    Before she or Nicky could react, an SUV rolled up beside them. Rio jumped slightly when she heard a whistle.

    “Well, aren’t you a sight,” came a smooth, familiar voice. “Has anyone ever told you that you resemble a Greek goddess? A beauty so rare, you must have been sculpted by the gods.”

    Rio grinned and turned around—only to find herself face-to-face with her lover.

    “Well, yes, actually.”

    Agatha’s face fell. “Who!?”

    Rio chuckled. “You, you dork!”

    A redness crept across Agatha’s cheeks with embarrassment. “Oh.” But it was quickly replaced with confusion. Her eyes zeroed in on the little fluff ball in her son’s arms.

    “What the—” She parked in the driveway, got out, and made her way over to her family. “What’s that?” She pointed at the kitten in Nicky’s arms. And dammit, Agatha was prepared to give them a whole speech about why it was a bad idea—until they both gave her that same damn look of sadness. With their pouty lips and sad eyes!

    “Please, Momma! Look at her, isn’t she cute?” Nicky held her up for her to see. Agatha’s eyes shot between the kitten, her son, and then her girlfriend. “Wh—what… n-no, we can’t… we…” She stomped her foot and growled. “No! We have two pets already and a baby on the way! Nicky, put it down!” She snapped her fingers and pointed at the ground. “Now!” Her voice carried that rare sternness that Nicky hadn’t heard in a long time. The scene was completely foreign to Rio.

    Rio upped her charm factor, bringing out the puppy eyes. “Baby, please. Look, she doesn’t have anybody! The kitten distribution system doesn’t make mistakes. The universe chose me—chose us! A new family member! I’ll take full responsibility, I swear!” She took the kitten from her son and snuggled her close to her face. “Please, baby! Please! It’s all I want!” Agatha had a hard time refusing. A really, really hard time. “Rio! I said—ugh, for god’s sake! We can’t, I—” She glanced at Nicky, who was mirroring Rio completely. And dammit, he was getting good at it! She pinched the bridge of her nose and growled. “I swear to—fine! Let me see her.” She held out her hands.

    Rio and Nicky cheered, and the eldest happily handed the kitten to the younger woman.

    Agatha lifted a brow. “Ebony?” She said the name as if recognizing a longtime friend. “You just won’t leave me alone, will you?” She sighed. “Fine, I guess you’re an honorary Harkness-Vidal now.”

    Rio’s eyes widened slightly in surprise. “Ebony? That’s Blaire! I already named her! No takesies-backsies! And she can just be a Harkness! Considering I’ll be one soon enough.”

    Agatha’s face fell in surprise. She wasn’t sure where to even begin. “Okay, first of all—interesting on the last name thing. Second of all, I just didn’t want you to feel left out, and I’ve been seeing this little shit on my way to work for weeks. She follows my car every day and rubs up against my foot when I stop for my morning espresso at the café down the street. I’d recognize these little socks and clipped ear anywhere—plus she’s got that evil little look in her eye! I started calling her Ebony one day. So, I’m sorry, dear, but she was already dubbed Ebony.”

    Rio groaned in frustration and crossed her arms. “I’m not backing down on this.”

    Agatha tucked the kitten beneath her arm and lifted a brow. “Oh, we’ll see about that.”

    A week flew by. Every morning, Rio would go out for a jog after Agatha left for work and Nicky went to school. And every day, Blaire—or Ebony, depending on who you asked—would paw at the windows, whining for her mommy to come back.

    Sometimes, Rio considered taking her on her jog. But her little legs wouldn’t be able to keep up.

    “Blaire! Pspspsps! Come here, cutie, where are you!?” Rio stuck her head into the living room after coming back from her jog, peeking around for her new little companion. “Cutie pie?” She grabbed a bag of treats and shook them, but still—no answer.

    Panic bubbled in her chest.

    A couple of hours passed, and still no kitty.

    It was almost time for Agatha to get back with Nicky from the doctor! Shit! And Agatha had grown rather attached to the little girl—just as Rio and Nicky had!

    “Baby! Come out, please!” Finally, after hours of searching, she heard a faint meow coming from the basement door. “Oh my sweet angel! How’d you even get down there!?” She pulled open the door, and sure enough, her precious kitten came barreling out.

    “Silly goose, let’s get you all fed!” She laid down a bowl, smiling ear to ear as she watched the little sweetie eat away.

    She heard the front door open and quickly made her way over to greet her two loves.

    “My two favorite people!” Rio gushed, pulling them in for hugs and kisses. “Mommy! I got a sucker!” Nicky held up the confection.

    “No bugs this time?” Rio asked disappointedly.

    Nicky shook his head, and Agatha gagged.

    “Alright, enough of that. Oh, look at Ms. Ebony! Coming down from your nap, are we?”

    Rio shot around, and sure enough, the kitten was trotting down the stairs, her bushy fur a mess from presumably napping.

    She did a double take toward the kitchen but noticed no cat in front of the food bowl. “Woah, she’s fast!”

    After Rio made dinner, the family retired to the living room. “Blaire’s so funny! She was chasing an ant in the kitchen!” Nicky looked up. “I thought I left her in my room… oh well.” They watched their movie before getting ready for bed.

    Agatha was the first to wake. She got out of bed gently so as not to wake Rio. The woman had been working so hard these past few weeks—she just wanted her love to sleep in.

    She smiled at her, brushing some of her hair behind her ear. She saved the image in her mind, archiving it away for special keeping before making her way downstairs.

    A little meow got her attention, and she lifted a brow. “Oh, yeah. I forgot about you. Come here—let’s eat something, shall we?”

    She scooped a bit of wet food onto a bowl and placed it in front of the kitten. “Bon appétit.” She took a sip of her coffee as she watched the little munchkin eat. “You’re gonna drive me up the wall, I just know it. But Rio and Nicky adore you, and I guess…” she sighed. “You’re kinda cute.” She rolled her eyes with a faint smile, then headed for the living room to sit down for a moment, wanting to read a bit before starting her day. Not a moment later, the kitten came and sat in her lap.

    “What? Not hungry?” She patted her on the head. The kitten yawned before circling in her lap, then plopping down.

    A second later, Agatha heard a meow from the floor. Her eyes shot down— and there was Ebony, licking the food off her mouth.

    Agatha’s eyes snapped back to the fluffy thing she was stroking in her lap. She froze.

    “…Ebony?” The kitten on the floor glanced up at her.

    “…Blaire?” The near-identical kitten on her lap looked up. Agatha blinked a few times, gently lifted the kitten off her lap, then got up to go wake Rio.

    She wanted to let her sleep longer, but… well… this was weird.

    Agatha paced back and forth, looking between the two kittens. Rio and Nicky, however, were grinning.

    “Looks like our problem’s solved,” Rio muttered.

    Agatha stopped pacing and threw out her hands. “What problem? The one where we’re stuck with two cats instead of one? When one was already too much!?”

    Rio chuckled. “No, silly. You get your Ebony, and I get my Blaire!” Agatha groaned. “Oh my god.”

    Nicky practically bounced with joy. “Yay! Now she’ll have a friend!” Agatha lifted Ebony up, and lo and behold—“I guess one of them is a he.” “Oh, and look! You got the boy you’ve been wanting so badly!” Rio teased. “And I get my little girl.”

    “So you just have two kittens now?” Jen asked with disbelief but excitement over drinks.

    Rio nodded with a smile. “Yeah! Isn’t it awesome!? Two new babies! Little Blaire and Ebony! I found Blaire, and Ebony must have followed Agatha home one night from work, I think Nicky let him in thinking it was Blaire. Don’t know how it took us a week to notice, I thought I was overfeeding the kitten but I guess they were sharing.”

    Alice chuckled. “Your hands are gonna be full! That’s for sure.” Agatha chugged her virgin margarita. “Tell me about it! I told her! She didn’t want to listen!”

    Rio rolled her eyes, “Oh don’t pretend you don’t love them! They’re our new babies. We’ll make it work.”

    Agatha couldn’t help but smile. “Well you’re scooping the litter.” She poked her finger against her lovers chest. Before anyone else could say anything Agatha stood. “I gotta pee. Be back in a minute.” Rio flashed her a loving smile. “I’ll count the minutes.” Her smile shifted to a grin as her eyes dropped down to her love’s large belly. “Beautiful.” She looked back up at her girlfriend, meeting her eyes.

    Agatha glared down at her. “You think this,” she gestured down at her large belly. “Is beautiful? Honestly?”

    Rio simply nodded. “I do. Very much so. You’re stunning. Glowing I’d dare say, even if it is cliché. I love that you’re carrying my baby. You look gorgeous no matter what to me. And I really like your belly!” “Oh my god! Get a room you two!” Jen groaned.

    Alice chuckled. “You’re just jealous you’re the only one who doesn’t have a partner Jen! Their love is beautiful.”

    “I’ll drink to that!” Hela spoke up as she slid in to the booth beside Alice. “Now’s your chance Harkness! Go before you wet yourself.” Agatha rolled her eyes but took her leave.

    She glanced back noticing Alice taking both Hela’s and Jen’s hands and lifted a brow.

    She immediately felt relief when she sat down in the stall. So much so she didn’t notice when someone else walked in.

    “Oh my god! You need to come out of me soon!” Agatha groaned as she exited the stall. “You’re getting heavy!”

    She turned the faucet on, unaware of the eyes on her back. “Oh my god! You’re pregnant!?”

    Agatha’s eyes widened and she looked up coming face to face with her through the reflection. Her face fell and she snarled. “I’m not giving you the satisfaction. Leave me alone or I’ll make you regret it!” There was no room for argument in her tone.

    The woman simply chuckled. “Or what? What will you do? You look like someone put a watermelon inside of you.”

    “Fuck off, Sara!” Agatha headed for the door but the blondes voice stopped her in her tracks.

    “I wanted to apologize!”

    Agatha met her gaze and lifted a brow. “I’m not the one you had running from a party crying.” She crossed her arms and sneered. “You’re talking to the wrong person, but then again I’d prefer it if you didn’t associate yourself with my love.” She paused before adding, “Ever!” Sara held up her arms. “I get it. I should apologize to her too. I won’t talk to her anymore though. I’m sure my presence would only upset her. I just wanted to make things right, that’s all. Rio’s a good… woman.” The blonde flashed a toothy smile.

    Agatha didn’t appreciate the pause before she said woman. “Alright well I’m leaving.” She headed for the door, but once again Sara stopped her with her words.

    “But I have to know, what’s it like?”

    She stopped dead in her tracks and slowly turned, eyeing her dangerously. “What!?”

    Sara grinned. “Let me rephrase that. What’s it like taking a… y’know? I’ve been curious lately.”

    Agatha growled. “I’m done!” She turned but this time Sara grabbed her arm placing herself between Agatha and the door.

    “Don’t you want to know what it’s like with a real woman? You’re too good for her, you know. I’m sure I can show you what it’s like to be with an actual les—“ Agatha smacked her hand away. “Don’t fucking touch me!”

    It didn’t faze Sara. She simply chuckled. “What? Is she that good? Is Rio great in the sac? I’m sure I could make you cum just as good if not better with a damn strap. Let alone my fingers. I’m being serious, Agatha! You’re way too hot! Too smart! Come on!” Her voice dropped to seductive tone, her eyes flicked up and down the pregnant woman’s body. “Let me show you, then you can actually know what it is you want.” She shortened the space between them, pressing her up against the counter.

    Rio glanced down at her watch surprised at how long it was taking Agatha. She sent her message and waited a few more minutes. When she noticed she hadn’t even looked at it she got up to go check on her.

    “Back the fuck up!” Agatha shoved her back, Sara looked annoyed but tried to rectify the situation.

    “Agatha be serious for a second. Just think! You’re a lesbian, yeah? Don’t you want to know what it’s like to be touched by an actual woman? I know better than anyone what it’s like to be tricked by her! Rio might be a pretty face and a great time, but in reality she’s a liar! A disgusting con artist! I mean she got you pregnant for Christ sake! I’m sure you didn’t even want that!”

    “I’m not talking to you about this! Rio is a better woman than you’ll ever be! Now move!” Agatha felt her phone vibrate in her maternity dress. Her fingers burned to grab it. But she didn’t want to have to stress her out by all of this. She just wanted to get back to her friends and love. “Just admit it! Say Rio isn’t a real woman! Allow me to show you a real lesbian romance! I am so much better than her! Look,” she pulled out her wallet and showed off all of the bills and cards. “I’m very wealthy. I have my own company, I even have my own kid! We have so much in common! Rio can’t possibly match up to me! I can even take care of you! You’d never even have to work again! I’ just want to help you! Rio’s just not go—“ “SHUT UP!” Agatha shouted.

    Not a second later the door flew open.

    Rio noticed the blonde’s back to the door—and Agatha’s furious face. Something in her snapped from seeing her girlfriend in such distress like this. She saw red.

    The situation escalated when the blonde turned around, revealing herself to be her. Her horrible ex with boundary issues, the one who couldn’t comprehend the word no.

    Sara rolled her eyes and spoke with contempt. “Oh, great! It’s you! I can’t believe you got her pregnant! So you really are a man. What’d you do? Did you rap—ARGHHH!”

    Agatha’s fist collided with her jaw, knocking her to the floor. Not giving her the chance to finish that horrific sentence.

    Stepping over her Agatha shouted down at her, “Don’t you fucking dare suggest something so horrible about Rio! I’m sick of your damn mouth!” Her tone dripped with venom. “Rio is an amazing woman! The woman of my dreams! The love of my life! I would never in a million years want you!”

    She took a breath and stepped away, forcing herself to calm down. Rio was still in shock. Her eyes flicked to the blood on Agatha’s fist, and she panicked. “Agatha, are you okay!?” She reached out for her. But Agatha just smiled and nodded. “I feel amazing.” She washed the blood off and placed a comforting hand on her love’s back. “Come on, baby. Let’s go back to our friends.”

    Rio did a double take at Sara, who was lying on the floor clutching her bruised face. The oddly satisfying sight faded as Agatha pulled her out of the bathroom.

    “Your fist doesn’t hurt?” Rio asked worriedly, reaching for her hand and kissing it.

    “It’s a faint pain, but it’s fading already—and it was worth it.” Rio stopped Agatha in her tracks. “Baby?”

    “Yes?” Agatha felt worry flood her at the scared look in Rio’s eyes. But the older woman simply frowned, shook her head, and pulled her girlfriend into a tight embrace. “I love you. I love you so much. I’m so sorry if she put her hands on you or if she said horrible things to you! I’m sorry you had to even be involved in any of that, and I—” “Rio, please.” Agatha pulled back just enough to gaze into her eyes. When she noticed her tears, she felt her heart break. She caressed her face and sighed. “It wasn’t your fault.”

    “I—I wasn’t there. It’s my job to protect you and the baby, and I—” Agatha shook her head and pressed her forehead against Rio’s. “I promise you, it wasn’t your fault. And I’m a big girl, I can handle myself. Besides —” She grinned, “You don’t understand how… cathartic that was. To lay into her like that. She’s a terrible person, Rio. But that by no means makes you anything like her. She never deserved you. You’re so perfect, I can’t even begin to describe it. But…” She smiled lovingly pausing for a moment before continuing. “Well, I honestly could go all day about how perfect you are, but we’d be here for hours!”

    This managed to pull a chuckle from Rio herself. “I could say the same. I think I’d get really annoying about how perfect you are.” Agatha waved a finger at her. “Oh, don’t you spin this on me now. You’re the one on trial!” She booped her nose. “My beautiful and loving girlfriend!”

    Rio opened her mouth to speak, but before she could get the words out, her stomach growled, interrupting her mid-breath. Her face flushed with embarrassment at the untimely betrayal of her own body.

    But Agatha only seemed amused. “Aww, come on, darling. Let’s get you fed! I could go for some pasta. We could share? Maybe get those breadsticks you love so much.”

    “I mean, I do enjoy sharing with you. But you’re eating for two now—I’d feel bad taking from you and the little one.”

    Agatha chuckled as they made it to their table.

    “Ugh, finally! What took you so long!?” Jen groaned. “We’re starving!” “Sorry, was kicking someone’s ass in the bathroom,” Agatha said nonchalantly before sitting down.

    The three women at the table looked at each other, then back at her, wondering if she was serious. Their eyes shifted to Rio, looking for confirmation, only to see her shrug awkwardly.

    “Who!?” Alice and Jen asked at the same time.

    “She was just joking,” Rio tried to laugh it off as she took her seat beside Agatha. But the lie was futile. She just wanted to move past this. Dread settled in her stomach at the what if. What if Sara called the police on them? “I was not! That Sara bitch was coming onto me in the bathroom and speaking bad about Rio. So I decked her to shut her up! End of story.” Rio’s hands stiffened against the edge of the table. On the other hand, she could go back and finish the job herself.

    Hela growled and stood up. “She still in there!?”

    Agatha flipped her hair over her shoulder and pursed her lips, utterly unconcerned. “Dunno, don’t care. Wanna feed my baby and my infant.” She placed her hand against Rio’s back, rubbing soothing circles—an attempt to calm her down. Realized she basically just dropped a bombshell on Rio. “I’m gonna go back in there,” Rio grumbled under her breath, staring at her hands on the table. “I’m gonna—”

    “You’re gonna stay right here and order something,” Agatha finished for her.

    Rio’s head shot up, meeting her gaze. “But you said— ugh! What did she do!? Did she touch you inappropriately? Hurt you? Try to exploit you? Because if she did, I swear to God, Agatha, I’m not afraid to—” Agatha grabbed her shoulders, kneading them gently. “Rio, honey, please. Calm down. I promise I’ll tell you all about it when we get home. It wasn’t anything that bad, I promise. I just want to have a nice evening with you and our friends. Please? Don’t let her ruin our night.”

    “But she—”

    Agatha started pouting, and—dammit! Is this what it was like!? To endure the power of the puppy face!?

    “Okay, I’m so—umfh!”

    Agatha cut her off with a searing kiss before she could even finish that sentence. She intentionally made it heated, hoping it would serve as a distraction for her love.

    So much so that she shoved her tongue into her mouth, and Rio forgot where she was. Oh God. It was so good! Her toes curled, and she groaned. Her eyes rolled back, and she practically pulled Agatha onto her lap, needing much, much more. What was she doing to her right now!? They completely forgot about the three women sitting across from them. And while Alice could potentially get into this, Jen and Hela could not. Given Jen’s past strained friendship with Agatha, and Hela’s sisterhood with Rio, the two quickly looked anywhere else.

    To break the tension—and their horny spell—Alice let out a whistle. “Hell yeah! I can toast to that! Can I come back with you guys and watch!? That was so fucking hot! Damn!”

    The two women pulled apart, both glaring at Alice.

    Alice couldn’t care less. Instead, she glanced at the two women beside her and chuckled at their obvious disgust. “Oh, grow up, you two. We’re all adults. I at least get Hela’s disgust—what’s your excuse?” She gestured toward Jen.

    Alice smirked at the grimace on Jen’s perfect little face. “Alice, that’s our boss. It’s a little weird. I dare say Rio was a second away from putting another baby inside of her at this very table.” Jen tapped against the wood as she spoke.

    “Oh fuck off Kale! You’re lucky this is after hours or else you’d be getting detention!”

    “I’d bet you’d like that wouldn’t you Agatha.” Alice teased with a wink. “I’m still worried about the issue at hand,” Hela brought up. Agatha groaned. “Guys, I just want to enjoy the rest of the night. Please?” Both Hela and Rio let out frustrated growls.

    “You don’t understand how bad I wanna kill that bitch, Agatha,” Hela grumbled. “Now she’s coming after you!? She needs to be locked in a psych ward.”

    “I think I do understand,” Agatha countered, exasperated. “But I just want to be done with it all.” She turned to Rio, pleading with her eyes. “Please, can we drop this? Just for dinner? I’ll tell you anything you want to know afterward. I promise.”

    Rio sighed, then nodded. She glanced at Hela and offered a small, comforting smile. “It’s okay, sis. I want to be present with all of you. And I don’t want Agatha more stressed than she probably already is. Let’s just go back to our night, okay? We’ll figure everything else out later.” Hela exhaled sharply but relented. “Okay. But we seriously need to discuss this another time. This is serious.”

    “Agreed,” Rio said, her tone firm but gentle.

    The drive back was tense. No one spoke.

    Rio felt bad that Agatha had to drive, considering she was the designated driver. Being pregnant and all, she couldn’t drink.

    They dropped Jen off first. Both Rio and Agatha shared a look when they saw Jen peck both Alice and Hela on the cheek goodnight.

    Hela simply muttered, “Don’t ask,” to a smirking Rio.

    Rio held up her hands in surrender. “Hey, you guys can do whatever you want. I’m the last person to judge.”

    Alice grinned. “It’s a new thing. Very new. We’re just trying it out, but if it doesn’t work out, I’ll always stay with Hela.”

    Rio smiled at the sentiment but still felt exhausted, ready to be done with the day.

    Twenty minutes later, after dropping off Alice and Hela, they finally made it home.

    Rio sighed in relief. “Oh my god, I need a shower. Maybe a nap.” Agatha hummed in agreement. “Sounds nice. I’ll catch up on some laundry while you relax.”

    “Well, I was hoping you’d join me,” Rio admitted. “I can help with the laundry after?”

    Agatha smiled as they stepped inside. “Sure.”

    Once they were settled in the shower, Rio held Agatha against her chest, letting her love’s worries melt away in the warmth of the water. After a few moments, Agatha broke the comfortable silence. “She tried to convince me to leave you for her.” Her voice was calm but firm. “She grabbed my arm, but I told her to let go. At some point, she backed me into the sink, but I shoved her away. She tried convincing me with her money and whatever else, but I didn’t want to even look at her face, let alone listen to her voice.”

    Rio let out a heavy sigh. “She didn’t hurt you?”

    Agatha shook her head. “No. Not physically. But I didn’t appreciate what she said about you.” She pulled Rio tighter. “I don’t want her. I don’t want anyone else. She tried to convince me you aren’t a real woman, but you’re the realest woman I’ve ever met in my life. And you’re all I want. All I need.” She met Rio’s eyes, her voice unwavering. “She could never be as great a woman as you. I promise you that. There’s no one quite like you.” Rio smiled softly, tilting her head. “And what would that be, exactly?” “Well, as I said before, I could go on and on, but I think the water would get cold.” Agatha smirked. “For now, I’ll say you’re the kindest woman I’ve ever met. And funny too. In a… quirky way.”

    “Quirky?” Rio raised an amused brow.

    Agatha nodded. “Absolutely. But I love it. It’s what makes you so charming.” She twirled a lock of Rio’s hair between her fingers. “You have a unique charisma about you. It’s oddly attractive and endearing. You manage to capture the attention of those around you, in a good way.” “I’ve heard ‘weird’ and ‘awkward’ before,” Rio said, amused. “But never ‘charming’ and ‘charismatic.’”

    “You are weird and awkward, but somehow, you’re also smooth. I don’t know how you can be awkward one minute and smooth the next.” “ADHD?”

    Agatha shrugged. “Possibly.” She giggled. “It would explain why you can never sit still and why I have to decipher what you’re saying sometimes because you can’t keep on topic before getting distracted by another thought.”

    Rio grinned. “Guilty. Distractions are a bitch, huh?”

    “Yes! Especially when I’m trying to go over business plans with you! How did Hela survive?”

    “Oh, that’s easy. She just made me do all the planning. Took forever! She hates planning things like that. You have no idea how messy it was trying to get our business up and running.”

    “Oh, I have some idea.”

    “I guess you do, and—oh, before I forget, did you pick up the cat food today? The special kind for kittens?”

    Agatha lifted a brow. She opened her mouth to speak, but Rio beat her to it. “Oh! Also, I planned on doing this thing with Nicky and—what was it called?” She looked off into the distance, racking her brain. “Um…” She tapped her chin, struggling.

    “Brain empty?” Agatha teased.

    “Huh?” Rio blinked. “Oh, um, yeah. What were we talking about?” Agatha sighed, rolling her eyes. “Oh, for the love of—how perfect you are.” Rio snapped her fingers. “Oh yeah! Trampoline park!”

    “Wait, what?” Agatha burst into laughter. “I can’t! I love you so much! You’re so scatterbrained and random! I love it!”

    Rio blushed at her laughter, rubbing the back of her neck. “Oh.” She let out a nervous chuckle. “I guess I got off topic. Whoops. Guess I’m a little dinged up in the ol’ noggin.” She tapped her head.

    Agatha shook her head, smiling fondly. “No, you’re perfect to me. Don’t ever change. I love you, Rio Vidal.”

    Rio flashed a toothy grin, and dammit—Agatha had gotten so used to seeing her cute little tooth gap that she’d stopped processing it! “I love you too, Agatha Harkness.”

    Chapter 18: What more could I wish for!

    Chapter Summary Birthday cake Matching outfits Excercise Chapter Notes I’m sorry for the wait. Life got busy. But I made it. I have a clear plan for the last two. I hope you guys enjoy this one.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Rio sat on the couch stroking Blaire’s fur. The house was quiet, and once again she was alone, with nothing to do. Her eyes drifted over to the framed photo on the coffee table.

    The ultrasound image of their baby.

    The whole thing was stressful to say the least. They had done this once before. The ultrasound photo at seven weeks hadn’t shown much, but this one was a bit clearer.

    The second appointment had been a few weeks ago, when Agatha was a little over twelve weeks along. And every single time Rio felt her nervousness bubbling in her belly.

    The ultrasound technician had commented on how fast the baby was growing. It was common for experienced mothers, but still, she was growing fast, too fast. It worried Rio, just a little.

    “What do you think, Blaire? Does the baby have my eyes?” She angled the kitten toward the photo, but Blaire seemed completely uninterested and wiggled to get out of Rio’s grasp.

    “Alright, fine! Go on. Looks like Ebony is here to stay!” She stuck her tongue out at the kitten scurrying away and patted the one sleeping at her side. “I can’t believe you two are siblings. You’re rambunctious, and he’s a little snuggle bug. I mean, we just played for the last hour! I’m tired! You’re killing your mother!”

    The kitten meowed back at her, with something akin to attitude. Rio was taken aback by her baby girl’s mouthiness. “I don’t have to take this! Matilda, Scratchy, and Ebony don’t give me lip!”

    Speaking of, she glanced around, looking for the little guy, and sure enough, he was sitting in his bed in the corner, chewing on some lettuce. She smiled, happy he was content. She took her leave and headed for her office, where her sweet Matilda was no doubt fantasizing about catching the flies outside.

    “There’s my sweetheart. Let’s get your cage cleaned, shall we?”

    “Meoooooow!”

    Rio arched an eyebrow and turned, seeing Blaire purring and slow blinking at her with all of the love and affection her little heart could give. “Dammit! How could I say no to that face. Fine, come to Momma!”

    The day was almost here!

    Agatha couldn’t believe it! In just a few days her baby boy would be twelve!

    Where had the time gone!?

    “Alright! You got the candles and the balloons!?” She asked quickly while jotting her list down.

    “Check and check.” Rio beamed, excited she was getting to help plan their son’s birthday party.

    “And I got the cake ordered, we can pick it up in two days. I made sure to get those little cartoons put on it.”

    Rio chuckled. “You mean anime?”

    “Yeah, that. Alright. Now.” She flipped to her next page. “We just need to make sure we have enough tables and chairs for the backyard, so the kids can eat. I also planned on getting some backyard games for them. Oh!” Agatha looked up from her papers. “Did you get in touch with that magician?”

    Rio gave her a look of disbelief. “Ugh! We don’t need that! I can do that! I’ve got magical fingers, baby.” She wiggled her fingers with a smirk accentuating her point.

    The flirtatious action stirred a confusing feeling inside Agatha’s chest. Rio needed to make her point clear, so she approached her girlfriend, reached behind her head and pulled a rose out of nowhere. “M’lady!” Agatha wasn’t so easily impressed. But still, she giggled and took the rose. Rio just had a way about her and— “Rio, stop, you’re making me blush.” The younger woman hid her smile behind the flower. Shying a bit from her lovers charm.

    Rio smirked. “Am I now?” She slid her fingers up her arm. “You’re cute when you’re flustered.” She leaned in for a kiss, but before she could make contact Agatha moved back.

    “Wait! We have to stay on track! Do not seduce me, temptress!” She pointed her pen at her. “The catering place?”

    Rio’s smirk shifted to an amused smile. “Reserved the best meal package for the big day!”

    “And that action figure he’s been wanting?”

    “Ordered.”

    “And the game?”

    “Picked it up this morning at Walmart.” Rio offered a toothy grin. “And you’re sure we aren’t missing anything?” Agatha could have sworn she was forgetting something.

    But Rio simply shook her head and shrugged. “Nope, that’s all the important stuff.”

    The next couple of days were stressful for Agatha. She had to make sure everything was perfect—nothing could go wrong.

    It didn’t matter how many times Rio reassured her that everything looked great and that they had everything they needed. Agatha still fretted over the tiniest details.

    Now it was time for the kids, and some of her friends to come over, per Nicky’s request. Apparently, he considered his mother’s friends his friends too, which was honestly kind of sweet.

    The day actually went really well—aside from Tommy getting an upset stomach halfway through and having to go home to nap it off. Poor little guy.

    She also felt bad for Rio since Hela couldn’t make it, apparently having had some business out of town.

    But Nicky had a blast, and all his friends had fun.

    Agatha enjoyed watching him stick to Mayday’s side the entire time. She never realized how shy her boy actually was—he only seemed confident when he was with her. It reminded her of how Rio could be. After everyone left and they cleaned up, they finally had a moment to themselves. It was late, just in time for bed. But that was okay. They could cuddle.

    But the moment their heads hit their pillow they immediately passed out.

    Agatha’s alarm went off, waking her first, Rio somehow managed to sleep through it, which was strange considering she was the morning bird. Regardless, the sound was getting annoying.

    Agatha reached for her phone then swiped up to shut off the grading sound. But was confused when she saw it was actually a notification that she had gotten a message and was from Hela.

    Hela: I’m so sorry I was busy! I hope you had a good birthday! Agatha arched a brow and sent her a message asking if she meant Nicky’s. Hela: Huh… oh. No. I guess that was yesterday. Kinda crazy to be honest. Tell the kid I said happy birthday. I’ll be sure to pick him something up. Agatha waited a moment before Hela sent another follow up text. Hela: Are you wanting to ignore it this year altogether? It’s fine if you do, I get it. You can always count on me, you know I’ll always listen. Just like I always have.

    Squinting at the screen, Agatha blinked a few times. That was when she realized—she wasn’t holding her phone, but Rio’s.

    She stared at the message, trying to piece together this puzzle. Instead of responding, she simply placed the phone back down and got out of bed. Glancing over at Rio, she smiled. The sunlight casted a soft glow over her raven locks and skin, making her look even more ethereal. Agatha sighed at the dreamy sight, but her thoughts quickly fluttered back to what Hela had said.

    Before she could get too lost in thought she decided to just head downstairs and start breakfast.

    Roughly an hour later Rio made her way downstairs, yawning and stretching, looking peaceful as ever.

    Dammit!

    How can anyone look that good in the morning!?

    Agatha didn’t want to press the issue. But she still wanted to know what Hela meant. She decided to wait until after Nicky left for Wanda’s for his sleepover with Tommy.

    The two women sat across from each other at the dinner table, enjoying their meal.

    But the quiet only left room for their thoughts to race.

    Agatha lifted her glass to her lips, but before taking a sip, she asked, “So… anything on your mind lately?”

    Rio shrugged without looking up, still staring at her plate while pushing her food around.

    Agatha frowned, concern etching her face as she lowered her glass. “Everything okay? Did I under-season the meatloaf?”

    Rio’s head snapped up. “What? No!” She set her fork down and sighed. “I’m sorry, I’ve just been… tired, I guess.” She shrugged again. “It gets lonely here without you two. There’s only so much I can fix around the house—unless I start breaking things on purpose.” She let out an awkward chuckle, but it quickly fizzled out. Her gaze dropped to her lap as a somber expression washed over her features. “I don’t have much to do once the chores are done, and I can finish them pretty fast most days. After that, I just… wait, I guess.”

    Agatha mentally facepalmed. How was she supposed to bring up the confusing text, when Rio was already going through something? Maybe Hela meant something else, or it was just an autocorrect? Yes, that had to be it.

    Agatha sighed before making a suggestion. “Rio, darling, if you’d like, you could come to the office and help out. I’m sure I could find something for you to do. I’d compensate you, of course.”

    Rio’s eyes lit up. “Really!?” She quickly reeled herself in, clearing her throat. “I mean… you won’t get in trouble?”

    Agatha chuckled. “What’s gonna happen? I smack myself on the wrist? I listen to no one.”

    “Oh! Sorry! I forgot!” Rio giggled awkwardly, then a thought came to her and she smirked. “Does this mean you’ll be my boss?”

    “Well… not directly. I know we need help on the lower floors, and—” Agatha paused, as she noticed Rio’s gaze flicker down her body, with a ridiculous grin plastered across her face. “Are you checking me out right now?”

    “Maybe.”

    Her tone was unapologetically honest, while she continued eyeing Agatha up like the delicious morsel she was.

    Agatha arched a brow, before leaning to the side to peak under the table. “Pfft! Seriously?” There was no denying what Rio was feeling right now. Not with the tent in her pants. Agatha leaned back up, shaking her head side to side, amused by Rio. “You dirty dog.”

    Rio noticed a bit of cleavage peaking out from Agatha’s shirt, the tempting visual forced a growl to slip from her mouth before she bit her lip. “Woof.”

    Before things could get out of hand, Agatha raised a hand. “I… there’s something on my mind. I just need to ask you about it. I’m sure it’s nothing, but I need to ease my mind.”

    Rio’s face fell. “Oh.” She sat back, forcing herself to relax. She was momentarily disappointed that the moment wasn’t going where she had hoped, but it wasn’t that big of a deal. Still, she wished her member would go down already. “What’s on your mind, honey? You can ask me anything. Go on, shoot.” She offered a small smile.

    “When’s your birthday?”

    Rio’s smile vanished.

    The change was instant, and Agatha noticed right away.

    Rio’s silence said more than words ever could.

    Agatha needed to fill the space with something, she couldn’t just sit there in silence. “Rio… I accidentally picked up your phone this morning, thinking it was mine. Hela said happy birthday. At first, I assumed she meant for our son, but she said no.” She paused, her expression tightening for a moment before slightly relaxing. “Was your birthday this week?”

    Again, Rio hesitated to answer.

    So Agatha waited—giving her time.

    Eventually, Rio found the courage to speak, but she couldn’t meet Agatha’s eyes. Instead, she stared down at the table, nervously fiddling with her hands. “It was… Saturday.” Her voice was small. “I was born on the nineteenth. Of… this month.” She chanced a glance up and caught Agatha’s frown. She couldn’t hold her gaze for more than a second before looking back down.

    The silence stretched longer than it should have.

    The sound of cars passing outside filled the space.

    “Why didn’t you tell me?”

    Agatha sounded… sad? Upset? Maybe a little angry?

    Rio kept her eyes down. “B-because I… didn’t think it—um—it just never came up, and I—” Her eyes flickered up again. “Nicky’s was so close, I just…” She sighed. “It wasn’t important.” She shrugged.

    Apparently, that was the wrong thing to say. Agatha’s brows furrowed slightly, and she glared at Rio. “Why the hell wouldn’t it be? You don’t even share the same birthday.”

    Rio desperately wanted to fix this. “I-I know, but it was so close, I just wanted to focus on him and—”

    “Rio! You could have told me.” Agatha’s hand hit the table with an accidental smack, making Rio flinch.

    “I… I know I should have. But…” She struggled to find the words. “But?”

    The agitated groan that escaped Rio surprised Agatha.

    “Can we drop this for now, please?”

    Agatha clasped her head in her head, needing a second to think. “Rio, please. I just want to know. Why keep this from me? From us? Why not te —“ “Because, I don’t care about it! There! Happy!?” Rio snapped, startling Agatha.

    She opened her mouth to respond, but Rio continued before she could utter a single syllable.

    “You don’t understand! That day is just a reminder of the way I was born! Of the fact I wasn’t what my parents wanted!” she covered her face with her hands, attempting to calm herself down.

    Agatha stood up and reached out, but hesitated before lowering her hands altogether. “Rio, I’m sure you didn’t think that when you celebrated bef—“ “I didn’t!” She dropped her hands and shouted. “I never had one!” Then slammed her hand on the table. “I have never, in my entire life, had a single birthday party, ever! No one to sing me happy birthday! No one to share cake with! No one to give me a damn gift! No one, Agatha!” Every word struck Agatha like a knife to her heart. She had to take a few steps back, she wasn’t used to Rio being this angry. As she spoke her voice came out quiet and shaky. “I-I’m sorry. I’m so sorry! I-I didn’t realize.” She felt the tears slip from her eyes and immediately covered her face. Rio caught her breath, her expression fell as she watched her love weep into her hands—all because she had just shouted at her. She stood up quickly and rushed to her side. Her voice was shaky but soft.

    “Hey, wait, no, I… I didn’t mean to—” She hesitated, reaching out, unsure if it was okay to. “A-Agatha? I’m sorry. Can I…” She gulped. “Can I—do you want me to—”

    Agatha dropped her hands and pulled Rio in for a hug, holding her tight. This took Rio by surprise. Why would Agatha want to hug her after she’d just shouted? After she’d lied? Her hands hovered over Agatha’s back for a moment before finally relaxing.

    “I’m not mad, Rio.” Agatha pulled back to meet her eyes. “Sure, I was a bit surprised—maybe a little upset. But I care about you more. I’m sad for what you had to go through. I just want you to experience now what you couldn’t then. I want to give that to you.”

    Rio sighed. “It’s okay, Agatha, really. I stopped caring about it a long time ago.”

    “But you have me and Nicky! We want to celebrate your life and show you how much we appreciate you—the way you have for us! Your life is worth celebrating, Rio!”

    The words struck something deep inside of her. Rio’s lip wobbled, seconds before her tears started to fall. “Y-you mean it? You want to… celebrate my birthday?”

    Agatha teared up again but nodded. “Of course I do! I love you so much! Nicky loves you so much!”

    “Y-you don’t think…” Rio shuffled her feet, trying so hard to finish her question, but her voice was small, breaking as she struggled to even speak. “You think my life is… worth it? That it wasn’t a… mistake?” She looked down, still fearing that maybe… Agatha would say—

    “Rio, if something ever happened to you, I don’t know what I’d do! You are so important to me—to our son! Your life is worth more than you could ever know! None of it was a mistake! Baby, look at me, please!” Rio hesitated but eventually met Agatha’s gaze. All of the air left her body when she saw her love’s face drenched in tears.

    “Let me help you see what I see everyday, when I’m blessed to gaze upon you! Let me help you feel what I feel for you in my heart! Let me help you celebrate the birth of an amazingly kind and beautiful woman! The love of my life! The mother of my child! You gave me the greatest gift I could have ever asked for, and he’s made me so happy for the last twelve years! Let me repay you for what you’ve given me. It can just be the three of us, or Hela can come! Or we can invite our friends! Whatever you want! It’s time you start being celebrated, Rio. Because you’re worth celebrating!” Rio swallowed back the rest of her tears and nodded. “Okay! We can do that. Let’s have a belated birthday party.”

    After winding down from all the excitement and stress—an hour of massaging each other while sharing what they loved most—Agatha finally brought up the question that had been on her mind since learning about it. “I hope this is okay to ask, but you and Hela never celebrated each other’s birthdays?”

    Rio shook her head. “No. Neither of us really cared for the idea.” “But she wished you happy birthday over the phone.”

    “Yeah, we at least do that. We kinda silently vowed to just write or text it once to each other every year and that was that. I don’t know why or how it started, but it did. It’s honestly just a habit at this point. I love her, but neither of us ever cared. It’s just a reminder if anything. Aside from her, she’s the only one. At least in written form.” Rio shrugged again that day. “I guess at least I had that. Otherwise my story would have been much sadder. It’s just my reality. You learn to live with it.”

    “Well that changes today! No more running away from it! It’s time Rio Vidal celebrates the day of her birth head on! And you can bet your cute ass you’ll have the greatest cake in all of New Jersey! Maybe even the country!”

    Rio giggled. “Walmart works. Or I could bake it and—“ “No! That’s not how this works! This is your first birthday party! I won’t allow you to settle for just a Walmart cake! And the birthday girl doesn’t bake her own cake! Someone else does it for her!”

    “Oh. I didn’t know there were rules to these things.”

    Agatha chuckled. “Well, there aren’t I guess. But most people don’t make their own cakes. At least the people I’ve met. And I meant what I said, I will personally find you the perfect cake.”

    Rio softly smiled. “I think I’d like it if you made me one.” Her cheeks flushed at the thought. “If that’s alright with you of course?” “Of course it is! It’s more than okay! I’ll make you the greatest cake ever!” Agatha threw her hands up in the air, signifying the greatness of said cake, pulling another chuckle out of Rio in the process.

    “Shit! Wanda, what am I gonna do? I’ve never baked a cake myself! At least nothing that wasn’t from a box, and even then, it comes out crappy! How am I going to make the greatest cake ever if I have little to no practice baking!?”

    Wanda watched Agatha pace back and forth in her kitchen, the amusement of it all was entertaining.

    “Well, I could help you. Rio said she was fine with a Walmart cake. I don’t think she’s expecting some Cake Boss-level masterpiece. And besides, she was in foster care. I’m sure it’ll be the greatest cake in her book anyway. I can’t imagine she’s had very many birthday cakes.”

    Agatha furrowed her brows and grumbled under her breath.

    “Huh?” Wanda strained her ears to hear her.

    “I said, my sweetheart has never had her own cake!”

    “Oh!” Wanda frowned. “Hm… Well, I’ll help you. I’m not a master baker or anything, but I’m sure if we put our brains together, we can figure this out. It’s just baking—how hard can it be?”

    Two hours later…

    “Shit.”

    Agatha groaned and set her mixing bowl down. She stepped back and looked down at herself covered in flour. “You know, I didn’t think this would get so messy! But here I am!” she snarled, yanking off her useless apron, which had egg smeared all over it. Bits of egg clung to her maternity shirt beneath, and somehow, she had some in her hair! Her eyes flicked up to Wanda, noticing how… less filthy she was—and she was fucking laughing!?

    “Aw, I told you to turn the stand mixer down. Not my fault.” Wanda turned away, the hand over her mouth doing little to conceal her laughter. “You think this is fucking funny!?” Agatha grabbed a bit of egg yolk from the counter and whipped it in Wanda’s direction, not expecting her to have turned back so soon.

    “No, I’m just—Argh!”

    Wanda blinked in shock, confused, before quickly wiping the yolk from her cheek and mouth. “What the fuck, dude!?”

    “Ha! That’s what you get! Here, have some flour too!”

    “No! Wai—” Before Wanda could even blink, a thin plume of flour billowed in front of her. Most of it dispersed in the air before reaching her. Leaving nothing but a pathetic cloud.

    Agatha looked annoyed, but Wanda found it hilarious.

    “Ha!”

    “Alright, enough of that. We need to focus! I need to get this right for Rio!” “Well maybe we could—“

    Both women’s heads turned at the sound of the front door opening and a familiar voice.

    “Momma?”

    “Nicky?” Agatha replied. “You’re home already?” She glanced at her phone then back up at the boy running to her. “It’s only one, my sweet boy.” She kissed his head and hugged him. “Are you playing hooky for math class?” The boy shook his head. “No.” He chuckled. “But lucky me! They found lice on a third grader, so they sent everyone home early! Mommy picked me up while she was shopping.”

    Agatha’s eyes widened and she quickly pushed the boy back. “Oh! Um…” she tapped her fingers together nervously. “Do you feel itchy?” He shook his head.

    “Well let me check your hair in the bathroom, why don’t we throw those clothes in the dryer for a bit just in case, alright? Then you take a shower.” Nicky groaned, but nodded.

    “Oh, don’t give me that. You should count yourself lucky you don’t have it. That we know of! Or else Im getting a nit comb, mayo and Saran Wrap!” Nicky visibly shuttered. “Not again! I was only five! I can’t go through it second time!”

    “And you have longer hair! And while I’d hate to see it go if I have to I’ll shave it off!”

    Nicky’s hands flew up to his head. “Not my hair! My beautiful locks! You’ll break mine and mommy’s heart! It’s my best feature!” The boy ran off toward the downstairs bathroom whining.

    Agatha huffed following after him. “Best feature? Everything about you is amazing!” She grumbled on her way. Rio came in just before she went inside. Agatha sighed in relief, but kept her gaze on the bathroom door. “Oh good, there you are. Can you help me check his hair? It’s such a pain, and I hated it the last time I had to do it. And—“ she turned, and finally noticed the shower cap Rio was wearing and immediately stifled a chuckle. “I am not getting lice again! I’ve gotten it too many times in foster care! It’s practical, do not laugh at me! Or I’ll give you something to laugh about.” She zeroed in on Agatha’s sides, lightly tickling her.

    Agatha struggled in her girlfriend’s grasp. “Rio! We have to focus! Boy! Hair! Lice!”

    Rio dropped her hands and nodded. Finally taking Agatha in. “Why are you covered in—” she trailed off trying to figure out what it even was. “What are you even covered in?”

    Agatha had almost forgotten about it. “Oh, that. It’s nothing. Let’s get this boy clean!”

    After checking every inch of their son’s scalp and finding a fortunate lack of bugs or eggs they settled on having him shower and tossing his clothes in the dryer, just to be safe. Then Agatha hurried back to the kitchen where Wanda was, playing on her phone at the table.

    The red head groaned in relief. “Finally! Jeez! You guys were in there for two hours!”

    “Do you know how long it takes to check a kids hair.” Agatha glanced down at her watch. “We’ll have to pick this up tomorrow, Tommy will be home soon, and I’m sure you need to make dinner.”

    Wanda chuckled. “Wow, kicking me out? And after I cleaned your kitchen for you?” She gestured around her.

    Agatha glanced around, noticing the lack of mess and smiled. “Aren’t you sweet. I promise you can come over tomorrow. Rio’s going to spend the day with Hela. It’ll be perfect.”

    Wanda smiled but nodded. “Alright, Harkness. I look forward to it.” She stood. “But no more egg fights! That was disgusting!”

    “I can’t make no promises.”

    Agatha got up bright and early, comtemplating her decisions and how she wanted to go about making this cake. She watched YouTube tutorials and read a myriad of recipes online.

    After roughly an hours she felt okay enough to attempt this. She stood in the kitchen, sleeves rolled up and hair tied back, eyeing the ingredients laid out on the counter. Flour, sugar, eggs—everything she needed to practice making a cake for Rio’s belated birthday. Her back-up should be arriving any moment.

    And almost like clockwork a sharp knock at the backdoor announced Wanda’s arrival. “You ready to make a mess of your kitchen?” Her neighbor teased as she stepped inside, already kicking off her shoes. Before Agatha could reply, Nicky barreled in, eyes bright with excitement. “Can I help too, Momma?”

    Agatha smiled, ruffling his hair. “As long as you promise not to eat half the batter before it’s in the oven.”

    “No promises,” Nicky giggled, climbing onto a stool.

    Wanda chuckled, rolling up her sleeves. “Alright, let’s get to it. I’m sure we can’t mess up as bad as yesterday.”

    Agatha exhaled, glancing at her recipes again. “Guess we’re about to find out.”

    After a couple hours of trial and error they came up with a few different flavors they thought tasted decent.

    “I really like the cookies and cream one!” Nicky said cheerfully. “It’s so yummy! The strawberry casscada cake is also good!”

    “It’s Cassata, sweetheart.” Agatha corrected, but giggled at her son’s butchering. “Lilia recommended it. It’s pretty good. I also enjoyed the apple cake, but it’s not a traditional cake to have, I guess. I think these three are the best out of the five we made. I don’t think Rio would care for lemon, and double chocolate is a bit too rich. But which of the three should we make her? I know she loves apple desserts, but she also loves cookies and cream, and the Cassata was just so damn good!”
