    Bringing both mothers relief, especially Agatha.

    Rio quickly handed the baby to Agatha, both of them were immediately overwhelmed by comfort and love.

    Agatha couldn’t contain herself when she saw the baby’s sex. “Looks like you were right, baby. She’s a girl. What are we going to name her?” Rio felt like she was going to cry, completely overwhelmed as she took in her two loves.

    Both women gasped when the baby’s eyes fluttered open. They were as blue as Agatha’s.

    “She has your eyes,” Rio whispered. “Your beautiful eyes.” Her gaze drifted to the field of purple daisies blooming beside them. All she could think of was Agatha.

    “Daisy,” Rio muttered.

    “Huh?” Agatha glanced up at her.

    “Daisy Harkness.” Rio gently wrapped her t-shirt around the baby. “Is that okay? Do you like that name?”

    Agatha nodded, teary-eyed. “I love it. Daisy.” She looked down at the infant in her arms and smiled. “Our Daisy.”

    “Our sweet little girl! We finally have you! I can’t believe—” Agatha cried out again.

    “Agatha!?”

    “Take her,” Agatha groaned in pain.

    “What’s wrong!?”

    “Rio! Take her!”

    Rio did but didn’t understand why until—

    “There’s another one!” Agatha cried.

    “Huh!?” Rio sat back and looked between her legs, her eyes went wide when she saw another head crowning.

    “There’s another baby, Rio!”

    “What!?”

    Chapter End Notes I know this one was on the shorter side. But I wanted to split it in half and leave it on a bit of a cliffhanger. But I’m sure you all saw it coming:) let me know what you think! I love your comments!

    Chapter 20: My sweet Rio!

    Chapter Summary Continuation of the last chapter right after Agatha gives birth. Chapter Notes Please check out notes at end See the end of the chapter for more notes Rio grabbed the baby from Agatha. When she sat back, she was shocked to see another head crowning.

    “There’s another baby!” Agatha cried out.

    “What!?”

    “Rio, please! Get them out!”

    With shaky hands Rio laid their crying baby down, before reaching forward. A-another…

    T-twins!?

    “Push, Agatha!”

    Agatha cried out again before pushing. “You did this to me!” She shouted. “Argh!!! Rio! Get them out, now!”

    “I’m here! I’ve got you!” Rio didn’t know what to say. She just wished she could take all of her lover’s pain away.

    Fortunately, it wasn’t as long as the first round.

    For the second time that afternoon she birthed another infant—this one much smaller than the first.

    Rio’s eyes were wide as she cut the cord, it was different this time. The baby didn’t cry, move, or even breathe.

    She rubbed their little chest, trying to get them to cry. “Come on.”

    “Rio?” Agatha’s voice shook with worry.

    “Hold on, honey. Everything is alright.”

    “Why aren’t they crying!?”

    The pain in Agatha’s voice broke Rio’s heart.

    “I’m working on it, my love.” She kept rubbing their chest, and when it didn’t work, she blew gently on their face—until finally… The sound of a baby wailing pierced the air. Their tiny arms flailed as they took their first breath.

    Both mothers let out a sigh of relief.

    “A boy.” Rio smiled. She handed the small infant to Agatha. “I guess we were both right, my love.”

    Agatha took their baby boy and kissed his little face. “Oh, my sweet heart. I’m so happy to hear your little cries. You’re breathing! You’re okay!” His eyes fluttered open, revealing a beautiful shade of brown. He looked just like Rio, but with brown hair like her own.

    She stared at him for a moment. So enraptured by his likeness. “Rio…”

    “Yes?”

    “No. That’s his name. Rio.” She looked up at the love of her life. Rio’s eyes widened. “A-are you sure? I mean what if he’s actually…” “Then I will love him or her, just as much as I love his Mommy! Regardless, these are my babies! Our babies! He looks so much like you, my love! How can I not name him after the person I am so in love with?” She held him up so Rio could see his face. “He’s perfect. They’re both perfect.”

    “He’s beautiful!” Rio took him in her arms and kissed him. “We’ll treasure them.” She grabbed Daisy and held both infants close to her chest. Agatha took a mental picture. The only thing that could make this better would be having Nicky here. But it’s probably a good thing he wasn’t. “You don’t think there’s a third do you?” Rio joked with a hint of worry. Agatha chuckled. “Thankfully it was just the two.” Her chuckle was interrupted by a groan. “B-but maybe a hospital would be nice.” Rio frowned at her whimpering. She handed Agatha the babies, hoping their presence would comfort her, it seemed to help at least.

    She looked around, making sure there were no animals insight, she tightened her grip on her knife before relaxing at the sound of her babies cooing. She turned back to them and felt her heart melt.

    Agatha laid there with her eyes shut, smiling. Holding both twins to her chest.

    Rio took a breath and lowered Agatha’s dress. She glanced down, her heart fluttered when she noticed her phone was getting a bar. She grabbed it quickly, dialed emergency services and prattled off their location over and over again. Stating her girlfriend just gave birth and they needed help.

    When she was done she moved so she was protectively hovering over her fiancé and infants. Shielding them from any potentially threats around them. She caressed Agatha’s face, gazing lovingly at her. “You did amazing, baby. I’m so proud of you.” She sniffled as her tears came to her eyes. “Just hold on, help is on the way. I’ve got you. I’ve got all three of you, you’ll be okay. You’re safe.”

    Agatha’s smile widened.

    “I need to get you to the truck, at the very least. You shouldn’t be out here like this. Or the babies.”

    Agatha whimpered at the idea but she knew she didn’t have much of a choice. “Oh, I’m not going to like this.”

    Rio frowned. “I’ll try to be gentle. Hold on tight to the babies.” Agatha nodded. “Okay, I’m re—“ she sucked in a painful breath when Rio lifted her off the ground.

    “I know, honey. I’m sorry. Do you want me to walk fast or go slow?“ Agatha wasn’t sure. On one hand they’d get to the truck quicker and get this over with. On the other it sounded like a lot of movement that would rattle her tired and pained body around.

    She sighed, “Slow, I don’t want to startle the babies.”

    “Okay, let’s get you three to the truck.”

    The trek back wasn’t long, but considering Agatha had just given birth and was holding two fussy newborns, it felt like a lifetime.

    “Okay, I’m going to lay you in the back.” Rio managed to open the door and gently settle Agatha and the twins down in the back seat before climbing in beside them and closing the door. She reached over to start the ignition, turning on the fan in hopes of cooling off her fiancé and their babies. She glanced out the windshield before turning back to Agatha. “Okay, help should be here soon. Just h—” Rio stopped.

    Agatha had shut her eyes, looking at peace, it brought a smile to Rio’s face. The babies even followed suit, relaxing against their Momma. Eventually, Agatha drifted off. The last thing she heard was her babies relaxed breathing and Rio telling her how much she loved them.

    Agatha tossed and turned as she gained a bit of consciousness. She could see light at the back of her eyelids and groaned, squeezing them tighter. She attempted to shift her body but failed.

    Why was she in pain?

    More awareness slipped in.

    She felt warmth of soft skin, that wasn’t her own, against her palm. It was a welcoming warmth.

    Familiar.

    And safe.

    She grasped it.

    It felt like home.

    She heard a soft gasp, and the grip on her hand tightened. Then gentle kisses were scattered across the back of her hand. “Aggie?”

    The voice was quiet and tired.

    She immediately recognized it.

    Rio.

    “Rio…” she breathed out, her eyes fluttered open.

    The first thing she saw were happy, exhausted brown eyes—eyes she’d fallen deeply in love with over the past year.

    The same brown eyes that had haunted her subconscious for the last twelve years. The very ones that looked back at her when she looked at her loving son and—

    Her eyes widened and she sat up quickly.

    “The babies! Ugh!” she groaned in pain.

    Rio panicked and gently nudged her to lie back down.

    “Agatha, it’s okay. We’re at a hospital. They’re alright. They’re being cleaned and looked over. And you just gave birth to two babies without any medical aid—you need to take it easy.”

    It took her a moment, but after catching her breath Agatha nodded and relaxed.

    “And Nicky?”

    “He’s on his way. Wanda’s bringing him. Lilia and Hela are also on their way.”

    “Okay.” She sighed, easing her body into the bed. “You look tired.” Rio offered a small smile. “I couldn’t sleep. Not until I knew you were okay.”

    Agatha let out a soft breath. “You should sleep.”

    Rio shook her head. “I’ll be okay. I promise. I’ll take a nap after we get time with the babies.”

    Agatha wanted to argue, but she knew how important this was to Rio. So instead, she simply nodded. “You’re my hero, Rio. My perfect partner.” She lifted her hand, eyes flicking to her engagement and promise ring. “I’m so happy you’ll be my forever. I love you.” Lowering her hand, she took in her love with a soft gaze. “I’m so happy.”

    Rio’s smile brightened. “I’m happy too, so, so happy! I can’t wait to spend every second with you and our babies.”

    Ten minutes later, Wanda arrived with Nicky.

    “Momma!” Nicky cried, his feet speeding up as he charged straight for Agatha’s bed, not slowing down.

    Rio reacted fast, springing her arms out and catching him before he could pounce on his other mother. “Easy, buddy. Momma’s gonna be okay, but she’s been through a lot. You don’t want to accidentally hurt her, do you?” Nicky shook his head, while letting out a sniffle, then turned toward his Momma. “Momma! Are you in pain? I can’t believe you had the baby outside! I was so worried!”

    Agatha lifted a brow, glancing at Rio, who simply shrugged, then looked back to her boy. “Nicky, honey, come to Momma.” She opened her arms. Nicky turned to Rio, silently asking for permission.

    Rio smiled and nodded. “Be gentle. You can hug her, but don’t lay on her.” He nodded back then carefully climbed into the hospital bed with Agatha. “Momma’s okay. It was a surprise.” She glanced up at Rio, then over at Wanda with a smile, then back down at her son. “Your Mommy was there the whole time and took such good care of me. She’s basically a doctor herself, you know?”

    That managed to get a laugh out of Rio.

    “Mommy Rio really took charge and made me feel calm and safe. I couldn’t have done it without her.” Agatha looked back up at Rio, smiling softly. Rio couldn’t help the tears that reached her eyes. “It was a surprise. In so many ways, not just being early.”

    Nicky turned, puzzled by his Mommy’s words.

    Agatha reached out, cupping her son’s chin and gently angling his face back toward her. “My darling boy… well, you have a brother.”

    Nicky’s eyes widened. “You were right, Momma!” He smiled at his Momma, but then froze and turned back to Rio. “I’m sorry you don’t have any girls, Mommy.”

    Before Rio could say a word, Wanda jumped in. “Oh, you have two boys! Just like me!”

    Agatha chuckled. “Nicky.” She spoke softly, needing his attention. “Your Mommy was right and so were you.”

    Nicky turned back, confusion clouding his face. “But I thought you said —” “It was a surprise because… we had twins. A girl and a boy.” Nicky froze, visibly stunned.

    Wanda gasped “What?! You’re serious?!” She blurted out.

    Both women nodded, smiling.

    “Believe me. It was a shock!” Rio laughed, almost breathless. “Two babies… I wasn’t expecting that one. Guess it explains why Agatha got so big and so quickly too!”

    “How’s that even possible? They missed it on the ultrasound?” Wanda asked perplexed.

    Rio shrugged. “Sometimes things just happen. They actually said Daisy must’ve been right in front of Junior. She’s a lot bigger than him—that didn’t help.”

    Wanda smirked. “Wait, what are their names?”

    Rio sighed playfully.

    Agatha chuckled. “So glad you asked. Rio named our sweet girl, Daisy.” “Because Daisy reminded me of Agatha—

    and she happened to be lying in a field of purple daisies. I just felt like a purple flower was the best combination of us. In that moment, nothing seemed more perfect than that name.”

    Wanda sighed dreamily. “And the little boy? You said Junior, right?” She perked up, eager to find out the origin of this newborns name. With a soft smile, Agatha said, “Rio. I named him Rio. Because he’s perfect, just the way he is—no matter who he becomes.”

    Rio’s heart warmed all over again at hearing Agatha’s touching words.

    It hadn’t taken long for the other two women to arrive. The duo filled the room with questions of their own, but were unable to receive any answers from the two mothers, as the doctor had just arrived shortly after them. “Ms. Harkness, Ms. Vidal.” He nodded at them, then smiled over at Nicky. “You are the proud mothers of two healthy babies.”

    The room let out a collective sigh of relief, with added gasps from Hela and Lilia, who for once didn’t see that coming.

    “Daisy is cleared to go home in a week. She’s a good weight for being a month premature, but we need to keep Rio jr for at least two weeks to make sure there are no complications.”

    Rio noticed Agatha’s relieved expression falter, so she stepped in to speak. “But I thought you said they were both healthy?”

    The doctor turned toward Rio. “Yes, they are. But it’s a precaution we take with underweight babies — on top of the fact that he’s also premature. He’s much smaller than his sister. Small enough that he wasn’t detected on the ultrasound. He’s going to be great at hide-and-seek.” The doctor chuckled, making a small joke to lighten the mood.

    Agatha still looked worried, so the doctor offered more reassurance. “We just need to ensure they’re developing well. We’ll have them sleep in incubators, and you’ll be moved to a larger room to accommodate your family.”

    Rio nodded quickly. “What about Agatha?”

    “Yes, she’ll be cleared for release in 48 hours, but after that, we don’t expect you to leave just yet — at least not until both of your babies are discharged.”

    Both women nodded. “Thank you, Doctor.”

    The nurses smiled warmly and carefully handed Agatha the babies. She softly gasped as she cradled them in her arms.

    Nicky couldn’t contain his excitement. “Aw, they’re so small — especially that one!” He pointed to Rio Jr.

    “That’s your little brother, Nicky,” Agatha said with a happy giggle, tears welling up as she gazed at his tiny face. Then she turned toward Daisy. “And this… this is your sister, Daisy.”

    The doctor excused himself, and the nurses followed, giving the couple privacy with their babies and friends.

    Hela made her way over to Rio and whispered in her ear, “Well jeez, Rio, you knocked her up so hard two of your swimmers made it to the finish line.”

    Rio elbowed her in the side and muttered, “Do I need to have Alice muzzle you and Jen tie you up?”

    Hela sighed dreamily. “Oh, that would be a great gift idea.” She patted Rio on the back. “Seriously though, congrats. You’ve made a very happy woman out of Agatha — and I can see it in your eyes that you’re on cloud nine yourself. I’m proud of you, sis. I really am.”

    Rio smiled. “Thanks, sis.” She turned back toward her fiancé. Oh, that’s right. She hadn’t told anybody yet.

    But that was okay. It could stay between them a little while longer. Someone would probably bring it up once they noticed their rings. For now, she just wanted to focus on her family.

    Agatha turned toward Rio, looking exhausted but so, so happy. She didn’t need to say anything; Rio already knew.

    She approached, leaned down, and kissed both babies on their heads, then kissed Agatha.

    “My family. My sweet, little family. All mine.” Rio held back her tears and reached out to pull Nicky in at her side, kissing his head too. “I love all of my babies.” She hugged him tight. “All three of you.”

    “And Scratch, Matilda, and the kitties?” Nicky asked, which made everyone in the room laugh.

    “Yes, I love them too.”

    Self-Esteem, something Agatha couldn’t seem to hold onto lately.

    She stood in her bedroom, staring at her reflection in the floor-length mirror —taking in the stark changes to her face and body.

    Had she gotten a couple more wrinkles on her skin?

    She lifted her hand to the crow’s feet beside her eyes. They had deepened quite a bit in the last three months. As well as the laugh lines beside her mouth. She sighed, dropping her hand. Her gaze shifted lower. She closed her eyes and took a breath before pulling up her shirt, chancing a glance. She frowned.

    Pink stretch marks and sagging skin stared back at her.

    Her belly had stretched so much since her second pregnancy, the old, silvery faded marks were now replaced with fresher, deeper ones. It made sense—this pregnancy had wreaked havoc on her body. It hadn’t helped that she wasn’t exactly the ideal age for getting knocked up. And she’d had twins for god’s sake.

    Her lip quivered at the sight.

    To add salt to the wound, she’d been wanting to be intimate with Rio for weeks.

    Several months had gone by in the blink of an eye, and all throughout, Rio had been ridiculously perfect for all three of them. Taking charge with the babies and their eldest son.

    Plus…

    Taking care of her in the process.

    And yes, as expected, it had taken time for her libido to come back—not to mention the healing. And yet, Agatha didn’t dare bring it up, and Rio was sweet enough not to push. They’d both been too busy with the babies anyway.

    Even still, Agatha couldn’t help but wonder if maybe—

    Tears pricked at her eyes as her brain dared to think that maybe… Maybe Rio didn’t—

    No!

    She yanked her shirt back down over her postpartum belly and turned away from the mirror.

    This was ridiculous.

    Rio wasn’t like that.

    She’d never.

    Agatha’s gaze drifted to their neatly made bed. Rio had made it for them that morning, even though she was busy planning the reopening of her business— while helping juggle the twins.

    Her thoughts drifted again.

    Turning chaotic.

    Her logic and fear were at war with one another, like a tornado running rampant in her brain and heart.

    Her confidence had long since plummeted—along with her energy. But she wouldn’t let Rio know. They needed to focus on the babies, and their twelve-year-old son. Agatha couldn’t afford to be selfish over such ridiculous thoughts.

    She shook the painful feelings away and took a few steps forward. But as she moved, the ache between her legs returned.

    It had been hard.

    Her hormones were still all over the place.

    Her body craved her partner.

    Craved to be held.

    To be loved.

    She just wanted Rio’s touch.

    She needed her close.

    Agatha groaned, mustering enough will to ignore it and pick up the basket of laundry from the floor. She should fold these clothes, then— “WAAAAAAAHHHH!”

    The sound of a baby wailing through the monitor cut through her thoughts. She quickly set the basket down and booked it to the nursery. Laundry would have to wait.

    She was so behind on chores today. She hoped Rio would be home with Nicky from basketball practice soon.

    Hours flew by.

    She rocked one baby in her arms while breastfeeding the other. Her body began to tilt to the side. Her eyes felt heavy. She was losing the strength to stand.

    Her stomach growled with a hunger that hadn’t been satisfied since breakfast, and it was already pushing 4:30.

    To top it off breastfeeding on an empty stomach made the hunger pains hit faster.

    She felt light-headed, nauseous. But it didn’t matter. She pushed through it. Her babies were having a rough day. She needed to help them get through the thick of it.

    She sat Daisy down and sighed.

    Another thirty minutes passed…

    Finally, Rio Jr. fell asleep, unlatching from her nipple. Daisy still fussed in the crib, upset over god knows what.

    Agatha gently laid Jr. in his crib and hurried back to tend to Daisy. “Shhh, Momma’s here. I got you. Everything’s okay, my sweet girl.” She was so tired… she hadn’t noticed the figure standing in the doorway. Not until she felt arms slip around her waist and lips press against her neck. “You’re working too hard. You need rest. Let me take over.” “No, I’m fine. It’s okay. You should relax—you were out all day and—” “Agatha.”

    Rio’s stern voice cut her off. Agatha sighed, then turned, meeting her lover’s gaze.

    The older woman caressed her tired fiancé’s face, swiping her thumb gently across her cheek. “You could’ve called me. I would’ve come home sooner. I was just helping out—it’s not like I needed to be there the whole five hours.”

    Agatha shook her head. “You haven’t had a moment to spend with Nicky, let alone yourself. I can handle them on my own.”

    Rio sighed, taking Agatha’s hands in hers. “Baby, look at you. You’re so tired. I’m here to help. We’re a team.”

    Agatha turned away, avoiding her gaze.

    “Lately it hasn’t felt that way.”

    Rio blinked fast—her face fell, panic and doubt for herself set in. “H-have I not been helping enough? I’m sorry! Am I not doing this right? I’m sorry, Agatha—what can I do to he—”

    Agatha’s turned back so fast, her eyes wide. “Rio, no! That’s not—baby, you’ve been taking on so much by yourself. You’ve been nothing but supportive and amazing and perfect! I just want you to have a break, that’s all.”

    Rio let out a sigh of relief. “That’s it? Okay.” She composed herself before reaching out and tucking a strand of hair behind Agatha’s ear. “I don’t think you understand how much I want to be involved. How much I want to help you. You need me. I’m strong. I’ve got the energy to do this. I promise I’m okay. I’m…” She grinned. “…the father of this family. I need to be strong.” Agatha didn’t know what to say. She muttered something under her breath and dropped Rio’s hand, eyes falling to the floor.

    “Huh?” Rio couldn’t hear her, and she didn’t understand the sudden mood shift.

    “I…” Agatha looked back up. “I don’t want you to run yourself ragged, Rio. I’m scared.”

    “Why? Baby, I’m here—for you, for the babies, for Nicky.” “That’s just it! I’m scared you’ll grow to resent me and them. You have less time for yourself. You’ve been on baby duty nonstop. Aren’t you…” Her voice dropped, nervous and fearful, “…sick of it?”

    Rio’s face fell, she crossed her arms and scoffed. “No! Absolutely not! All four of you—you’re my family! It’s my duty as a parent and partner to be there, supporting you 110%. You did most of the work growing these babies. You birthed them. For godsake, you raised our sweet boy for so long, all by yourself. This has been the greatest year of my life, Agatha, and it keeps getting better. Every morning I get to wake up next to you! Every day, every moment I spend with our babies—it’s the greatest gift I’ve ever been given. I’ll never get sick of this. You’re all mine, and I’ll damn well make sure you’re taken care of.”

    Agatha mentally fanned herself off, while holding herself back from kissing Rio to death.

    Soft cooing sounds caught Rio’s attention. She glanced down then smiled at Daisy. “Aww, she must’ve missed my voice. She’s out like a light.” She reached down to caress her daughter’s face. “My sweet little flower,” she murmured, running her fingers along her soft cheek.

    “Are you kidding me? She’s been fighting me for hours! And you just…” Agatha threw her hands up in the air, groaning. “Clearly, she has a favorite.”

    “Oh, stop. I’m sure she’s just being stubborn,” Rio glanced back at her fiancé. “Like you.” She chuckled, reaching up to pinch Agatha’s cheek. The younger woman flinched.

    “Ow!”

    “Stubborn—but pretty.” Rio added.

    “Wow. Thanks.” Agatha muttered.

    Rio smiled and leaned in to peck her lips. “Let’s lay you down, shall we?” “Huh?”

    “You need a nap. Before dinner. Then afterward I’ll run you a bath. Sound good?”

    “You spoil me.”

    Rio grinned.

    “I know.”

    Agatha watched with bated breath as Rio worked hastily to set up her bath. She hadn’t undressed in front of her since before giving birth. Should she now?

    “Okay, I think that’s the perfect temp. It’s hot to me, meaning it’s warm for you!” She turned and smiled. “Want me to get you a book? Or a candle? Anything, really.”

    Agatha shrugged. “This is plenty. Thank you, Rio.”

    Rio gave her nod, then stood up, taking her leave. “Enjoy, my sweet.” She gave her a chaste kiss against her hair then headed for the door. Agatha continued staring down at the bath as she waited for the sound of the door clicking. Then she began undressing.

    She glanced at the mirror above the sink and sighed again. Maybe… she should…

    “Rio?”

    Agatha called out to her girlfriend. She cursed herself for her sudden bluntness.

    “Yes?”

    She heard Rio’s voice through the door.

    Agatha couldn’t help but chuckle softly at that. Expecting maybe she’d peak her head in through the door, but no.

    “I love you so much, thank you for the bath.”

    There was a moment of silence before a response.

    “Of course, my love. Anything for you. I hope you relax, I’m gonna go help Nicky with his math homework. Enjoy.”

    Agatha sighed then nodded to herself as she heard Rio’s footsteps fade into the distance.

    Not yet.

    Another few days passed. Rio was working hard, bouncing Jr in her arm while trying to figure out new interior designs for her upcoming funeral home location.

    With her cell phone propped between her cheek and shoulder, she had a funny look on her face as she stared at her laptop.

    “I’m not sure I like the look of the wood design. Maybe a different color? Also, were we going to do something a bit different for the chapel? I’m not sure what you wanted, Hel’s—considering that’s your department. Should we plan that aspect when we can meet up in person? I’m still stressing over the equipment for my prep room, and I planned on having it in the basement. I like this fixture here for the viewing area—what do you think?” Agatha sipped her coffee as she walked past Rio. She hadn’t meant to eavesdrop, but something in Rio’s words caught her attention. Curious, she paused, backed up, and glanced over her shoulder—just in time to sneak a peek at an intricate, gothic-looking chandelier on Rio’s screen. “That’s gorgeous!”

    Rio jumped, startled. She hadn’t realized Agatha was there. Her eyes widened as she turned, trying to catch her breath.

    Agatha wore an amused expression, though she felt a little bad for startling her. “Sorry. Didn’t mean to sneak up on you.”

    Rio lifted a brow, her breathing evening out as she smiled. “That’s my job, amor.”

    Agatha chuckled. She glanced down at Jr. and smiled. “Someone’s tuckered out.”

    Rio looked down at the peacefully sleeping infant in her arms. “I suppose you’re right. I should put him down so he can nap. Little cutie pie.” “I know he is. He has your face, after all. How could he be anything but cute?”

    Rio blushed. “Stop it! Hela can hear!”

    Her face turned even redder as giggles erupted on the other end of her phone.

    “Bye Hels!” Rio hung up immediately then stood. “Alright, come on.” Agatha couldn’t help but giggle at her lover’s flustered state, but followed her nonetheless.

    They retreated upstairs.

    Rio laid the sleeping boy down in his personal crib beside his sisters, while Agatha watched lovingly.

    Who knew that at forty she’d be the mother of an infant—and twin infants, to boot! Not to mention engaged! She held up her hand and gazed at her beautiful engagement ring, nestled just above her promise ring, and softly gasped at the dreamy sight.

    To top it off, the proposal had been perfect. Though, she felt a little bad for going into labor practically right after.

    But again, Rio was just perfect and—

    She noticed Rio not moving and lowered her hand so her eyes could focus on her.

    The older woman was gazing over at her and smiling.

    “Hi, you.” Rio tilted her head, her smile softened.

    Agatha couldn’t help but admire the sun beaming through the blinds and curtains behind Rio’s head practically encasing her in a halo of light. Little did she know the same light was making her own eyes sparkle back at Rio. Enchanting the other woman right in her very spot.

    “Hi.” Agatha replied simply with a small chuckle and smile of her own. A beat of silence.

    Then…

    “You’re beautiful, Agatha.”

    Agatha’s smile faltered for a moment. She felt her cheeks flush and she lightly gasped. She didn’t know what to say. She looked down shyly for moment before looking back up and meeting her lover’s gaze. “Have you looked in a mirror, angel? You’re practically glowing.” Rio’s smile brightened. Her brown eyes shimmered as she beamed with happiness at Agatha’s words. “You’re a sweet talker aren’t you?” Agatha smirked, she approached Rio and reached out, taking her in by her waist and wrapping her arms around her. “For you, my breathtaking woman, always.”

    Rio bit her lip and leaned down slowly, giving Agatha time to pull away. Their lips were inches apart. Agatha felt her breath stutter and her heart pound—then finally, Rio’s lips were on hers. They were as sweet as she remembered, and just as soft.

    Rio was gentle and unhurried, taking her time, just being there with Agatha. When she finally pulled away, she brushed her hand through Agatha’s hair, grinning like an idiot.

    Agatha sighed dreamily.

    Rio could get lost in her eyes forever.

    “So I was wondering if—“ “WAAAAAAAAH!”

    Both women jumped as they were startled, they looked down to see Daisy wailing, they jumped into action, trying to get her to stop before she woke up Jr.

    “Well I guess my voice isn’t as soothing as I thought.” Rio joked. Agatha merely sighed at the poorly timed interruption, before speaking. “Your voice is soothing to me, I promise. Daisy’s just cranky.”

    Another week gone by in the blink of an eye.

    Still nothing…

    The events in the nursery replayed in Agatha’s mind over and over again. It was the closest they had been to intimacy in months.

    “Agatha?”

    She noticed movement in front of her and glanced up from her coffee, focusing on the concerned redhead across from her.

    “Oh, sorry, Wands. You were saying?”

    Wanda lifted a brow. “I… wasn’t saying anything. You mentioned Nicky was working on a science project and Rio had been helping him with it?” “Oh… yeah. That’s pretty much it. They’ve been busy on it for a month. It’s almost done, too! He did his project on tarantulas.” Agatha shivered at the thought. No matter how much she tried to get comfortable with Matilda, the spider still managed to send shivers up and down her spine. Her mind drifted back to Rio…

    “Are you okay?”

    Agatha blinked the thoughts away. “Yeah. Why wouldn’t I be?” “Lately I’ve just noticed your mind drifting. And now that I really look at you—you look exhausted.”

    “I know. I guess this pregnancy’s affected me more than I realized.” “And Rio? How’s she?”

    “Well, I can’t speak for her. But from what I can see, she’s been doing amazing. Sure, she gets tired when she pulls an all-nighter, but she doesn’t seem as affected as I’ve been. Mentally and physically speaking.” “Well, that would make sense. She didn’t carry and give birth to them. It’s a good thing you have a shit-ton of maternity leave.”

    Agatha let out an amused chuckle. “Trust me, if I didn’t, I’d be taking just as much time, regardless.”

    Agatha let out an amused chuckle. “Trust me, if I didn’t, I’d be taking just as much time, regardless.”

    Wanda nodded. She crossed her arms, lost in thought for a moment. “You said you’re exhausted—mentally and physically?”

    Agatha nodded.

    “How are you emotionally?”

    “Great,” Agatha answered a bit too quickly.

    Wanda lifted a brow. “Okay.” She grabbed her drink and took a sip. Agatha didn’t bother pretending she hadn’t caught the doubt in Wanda’s tone. “How couldn’t I be? Nicky’s doing great in school, the babies are thriving, and Rio’s been amazing.”

    Wanda nodded slowly. “That’s good,” she said, but there was a weight behind it—gentle, but edged with suspicion, like she was waiting for something Agatha wasn’t saying.

    “I am! I’m fantastic! You should see how good Rio’s been doing! She’s so helpful! Just the other day she made me breakfast in bed because I wasn’t feeling well. Then she went and got me my favorite chocolates. After that, she came back and took over baby duty.”

    Wanda nodded. “I never had a doubt Rio would be a great mommy. She’s a good woman.”

    Agatha sighed dreamily. “I know! I’m so lucky. I just love her.” They sat in silence for a moment before Wanda spoke again. “How’s the intimacy been?” she asked, setting her glass down.

    Agatha’s face reddened. “Oh… well… we… um… haven’t… since before the twins were born.”

    Wanda sighed. So this was the problem. “Is there a particular reason why? Have you just not gotten that feeling back yet, or…?”

    “Well… it’s not that…” Agatha trailed off, unsure of how to proceed. “It’s… y’know.” She muttered the rest under her breath. “After you have a baby, it can significantly alter a woman’s body, making her look much different. It’s not exactly nice to look at.”

    Wanda slammed her glass down, making Agatha jump.

    The redhead stood up, her voice booming with anger. “Do not tell me Rio is refusing to be intimate because of some loose skin and stretch marks! I swear to God, Agatha, I’ll march right over there and—”

    Agatha panicked, waving her hands in front of her. “No! It’s me, Wanda! I’m the one who’s uncomfortable! I haven’t even talked to Rio about it. She doesn’t know I’m feeling this way.”

    Wanda froze. The realization hit her, and she slowly took her seat. Clearing her throat, she spoke again. “I… apologize for my outburst and assumption. I shouldn’t have assumed the worst of Rio. But…” she took a breath. “Agatha, you’re beautiful and—”

    Agatha held up her hand. “Oh, please don’t even bother.”

    “I mean it! You’re beautiful, Agatha! I’m not just saying it. You need to talk to Rio about this.”

    “I—I don’t know, Wanda. I don’t want to, um… well…”

    Wanda crossed her arms. “You don’t want to what?”

    Agatha stuttered, trying to find the words.

    “Look, I’m not telling you to have sex right now. If you aren’t ready that’s your business, and hers. But you need to at least talk to her about this.” She gestured to her belly, but then paused for a moment. “It’s not just your image is it? You’re exhausted. You haven’t felt good about yourself as a whole?”

    “How’d you know?”

    “Because I’ve felt something similar after I had Billy.” Wanda reached out, placing a comforting hand on Agatha. “Look, Agatha you’re my best friend and I love you. As a friend I recommend talking to her. Do it how ever you feel most comfortable or… whatever. You just gotta make that first step.” Agatha began trembling. “I’ve just felt like I haven’t been giving enough. That Rio has been doing most the work and taking care of me and Nicky. I haven’t even had much time with him! She’s doing laps around me and yet I’m on the verge of passing out!”

    “Maybe…” Wanda snapped her fingers as an idea popped into her head. “Maybe you need a break. You two should go somewhere, alone. Somewhere romantic. Just the two of you.”

    Agatha’s eyes widened. “I can’t! I have to twin infants and a pre teen to look after! On top of my work that I do at home!”

    “And!” Wanda held out her arms. “You have friends!”

    “I… I don’t know, Wands. I don’t want to impose on anyone and… I’m not sure I’m ready to leave them.”

    Wanda took her hand, rubbing her thumb over her palm. “Agatha. I mean this in the nicest way. You need to get out of the house. It’s just a break, a couple days, just a weekend. Spend time alone, spend time with Rio. Nicky can basically take care of himself and I can watch the twins. I’m sure I can get the whole group to help me to.“ “You’re serious?”

    “Am I ever not serious?”

    Agatha huffed in defeat.

    “I’ll… talk to her.”

    Agatha waited until they were in bed to suggest it. Usually, they’d be doing their own things, but together.

    “So… I had a great time hanging out with Wanda today…”

    Rio glanced up from her book and smiled. “That’s great, honey. I’m glad.” Then she looked back down.

    “Yeah, we got to talking about motherhood and all that. The topic of stressors came up. She suggested it might be a good idea for us to… get away for a few days. Just you and me.”

    Rio looked up again, this time setting her book aside. “Oh yeah? What did you have in mind?”

    What did she have in mind?

    She hadn’t even gotten that far!

    “Oh… maybe… I don’t know…” She pondered on it for a moment. “Maybe a cabin? Somewhere to relax for a weekend?”

    Rio sat up, excited at the mere mention, her whole face lighting up. “Oh my gosh! Agatha! That sounds like so much fun! A weekend getaway together sounds perfect!”

    Agatha smiled at her lover’s excitement and sighed—she couldn’t possibly say no now.

    “Yeah?”

    Rio couldn’t help but squeal with excitement.

    “Yeah!”

    So they booked a gorgeous cabin a few hours away for the following weekend.

    Agatha had been beside herself about leaving her babies.

    “Maybe we should reschedule!? It might be too early for me to leave them,” She spoke quickly, reaching out for one of the twins in Wanda’s arms. Before she could move so much as an inch, Rio was grabbing her wrists. “Babe, they’ll be fine.”

    “But—”

    “Agatha.”

    “Rio…”

    The look of sadness and worry on Agatha’s face struck a chord with Rio, but she knew how good this would be for them both.

    Maybe breaking out her not-so-secret weapon would make things easier. Rio took a breath, pulled Agatha’s hands toward her body, hugging them close to her chest, before giving her The Face.

    “Please, baby. I’m so excited! I’ve been looking forward to this for two weeks. Please don’t cancel now.”

    Agatha struggled, trying to find the words.

    For an extra touch, Rio added, “You wouldn’t do that to me, would you?” Then she swayed side to side, to really sell it. “I really wanna have some alone time together. Just you and me.” Finally, she went in for the kill— pulling Agatha’s hands up to her face and nuzzling them against her cheek. “I’ll be so sad. This is all I want!”

    “But… what about…” Agatha struggled. Really struggled.

    “Agatha we need this! It’ll be so good for us both. You know it! We’ll be even better Mommas for our babies when we come back on Monday. If not for me, then do it for them.”

    That really got Agatha. Rio had a point, even still, it would help distress them and get them back in the swing of things. And… she’d do practically anything for Rio too. And absolutely anything for her children. “Okay, I’m sorry for being a pain.”

    Rio smiled softly the kissed her hands. “You have nothing to apologize for. Trust me, I’ll be missing them as much as you. But I also need a break. And time for us.” She leaned in, planting a reassuring kiss against Agatha’s cheek. “We’re gonna have such a nice time!”

    Agatha let out a sigh. “I’m trusting you Wanda. You said the group is coming over to help out?”

    Wanda nodded. “Oh yeah, we’re all going to have a great time! Isn’t that right Nicky?”

    The little boy glanced up from his board game with Tommy. “Huh? Oh, yeah! Auntie Hela is gonna play video games with us and we’re all gonna watch that new super spider bat movie! Auntie Alice is also bringing pizza!”

    “Well I guess you’re all set then.” Rio put her hands on her hips then pulled Agatha in to her side. “Nicky have fun buddy, and don’t give Wanda a hard time.” She flashed him a mischievous wink, pulling a giggle from the boy. “Okay Mommy. Don’t give Momma a hard time either! Bring me back a souvenir?”

    Rio nodded. “Oh I promise! I’ll get you something super cool!” Agatha groaned, pressing her face into Rio’s neck. This whole thing was just so hard!

    “I better get this one out on the road before she changes her mind.” Rio chuckled. “Thanks again Wanda. Tell the group I said thanks as well and we’ll be back Monday morning.”

    Wanda waved at the couple as they made their way out to Agatha’s SUV. “Awe, they’re my favorite couple.” Wanda giggled then looked down at the twin babies in her arms and lit up at the smiling faces. “Well I’m going to have so much fun hanging out with you two! Yes I am!”

    Rio led Agatha to the SUV with a reassuring hand on her back. “I promise they’ll be okay. It’ll be good for them too. Trust me, okay babe? We’re gonna have a great time together.”

    Agatha nodded and sighed. “I know.”

    “And hey! Now we’ll be able to catch up on those movies you’d been wanting to watch together!”

    Agatha smiled while getting in the passenger seat. “That does sound like fun.”

    Chapter 21: Will you still love me, when I’m no

    longer, young and beautiful!?

    Chapter Summary Agatha and Rio have their much needed getaway together.

    Chapter Notes Please read notes at end:)

    See the end of the chapter for more notes It took them a while to reach the exact location of their cabin. After a few hours on the road, a couple of restroom breaks and switching seats, they finally arrived at the cabin—tucked away in the woods, at the end of a long, winding road.

    “Wow! Babe! I didn’t realize you rented something like this!” Rio couldn’t believe her eyes as she took in the large log cabin. “It’s so pretty!” She looked over at her fiance in the drivers seat, beaming. “This is gonna be awesome!” Then she looked back at the cabin they’d be staying for the next three days.

    Agatha couldn’t help the smile that creeped onto her face at her lover’s excited reaction.

    The older woman was the first to bolt out of the SUV the second Agatha put it in park. She couldn’t wait any longer. She needed to get a look inside. She let out a squeal as she burst through the front door into the large spacious living area.

    “Wow!”

    She spotted a large comfy couch and couldn’t help herself. After a few hours of driving she couldn’t deny herself the comfort of lovely, high quality furniture. She flung herself onto it, pulling a throw pillow to her chest, enjoying the beautiful walls adorned with different paintings of wilderness animals and woodland views.

    “Oh! Wow!”

    Agatha crossed her arms while leaning up against the frame of the door, smirking at her love’s antics.

    “Like it?”

    Rio nodded, still taking it all in. “It’s amazing! I’ve never been inside one of these before!”

    Agatha softened. She was still so happy she could give Rio some firsts.

    A couple hours flew by, of them lounging and enjoying the view from the large window as the sun began to set.

    “Hear that?”

    Rio glanced over at Agatha who was across the room by the open window, Rio lifted a brow at the younger woman’s question. “No…? I don’t hear anything.” Rio paused for a moment to really listen. “Except for the crickets.”

    Agatha smirked. “Exactly!”

    She strode over and plopped herself down right beside her lover. “No cars! No distant sounds of neighbors, and no… sounds of infants crying.”

    Rio nodded then Agatha took Rio’s hands in her own.

    “It’s just us. Just you, me and nature.”

    “You mean I’m stuck in the middle of nowhere for three days with no one but you to keep me company?” Rio affectionately booped Agatha’s nose as she spoke with dramatic sarcasm. “How will I ever survive!?” Agatha snickered. “How indeed…” then she smirked and arched her brow. She walked her fingers over Rio’s hand, up her arm flirtatiously, while keeping eye contact. A look of pure mischief had overtaken her features and she gazed at Rio like she’d been starving for days.

    “There’s something I’ve just been dying to do.”

    Rios chest rose and fell a bit quicker as her eyes glanced at Agatha’s wandering hand and then back up to her hungry blue eyes, her brown were being overtaken by her pupils expanding, focusing on this woman in front of her. “Yeah?”

    Agatha slipped a strand of Rio’s hair behind her ear while nodding. “Oh yeah. You know what that is, baby?”

    Rio‘a breath hitched, “What?”

    Agatha slipped her other hand between them, catching Rio by surprise with what she was holding.

    “Kick your ass in Mario kart.” Her grin returned full force as she held up the purple and green joy-cons. “And I think I’m picking a certain green character.”

    Brown eyes widened. “No… not my Yoshi.”

    Agatha nodded. “Oh yeah, otherwise…” she leaned in, her lips ghosting over Rio’s ear. “You’ll have to beat me to it.”

    Neither of them made a move at first—you could hear a pin drop between them—until one of them twitched, and Rio suddenly tried to snatch the controller from Agatha.

    “Haha, too slow!” Agatha moved her body back, holding her arm away as her girlfriend tried snatching the little purple controller from her. “Are you really playing keep away? From moi!?”

    Agatha giggled, leaning her body back even more, Rio was laying on her at this point, focused on getting a controller to have a chance to get her favorite character.

    It finally dawned on Agatha of their position, causing her cheeks to flush. Her hands stopped in their avoidance of prying hands, at the rush of wetness to her core distracting her for a moment, allowing Rio a chance to grab one of the controllers.

    “Yes!” She sat back fast, holding the purple controller to her chest like it was a prized possession. “I win!”

    Suddenly Agatha was pulled back into their playful banter and she shook her head. “I’m afraid not, my love. Not until one of us gets the mean, green, driving machine!” She sprung off the couch toward her bag where she had stored Rio’s switch. The older woman had followed after her and was on her tail, grabbing at her back, trying to keep her from getting the device, and in the process pulling giggles from Agatha. “Hey, that’s cheating!” Rio shook her head and reached out for Agatha’s bag. “Alls fair in love and war, my darling! And This. Is. War!”

    After a minute of struggle the two ended up on the floor giggling and laughing in each others arms. Agatha looked down, surprised that Rio had ended up on the bottom. “How’d you…”

    “Didn’t want you to get hurt. You’re always welcome to land on me!” For some reason Agatha found the statement to be hilarious and her giggling turned into a full on fit of laughter.

    Rio was going to join her until a growling sound caught them off guard. Agatha’s cheeks flushed again, but with embarrassment this time. “Awe babe! Are you hungry?” Rio sat up, bringing Agatha with her. The younger woman hid her face in the crook of her lovers neck, hiding from the shame and embarrassment of her stomach growling.

    “I… I guess so.”

    Rio smiled, and rubbed her back. “Now that I think about it, I’m pretty hungry too. Why don’t we get started on dinner? Get some food in our bellies. What do you say?”

    Agatha took a moment then sighed. “What about the game? I was looking forward to beating you!”

    Rio chuckled. “Aw we can do it after we eat! I promise!” Agatha tightened her arms around Rio, feeling strangely clingy in that moment. She just missed being physically and emotionally close—and being on her lap, in her arms… it just felt so right. “Okay. Spaghetti and salad sound good?”

    “It sounds perfect.”

    The two got to work on dinner, chatting about activities they wanted to plan for the family and how Nicky was progressing in school, at some point they ran out of things to talk about and just savored the sounds of crickets, enjoying the comfortable silence between them.

    The room grew a bit colder, it distracted Rio, so Agatha worked on finishing up the cooking while she looked around trying to find its source. She felt a shiver run up her spine from the direct chill coming from one of the cracked windows. “Oh you are so getting shut!” She muttered before closing it.

    Though, the little chill reminded her it was going to be cold tonight, so with that thought in mind she turned and glanced over at the fire place. “Hm…” she walked over and glanced around, fiddling with it, until she found a fancy little remote she assumed went to it. She pressed the large red button igniting the fireplace. “Ah-ha! We have fire!”

    “Look at you, been out here for a couple hours and you’ve already made fire! Thinking like a true camper!”

    Rio cracked a grin and turned facing Agatha who was on the other side of the room. “Oh yeah. I’m a total Boy Scout! Got my badge for starting fires when I was only ten!”

    Agatha chuckled. “Boy Scouts huh?”

    “Well… no. Unfortunately. I was in Girl Scouts. And while the gender shouldn’t matter it was the subjects and activities that I disliked. I would have rather been in the woods, catching fish and tying knots… hell even helping old ladies cross the street would have been great! But nope! I was selling cookies, and learning how to handle my complex female emotions.”

    Agatha scoffed. “I’m sure my mother would have enjoyed me being a Girl Scout.”

    Rio smiled. “You would have looked so cute in those uniforms! Like a little doll, I bet!”

    Agatha rolled her eyes. “Okay, goofball.” She waved her over. “Come on, foods ready.”

    With a skip in her step Rio made her way over to help set out plates and cups.

    “I bet you’d look cute in one of those Boy Scout uniforms. I can see it.” Agatha snickered. “I should have Nicky join, maybe you could volunteer?” Rio nodded. “Oh! I would love that!”

    A few minutes passed and they were finally eating dinner at the large wooden table, beside the hearth, enjoying each other’s company. They continued conversing about random subjects, enjoying the other’s company. After a few minutes they fell into a comfortable silence, again.

    Rio was lost in her head, glancing around the cabin, enjoying their moment together. Then she glanced back over at Agatha who was enjoying her meal. Something shifted… nothing about Agatha’s appearance changed, but watching her, just relaxing and enjoying herself… Rio just couldn’t keep her eyes off her.

    Her hair was extra wavy today, her eyes seemed to sparkle just a little more in that moment and her skin was practically glowing. She looked positively striking and Rio was enraptured.

    Agatha hadn’t even notice at first, but the moment she had, Rio realized what she was doing and forced herself to stop, she wasn’t going to push for anything. The moment on the couch was just playful and adorable couple stuff, it wasn’t that deep.

    “All done?” Rio flashed a charming smile, holding out her hand for the dirty plate, but something about it felt forced.

    Agatha noticed the shift in mood—confused, but handed her the plate anyway. “Thank you…” She arched a brow, wondering what had changed. Not wanting to make things awkward, she added, “Beautiful.” Rio’s smile brightened a bit as she went over to the sink to wash their plates. Trying her best to calm her beating her heart.

    Agatha looked down at the table anxiously. “I’m gonna go wash up.” She pushed her chair back but paused, waiting for Rio to reply. “Okay, honey.”

    Agatha wasn’t sure what else to say. She sighed softly, staring at Rio’s back as she washed the dishes. “If you need me, I’ll be upstairs.” “I know, sweetie.” Rio continued cleaning off their dishes. “Alright, thank you again for doing that.” Agatha made her way toward the stairs. She hoped that Rio would at least come up to the room and talk with her while she got in.

    Just… something.

    She made her way into the bathroom, got undressed, then got in the tub. She waited And waited…

    Nothing.

    She sighed.

    She focused on washing herself up then quickly got out.

    She walked past the bed while toweling herself off, and stopped when she noticed Rio’s hoodie—the one she’d worn at dinner…lying on the bed. So… she did come up here. And didn’t even say a word!?

    She must have been quiet if Agatha hadn’t heard her. With a sigh, she picked up the article of clothing and brought it to her nose, inhaling its sweet fragrance. Tears welled in her eyes. She just missed her so much. They barely even saw each other in bed anymore. Lately, the only times Agatha saw Rio were right before falling asleep and first thing in the morning.

    But depending on who was up all night with the babies, their sleep schedules shifted. Rio was usually the one getting up, and sometimes she’d sleep in longer than Agatha to make up for the lost hours. More often than not, though, Rio would still get up before Agatha to start breakfast and make sure Nicky got to school.

    Some nights Rio barely slept at all—yet somehow, she still had an endless supply of energy.

    Maybe Agatha could try… tonight?

    As night fell, Agatha felt her anxiety creeping in.

    Which was a shame, considering how excited Rio was about the movie they were watching. It was some action flick—Agatha wasn’t really paying attention. She couldn’t help focusing on how warm Rio felt, curled up beside her.

    She hadn’t meant to, but eventually, she drifted off, lulled by the steady rhythm of Rio’s heartbeat.

    The next thing she knew, she was waking up in the bedroom of their cabin. It was dark. She looked around, reached out to her side—but Rio wasn’t there. So she got up.

    She noticed a faint light pouring in from the bathroom. Rio must have left it on accidentally.

    She entered the room—and froze. Her face turned bright red when she came face-to-face with a naked, dripping Rio, who was in the middle of toweling herself off. And wow, did her muscles look good.

    “Oh! Sorry, I should’ve knocked. I’ll let you have your privacy,” Agatha blurted, backing away. She tried to close the door, but it wouldn’t budge. Frowning, she looked down—Rio was holding the knob. “Oh… did you need something?”

    Rio shook her head but pulled the door open wider. Agatha still had her hand on the knob, and the motion tugged her closer to Rio. Dark eyes locked onto hers.

    “More like I need someone.”

    Rio slipped a hand around Agatha’s waist, pulling her in tight. “I need you, baby. I can’t take it anymore. It’s been too long.” Agatha moved in closer, resting her hand on Rio’s chest. “Oh, Rio…”

    The raven-haired woman drew her in—their lips inches apart—then—

    Agatha opened her eyes, looking around. It was dark, she was in the bedroom of the cabin.

    Talk about Deja vu.

    She reached out to her side and felt Rio next to her, she sighed. Guess it was just a dream. A pretty steamy one… She slid her thighs together and groaned.

    Wet and steamy…

    She wasn’t even in the mood to deal with it herself. She just rolled over and closed her eyes trying to fall back asleep. It really didn’t help when Rio slid against her back, wrapping her hand around her body, snuggling against her.

    It was definitely going to be a long night…

    “Agatha.”

    Agatha mumbled something into the pillow, still half-asleep. “Oh, pretty girl,” came the soft voice, “wake up. Come on.” She released a lazy groan and shook her head. “Don’t wanna…” Then came the giggle—warm and close. Then after—

    Kisses.

    Her eyes stayed shut as her mind drifted in that space between asleep and awake. She felt a delicate trail of kisses along her cheek, her jaw… the corner of her mouth.

    “Come on, my pretty girl. I miss you,” Rio whispered.

    “Rio…?” Agatha murmured, still dazed.

    “Mmh, yes, it’s me.” Rio pulled back just slightly, smiling down at her. “I made breakfast—turkey sausage and waffles. Let’s eat, come on.” She started to move away, but Agatha was quicker, catching her by her wrist and pulling her back down.

    “Woah! Honey?”

    Agatha’s breath hitched. “Rio… I—I…” She rolled her hips against her leg, a helpless whimper escaped her lips.

    Rio froze, eyes wide as she looked down, feeling the soft, insistent grind against her thigh. Her heart stuttered. “Oh, Agatha…” she breathed, her mind scrambling as the front of her jeans grew uncomfortably tight. “Rio…” Agatha’s voice trembled, needy. “Please… I miss you, baby… d- don’t you miss me?” Her bottom lip quivered.

    “Agatha?” Rio’s voice cracked with concern.

    “I—is that a no…?” Agatha whispered, her voice sounding fragile. Rio sat back slightly, brows furrowing. “Agatha, what are you talking about?” Her hands hovered in the air, uncertain. “Honey, open your eyes!” But Agatha kept them shut, still lost in a haze. She reached down, fingers brushing the hem of her own shirt, beginning to tug it up. “I’m talking about—”

    “Whoa, whoa!” Rio leaned in, gently catching her wrists. “What are you doing?”

    Agatha’s eyes finally fluttered open. She looked up at Rio, then at her own hands. Realization hit. She blinked, flushed with confusion and embarrassment. “I… I—I’m… what happened?” She faltered, her voice small. “I just woke up, I—I think I…”

    Rio hesitated, then slowly, let go, pulling her own hands back. Agatha sat up slowly, arms wrapping around herself as she stared down at the wrinkled sheets. “I guess I was… overheated.” She swung her legs over the edge of the bed, her shoulders stiff. “I’m gonna get up.”

    “Agatha?”

    Agatha was already at the bedroom door. “I think I’m just hungry. Let’s go eat, okay, Rio?” She turned, flashing a small smile over her shoulder. Rio hesitated, her brows slightly drawn, but she nodded. “Okay.” They ate breakfast in silence. The air between them was thick and heavy, like neither one of them knew how to break it.

    Agatha felt the push of tears at the back of her eyes—the tight, hot pressure that warned a breakdown was waiting just under the surface. But she held it in. She remembered everything from earlier, every blurry second she’d thought was just a dream, but wasn’t.

    Why was she upset?

    Because Rio had stopped her from taking off her shirt?

    Well… no.

    Technically, Rio had only asked what she was doing. She hadn’t scolded her, hadn’t yelled—she’d just been confused. Agatha had practically been sleep-humping her.

    Oh god!

    What was wrong with her?

    She was overreacting. That was all.

    With a sigh, Agatha set her fork down. Her stomach churned; if she ate any more, she’d be sick. She pushed back from the table, the wooden chair scraping loudly across the floor, and carried her plate to the sink, setting it down.

    “Agatha?”

    Rio’s voice was gentle and quiet.

    Agatha gripped the edge of the sink, her head hung low, she couldn’t stop the tears that slipped down her cheek and quickly wiped them away with her sweater sleeve.

    “Agatha, honey?”

    She heard Rio’s chair push back and footsteps approached. Agatha drew in a sharp breath, forced a bright smile onto her face, and turned around. “So, what would you like to do today?” Her voice was light and calm, too calm. Maybe if she could fool Rio, she could fool herself, too. Rio stopped mid-step, eyes worried and confused. “Oh, um…” it took her a second, she looked as if she was going to say something serious but instead relaxed her body and offered a soft smile. “I was hoping you might have some ideas? Rio found it amusing that Agatha was this excited over something so mundane. But maybe that was because Rio had lived in New Jersey her whole life, while Agatha was from Massachusetts.

    “I—yes. How did you—”

    “I have connections. Regardless, it’s important. For my family. As my future daughter-in-law, I beg you. It’ll all make sense when we speak in person. Please, for Agatha. For Nicky.”
